discussions.title: Bug: session materialization fails with EACCES on Android (hard links forbidden) — patch included
discussions.body:
## Bug: session materialization fails with EACCES on Android — hard links are forbidden (fix covers all 3 affected paths)

**Environment:** Android 15, Termux (aarch64), Node v26.4.0, dsh 0.1.0-rc.6.

### Problem

Every session materialization fails with:

```
EACCES: permission denied, link '<tmp>' -> '...session.jsonl.zstd'
```

`materializePosix` publishes the temp file with `link()` — chosen deliberately because it fails with `EEXIST` when the final path already exists, so concurrent materialization of the same id cannot clobber each other. But on Android, `link(2)` is forbidden on the app data filesystem and returns `EACCES`, so sessions can never be written at all.

An audit of every `link()` use in the dsh packages found **three** publication paths with the same failure:

| Package | Location | Semantics to preserve |
|---|---|---|
| `dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` | `materializePosix` | no-replace publish (EEXIST guard) |
| `dsh-fs-local` | `writeFileAtomic` with `createIfAbsent` | no-replace publish (`throwGuardedCreateFailure` backstop — its comment already anticipates "missing hard-link support" but treats EACCES as a plain `FS_IO_ERROR`) |
| `dsh-attachment-local` | content-addressed store | dedup (EEXIST → integrity verify) |

### Proposed fix (patches included)

Each fallback is strictly platform-gated (`error.code === 'EACCES'`), keeps the original `link()` path unchanged everywhere else, and reuses the existing existence backstop.

**1. session-persistence-jsonl** — on `EACCES`, re-run `rejectExistingLog` (the same existence backstop already used before the temp write) and publish via `rename()`:

```diff
--- a/packages/session/session-persistence-jsonl/src/index.ts
+++ b/packages/session/session-persistence-jsonl/src/index.ts
@@ -12,7 +12,7 @@ import { Context } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
 import z from '@deepseek-ai/schemastery'
 import { readdirSync } from 'node:fs'
-import { open, mkdir, readFile, readdir, realpath, link, rm, stat, truncate } from 'node:fs/promises'
+import { open, mkdir, readFile, readdir, realpath, link, rename, rm, stat, truncate } from 'node:fs/promises'
 import { dirname, join, resolve } from 'node:path'
 import { performance } from 'node:perf_hooks'
 import { scheduler } from 'node:timers/promises'
@@ -548,6 +548,14 @@ export class JsonlSessionPersistence extends SessionPersistence implements Persi
     try {
       await link(tmp, finalPath)
       linked = true
+    } catch (error) {
+      // Android (bionic) forbids hard links with EACCES; emulate the
+      // no-replace publish with an existence check + rename (narrow TOCTOU
+      // window, same class as the EEXIST guard above).
+      if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== 'EACCES') throw error
+      await this.rejectExistingLog(finalPath, id)
+      await rename(tmp, finalPath)
+      linked = true
     } finally {
       // Remove an unpublished temp on failure. After publication, defer cleanup
       // until the directory entry is durable so cleanup cannot reject a live log.
```

**2. fs-local `writeFileAtomic`** — on `EACCES`, inspect the publication target; if absent, `rename()` (same no-replace semantics as `link()`); if present, keep the existing `FS_NOT_OBSERVED` rejection:

```ts
if (createIfAbsent !== undefined) {
  try {
    await linkFile(tempPath, absolutePath)
  } catch (error: unknown) {
    if (!isEACCES(error)) {
      await throwGuardedCreateFailure(error, absolutePath, createIfAbsent.displayPath, inspectPublicationTarget)
    } else {
      let existing: BigIntStats | undefined
      try {
        existing = await inspectPublicationTarget(absolutePath)
      } catch (metadataError: unknown) {
        if (!isENOENT(metadataError) && !isENOTDIR(metadataError)) throw error
      }
      if (existing !== undefined) {
        await throwGuardedCreateFailure(error, absolutePath, createIfAbsent.displayPath, inspectPublicationTarget)
      } else {
        await rename(tempPath, absolutePath)
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**3. attachment-local content-addressed store** — on `EACCES`, publish via `rename()` directly: the target name is the sha256 of the payload, so a concurrent writer can only ever produce identical bytes under the same name (rename cannot clobber with different data). Two further Android-specific fixes were needed here, both found during verification:

- the trailing staging `unlink()` runs after the rename fallback has already moved the staging file away, so it must tolerate `ENOENT` (the normal state on that path); any other unlink failure still surfaces as `ATTACHMENT_WRITE_FAILED`
- `ensureDurableDirectory` walks every ancestor up to the filesystem root and fsyncs each one, but Android app sandboxes refuse to open system-owned ancestors (`EACCES: permission denied, open '/data/data'`), so `saveImageFile` failed before ever reaching the link step; the walk now stops at the first EACCES/EPERM ancestor (durability of OS-owned levels is the OS's responsibility)

The complete change is a single ready-to-merge commit on `lesliechowsh/deepseek-harness`, branch `fix/android-hardlink-eacces` (base `master`, single commit), if that is easier to cherry-pick.

### Known limitation of the fallback

`link()` is atomic no-clobber; the check-then-rename fallback narrows that guarantee: two concurrent writers can both pass the existence check and the second `rename()` silently clobbers the first, which `link()` could never allow. In practice dsh serializes per-target writes (per-targetKey locks), and for the attachment store the clobber would be byte-identical (content-addressed), but the session layer would lose data silently in a same-id race. The fallback comments in the patch are annotated as **best-effort** accordingly. If the atomic guarantee must hold, `renameat2(RENAME_NOREPLACE)` (Linux 3.15+, all Android kernels) is the exact equivalent of `link()` — the project already uses FFI syscalls on Android (koffi statx) and lazy koffi on Windows, so the pattern exists; a shared helper for all three paths would restore the contract fully.

### Testing (Android 15, Termux, aarch64, Node 26, dsh 0.1.0-rc.6)

- Attachment `saveImageFile` (real PNG, exercised the EACCES link path): save OK, target bytes match, no staging residue, dedup returns the same id on a second save
- `writeFileAtomic` createIfAbsent: first write OK (EACCES → rename), second write to the same path rejected with `FS_NOT_OBSERVED` (no-replace semantics hold), plain writes unaffected
- Headless agent run writing files via the file tools: succeeded, session persisted; sessions materialize and load, `session.jsonl.zstd` files land in `~/.dsh/sessions/` (with the `danger-full-access` preset)
- Non-Android platforms are unaffected (the `link()` path is unchanged)

### Action wanted

If this looks reasonable, the fix could be cherry-picked from the branch (single commit) or applied from the patches above. Happy to adjust the approach (e.g. the `renameat2` helper) or add mock-EACCES unit tests if maintainers would prefer that route.

One caveat: the full pre-fix stack trace is no longer reproducible here since the fix is applied locally — only the error line shown above. Happy to capture a stack from an unpatched checkout if useful.

discussions.title: [bug] Native folder dialog truncates paths at characters whose UTF-16 low byte is 0x00 ("05agent开发" → "05agent")
discussions.body:
## Status: 用户报告；已静态定位根因并本地修复验证（实机复验待确认）

### 现象

在 Windows 的 dsh Web GUI 中切换 / 创建 workspace，点击原生文件夹选择对话框（Select Workspace Directory）选中目录后，**路径中的部分汉字被截断**，导致 workspace 创建失败：

```
workspace create failed: workspace-invalid-path: cannot create a workspace at
"F:\01_workplace\05agent": ENOENT: no such file or directory, realpath 'F:\01_workplace\05agent'
```

- 用户实际选择的目录是 `F:\01_workplace\05agent开发`，报错路径中**「开发」被整体截断**——从「开」（U+5F00）开始及其后的所有字符丢失。
- 用户经验观察：纯英文 + 数字、以及部分纯中文目录名不受影响；仅"中英混排"目录名出问题。
- 该行为与目录名中**具体包含哪些字符**有关，并非"混排"本身（见根因分析：触发条件是字符码位的低字节为 0）。

### 环境

- 仓库：`deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness`
- HEAD：`47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a`（`Merge pull request #2519 from deepseek-harness/feat/npm-public`）
- 平台：Windows 10 Pro 10.0.19045；Node.js v24.16.0；pnpm 11.21.0
- 运行方式：源码检出 + `pnpm dsh web`（tsx 源码模式；目录选择 worker 同样走源码分支 `import.meta.url.endsWith('.ts')`，见 `win32-dialog-host.ts:27-30`）
- 复现路径：Web GUI → 切换 workspace → 原生目录选择器 → 选择含"低字节为 0"字符的路径 → 报 `workspace-invalid-path` 错误

### 代码路径

**客户端包装**：`packages/client/runtime/src/client/workspaces/service.ts:212`

```ts
throw new Error(`directory picker failed: ${response.result.error.message}`)
```

**路径字符串读取**：`packages/host/directory-picker-native/src/win32-dialog-bindings.ts:37-44`，调用点在 `:159`（`IShellItem::GetDisplayName(SIGDN_FILESYSPATH)` 的返回值）：

```ts
function readUtf16(koffi: Koffi, address: unknown): string {
  const bytes = Buffer.from(koffi.view(address, 32768))
  let end = 0
  while (end + 1 < bytes.length && bytes[end] !== 0) end += 2
  return bytes.toString('utf16le', 0, end)
}
```

### 根因分析

`readUtf16` 用**单字节判 NUL** 来定位 UTF-16LE 字符串的结束位置，这对 ASCII 成立，但对任意"码位低字节为 0"的字符会**提前截断**：

- Windows 路径是 UTF-16LE 编码。ASCII 字符（如 `a`，U+0061）的低字节非 0（`61 00`），只有真正的字符串终止符 `00 00` 会命中偶数字节偏移处的 0x00，因此单字节检查在纯 ASCII 下是正确的。
- 但码位形如 `U+XX00` 的字符，其 UTF-16LE 字节序为 `00 XX`——**偶数字节偏移处恰好是 0x00**，被误判为字符串结束。
- 例：「开」= U+5F00 → 字节 `00 5F`。路径 `F:\01_workplace\05agent开发` 中，「开」从第 14 字节开始，扫描在 `bytes[14] === 0` 处停止，结果 `toString('utf16le', 0, 14)` = `"F:\01_workplace\05agent"`——与用户报错完全一致。

**字节级复现**（node 模拟，路径 `F:\01_workplace\05agent开发`）：

```js
const path = "F:\\01_workplace\\05agent开发";
const bytes = Buffer.from(path, "utf16le");

// 旧逻辑（单字节判 NUL）
let end = 0;
while (end + 1 < bytes.length && bytes[end] !== 0) end += 2;
console.log(bytes.toString("utf16le", 0, end)); // "F:\\01_workplace\\05agent"  ← 截断

// 正确逻辑（UTF-16 单元双字节全 0 才算终止）
end = 0;
while (end + 1 < bytes.length && !(bytes[end] === 0 && bytes[end + 1] === 0)) end += 2;
console.log(bytes.toString("utf16le", 0, end)); // "F:\\01_workplace\\05agent开发"  ← 完整
```

**受影响字符范围**：所有低字节为 0 的码位，包含大量常用 CJK 汉字（如「一」U+4E00、「开」U+5F00）、部分谚文音节等。因此：

- 用户"纯中文目录没事"的经验是**巧合**——其目录名（如「资料」「疲劳问卷」）恰好不含此类字符；任何包含「一」「开」等字的纯中文目录同样会截断。
- 正确表述：**目录名（或路径任意段）包含低字节为 0 的字符即触发**。

**影响面**：全仓库 grep 确认仅此一处存在该扫描模式（`bytes[end] !== 0` 循环仅出现于 `win32-dialog-bindings.ts:40`）；koffi 自身的 `str16` 处理不受影响。修复隔离、风险低。

**安全 / 正确性影响（目录混淆）**：若截断后的**前缀路径存在**，realpath 校验会通过，workspace 将被创建在用户**未选中的目录**上，agent 随后在错误目录中读写、执行——属于路径混淆（path confusion）。两种场景对比：

- 前缀不存在（本报告实测场景）：`F:\01_workplace\05agent` 不存在 → 创建失败，表现为功能缺陷（拒绝服务级）；
- 前缀存在（推演场景）：用户选择 `F:\docs\开单系统`，截断为 `F:\docs`（存在）→ **realpath 通过**，workspace 静默创建在 `F:\docs`，agent 在错误的目录上工作，危害更大且无任何告警。

### 期望行为

- 目录选择器返回的路径必须**原样完整**保留（如 `F:\01_workplace\05agent开发`），不能丢失任何字符。
- workspace 创建目录必须与用户在对话框中选中的目录**严格一致**，不允许任何静默的路径改写（截断 / 规范化），杜绝"选中 A、实际在 B 建 workspace"的目录混淆。
- 终止符判定应基于**完整的 16 位 NUL 单元**（`00 00`），而非单个字节。

### 建议

1. **修复 `readUtf16` 的终止符检查**（已验证可修复截断）：

   ```ts
   function readUtf16(koffi: Koffi, address: unknown): string {
     const bytes = Buffer.from(koffi.view(address, 32768))
     let end = 0
     // The terminator is a full 16-bit NUL unit, not a zero low byte: a code
     // point like U+5F00 (开) has a zero low byte, and a single-byte check
     // truncates the string at the first such character.
     while (end + 1 < bytes.length && !(bytes[end] === 0 && bytes[end + 1] === 0)) end += 2
     return bytes.toString('utf16le', 0, end)
   }
   ```

2. **补充单元测试**：覆盖含低字节 0 字符的路径（`05agent开发`、「一」开头、纯 CJK、谚文等），以及纯 ASCII、纯 CJK（无 00 低字节）、空串、超长路径（32768 字节 `koffi.view` 上限边界）等用例；建议同时覆盖源码分支与 built `worker.cjs` 分支。
3. 后续可考虑抽查仓库其它手工读取 Win32 字符串的路径（本次 grep 未发现同类模式），防同类问题扩散。

### 未确认项

- 本机已应用上述本地补丁（`win32-dialog-bindings.ts`），但**用户实机复验结果待确认**（本报告撰写时尚未收到复验反馈）。
- 报告基于源码静态分析 + 字节级模拟复现；未运行仓库测试套件（`vitest`）验证补丁对既有用例的影响（改动仅限终止符判定，语义上只放宽了扫描，不改变纯 ASCII 行为）。
- built（CJS `worker.cjs`）产物由同一源码编译，推断同样受影响；未对 built 产物实测。
- 非 CJK 场景（U+XX00 类字符在韩文/日文中的出现）未逐一实测。
- 「目录混淆」场景（截断后前缀路径存在、realpath 通过、workspace 建在错误目录）为静态推演，未实机验证。

discussions.title: [bug] Message edit failure notice is not aligned with the message itself (error toast detached from the edited message)
discussions.body:
## Summary

In the DSH Web GUI, when **editing a queued (unsent) message fails**, the failure notice is not placed anywhere near the message row being edited. The error toast/notice is rendered inside the **composer input bar**, fully detached from the queue-dock row that failed, and it carries **no message identifier** (no id, no preview, no time). With more than one queued message, the user cannot tell which message's edit failed.

## Environment

- Repo: deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness
- HEAD: `47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a` (Merge pull request #2519 from deepseek-harness/feat/npm-public)
- Web GUI: dsh web (127.0.0.1:3080)

## Reproduction

1. Start a turn / queue at least two messages (so the queue dock lists more than one row).
2. Click the edit (pencil) action on one queued message and save a changed text while the host rejects the mutation (e.g. the row has already started being sent — `queue.editFailed`).
3. Observe the error text appears in the composer input bar area, not beside the edited queue row; the user cannot tell which message failed.

## How the edit failure is surfaced today (component + line)

Message "editing" in this UI means editing a **queued/unsent** message in the queue dock (there is no in-transcript edit of already-sent user messages in this build). The failed edit is reported through the shared per-session **notice** channel, and the notice is only rendered by the composer bar.

1. `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/queue/QueueDock.tsx:69-76` — `saveEdit` calls `applyAction(editing.id, { kind: 'edit', ... }, t('queue.editFailed'))`.
2. `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/queue/QueueDock.tsx:52-67` — `applyAction` catches the rejected `updateQueue(...)` and runs `notify('error', failure)` (**line 62**). The `editing` row's `id` (`QueueDock.tsx:36`) is discarded here.
3. `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/queue/QueueDock.tsx:239` — the injected `notify` writes to the shared facade: `conversation.input.for(actx).notify(level, text)`.
4. `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/input/facade.ts:345-348` — `SessionInputShell.notify` sets the **single shared** `notices` store (`this.notices.set({ level, text, seq })`). Only `{ level, text, seq }` is stored — `InputNotice` (`.../input/contract.ts:87-91`) carries no queue/message id.
5. `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/apply.ts:355` — the composer-bar entry binds `hooks.notices = shell.notices`.
6. `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/skeleton/InputBar.tsx:55` — `const notice = useNotices(s => s)`.
7. `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/skeleton/InputBar.tsx:660-664` — renders `<div role="status">` with `notice.text` **inside the composer card**.

Layout: the **queue dock** renders in slot `conversation.input.dock` **above** the composer bar here — `packages/client/ui-conversation/src/client/skeleton/ConversationRoot.tsx:164` (`renderSlot('conversation.input.dock', zone)`) then line 165 `inputBar`. So the edited row lives in the dock strip; the error notice lives in the composer bar below it.

## Root-cause analysis (ranked)

1. **(Confirmed primary) The failure notice is a detached, shared, last-writer-wins notice, not tied to the edited row.** `QueueDock.applyAction` drops the row id and raises a generic `notify('error', t('queue.editFailed'))` (`QueueDock.tsx:62`); that notice is rendered only by the composer bar (`InputBar.tsx:660-664`), far from the dock row. The `InputNotice` shape (`{ level, text, seq }`) has no message identifier, so the text cannot reference which message failed.
2. **No per-row error surface in the queue dock.** `QueueDock.tsx` has no row-level error state; an edit failure does not mark the failing row, does not flash it, and does not keep it in an edit/error state — only `editing` is cleared on success (`QueueDock.tsx:75`), and on failure `editing` stays, but no visible error tells the user *that* row failed vs. stopped at the generic notice.
3. **Multiple rows + collapsed dock make misalignment worse.** When >1 message is queued the dock collapses to a count header (`QueueDock.tsx:38`, `:81-96`); the generic notice in the composer gives the user no way to locate the offending row.
4. **Request/log association is present but unused for presentation.** `QueuedMessage.id` / `messageId` / `preview` / `text` are available (`packages/client/runtime/src/client/sessions/conversation.ts:313-324`) and the failed `updateQueue` item id is in scope in `saveEdit`, but none of it reaches the notice.

## Expected behavior

The edit-failure notice should be clearly associated with the specific message, for example:
- Render the error **under the failing queue row** (inline in the dock), or
- Keep/label the edited row in an error state (e.g. red border + message), or
- At minimum, include a message identifier in the notice text (the row's preview excerpt or send time) so the user can find which message failed.

## Suggested fix direction

- Give `QueueDock` a per-row error field (e.g. `errorRowId` + message) and render it inline under the failing `<li>` (`QueueDock.tsx:98-208`), instead of (or in addition to) the shared facade notice.
- Or extend the notice contract `InputNotice` (`input/contract.ts:87-91`) with an optional `target`/`sourceId`, and let the queue-dock renderer pick up failures for its own rows.
- Ensure the failing row stays visually identifiable (does not silently reset) until the user acknowledges or retries.

discussions.title: Two remote-execution-world gaps in dsh-base (tool-fs-search rg path; fs-sandbox modes), with fixes
discussions.body:
While building a third-party remote-sandbox provider suite against `deepseek-harness@0.1.0-rc.6`, I hit two spots where `dsh-base` assumes the execution world is host-local. Both are invisible with the local providers and only surface once `ctx.fs`/`ctx.subprocess` point at a remote sandbox — exactly the portability the capability seams are designed for ("pointing them at a remote sandbox moves Bash, PTY, and LSP with them"). Reporting them together since they're the same class of issue, each with a concrete fix.

### 1. `tool-fs-search` hardcodes the host ripgrep path

`runRipgrep` in `packages/fs/tool-fs-search/src/search-core.ts` builds `argv` as:

```ts
argv: [await resolveRgPath(), '--no-config', ...argv]
```

`resolveRgPath()` returns the absolute path of the **host's** `@vscode/ripgrep` binary, handed straight to `ctx.subprocess.spawn` as `argv[0]` — it never goes through `resolveExecutable`. `tool-fs-search` is mounted in the shipped `dsh-base` bundle, but any remote execution world has no such host path, so every `glob`/`grep` fails with a spawn error. The `examples/headless-agent/e2b.cordis.yml` overlay happens to avoid it by not mounting the plugin, so it's easy to miss.

**Suggested fix:** resolve the search binary through `ctx.subprocess.resolveExecutable('rg', ...)` (falling back to the packaged path for the local provider), so the executable is located in whatever execution world is mounted. A provider can then ship `rg` in its sandbox image.

### 2. Sandbox permission modes have no remote semantics

`dsh-fs-sandbox`'s `SandboxedFileSystem extends LocalFileSystem`, and `writableRoots()` in `packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/roots.ts` canonicalizes `policy.workspaceRoot` together with the host's `/tmp` and `os.tmpdir()` via the host `realpath`. In a remote world those are the wrong filesystem's paths, so `read-only` and `workspace-write` silently don't apply — the e2b example is forced to hardcode `danger-full-access`. The two model-visible escalation modes effectively can't be honored by a remote fs provider today, with no warning.

**Suggested fix:** let a remote fs provider enforce the mode against its own execution-world paths (the seam already passes `sandboxPolicy` down to `writeText`/`editText`), and keep `writableRoots()`' host-`/tmp` mixing to the local backend.

Happy to open PRs for either if external contributions become welcome later — I understand the current stance. In the meantime I've worked around both in a provider suite (sidecar ships `rg`; the sidecar enforces the mode against sandbox paths). Thanks for the seam design — it made the remote world genuinely composable once these two host assumptions are handled.

discussions.title: dsh-remote-sandbox: crash-resilient, workspace-synced E2B execution world (fills the dsh-e2b POC gaps)
discussions.body:
**[dsh-remote-sandbox](https://github.com/weijiafu14/dsh-remote-sandbox)** — a provider suite that turns the E2B execution world into something you can run real work in.

The official `dsh-e2b` POC proves the fs/subprocess seam can point at a remote sandbox, but (by its own README) the sandbox is *"deliberately ephemeral"*, dies after five minutes, keeps a process's whole output in host memory, and *"neither uploads nor synchronizes the host workspace"*. This suite fills exactly those gaps:

| | official `dsh-e2b` (POC) | `dsh-remote-sandbox` |
|---|---|---|
| Sandbox lifetime | fixed 5 min, then deleted | heartbeat keep-alive, lives as long as the task |
| Connection drop / pause | sandbox death = task death | transparent resume of the paused sandbox (disk retained) |
| Hard crash | none | recreate + restore workspace from the last snapshot |
| Host workspace | not synced | tar IN at open, tar OUT on request/teardown |
| Process output memory | whole stream in host memory | bounded in-memory tail + optional host spill |
| fs op round trips | 3–8 SDK commands per mutation | **one** (a pure-JS sidecar does it atomically in the sandbox) |
| `glob`/`grep` | broken in a remote world (see #490) | works — `rg` ships with the sidecar |

**How it's built:** a ~160 KB pure-JS sidecar (no native deps) runs inside the sandbox and executes fs/process primitives locally over one WebSocket, so a filesystem mutation is one round trip instead of a chain of SDK shell commands. A keeper owns the sandbox lifecycle — heartbeat keep-alive, and on a dropped connection it resumes the paused sandbox or, only if it's truly gone, recreates it and restores the workspace. The providers derive the current connection per call, so recovery is invisible to `ctx.fs`/`ctx.subprocess`. LLM/git credentials never enter the sandbox.

**Install:**
```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add dsh-remote-sandbox
export E2B_API_KEY=e2b_...
```

**Tested:** 37 unit/provider tests (real sidecar bundle, the real dsh `FileSystem`/`SubprocessRuntime` base classes, keeper lifecycle/recovery/sync) plus 6 real-E2B end-to-end scenarios — keep-alive past the base timeout, resume after pause, recreate after a hard kill, grep over a large tree with bounded host memory, tar round-trip, and a custom sync override. All green.

`syncIn`/`syncOut` are overridable from `cordis.yml` (`!!js`) if you'd rather sync via git, object storage, or a shared volume. MIT. Feedback and issues welcome — it's early, and dsh is moving fast. Built against `0.1.0-rc.6`.

discussions.title: [RFC] 增加评测隔离模式：当前 workspace 缺少读取隔离能力
discussions.body:
## TL;DR

- **现状**：DSH 当前三档权限（`read-only` / `workspace-write` / `danger-full-access`）限制的是文件修改范围，读取仍然可以访问 workspace 以外的内容。选择一个空的 workspace，并不能保证 Agent 只看到这个目录里的东西。
- **影响**：在评测任务里，机器上其他目录的代码、答案、历史会话都可能被 Agent 读到，评测结果因此会受运行环境影响。只是给每个任务分开 workspace 和会话 ID，并不够。
- **建议**：增加一个可选的评测隔离模式，并在评测文档中写明当前的隔离范围。

## 我们遇到的情况

我们最近在用 DSH 作为评测基底，运行 GPU kernel 优化任务。每个任务里，Agent 会围绕一个算子反复修改实现、运行测试、比较性能结果。

一次测试中，我们特意选了一个空目录作为 workspace，想要一个干净的环境。但在看轨迹时发现，Agent 读到了同一台机器上另一个目录里、上一轮任务留下的内容。这些内容并不属于当前 workspace。

我们随后查了文档和源码，发现这不是实现上的疏漏，而是当前沙箱设计明确允许的行为：现有权限模型限制的是写入范围，读取保持开放。

排查中我们还发现，即使 Agent 没有主动调用文件工具，第一轮的上下文也可能包含 workspace 以外的信息：`discoverInstructionFiles` 会先探测 `$DSH_HOME/AGENTS.md`，再沿祖先目录逐层收集 `AGENTS.md` 和 `CLAUDE.md`（[packages/context/agent-instructions/src/files.ts L267-L307](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/context/agent-instructions/src/files.ts#L267-L307)）。这也是为什么只选一个空目录当 workspace，并不能保证任务环境是干净的。

所以这篇不是要报告一个缺陷，而是提一个能力上的建议：评测场景需要一个额外的隔离模式。

## 一、现状

DSH 当前三档权限（`read-only` / `workspace-write` / `danger-full-access`）限制的都是写入行为，读取保持开放。

相关证据（基于 commit `47f9438`）：

CLI 文档写明：

> Bash 和文件系统修改仅限于会话 workspace 与平台临时根目录；读取、网络访问和进程可见性不受限制。

[apps/cli/reference/README.zh.md L68-L70](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/apps/cli/reference/README.zh.md#L68-L70)

`fs-sandbox` 的模块注释写明：

> Reads pass through untouched: every mode permits reading.

[packages/fs/fs-sandbox/src/index.ts L1-L28](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/fs/fs-sandbox/src/index.ts#L1-L28)

这一行为也已经被回归测试固定下来。在同一个 `workspace-write` 的测试块里，跨 workspace 的写入会被拒绝，而读取父目录会成功：

```ts
expect(bashRead.isError).toBe(false)   // bash: cat ../shared.txt
expect(fsRead.isError).toBe(false)     // fs:   read ../shared.txt
```

[packages/examples/agent-spine-demo/tests/multi-project-sandbox.e2e.ts L210-L244](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/examples/agent-spine-demo/tests/multi-project-sandbox.e2e.ts#L210-L244)

我特意把这条测试列出来，是因为它说明放开读取是当前的设计约定，不是遗漏。所以下面提的是增加一个新的档位，而不是改变现有档位的行为。

补充一点：这也不是配置能解决的问题。权限预设表本身是可以覆盖的——界面上那三档就定义在部署配置里（[packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml L193-L205](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml#L193-L205)）。但一个预设只是把两个开关捆在一起：`sandbox` 的取值只有 `read-only` / `workspace-write` / `danger-full-access`，`approval` 的取值只有 `ask` / `never`，两者都不接受路径参数。环境变量 `DSH_PERMISSION_MODE` 也只是在这三档里选。也就是说，现在的配置里没有可以写出「这些目录不许读」的地方，自定义预设也只能在这几种组合里挑。

## 二、为什么评测场景需要额外的隔离能力

### 1. 评测结果会受到机器上其他文件的影响

[BENCHMARK.md](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/BENCHMARK.md) 里关于隔离目前只有一句：

> Use separate workspaces and session IDs for independent benchmark tasks.

但当前的 workspace 之间并不存在读取隔离。

如果不同题目的目录放在同一个文件系统里，或者参考答案、用来评分的测试和其他产物放在一起，Agent 可以通过 `../`、绝对路径、`grep`、`find` 等方式访问到。已经跑完的其他任务留下的会话记录，也在同样的可见范围内。

也就是说，评测结果是否可信，取决于这台机器上其他目录里放了什么，而不是只由当前任务目录决定。

我们把 DSH 用作 kernel 优化评测基底时，这是一个实际的约束：目前只能把整个 DSH 放进每道题独立的一次性容器里，才能保证环境干净。这个要求本身合理，但值得写进文档和能力设计里，而不是让每个做评测的用户自己发现一遍。

### 2. `$DSH_HOME` 不在当前的读取隔离范围内

会话记录默认就放在 `$DSH_HOME` 下。在默认配置下，只要 Agent 能用文件工具和 bash，同一台机器上其他会话的记录、系统提示词和配置就都不在读取边界之内。

在共用的机器上，这涉及隐私；在评测场景下，这会影响实验结果。

`credentials-local` 的 README 已经描述过类似情况：

> the shipped `workspace-write` file policy confines mutations rather than reads … no sandbox mode singles it out. … That is discretion, not a boundary.

[packages/credentials/credentials-local/README.md L52-L70](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/credentials/credentials-local/README.md#L52-L70)

我们的建议是：DSH 自己的主目录可以考虑单独对待，即使整体的读取策略保持开放。

### 3. 现在的命名容易让人以为 workspace 限制得更严

`Read Only` / `Workspace Write` / `Full access` 这组名字，容易让新用户以为 workspace 在读取上也有约束。这不是主要问题，但在文档或界面上写明当前行为就能减少误解。

## 三、最小复现

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/dsh-read-demo/task-01 /tmp/dsh-read-demo/answers
echo 'ANSWER=42' > /tmp/dsh-read-demo/answers/solution.txt
```

在 Web 里新建会话，workspace 选空目录 `task-01`，权限保持默认，然后让 Agent 看看上一级目录里有什么。Agent 可以读到 `../answers/solution.txt`。切换到 `read-only` 结果一样，因为这一档限制的是写入。

这个例子只是从用户角度复现一次；这个行为本身已经由仓库自己的端到端测试覆盖。

## 四、建议

### P0 — 在轨迹里标记读到 workspace 以外的操作

不改变当前行为，只增加可见性：当读取的路径不在当前 workspace 里时，在轨迹中加一个「出界读」标记。

这样不改动权限模型，不用修改沙箱实现，也不影响现有的测试约定。

对做评测的人来说，先能看出一次任务有没有读过外部内容，这一步很重要。有了标记就能快速判断某次运行是否受到外部信息影响，不用逐条翻工具输出。

### P1 — 增加一个可选的评测隔离模式（设计提案）

目标是缩小 Agent 能看到的文件范围，而不是替代容器。具体怎么实现可以再讨论，更严格的文件系统隔离、容器镜像、microVM 都是可选项，这里不限定做法。

我也看过 [`a90ccc44`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/commit/a90ccc4453221da577fce51f75812ceb228568ae)（2026-07-30，撤回 `readDenyPaths`）。撤回的理由是成立的：`bwrap` 需要在自己已经设为只读的目录树里创建绑定挂载点，所以在还没有这个父目录的全新安装上，整个隔离都会失败；`Landlock` 无法从自己对 `/` 的读取授权里去掉单个路径，只能报 `partial`。那个 commit 的结论是：

> 一个在能用的地方破坏隔离、在不能用的地方误报的保护，比一个写明的缺失更糟。

所以这里不是建议把那条路再走一遍。之前的做法是在已经全部开放的读取上做减法，受限于这两个后端的能力；而评测隔离模式要的是一开始就给出一个更小的环境。但也得承认：真实的 Agent 环境要跑起来，需要运行时、编译工具链、CUDA 这些依赖，能看到的范围会逐渐接近一个完整的执行环境。所以这更像是评测环境本身的设计问题，而不是给沙箱加一个参数就能解决的。

这一档只在评测和处理不可信内容时开启，默认用法不需要改变，现有 `workspace-write` 的测试也不用调整。

### P2 — 处理 `$DSH_HOME` 的默认可见性

在 P1 下这个问题自然就包含进去了。在现有档位里，可以先从小范围做起，比如在 `fs-sandbox` 里增加读取方向的判断。这一层是在进程内做的路径检查——它已经在为写入和编辑做同样的检查——并不依赖 `bwrap` 或 `Landlock`，所以上面提到的那两个内核层面的问题在这里不会出现。

更轻的做法是把会话记录和敏感产物分开存放、收紧文件权限，并提供一个明确的导出接口。

bash 这条路径能力不同，拦不住，应该作为已知限制写进文档，而不是当作已经解决。

### P3 — 补充 `BENCHMARK.md` 的说明

建议在 `BENCHMARK.md` 里写明：严格的评测需要把整个 DSH 放进每道题独立的一次性容器或 microVM，并且当前三档权限都不提供答案层面的隔离。这一项成本最低，也最能让做评测的用户少走弯路。

## 五、与 #159 的关系

[#159](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/159) 里，模型直接调用的读取操作读到了 workspace 以外的文件（`isError: false`），这可以作为旁证，但那篇讨论的主题是 `workspace-write` 的写入边界存在先检查、后执行之间的竞态。

两者关注的不是同一件事：#159 说的是写入限制的实现缺口，这篇说的是读取隔离的范围本身。所以单独发一帖，避免把两个问题混在一起。[#250](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/250) 和 [#268](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/268) 的正文里也各自引用过同一条读取行为。

---

感谢阅读。希望这篇讨论能帮忙把 DSH 在评测场景下的使用边界说清楚。当前设计对于日常写代码的场景是有价值的；这里想讨论的是，当 DSH 被用来跑评测、或者处理不可信内容时，是否需要增加一层额外的隔离。

discussions.title: Show: dsh-turn-index dsh的侧边导航插件，多轮问答时可选择跳转
discussions.body:
# dsh-turn-index — a turn-index sidebar for DSH Web（社区插件 · Community plugin）

Hi everyone! I built a small client-side plugin for the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI, and I'd love to share it with the community.

## What it does

A **turn-index sidebar** pinned to the right side of the chat flow: one entry per user turn. Click any entry to smoothly scroll to that turn with a brief highlight flash; while you scroll-read a long session, the sidebar keeps the current turn highlighted (scroll-spy).

- One index entry per user turn; steering follow-ups within a turn are shown indented (↳) without breaking turn numbering
- Click to jump — anchored to the chat DOM, reliable even in very long sessions
- Scroll-linked highlighting; expanded list auto-follows the current turn
- "Load earlier turns" pagination for history windows
- Falls back gracefully from the trajectory view (one click to switch back)
- Avoids the tool-details panel; collapses to a 44px dot rail at ≤1024px
- Bilingual (中文 / English) via the harness locale service
- Zero host-side runtime logic: no file access, no network, no credentials — the only persistence is UI preferences in localStorage

## Why

DSH sessions can grow to hundreds of turns; jumping back to an earlier question used to mean endless scrolling. This gives every turn a table of contents.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-turn-index        # npm, v0.1.1
# or via tag tarball:
dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/Simon314620/dsh-turn-index/archive/refs/tags/v0.1.1.tar.gz
```

Then restart `dsh web` and hard-refresh the page.


## Update — v0.1.1 (bug fix)

Fixed an auto-follow bug that kept yanking the index list back to the current turn, which made scrolling up to earlier turns impossible. Now auto-follow only reacts to real turn changes, with a 1.5s grace period after manual scrolling. 26 tests green (2 new regression tests).

## Links

- GitHub: https://github.com/Simon314620/dsh-turn-index (MIT, README in 中文/English)
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-turn-index
- Verified on: DSH 0.1.0-rc.6 · Windows 11 · Node 24 · pnpm 11

This is an **independent community plugin**, not affiliated with the official project. Feedback, issues, and PRs are very welcome — thanks for taking a look! 🙏

discussions.title: 会话统计条被截断时省略号会切在半截数字中间
discussions.body: # 会话进行一段时间后，底部（输入框上方）会出现一行会话统计，例如： #### 然而全部的内容也就止步于全部的`输出：xxx tok`： ## 问题有两个： 1. 显示不全：该行被限制在对话栏宽度（748px）内单行展示，超长部分以省略号截断，例如上面的"输出 …"——省略号切在数字中间，既难看也读不出含义。 2. 完整数据没有好的去处：目前唯一的兜底是鼠标悬停 500ms 后弹出 tooltip 显示整行文本,其`span`的`class=._bubble_owhem_8`。它不可发现、纯文本单行、触屏设备完全不可用，也谈不上对比和停留阅读。 # 解决方案： 直接全部显示，不影响美观，不改反而膈应人 数据来源都是现成的（会话统计与 token 用量 projection 已在读取），改动集中在统计行组件本身，实现成本不高。

discussions.title: dsh-vision-router：图片轮次原生路由 + 内置免 Key 免费视觉模型（已发布）
discussions.body:
# dsh-vision-router：图片轮次原生路由 + 内置免 Key 免费视觉模型（已发布）

保留 DeepSeek 做日常推理，**含图片的那一轮整轮交给视觉模型看原图（像素级，非文字转述）**，其余轮次留在 DeepSeek。开源仓库：[ysr666/dsh-vision-router](https://github.com/ysr666/dsh-vision-router)。

## 与描述桥方案的区别

现有 dsh 视觉插件大多走"描述桥"（图片 → VLM 文字描述 → 交给 DeepSeek，有信息损耗）；本插件走**路由桥**：通过 `agent/pre-step` 检测图片轮，`agent/request` 瀑布把该轮路由改写到视觉模型（`agent/request-error` 驱动降级），视觉模型看到的是原始像素。

## 特性

- **轮次级路由 + 反向路由**：插件注册包装路由 **「DeepSeek + 自动识图」**（`deepseek-vision`，声明 image 输入通过宿主准入，右下角显示"DeepSeek-V4-Pro（自动识图）"即你的主力模型）；图片轮走视觉模型原生看原图，纯文字轮自动反向路由回 DeepSeek，日常体验与成本不变；
- **降级链**：地区限制 / ToS 风控 / 402 额度 / 429 限流 / 网络错误自动换下一个模型（多供应商独立链路）；
- **内置免费视觉模型兜底**：`vision_describe` 在所有配置模型失败后自动落到 **OVHcloud AI Endpoints 匿名层**（`Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct`）——**无需账号、无需 Key、无需代理**；匿名额度为**每个 IP、每个模型每分钟 2 次**（免费层尽力而为）；
- **`vision_describe` 工具**：1–4 张图片对比（本地路径或会话上传附件）、JSON 结构化输出、内容寻址结果缓存、sharp 大图自动缩放；
- **按域名代理**：只把视觉供应商域名走本地代理，DeepSeek 保持直连；
- **错误分类**：失败信息带针对性建议；25 项测试、Node 22/24 CI 全绿。

## 安装

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:ysr666/dsh-vision-router
```

profile 补丁加一行 `vision-router` 行（配置见 README，模型需在 OpenRouter 设置中声明 `input: [text, image]`），重启即可。

> **⚠️ 宿主准入说明（感谢社区反馈指出）**：harness 的发送准入先于任何插件运行——当前会话模型不含 image
> 输入声明时，图片消息会被直接拒绝；DeepSeek 适配器硬编码 `inputModalities: ["text"]` 且无法设置覆盖。
> 因此会话入口模型请选**「DeepSeek + 自动识图」包装路由**（插件注册，模型选择器可见），
> 或任何声明了图片输入的视觉模型；插件用 `reverseRouting` 把纯文字轮自动改回 DeepSeek。
> 已修复 issue #1（改道时不再透传 reasoningEffort，兼容 SenseNova 等供应商）。

## 借鉴与对照（逐项核实）

| 项目 | 我们借了什么 | 我们更强的点（已实现/实测） | 仍需追赶（如实说明） |
|---|---|---|---|
| [dsh-vision-sidecar](https://github.com/121103qwq/dsh-vision-sidecar) | OVHcloud 免注册匿名端点（已实测直连+代理均可用）；描述持久化思路 | ①原图路由（像素级，无转述损耗）②降级链+错误分类 ③JSON/缓存/缩放 ④多供应商链路 | ①描述持久化进会话日志未实现 ②其免 Key 默认覆盖所有图片轮；我们目前只兜底工具，轮次路由仍需用户配置的模型 |
| [dsh-vision-proxy](https://github.com/Flyvhidbwo/dsh-vision-proxy) | 图片转译思路（我们用 `vision_describe` 按需替代常开转译） | 原图路由、降级链、缓存、JSON、缩放；不包装 provider，只改路由 | 他们解决了粘贴图片的 GUI 准入；我们只支持拖入 png/jpeg/webp/gif |
| [dsh-vision-provider](https://github.com/libinyam/dsh-vision-provider) | 纯配置注册 OpenAI 兼容多模态路由 | 在其之上叠加自动路由、降级链、工具、免费兜底 | —（功能超集） |
| [modlens](https://github.com/liustack/modlens) | 引擎复用思路（未采用：自带供应商链，不依赖本机 CLI） | 自动轮次路由、免 Key 兜底、缓存、零 CLI 依赖 | 其"证据化转写"（布局区域/实体清单）更细；复用本机 CLI 登录我们不提供 |
| [dsh-vision-toolkit](https://github.com/Anionex/dsh-vision-toolkit) | 意图化工具集思路 | 更轻：路由 + 一个通用对比工具，开箱零配置 | 其 10 个工具（像素校验、UI 还原）远更全，此维度我们不比 |
| [dsh-tool-vision](https://github.com/Scorp1o117/dsh-tool-vision) | 瀑布图片桥思路（`rewriteImages`） | 轮次路由、降级链、免 Key、缓存、多供应商 | 其 `llm/stream` 桥对文本模型粘贴图全覆盖；我们仅关闭路由时改写 |

**自证**：25 项测试 CI 全绿（Node 22/24）；免 Key 端点用插件真实代码路径实测返回正确识图结果。

## 致谢

本插件借鉴了以上全部社区项目的思路，特别是 [dsh-vision-sidecar](https://github.com/121103qwq/dsh-vision-sidecar) 的免注册免费端点发现。感谢所有作者让 dsh 生态更好。

discussions.title: session-persistence-jsonl: recover from stale duplicates left by an interrupted rewrite (seq gap makes history unreadable)
discussions.body:
## Bug: `seq gap in committed region` makes session history unreadable after an interrupted rewrite

### Symptom

The web GUI shows: `history unavailable for session "...": Error: corrupt session log: seq gap in committed region at line N (expected 87804, got 87800) (internal)`.

On-disk, `~/.dsh/sessions/<project>/<session>/session.jsonl.zstd` contains **stale duplicate rows**: when the `dsh web` process is killed/restarted while writing (or two writers race during a restart), an interrupted rewrite leaves an older segment re-emitted after the cursor already passed it. The row at the gap contains events with `seq < events.length`, so `SessionLogScanner.consumeEventLine` (`packages/session/session-persistence-jsonl/src/format.ts`) sets `issue` and — because the duplicated tail includes `turn/end` rows — throws. The whole session then fails to load every time, even though the committed prefix and the post-duplicate tail are both intact.

Also observed in the same restart pattern: `corrupt Zstandard session log: first frame is not exactly one header line` (torn first frame), which is a separate code path.

### Why this is recoverable

The duplicated rows are byte-identical re-emissions of events the scanner already accepted (their `seq`s are strictly below the cursor). The file is contiguous except for that duplicated region: skipping stale events until the cursor resyncs reconstructs the exact original event stream. Genuine data loss (a *forward* gap, `event.seq > events.length`) is not recoverable this way and should stay fatal.

### Proposed fix (read-side only, ~10 lines)

In `consumeEventLine`, distinguish the two mismatch directions:

```ts
const rowStart = this.events.length
for (const event of decoded) {
  if (event.seq === this.events.length) {
    this.events.push(event)
    continue
  }
  if (event.seq < this.events.length) {
    // Stale duplicate left by an interrupted rewrite: skip it and keep
    // scanning; the cursor resyncs once the duplicated region ends.
    continue
  }
  // A forward gap (events genuinely missing) is unrecoverable.
  const expected = this.events.length
  this.events.length = rowStart
  this.issue = new Error(
    `corrupt session log: seq gap in committed region at line ${this.eventLine} `
    + `(expected ${expected}, got ${event.seq})`,
  )
  if (decoded.some(candidate => candidate.type === 'turn/end')) throw this.issue
  return
}
this.committedBytes = endByte
```

Behavior change: a duplicated `turn/end` tail no longer throws; it is skipped and the read completes with the deduplicated stream. Forward gaps still throw with the original message. Unparsable rows keep their existing semantics.

### Tests

Two cases added to `packages/session/session-persistence-jsonl/tests/jsonl.spec.ts`:

- `skips stale duplicate events left by an interrupted rewrite and resyncs` — duplicates spliced mid-log; expects the original event array and full `committedBytes`.
- `skips a stale duplicated suffix even when it repeats turn end events` — duplicates at the tail including `turn/end`; previously this threw, now it reads cleanly.

End-to-end verified against the real `readPrefix` path with synthetic zstd logs (header frame + event frames), including the exact "duplicate tail with turn/end" shape from the field report, plus a forward-gap control that still fails as expected.

### Standalone patch

A ready-to-apply patch (plus diagnostic/verification scripts) is published here:
https://github.com/zhangyuyao-zx/deepseek-harness-mac/tree/main/session-repair

Happy to adapt it to whatever direction the team prefers (e.g. truncate-at-gap instead of skip-and-resync, or treating the whole post-gap tail as uncommitted).

---

（中文摘要）`dsh web` 进程在写入中被中断/重启时，会话日志会残留重复行，导致 `seq gap in committed region` 报错、历史无法加载。建议在扫描器里把 `seq < 游标` 的过期重复行改为跳过并对齐，真正的前向缺口保持致命错误。附测试用例与可直接应用的补丁。

discussions.title: 要想完美驾驭 V4Pro，热插拔用好了，真是妙不可言！
discussions.body:
全插件框架是真的爽——改一行配置，插件原地换血，那种热插拔的手感一用就回不去了。

**要想完美驾驭 V4Pro，热插拔用好了，真是妙不可言！**

拿 V4Pro 试了试狂暴模式，秒喷上百 token，丝滑到上头，油门直接焊死。可飙得越爽越容易翻车：模型张口"我做完了"，一查，验证没跑、产物没影、边界还踩了。

**框架好不好，编排是否可靠，智能体的跨会话记忆、暴力上下文通识，才是检验标准！**

于是给它配了两件套：

- **[IronLaw](https://github.com/Porphyrioon/ironlaw)** —— 刹车片：执行前拦危险命令，执行后记真实证据，喊 "done" 前先过完成闸门，没凭据不让停。
- **[IronLaw Memory](https://github.com/Porphyrioon/ironlaw)** —— 记忆：Tag+Scope 是个人实战凝练出的最顺手、最丝滑的智能体记忆系统，跨周期、跨会话、跨工具，保守支持多智能体共享记忆，按需取用。

装上之后，**终于敢在插件框架下，放肆激发 V4Pro 的狂暴模式了！** DSH 负责一路狂飙，IronLaw 负责别冲出赛道。

已发布的这几个组件，都是效率工程实践组件之一，后续还有其它组件陆续开源。`dsh-plugin` topic 可搜到，欢迎上手轻喷。

discussions.title: 【实用插件更新】dsh-tool-underseal：授权密封师，多模型无缝协作神器 ｜ hash-sealed authorization for DSH agent delegation
discussions.body:
## 中文

DSH 的 subagent / workflow / goal 把任务授权放进聊天文本——而聊天会被压缩、改写、注入。本插件把授权变成仓库里的哈希密封文件，并从工具管线强制"先验封、再干活"：

- **8 个类型化工具**（`underseal_doctor/pin/seal/start/event/resume/audit/retire`），对冻结的 underseal 协议做 1:1 封装：每个工具经 `ctx.subprocess` 启动 vendored 适配器，要求 `UNDERSEAL_ADAPTER_*` 规范标记，失败抛 `E_*` 稳定错误码。
- **worker 签到锁**：单调的 `ctx.tools.guard()` 在 sealed assignment 产生 READY 证据前拒绝 `write`/`edit`/`pwsh`/`bash`——"先签到再碰文件"是派发路径上的机器规则，不再依赖提示词。
- **供应链哨兵**：vendored 验证器、bundle 补丁、skill 正文三处字节级 hash pin（E1/E2/E3），漂移即 fail-closed，整包拒载也不运行被篡改的字节。
- **第三方可审计**：验证器是单文件、零依赖的 Python；任何人不信任任何 agent，都能从仓库独立重算范围合规（`audit-scope` 对比 Git HEAD 的变更集合与密封范围）。

工程可信度：严格 `tsc` 零错误（对照 checkout 真实类型）；guard/sentinel 单测 54 + 39 断言全过；DSH 0.1.0-rc.5 运行时实测（双层挂载、完整仪式链端到端）。原版 Codex 时代三天生产记录（输入缓存命中率 99.164%，输入/输出 173:1）作为设计动机记录在 README：仪式不再常驻上下文，稳态回合只带 8 个工具 schema（约 1–2K token）加有界结果。

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add dsh-tool-underseal
```

- npm：https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-tool-underseal
- 源码：https://github.com/Hyperionjust/dsh-tool-underseal

欢迎提问题。

---

## English

DSH delegates work through subagent / workflow / goal, but the authority travels as chat text — which can be compacted, rewritten, or injected. This plugin moves the mandate into a hash-sealed file in the workspace, and enforces "verify before touching files" inside the tool pipeline:

- **8 typed tools** (`underseal_doctor/pin/seal/start/event/resume/audit/retire`) wrapping the frozen underseal protocol 1:1 — each spawns the vendored adapter through `ctx.subprocess`, requires the canonical `UNDERSEAL_ADAPTER_*` marker, and throws the stable `E_*` code on failure.
- **Worker check-in lock** — a monotonic `ctx.tools.guard()` denies `write`/`edit`/`pwsh`/`bash` until the sealed assignment has `READY` evidence: a machine rule on the dispatch path, not a prompt.
- **Supply-chain sentinels** — the vendored verifier, bundle patch, and skill body are byte-pinned (E1/E2/E3) and fail closed on drift; the package refuses to load rather than run tampered bytes.
- **Third-party auditability** — the verifier is a single, dependency-free Python file. Anyone, trusting neither agent, can re-derive scope compliance from the repository (`audit-scope` checks the changed-file set against the sealed scope).

Engineering confidence: strict `tsc` exits 0 against the checkout's real types; 54 + 39 guard/sentinel unit assertions pass; runtime smoke on DSH 0.1.0-rc.5 (both layers mount, full ceremony chain end-to-end). A three-day field record from the original Codex-era deployment (99.164% input cache hit rate over 289.5M tokens; 173:1 input/output) is documented in the README as the design motivation: the ceremony no longer rides in context — a steady-state turn carries only the 8 tool schemas (~1–2K tokens) plus bounded results.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add dsh-tool-underseal
```

- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-tool-underseal
- source: https://github.com/Hyperionjust/dsh-tool-underseal

Feedback welcome.

discussions.title: Third-party settings namespaces never appear in plugin-configuration on rc.6 (hardcoded WEB_SETTINGS_NAMESPACES)
discussions.body:
## Third-party settings namespaces never appear in plugin-configuration on rc.6

On `dsh-host-apiproxy` 0.1.0-rc.6 (the current public release), the plugin-configuration page only shows settings namespaces in a **hardcoded allowlist**:

```js
const WEB_SETTINGS_NAMESPACES = [
  "agent-loop", "shell", "locale", "permission",
  "ui-conversation", "ui-theme", "web-search-deepseek"
];
```

`settings.describe` filters registered namespaces by this list, and `settings.update/replace/mutate` reject anything else with `settings-not-exposed` — even when the owning plugin registered the namespace successfully via `installSettingsSection` (dsh-settings).

The source comment acknowledges the gap:

> "a namespace absent here answers `settings-not-exposed` even when its owner registered it ... Moving that declaration to `settings.register()`, so a plugin can expose its own configuration without a change in this package, is deferred work."

### Impact

Third-party plugins written for register-time exposure don't work on the public release. Example: the `@linxin666/dsh-web-ui` family (pet, dsh-ssh, task-board, live-stats, remote-web-ui, skin-background) registers its namespaces correctly, but every settings card renders "nothing while the namespace is unavailable" and writes answer `settings-not-exposed`.

### Repro

1. Install any plugin that calls `installSettingsSection(ctx, settingsNamespace('x'), ...)`.
2. `POST /api/settings.describe` → the namespace is absent.
3. `POST /api/settings.update` on it → `settings-not-exposed`.

### Suggestion

Ship the deferred work: let `settings.register()` / `installSettingsSection` expose the namespace (e.g. an `expose: true` option) so third-party plugins can surface their configuration sections without a `dsh-host-apiproxy` change. A config-level allowlist would be a smaller stopgap for rc.x.

discussions.title: headless 模式希望支持流式输出与结构化事件流（stream-json）
discussions.body:
## 使用场景

我们在自己的产品里把 dsh 作为 agent runtime 之一来调度（headless 模式：`dsh --profile headless <prompt>`），整体接入很顺。但在平台化场景下，目前的 headless 输出形态有几个明显的缺口，希望能讨论一下。

## 希望的能力

### 1. 流式输出

目前 `--profile headless` 模式下 stdout 只在最后一次性给出最终回复全文，执行过程中没有任何输出。对调用方（把 dsh 当执行内核的平台）来说：

- 用户界面在等待期间没有任何反馈，体验上是"卡死"的；
- 无法估算首 token 延迟、生成速度等基础指标。

希望支持逐 token / 逐 chunk 的流式写出（stdout 或指定 fd）。

### 2. 结构化事件流（stream-json 类）

kimi code、claude code 这类 CLI 的 headless 模式都支持 `--output-format stream-json`，以 NDJSON 逐行输出结构化事件（think / tool 调用 / done / error 等）。这对平台方非常关键：

- 可以向最终用户展示 agent 的思考过程和工具调用步骤，而不只是一个转圈等待；
- 错误能以结构化方式识别（目前 dsh 的错误码只能靠匹配 stderr 文本，如 `MISSING_CREDENTIAL`，比较脆弱）。

建议事件格式参考主流形态：`{"type":"token","text":...}` / `{"type":"step","kind":"think|tool",...}` / `{"type":"done","meta":{...}}` / `{"type":"error","code":..., "message":...}`。

### 3. headless 模式支持显式指定模型

目前 headless 模式走内置默认模型配置，命令行没有 `--model` 之类的参数（传了也会被忽略）。平台场景下不同 agent 角色需要绑定不同模型（比如产品经理用旗舰模型、测试用 flash），希望 headless 也能显式指定。

## 小结

优先级上 1 ≈ 2 > 3。如果 stream-json 事件流能覆盖 token 级增量输出，那 1 和 2 其实是一件事。辛苦评估，需要更多调用方视角的细节我可以补充。

discussions.title: 社区展示：ChatGPT 订阅登录 OpenAI Codex，以及 subagent 模型路由继承
discussions.body:
我基于 DeepSeek Harness `master` 实现了两项功能，并将全部代码发布到公开 fork，供社区审阅和复用。项目的[贡献说明](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.zh.md)目前不接受外部 PR（Pull Request），因此这里只作社区成果展示。

## 使用 ChatGPT 订阅登录 OpenAI Codex

提交 [`a47c1ff4d6`](https://github.com/Pygone/deepseek-harness/commit/a47c1ff4d69a9b61c34fcd9c474b90a980933ce3) 为现有 pi-ai 适配器加入 ChatGPT Plus/Pro 订阅登录：

- 新增 `/codex-login [browser|device]` 和 `/codex-logout`；
- 通过 `UserQuestionService` 处理登录方式选择、浏览器回调和设备码交互；
- 将 OAuth 凭据保存在 `$DSH_HOME/.pi-ai-auth.json`：新建目录使用 `0700` 权限，凭据文件使用 `0600` 权限；读取会拒绝符号链接、非普通文件以及所有者之外可读的文件；更新使用原子替换和跨进程文件锁；
- 区分用户取消与提供方结束等待，并隐藏可能包含 OAuth 机密的错误详情；
- 在 Web 对话区提供专用配对卡；不符合专用卡接管条件的请求仍由通用问题界面处理；
- 覆盖协议格式、凭据存储、交互、命令、适配器、Loader 组合、客户端组件和 Web 场景。

![Codex OAuth 真实服务器演示](https://github.com/Pygone/deepseek-harness/blob/showcase-assets/codex-oauth-real.gif?raw=true)

这段 GIF 录自提交 `a47c1ff4d69a9b61c34fcd9c474b90a980933ce3`。录制使用该提交的干净 worktree、重新构建的 Web 产物、单独启动的 `dsh web` 进程，以及彼此隔离的 `DSH_HOME`、`DSH_AGENTS_HOME`、工作区、会话状态和浏览器上下文。录制过程先通过真实 DeepSeek API 完成一次模型调用，再演示浏览器授权等待和取消登录；演示没有完成 OpenAI 授权回调或令牌交换。

## 进程内 subagent 继承父 agent 的最近一次模型路由

提交 [`7e1e183e5a`](https://github.com/Pygone/deepseek-harness/commit/7e1e183e5a325be286b576a1f444d624860e8329) 调整了进程内 subagent 的路由继承规则：

- 子 agent 默认继承父 agent 最近一次写入会话日志的提供方／模型路由；父 agent 尚未发起模型请求时，回退到父 agent 的创建配置；
- 子 agent 显式指定的提供方或模型分别覆盖对应的继承值；
- `maxTokens` 仍独立继承父 agent 的创建配置，不使用适配器在请求期间推导的值；
- 可继续 subagent 在创建时记录解析后的提供方／模型路由；冷恢复继续使用该路由，不受父 agent 后续切换影响。

## 代码

- 展示分支：[`showcase/codex-oauth-and-model-inheritance`](https://github.com/Pygone/deepseek-harness/tree/showcase/codex-oauth-and-model-inheritance)
- 与上游 `master` 的差异：[`deepseek-ai:master...Pygone:showcase/codex-oauth-and-model-inheritance`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/compare/master...Pygone:deepseek-harness:showcase/codex-oauth-and-model-inheritance)

## 审核与验证

我在发布前审核了两个提交，检查范围包括 OAuth 凭据文件的权限与锁、取消语义、错误脱敏、外部链接协议限制，以及 subagent 的路由覆盖、持久化和冷恢复。审核未发现阻塞性问题。

以下验证均在展示分支头部提交 `7e1e183e5a` 上完成：

- OAuth 相关测试：**124 项通过**；
- subagent 单元测试和集成测试：**116 项通过**；
- subagent 组装快照测试：**1 项通过**；
- `pnpm run lint`：通过；
- `pnpm run doc-sync`：**28 项通过**；
- 从干净 worktree 执行项目构建和 Web 构建：通过；
- 通过单独启动的 `dsh web` 服务器调用真实 DeepSeek API：通过。

欢迎大家审阅代码，并讨论这两项功能是否适合 DeepSeek Harness；也想听听大家对后续形态的看法：直接纳入项目、拆成独立插件，还是先提供相应的公共扩展点。

discussions.title: Proposal: add `agent/turn-starting` and `agent/turn-aborting` hooks for turn-boundary observability
discussions.body:
---

## TL;DR

Add two new plugin hooks to the agent loop so other plugins can observe turn boundaries without subscribing to step-level events and reconstructing turn boundaries themselves. No behavior change to existing events, session log shape, or `turnEnds` semantics. Three vitest fixtures demonstrate the new contract.

---

## Background

Today `ReactLoopAgent.turn()` fires one turn-level event — `agent/turn-stopping` — right before a turn ends naturally. There is no symmetric hook at turn *start*, and no hook fired in the abort path.

Plugins that want turn-level visibility today have to subscribe to `step/start`, `step/end`, and reconstruct turn boundaries themselves. This couples plugin code to internal step ordering, which the AGENTS.md warns against ("Plugins, not loop changes").

The two new hooks fill this gap.

## Proposal

### New hooks

| Hook | Type | Payload (declared) | Payload (delivered to listener) | Fires when |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agent/turn-starting` | `serial` | `{ agent: Agent; turn: number; signal: AbortSignal }` | same — `agent` injected by dispatcher | After the first `preStep` claim (which transitions the turn from idle to running) and `phase.turn = turn`, before the first `step/start` log entry — i.e. on the first iteration of the step loop, gated by `target === 'next-turn' && step === 1` |
| `agent/turn-aborting` | `serial` | `{ agent: Agent; turn: number; cause: AgentCancelCause; signal: AbortSignal }` | same — `agent` injected by dispatcher | Inside the catch block when `signal.aborted` is true, immediately before `throw error` |

The `agent` field is declared in the payload type but is auto-injected by the fused dispatcher (`AgentEventDispatch` in `packages/core/agent/src/dispatch.ts`) — mirrors every existing `agent/...` event. This is the convention: declared shape matches delivered shape.

Both hooks use `serial` semantics (mirror the existing `agent/turn-stopping`): plugins observe synchronously, but cannot veto the turn. Plugins that want to "refuse" a turn throw from inside the listener; plugins that want to cancel mid-turn call `agent.cancel(cause)` using the `agent` field injected into the payload.

### Where the hooks fire (in source order)

In `packages/core/agent-loop/src/agent.ts`, the current `turn()` flow becomes:

```
1. phase.kind === 'running' 断言
2. signal.throwIfAborted()
3. turn = phase.turn + 1
4. session.append('turn/start', { turn })          [既有]
5. phase.turn = turn                                [既有]
6. while (true) {
     a. preStep(turn, step)                         [既有 — 同步 claim]
     b. ► if (target === 'next-turn' && step === 1)
          dispatch.serial('agent/turn-starting', ...)  [新增 — fires once per turn]
          signal.throwIfAborted()                      [新增]
     c. step(start)                                 [既有]
     d. ...
   }
7. catch {
     if (signal.aborted) {
       ► dispatch.serial('agent/turn-aborting', ...)  [新增, before throw]
       turnEnds = { kind: 'aborted', reason }
       throw error
     }
     // ... 非 abort 错误路径不变 ...
   }
8. finally { session.append('turn/end', ...) }     [既有]
```

> **Note on placement:** `agent/turn-starting` is fired on the **first iteration** of the step loop (gated by `target === 'next-turn' && step === 1`), not at the literal point between step 5 and 6 above. Rationale: `preStep()` (step 6a) performs a **synchronous** claim of the next proposed step — `agent.followup(...)` and `agent.steer(...)` rely on this synchronous claim semantics to keep their `cancel` / status transitions race-free. Placing the `await dispatch.serial(...)` between step 5 and step 6 would insert an `await` microtask boundary before `preStep.claim()`, which would break two existing tests (`cancel.spec.ts:75` "does not restore work already claimed by a waking send" and `loop.spec.ts:587` "starts idle steering synchronously"). The implementation instead fires the hook after the first `preStep` claim and before the first `step/start` log entry — the **observable semantics are identical** (fires once per natural turn, after `phase.turn = turn`, before any model work).

### Why `serial`, not `waterfall`

`waterfall` lets listeners veto by not calling `next()`. For "veto turn start" this is too strong — a plugin that forgets to call `next()` would silently kill every turn. `serial` is observation-only and matches the existing `agent/turn-stopping` precedent.

Plugin-initiated abort is **not** a feature of these hooks. If a future need appears, it should be a separate `agent/turn-cancel-request` waterfall event with explicit veto semantics.

### Files touched

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `packages/core/agent-loop/src/agent.ts` | Add 2 private methods (`emitTurnStarting`, `emitTurnAborting`); call them at 2 insertion points in `turn()` and 1 insertion point in the catch block. Method shape matches the existing `emit('agent/error', ...)` style. |
| `packages/core/agent/src/runtime-types.ts` | Add 2 entries to the `interface Events` declaration-merge block. JSDoc follows the existing `agent/turn-stopping` template: `@mode serial`, `@param payload.agent`, `@param payload.turn`, `@param payload.signal`, plus the "Scope-filtered dispatch (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope`): agent-scoped listeners receive only that agent." line. |
| `packages/core/scope/src/scoped-events.generated.ts` + `packages/extensions/tool-cordis/src/api-catalog.ts` | Auto-regenerated from `pnpm run gen-scoped-events` and `pnpm run gen-cordis-catalog`. |
| `docs/subsystems/core.md` + `docs/subsystems/core.zh.md` + `docs/subsystems/core.i18n.yaml` + `docs/event-producer-consumer.md` | Auto-regenerated from `pnpm run gen-doc-graphs`. The agent-loop events table and producer/consumer mapping gain two rows. |
| `packages/core/agent-loop/tests/loop.spec.ts` | Append 4 new vitest fixtures (see Test Plan) |

No changes to `preStep`, `step`, `buildRequest`, `tool-calls`, `kick`, `inbox`, or session schema.

### Error handling guarantees

Three throw paths through the new hooks, each with a defined outcome:

1. **Plugin throws inside `agent/turn-starting`** — falls through to the existing error path. `turnEnds = { kind: 'error', error: { message, code: 'UNKNOWN' } }`. `agent/error` fires. `agent/turn-aborting` does *not* fire (not an abort). Session log records the full turn with reason `error`.

2. **Plugin throws inside `agent/turn-aborting`** — caught locally, re-emitted as `agent/error`, *not* rethrown. The original `error` from the catch (the abort) continues to propagate. This is required so a misbehaving listener cannot mask the abort cause.

3. **External abort arrives during `agent/turn-starting`** — the `signal.throwIfAborted()` after the hook throws. catch enters the aborted branch. `agent/turn-aborting` fires with the abort cause (this is the intended "abort lifecycle closes" path).

The code shape for path 2:

```typescript
} catch (error: unknown) {
  if (signal.aborted) {
    try {
      await this.dispatch.serial('agent/turn-aborting', {
        turn, cause: signal.reason as AgentCancelCause, signal,
      })
    } catch (listenerError) {
      this.dispatch.emit('agent/error', {
        turn, step: phase.step, error: listenerError,
      })
    }
    turnEnds = { kind: 'aborted', reason: signal.reason as AgentCancelCause }
    throw error
  }
  // ...
}
```

## Behavior guarantees

What stays the same:

- Every existing event still fires at the same point with the same payload.
- Session log shape unchanged.
- `turnEnds` sticky max-tokens semantics unchanged.
- `kick()` loop termination unchanged.
- Public `cancel()` API unchanged.

What's new:

- Two new event keys in the dispatch map; subscribers via `ctx.on('agent/turn-starting', ...)` / `ctx.on('agent/turn-aborting', ...)` get type-complete payloads after the declaration-merge update.
- Plugins listening to these hooks must be tolerant of being called once per turn.

## Test plan

Three vitest fixtures appended to `packages/core/agent-loop/tests/loop.spec.ts`. Each follows the existing `harness()` + `MockAdapter` + `ctx.on('agent/status')` pattern.

### Fixture 1 — `turn-starting` fires exactly once per natural turn

Setup: a `MockAdapter` returning one text response. A listener subscribes to `agent/turn-starting` and records `turn` numbers. Send one message, wait for idle.

Asserts:
- Listener was called exactly once, with `turn === 1`.
- Adapter received exactly one model request.
- Final `turn/end` event has `reason.kind === 'completed'`.

Proves: hook position is correct (between `turn/start` and first step); one fire per turn (not per step).

### Fixture 2 — `turn-aborting` carries the cancel cause before rethrow

Setup: a `MockAdapter` that returns the `'hang'` marker (a response the adapter never resolves — lets the turn enter its first step and park there). Listener subscribes to `agent/turn-aborting` and records `cause`. Send a message, yield ~30 ms so the turn reaches its first step and `agent.status` is `running`, then call `agent.cancel({ kind: 'user' })`. Wait for idle.

Asserts:
- Listener was called exactly once, with `cause === { kind: 'user' }`.
- Final `turn/end` event has `reason.kind === 'aborted'`.

Proves: external cancel → abort signal → catch aborted branch → hook fires before throw → cause preserved through session log.

### Fixture 3 — Plugin throw in `turn-starting` routes to error path

Setup: a `MockAdapter` with zero responses. A listener on `agent/turn-starting` throws `new Error('plugin refuses to start turn')`. A listener on `agent/error` records errors. Send a message, wait for idle.

Asserts:
- Adapter received zero model requests (turn didn't reach step).
- Final `turn/end` event has `reason.kind === 'error'`.
- `agent/error` fired exactly once.

Proves: the "veto turn start" capability plugins actually have — throw from the listener — produces a clean error path with full session log + error event, instead of silently dropping the turn.

### Fixture 4 — Plugin throw in `turn-aborting` is caught and re-emitted as `agent/error`

Setup: same `'hang'` adapter + 30 ms status guard as Fixture 2. A listener on `agent/turn-aborting` throws a sentinel error after recording the cause. A listener on `agent/error` captures the captured error.

Asserts:
- Listener was called with `cause === { kind: 'user' }` before throwing.
- Exactly one `agent/error` event was emitted, carrying the sentinel error (proves the catch in `emitTurnAborting` re-routes the throw).
- Final `turn/end` event has `reason.kind === 'aborted'` (NOT `error` — proves the listener's throw did not corrupt the turn-end or replace the original abort cause).

Proves: path 2 of the error-handling guarantees — a misbehaving `turn-aborting` listener cannot mask the abort or downgrade the turn-end reason.

## Open questions for the maintainers

1. **Naming**: `agent/turn-starting` vs `agent/turn-begin` / `agent/turn-open` — happy to follow whatever convention is preferred. The `agent/...` prefix mirrors `agent/pre-step` and `agent/turn-stopping`.

2. **Payload for `turn-aborting`**: should `cause` be the raw `signal.reason` (typed as `AgentCancelCause`) or wrapped in `{ kind, ... }`? Currently proposed as the raw `AgentCancelCause` value, matching how the agent's own `cancel()` method accepts it.

3. **Documentation entry**: `docs/architecture.md` is the proposed home. If there's a more specific "agent-loop events" catalog file, that's where it should land.

## What this proposal does NOT include

- Plugin-initiated abort from inside these hooks (deferred — needs a separate `agent/turn-cancel-request` waterfall if ever).
- Turn-level telemetry emission (separate proposal if needed).
- Refactoring of the existing `turnEnds!` non-null assertion or step/turn-end finally block (orthogonal, not touched).

## Working fork

A reference implementation lives on the branch [`feat/agent-turn-starting-aborting-hooks`](https://github.com/liuyang0508/deepseek-harness/tree/feat/agent-turn-starting-aborting-hooks) of the fork [`liuyang0508/deepseek-harness`](https://github.com/liuyang0508/deepseek-harness). Five functional commits land the proposal end-to-end (plus a marker commit `9864594` that bootstraps the branch from `master`):

| Commit | Subject |
|---|---|
| `ad09941` | feat(agent): declare `agent/turn-starting` and `agent/turn-aborting` events |
| `0231384` | chore(gen): regenerate `scoped-events` and `cordis` catalog |
| `90bded1` | test(agent-loop): cover `agent/turn-starting` and `agent/turn-aborting` hooks |
| `2954b4f` | feat(agent-loop): fire `agent/turn-starting` and `agent/turn-aborting` hooks |
| `3d35452` | test(agent-loop): cover `turn-aborting` listener throw → `agent/error` route |

Diff against `master`: [compare view](https://github.com/liuyang0508/deepseek-harness/compare/master...feat/agent-turn-starting-aborting-hooks) (10 files changed).

**Local checks** on the branch:
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/core/agent-loop` — 333 tests pass, including 4 new fixtures (`fires agent/turn-starting exactly once per turn in a natural completion`, `fires agent/turn-aborting with the abort cause before rethrow`, `records a turn-end with reason=error when a turn-starting listener throws`, `routes a turn-aborting listener throw through agent/error without corrupting turn-end`).
- `pnpm typecheck` — exit 0
- `pnpm lint` — exit 0
- `pnpm run gen-doc-graphs verify-doc-graphs` — exit 0 (declare-and-dispatch atomicity preserved)
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/core/agent-loop --coverage --coverage.include='packages/core/agent-loop/src/**/*.{ts,tsx}'` — `agent.ts` line coverage 100%, function coverage 100% for the new helpers. (The remaining uncovered line at `agent.ts:143` is in `runMaintenance`, pre-existing code not touched by this change.)
