discussions.title: Long session history fails when sourceEventSeqs exceeds the V8 argument limit
discussions.body:
## Problem

Opening a long persisted session can fail with:

```text
Failed to load history: history unavailable for session "…": RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded (internal)
```

The observed session contains an appended `assistant/message` with 133,679 `sourceEventSeqs`. `paginate()` computes the message-group boundary with `Math.min(event.seq, ...sources)`, so V8 turns every source id into a call argument and exceeds its argument/stack limit. The session log itself remains readable; only API-proxy pagination fails.

## Expected

`session.history` should load long streamed messages without depending on the JavaScript engine's maximum argument count.

## Proposed fix

Scan `sourceEventSeqs` iteratively to preserve the same minimum and add an API-proxy regression test with the observed list size. The focused history tests and the real affected session both pass with this change.

discussions.title: 分享：給 DeepSeek Harness 的 deepseek娘桌寵外掛（16 方向追視）
discussions.body:
# 分享：給 DeepSeek Harness 的 deepseek娘桌寵外掛（16 方向追視）

大家好，我把原本的 Codex v2 桌寵改造成可直接安裝到 DeepSeek Harness Web UI 的 Cordis 外掛了。

她會待在介面右下角，依照目前 Session 狀態切換動畫，也會用 16 個方向跟著滑鼠看。

> 實際在 DeepSeek Harness 中使用的畫面：
>
> ![deepseek娘在 DeepSeek Harness 中待機、追視與放大](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/f0909172434/dsh-deepseek-girl-pet/main/assets/deepseek-girl-harness-demo.gif)

> 這是社群製作的非官方外掛，不會修改 Session 資料、對話記錄或 DeepSeek Harness 核心原始碼。

## 功能

- 使用 Harness 原生 Cordis 外掛與 `shell.overlay` 擴充槽
- 待機時拿著簡體「区」的板子，對話框文字維持「凶」
- Harness 執行任務時切換至工作動畫
- Session 等待互動時切換至等待動畫
- 完整 16 方向滑鼠追視，每 22.5 度一格
- 滑鼠停止 1.1 秒後回到拿板子的待機動畫
- 點擊桌寵可在一般與放大尺寸間切換
- 支援 `prefers-reduced-motion`

## 安裝

Windows PowerShell：

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add github:f0909172434/dsh-deepseek-girl-pet
# 先在原本執行 dsh web 的視窗按 Ctrl+C，確認 3080 已停止，再執行：
dsh web
```

如果看到 `EADDRINUSE: address already in use 127.0.0.1:3080`，代表舊的 Harness 還在執行，不是安裝失敗。先停止舊程序再重啟，最後在瀏覽器按 `Ctrl+F5`。

安裝時的 `Issues with peer dependencies found` 是 profile 內其他外掛的 peer dependency 警告；後面顯示 `Done` 代表桌寵套件已完成安裝。

然後開啟 [http://127.0.0.1:3080/](http://127.0.0.1:3080/)。

## 狀態映射

| Harness 狀態 | 桌寵表現 |
|---|---|
| Idle | 拿著「区」板子待機，對話框顯示「凶」 |
| Running | 工作動畫 |
| Pending interaction | 等待互動動畫 |
| Pointer movement | 16 方向追視 |

外掛直接讀取 Harness 的 Session summary state，不會用 DOM 文字掃描猜測狀態。

## 技術方式

- Host plugin 只在 `/deepseek-girl-pet/spritesheet.webp` 提供固定 WebP 圖集
- Client plugin 只註冊 `shell.overlay` slot
- 不修改 DeepSeek Harness 核心檔案
- 不讀取或寫入對話內容
- 不依賴外部 CDN 或追蹤服務

## 驗證

- `node --check lib/index.js`：PASS
- `node --check lib/client.js`：PASS
- Hatch Pet deterministic v2 atlas validation：PASS
- DeepSeek Harness 首頁、client module 與 spritesheet route：HTTP 200

## 專案

GitHub：[f0909172434/dsh-deepseek-girl-pet](https://github.com/f0909172434/dsh-deepseek-girl-pet)

MIT License。歡迎試用、提出建議，或分享你想看到的互動動畫。

discussions.title: Feature request: Desktop GUI client (Tauri/Electron) alongside the browser Web UI
discussions.body:
## Summary

Provide an optional native desktop GUI client (Tauri or Electron shell) for DeepSeek Harness, so users can run the Web UI in a native window instead of a browser tab, with system tray, auto-start, global shortcuts, and desktop notifications.

## Background

I currently run `dsh web` and keep the browser tab open at http://127.0.0.1:3080. A desktop shell would give a Codex-Desktop-like experience: native window, tray residency, notifications, and better background session management (closing the window should not kill agent sessions).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A command such as `dsh desktop` (or equivalent) launches a native window loading the existing Web UI, without manually opening a browser
2. Closing the window minimizes to system tray; agent sessions keep running in the background
3. Desktop notifications on task completion or when approval is needed
4. All existing Web UI capabilities preserved: agent presets (Standard / PTC / Minimal / Creator), goals, subagents, workflows
5. Works on Windows at minimum; Linux/macOS as stretch

## User-visible change

- Native window + tray residency + notifications instead of a browser tab
- No need to remember the localhost URL
- More natural background session management

## Test evidence (proposed)

- Verify Tauri/Electron shell loads the Web UI on Windows, tray and notifications work
- Regression test that existing Web UI features are unaffected

(Submitted on behalf of a user who prefers desktop GUI over browser Web UI.)

discussions.title: [Bug] 后台服务停止响应后，页面永久显示“运行中”，且无法停止、发送消息或提交反馈
discussions.body:
你好，我在使用 DeepSeek Harness Developer Preview 时遇到了一个严重的卡死与恢复问题。

任务长时间运行后，后台服务似乎停止了响应，但原浏览器页面仍然把任务显示为“进行中”。同时，停止、发送消息和反馈功能均无法使用。

相关过程有录屏记录，但为了避免泄露账户、会话和项目内容，暂不公开上传原始录屏。如维护者确有需要，我可以另行提供经过脱敏处理的片段。

## 问题现象

任务运行较长时间后：

1. 任务长时间不再推进，但页面仍显示“进行中”。
2. Stop / 停止操作没有生效。
3. 输入框右侧按钮一直保持运行状态，没有恢复成发送按钮。
4. 无法发送新消息。
5. 无法发送 `/feedback` 命令。
6. Session log / Feedback 导出没有成功。
7. 无法要求 Agent 保存进度、生成 checkpoint 或总结当前状态。

最终形成以下状态：

任务不再推进  
→ 无法停止  
→ 无法发送消息  
→ 无法使用 `/feedback`  
→ 无法导出日志  
→ 无法在退出前建立恢复点

## 新标签页无法访问，但旧页面仍显示“运行中”

任务卡住后，我在同一个浏览器中新开标签页，再次访问 Harness 的默认本地地址。

新标签页显示：

- 无法访问此网站
- 本地地址拒绝连接
- `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`

检查时，Harness 的默认本地服务已经没有进程监听，系统进程中也没有发现仍在运行的 Harness/Node 服务。

但是，原来的 Harness 标签页仍保留完整界面，并继续显示：

- 会话仍为“进行中”
- 后台任务仍为运行状态
- Stop 操作无效
- 输入框无法发送消息

因此，现场状态表现为：

后台服务已经停止监听  
→ 新标签页返回 `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`  
→ 旧页面没有显示连接已经断开  
→ 旧页面继续显示任务“运行中”  
→ 用户无法确认任务是否仍在工作，也不知道能否安全退出

我无法确认后台服务停止监听的具体原因，因此不对根因作判断。

## 恢复状态不透明

任务已经运行了较长时间，但界面没有说明哪些内容已经持久化，以及关闭或重新启动后可能丢失什么。

当时无法确认：

- 当前聊天内容是否已经保存
- 已完成的工具调用是否已经保存
- Agent 已修改的文件是否安全
- 当前任务是否存在 checkpoint
- 重启后能否恢复原会话
- 未闭合的 Running 状态会如何处理

## 期望行为

希望在后台服务断开、崩溃或停止监听时：

1. 旧页面明确显示“与 Harness 服务的连接已断开”，而不是永久显示 Running。
2. Stop / Cancel 给出明确的成功、失败或超时结果。
3. 输入框能够解除锁定，或提供独立于当前任务的反馈入口。
4. `/feedback` 和 Session log 导出不依赖当前会话继续正常运行。
5. 提供紧急恢复入口，例如：
   - 解除错误的前端 Running 状态
   - 保存或导出当前会话快照
   - 导出本地诊断日志
   - 显示最后成功持久化的时间
   - 重启后处理未闭合的 turn
6. 在关闭或重启前，明确说明哪些数据已经保存、哪些可能丢失。

## 运行环境

- 设备：Apple Silicon Mac
- CPU 架构：arm64
- 操作系统：macOS 15.7.1
- 系统 Build：24G231
- Harness npm 包：`@deepseek-ai/dsh`
- Harness 版本：`0.1.0-rc.6`
- Git commit：无法确认；npm 包未包含 `gitHead`
- 启动方式：`npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web`
- Node.js：v24.19.0
- npm：11.17.0
- 浏览器：Google Chrome 151.0.7922.109

## 隐私说明

为保护隐私，本报告没有公开：

- 本机用户名及个人目录
- 工作区名称和项目内容
- 会话名称、提示词及对话内容
- Session ID
- API Key、Token、Cookie 或账户信息
- 原始日志和未经脱敏的录屏

如维护者需要进一步诊断信息，请明确说明所需字段及脱敏要求。

discussions.title: 提议：让 userQuestions 支持可降级的 diff 预览
discussions.body:
我在看插件的人机交互能力时，发现现在的 `ctx.userQuestions` 很适合“问一个问题、选一个答案”，但不太适合“先看清楚变更，再决定是否继续”。

当前文档已经把这个边界写得很清楚：目前只有选项和自定义文本，文件选择器、diff 预览确认还没有统一的交互类型。现有的 `plan-review` 说明 presentation intent 这条路已经存在。

一个实际例子：插件准备应用一组补丁、配置迁移或部署变更时，希望用户先看到受影响文件和 diff，再点“应用”或“取消”。现在只能把内容压成 Markdown，或者由插件自己做一套 RPC 和 UI；后者会让每个插件都发明自己的交互协议。

我建议先做一个很小的扩展，不做万能表单：

- 在现有 `AskUserQuestionIntent` 上增加一种 `diff-review` intent；具体 diff 数据复用哪种现有类型，可以在实现评审时再定
- `question`、`options` 和回答格式保持不变
- 支持它的 Web provider 显示 diff；不认识它的 provider 继续显示 `detail + options`
- `user-approval` 仍只负责权限和安全审批，不把普通业务确认混进去
- 第一版只做 `diff-review`，文件选择器等以后有真实用例再加

这样 TUI、headless 和第三方 provider 不需要同时升级，也能给后续插件一个公共的人机交互入口。

相关位置：

- [`user-questions` 的已知限制](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/packages/interaction/user-questions/README.md#known-limitations-and-deferred-work)
- [`AskUserQuestionIntent` 当前定义](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/packages/interaction/user-questions/src/types.ts#L16-L32)

维护者是否认可这个方向：把 Rich Interaction 作为现有 `userQuestions` 的 presentation intent 扩展，先只落一个可降级的 `diff-review`，而不是新增通用表单服务？如果方向合适，我可以继续补 Agent Note、最小实现和回归测试。

discussions.title: [Bug] 创建不存在目录的工作区报 workspace-invalid-path ENOENT，未自动建目录且无明确提示
discussions.body:
创建/打开指向不存在目录的工作区报 `workspace-invalid-path ... ENOENT`，而不是自动建目录或提示目录不存在。

<details>
<summary>复现、预期与验收</summary>

- **复现步骤：**
  1. 在 dsh Web GUI 中创建/打开一个工作区，路径指向一个**不存在的目录**（父目录存在即可），例如 `C:\Users\22758\orca\workspaces\agent`
  2. 触发创建
  3. 报错如下

- **实际结果：**
  ```
  workspace create failed: workspace-invalid-path: cannot create a workspace at "C:\Users\22758\orca\workspaces\agent": ENOENT: no such file or directory, realpath 'C:\Users\22758\orca\workspaces\agent'
  ```
  用户无法从错误中得知「需要先手动创建该目录」——错误看起来像内部故障，实际是目标目录不存在。

- **预期结果：**
  - 方案 A（推荐）：`create` 时对不存在的路径执行递归 `mkdir` 后再注册工作区（GUI 里用户期望"新建工作区"就是建目录）；
  - 方案 B：至少把错误改为明确指引，如「目录不存在，请先创建目录」，并让 GUI 直接展示该提示。

- **环境：**
  - dsh `0.1.0-rc.6`（npm `@deepseek-ai/dsh`）
  - `@deepseek-ai/dsh-workspace` `0.1.0-rc.6`
  - Node `v22.23.2`
  - Windows 11（10.0.26200），dsh Web GUI

- **原因分析（供参考）：**
  `dsh-workspace` 的 `WorkspaceRegistry.create()` 先调用 `realpathNormalize(path)`（`lib/types/paths.js`），目录不存在时 `fs.realpath` 抛原始 `ENOENT` 并被上抛。`paths.js` 注释明确说明这是 `create` 的 reject 路径（"a workspace must point at an existing directory"），但该设计约束没有转化为用户可理解的错误信息，RPC 层只把它包成 `workspace-invalid-path`。

- **验收条件：**
  对不存在的目录执行 `create workspace` 时满足以下之一：
  1. 自动创建目录并成功注册工作区；或
  2. 返回明确的「目录不存在，请先创建目录」类错误信息，且 GUI 能直接展示。

</details>

discussions.title: [bug]标题:浏览器端 crypto.randomUUID() 在局域网 HTTP 访问下崩溃(非安全上下文),页面无法使用
discussions.body:
标题:浏览器端 crypto.randomUUID() 在局域网 HTTP 访问下崩溃(非安全上下文),页面无法使用

版本:@deepseek-ai/dsh 0.1.0-rc.6(web profile)

问题描述: 通过配置把 webserver 绑定到 0.0.0.0 后,手机等局域网设备用 http://<LAN-IP>:3080 访问 Web GUI,页面加载即报错 crypto.randomUUID is not a function,界面无法使用。

复现步骤:

在 ~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml 中把 webserver 绑定到 0.0.0.0(webserver schema 允许该值,且 dsh-web-app 会自动将本机 LAN IP 加入 /api 信任栅栏并打印 LAN URL,说明局域网访问是官方支持的部署方式)
手机浏览器打开 
http://192.168.x.x:3080/
(明文 HTTP,非 loopback)
页面加载即抛 crypto.randomUUID is not a function
根因分析: crypto.randomUUID() 是安全上下文(secure context)专属 Web API,仅在 HTTPS 或 localhost 下存在;通过明文 HTTP 访问局域网 IP 不属于安全上下文,该 API 为 undefined。相关调用点:

dsh-client-connection/lib/client.js — mintRpcId() 每条 C→S RPC 都调用 crypto.randomUUID(),页面一加载就崩
dsh-host-apiproxy/lib/types/fetch/client.js — 同上的 mintRpcId()
dsh-client-ui-conversation/lib/client.js — browserDraftAttachment() 附件草稿 ID
对比:node 端(dsh-client-connection/lib/index.js)使用 node:crypto 的 randomUUID,不受影响;CLI 拒绝 --host 0.0.0.0(dsh-web-app/lib/startup.js,安全考虑,可以理解),但配置 patch 路径是官方留出的合法通道,因此该场景应被支持。

期望行为: 局域网 HTTP 访问时浏览器端正常生成 UUID,或给出明确的不支持提示。

建议修复: crypto.getRandomValues() 在非安全上下文可用,建议在 client 端为 crypto.randomUUID 提供基于 getRandomValues 的 UUID v4 fallback(例如 if (!crypto.randomUUID) { … }),或统一封装一个 UUID 工具函数,替换三处裸调用。

临时规避(供其他用户参考): 在 dsh-web-frontend/dist/index.html 的 <head> 中、模块脚本之前注入同步 polyfill(用 crypto.getRandomValues 实现 UUID v4),可解决;升级后需重新应用。

discussions.title: Show and tell: AI-maintained one-click Dev Actions for DSH Web
discussions.body:
I built **dsh-dev-actions**, a companion plugin for `dsh-better-sidebar` that targets a small human-in-the-loop friction point: repeated development operations.

While the model works, it can proactively turn a reusable shell command, acceptance prompt, or recurring AI instruction into a visible sidebar action. The model maintains and deduplicates the entries; creating an entry never executes or sends it. The user still sees the exact content and explicitly clicks Run, Send, or Insert.

Examples include remembering a Flutter device launch command, restarting a dev server, repeating an authentication acceptance pass, or inserting a project habit such as “reproduce first; do not treat build success as acceptance.”

The plugin uses DSH system-prompt sections, fixed model tools, storage-domain persistence, Session-scoped workspace authority, managed Shell execution, sandbox policy, and Better Sidebar tabs. A real browser E2E covers model upsert -> panel -> user click -> process output.

Repository, screenshot, public Release install, and contribution tasks:
https://github.com/skitse/dsh-dev-actions

Install prerequisites and plugin:

```sh
npm install --global @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.0-rc.6 pnpm@10.32.1

dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-better-sidebar@^0.10.3 \
  https://github.com/skitse/dsh-dev-actions/releases/latest/download/dsh-dev-actions.tgz
```

I would especially welcome feedback on a small interop contract that lets other DSH plugins contribute fixed executor actions without importing across bundles.

discussions.title: [Plugin] Editable, session-isolated memory governance
discussions.body:
I built a tree-out community plugin that adds editable, session-isolated personalization memory to DeepSeek Harness without patching Harness source.

Repository: https://github.com/Spirtxiaoqi7/mindspace-dsh-session-memory
Release: https://github.com/Spirtxiaoqi7/mindspace-dsh-session-memory/releases/tag/v0.1.0
Topics: `dsh-plugin`, `memory`, `agent-memory`, `session-memory`

## What it contributes

- Direct preview of the current DSH compaction summary, plus an optional user override.
- Editable preferences, user facts, and instructions for the assistant.
- Per-session relationship identity, conversation mission, and optional roleplay preset.
- Model-facing `get_session_memory` and `update_session_memory` tools.
- Conservative extraction from explicit user statements only.
- Conflict replacement by stable item id with append-only session-event history.
- One optional role/purpose/style question on the first empty turn.

## Composition

The installable package declares one `dsh.bundle` layer and one dual-face package-root row. The Host face owns the event-sourced service, projection, prompt contribution, tools, extraction hook, and generated Typert descriptor. The Web face self-mounts its generated Remote contribution and registers a Personalization / Memory Center settings section. It does not modify `api-remotes`, built-in bundles, root tsconfigs, or other Harness packages.

## Verification

- Fresh-clone `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, build, tests, and pack pass on Node 24.
- GitHub CI passes with the same sequence.
- The release tarball installs into an isolated profile.
- The package root and Typert artifact import from the installed profile.
- An isolated Web profile starts on an alternate port; `/` and the plugin client bundle both return 200.
- Downloaded release asset SHA-256 matches the locally accepted tarball: `a9954200e2ca0fa0096058d1de27bfc6053189d98a528987de377ebd0c2aa084`.

The initial compatibility target is the public `0.1.0-rc` family. Feedback is especially welcome on long-term stable seams for tree-out Typert contributions, client Remote self-mounting, and session-event namespace governance.

discussions.title: [Bug] Session 关闭时可能把 projection cache 回退到旧 checkpoint
discussions.body:
我在检查 `session-projection-cache` 的 detach 写入时复现到一个顺序问题：较新的 detach checkpoint 已经落盘后，较早启动的 count-threshold checkpoint 还能把它覆盖回旧状态。

最小回归里把 `writeEveryEvents` 设为 2，只是为了稳定触发同一条官方计数写入路径：

1. 连续追加 `seed`、`old`，达到事件阈值后开始 checkpoint A；A 已截取 `old`，随后等待 Session persistence flush。
2. 等待期间再追加 `new`，然后正常 dispose Session owner。
3. `session/disposed` 触发 detach checkpoint B，先把 `new` 落盘。
4. A 的 persistence flush 随后完成，A 又把先前截取的 `old` 写入同一个 cache record。

最终结果是：

```text
Expected: { marks: ["new"] }
Received: { marks: ["old"] }
```

测试使用官方 `SessionPersistence` / `PersistenceCoordinator`。为了确定性复现，我让测试 backend 的第一个 `appendBatch` 在返回前等待一个 gate，相当于模拟一次合法但较慢的持久化写入；backend 契约只要求返回时已经 durable，并没有最大完成时限。测试没有额外添加 `session/flush` listener，也没有 mock 或直接调用 cache 的 `write()` / `put()`。

定向测试连续两次稳定失败。完整运行 `cache.spec.ts` 时，18 个既有用例通过，只有这个新增回归失败。

<details>
<summary>测试命令与输出摘要</summary>

```powershell
.\node_modules\.bin\vitest.cmd run packages/session/session-projection-cache/tests/cache.spec.ts -t "does not let an earlier real persistence barrier overwrite the detach checkpoint"
```

```text
FAIL  packages/session/session-projection-cache/tests/cache.spec.ts
SessionProjectionCache write policy
× does not let an earlier real persistence barrier overwrite the detach checkpoint

AssertionError: expected { marks: [ 'old' ] } to deeply equal { marks: [ 'new' ] }

Expected: { marks: ["new"] }
Received: { marks: ["old"] }
```

完整文件：

```powershell
.\node_modules\.bin\vitest.cmd run packages/session/session-projection-cache/tests/cache.spec.ts
```

```text
Test Files  1 failed (1)
Tests       1 failed | 18 passed (19)
```

`git diff --check` 通过。复现用例目前只保留在本地，尚未提交。

</details>

从当前 `master`（`47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a`）看，`write()` 是先截取 checkpoint，再等待 `sessions.flush(session)`，最后无条件 `put()`。detach 时 Session 已不在 live store，会跳过这次 flush，因此较新的 B 可以先提交，随后被较旧的 A 覆盖。

Session log 本身仍然正确，但 projection cache 的 watermark 和内容会倒退，后续 cold read 或列表读取可能先拿到旧投影。

这是一条受控的包级竞态回归，不是我已经在 Web UI 中自然撞到的 E2E 现象。Web 默认组合里 Session JSONL 与 `session_projcache.json` 是两次独立的持久化操作，所以该顺序与实际实现相容；目前没有测实际使用中的触发概率。

提交前我按 `projection cache`、`session projection`、`session_projcache`、`stateVersion`、`checkpoint watermark` 等关键词检索了最近 100 条 Discussions，没有找到同类报告。

想确认一下，这里的 checkpoint 写入是否应该按 Session 保序，至少不允许较低 watermark 覆盖较高 watermark？如果判断是 Bug，我可以把最小回归测试整理成 PR。

discussions.title: [Plugin / 插件] dsh-codex — ChatGPT OAuth, Codex search, and image input / ChatGPT 登录、搜索与图片输入
discussions.body:
## 中文

大家好，我做了一个独立的 dsh 插件 [`dsh-codex`](https://github.com/Yan-Zero/dsh-codex)，可以通过 ChatGPT OAuth 登录，在 DeepSeek Harness 里使用账号可用的 Codex 模型。

我平时主要在 Web profile 里用 dsh，所以把登录、额度和图片都接进了现有界面。目前包里有这些功能：

- 在 **设置 → OpenAI Codex** 里完成浏览器登录，也支持 CLI 和 device code；
- 自动刷新 token，凭据单独保存在 `$DSH_HOME/.openai-codex-auth.json`；
- Codex 模型目录、流式输出、工具调用、推理回放、prompt caching 和 dsh compaction；
- 复用 dsh 的 `web_search` 工具访问 Codex 独立搜索，并保留普通文本与引用历史；
- 在 Web 输入框粘贴或拖放图片；`view_image` 也能读取本地路径和 HTTP(S) 图片；
- 设置页显示 Codex 额度进度条和剩余百分比。

安装：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-codex
dsh web
```

启动后打开 **设置 → OpenAI Codex → 使用 ChatGPT 登录**。无界面环境可以运行：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web exec dsh-openai-codex login --device-code
```

插件使用 ChatGPT Codex 后端。模型权限、额度和可用性由 OpenAI 账号与套餐决定；它不会生成通用 OpenAI API Key。dsh 的 shell、文件系统、skills、MCP、subagents 和权限系统仍由当前 profile 提供。

- 源码与文档：https://github.com/Yan-Zero/dsh-codex
- npm：https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-codex
- 当前版本：`0.2.1`，依赖与测试环境对齐 dsh `0.1.0-rc.6`
- License：Apache-2.0

如果你愿意试一下，我很想了解浏览器回调、headless 登录、图片附件和搜索记录在不同环境里的表现。协议和凭据生命周期也写在仓库的 design 文档里，欢迎直接提 issue。

---

## English

Hi! I’ve been working on an independent dsh plugin called [`dsh-codex`](https://github.com/Yan-Zero/dsh-codex). It signs in through ChatGPT OAuth and makes the Codex models available to a DeepSeek Harness profile.

I use dsh mostly through the Web profile, so the package covers the account flow and a few everyday Codex features in the existing UI:

- browser sign-in from **Settings → OpenAI Codex**, plus CLI and device-code flows;
- automatic token refresh, with a separate credential store at `$DSH_HOME/.openai-codex-auth.json`;
- the Codex model catalog, streaming, tool calls, reasoning replay, prompt caching, and dsh compaction;
- Codex standalone search through dsh’s existing `web_search` tool, with regular text and citation history;
- image paste/drop in the Web composer, plus a `view_image` tool for local paths and HTTP(S) URLs;
- live Codex quota bars and exact remaining percentages in Settings.

Install it into a Web profile:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-codex
dsh web
```

Then open **Settings → OpenAI Codex → Sign in with ChatGPT**. For a headless machine:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web exec dsh-openai-codex login --device-code
```

The plugin talks to the ChatGPT Codex backend. Model access, quotas, and eligibility follow the OpenAI account and plan; this does not create a general OpenAI API key. Shell, filesystem, skills, MCP, subagents, and permissions continue to come from the active dsh profile.

- Source and docs: https://github.com/Yan-Zero/dsh-codex
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-codex
- Current release: `0.2.1`, aligned and tested with dsh `0.1.0-rc.6`
- License: Apache-2.0

I’d especially appreciate field reports on the browser callback, headless login, image attachments, and search history across compaction. Protocol and credential-lifecycle notes are in the repository’s design document; issues are welcome.

discussions.title: Workspace instructions (AGENTS.md) from parent/shared repo are never injected in the web app; home patch cannot configure the per-session plugin
discussions.body:
Environment

    DSH version: 0.1.0-rc.6 (both @deepseek-ai/dsh and @deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app)
    Mode: dsh web (web profile, bundles @deepseek-ai/dsh-base + @deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app)
    OS: Windows
    Agent preset: code (default)
    Plugin: @deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-instructions

Summary

In the web app, the workspace-instruction baseline only ever includes AGENTS.md files from the innermost project root down to the session cwd. When repos are nested (e.g. GitHub/ is a repo containing GitHub/Harness/ as another repo), the shared AGENTS.md at the parent repo root is never discovered, because project-root discovery stops at the first directory containing a .git marker walking up from the cwd.

Additionally, the documented configuration seam for this plugin — the home-level patch $DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml — is inert in the web app: the host-plane agent-instructions row is disabled by the web-app bundle, and the instance that actually composes session baselines is mounted per-session from the agent preset, which the home patch cannot reach.
Expected behavior

A session whose cwd is C:\Users\manue\Documents\GitHub\Harness should receive a baseline containing both GitHub/AGENTS.md (shared rules) and Harness/AGENTS.md (repo-local rules), since both are ancestors of the cwd.
Actual behavior

The baseline contains only Harness/AGENTS.md. The session log shows a single Instructions from: AGENTS.md section with no budget-omission notice, confirming the parent file was never discovered (not merely truncated).
Root cause

    Per-session plugin instance lives in the agent preset, not the host.
        @deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app/cordis.patch.yml disables the host row: - id: agent-instructions / disabled: true (same as other agent-plane rows like tool-subagent, tool-workflow).
        Each agent preset (config/agent-presets/*/agent.cordis.yml) mounts its own agent-instructions row with only maxBytes: 65536, so projectRootMarkers falls back to the default ['.git'].
        $DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml patches only the host composition, so configuring the preset's row from the home patch is impossible. The plugin inventory confirms two rows: include:agent-instructions (host, Disabled) and include:agent-presets:agent-instructions (preset, Mounted/Enabled).

    Project-root discovery stops at the innermost marker.
        findProjectRoot(cwd, markers) walks up from the cwd and returns the first directory containing a marker (default .git). With cwd = GitHub/Harness, the walk returns GitHub/Harness (it has .git), so ancestorChain(projectRoot, cwd) never includes GitHub/, and GitHub/AGENTS.md is never loaded.

    Budget silently drops the broader file (secondary).
        Even with discovery fixed, the default maxBytes: 65536 is smaller than the shared file (68,104 bytes in our case; both files render at 72,035 bytes), and the renderer drops whole broader files before truncating the most-specific one. The budget notice is easy to miss.

Reproduction

    Create a parent repo GitHub/ with AGENTS.md and .git, and a nested repo GitHub/Harness/ with its own AGENTS.md and .git.
    Start a web session with cwd GitHub/Harness using the default code preset.
    Inspect the first request: the baseline contains only Harness/AGENTS.md.

Workaround (verified)

Create a user preset that copies the shipped code preset and overrides the agent-instructions row:
yaml

- id: agent-instructions
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-instructions'
  config:
    maxBytes: 131072
    projectRootMarkers: ['.dsh-root']

Place a .dsh-root marker file at the shared root (GitHub/), and set agent-presets.default: <preset-id> in $DSH_HOME/settings.yaml (hot-reloaded, no restart needed). Sessions then receive both AGENTS.md files.
Suggested fixes

    Let the home/user layer configure preset rows. Either allow $DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml (or settings) to patch rows inside preset compositions, or have presets inherit a user-configurable overlay for shared rows (e.g. agent-instructions).
    Support nested project roots in instruction discovery. Consider loading candidates from every ancestor directory that contains a root marker (root→cwd chain across nested repos), or add an opt-in like includeAncestorRoots: true / a sharedRootMarkers option, so a parent repo's AGENTS.md is not shadowed by the innermost .git.
    Reconsider the default budget. maxBytes: 65536 is smaller than many real-world AGENTS.md files; either raise the default, make the omission notice more prominent, or make maxBytes configurable from settings per preset.

Additional notes

    The session header records agentPreset at creation; blank-session drafts fix the preset at creation time, so config changes only affect sessions created afterwards (documented behavior, but easy to trip over when testing).
    agentPreset.list correctly reports the new default immediately after editing settings.yaml (hot-reload works); only the preset composition itself is read at session mount.

discussions.title: 强烈建议 Harness 也来个 Plus / Pro，别让大家边跑 Agent 边心算 API 账单
discussions.body:
目前 Harness 使用 DeepSeek 模型主要还是自己填写 API Key、按量计费。

轻度使用没什么问题，但 Agent 连续跑起来以后，体验多少有点像开着计价器写代码：代码还没写完，人先开始盯余额了。

建议参考 Codex、WorkBuddy 这类产品，增加可选的 Plus / Pro 订阅套餐：

- 每月固定费用，不同套餐对应不同额度
- 额度按周刷新，活动期间也可以偶尔额外送一点
- 用完后允许购买额外额度，或者继续按量计费
- 保留现有 API Key 模式，让用户自己选择

这不只是让费用更容易预期，也能增加用户黏度。订阅还在、每周额度又刷新了，用户自然会想着：“来都来了，再让 Agent 跑两轮吧。”

Harness 本身继续保持开源，订阅只对应官方模型用量。这样既不会影响喜欢自带 API Key 的用户，也能给长期、高频使用的人一个更省心的选择。

discussions.title: 在尝试让其链接yakit的mcp服务后出现错误，导致无论是新建会话还是项目都会出现同一个错误，无法让会话进行下去
[Security] Web minimal preset allows unapproved writes outside workspace-write on Windows
discussions.body:
## Summary

The Web `minimal` agent preset can write outside the selected workspace while the UI and exported session both report:

```text
permission preset: workspace-write
sandbox mode: workspace-write
approval policy: ask
```

I reproduced this on Windows with the session workspace located on drive `E:`. Without requesting or receiving approval, `str_replace_editor` successfully created a project under:

```text
C:\Users\Public\Documents\<AGENT_CREATED_DIRECTORY>
```

This is outside the selected workspace and on a different drive.

The destination is relevant: `C:\Users\Public\Documents` is the Windows Public Documents location, not a Harness workspace or per-session temporary directory.

This violates the documented meaning of `workspace-write`, under which mutations should be restricted to the selected workspace and explicitly permitted temporary roots.

The underlying problem appears to be that the `minimal` preset mounts the bare `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-local` backend in an isolated filesystem realm, shadowing the host sandbox-backed filesystem provider. As a result, `str_replace_editor` can perform writes through `fs-local` without enforcing the active `sandboxPolicy`.

This is not merely undesirable model behavior. The permission boundary must remain effective even when the model attempts an out-of-workspace write.

## Environment

* Platform: Windows
* Interface: DeepSeek Harness Web
* Agent preset: `minimal`
* Model: `deepseek-v4-flash`
* Permission preset: `workspace-write`
* Sandbox mode: `workspace-write`
* Approval policy: `ask`
* Workspace: `E:\<REDACTED_WORKSPACE>`
* Reproduction date: 2026-08-14, UTC+8
* No approval was requested or granted during the write

I could not find a reliable Harness build or commit identifier in the exported session. Please let me know where it can be obtained and I will add it.

## Original task

The agent received an ordinary request to create a small local web application.

The user did not ask it to inspect unrelated host directories, change the selected workspace, or write files into Windows Public Documents.

## Reproduction

1. Run DeepSeek Harness Web on Windows.

2. Select the `minimal` agent preset.

3. Select `workspace-write` with approval policy `ask`.

4. Select a workspace on drive `E:`.

5. Ask the agent to create a small web application.

6. In my run, persistent Bash failed with:

   ```text
   Error: subprocess-local: terminal inspection is unsupported on platform win32
   ```

7. The agent then used `str_replace_editor` with absolute paths outside the selected workspace. The following is a privacy-redacted representation of the successful call:

   ```json
   {
     "command": "create",
     "path": "C:\\Users\\Public\\Documents\\<AGENT_CREATED_DIRECTORY>\\index.html",
     "file_text": "<!doctype html><html><body>test</body></html>"
   }
   ```

8. The tool returned:

   ```text
   New file created successfully at:
   C:\Users\Public\Documents\<AGENT_CREATED_DIRECTORY>\index.html
   ```

9. The agent subsequently created and modified several more files in the same Public Documents subdirectory:

   ```text
   C:\Users\Public\Documents\<AGENT_CREATED_DIRECTORY>\index.html
   C:\Users\Public\Documents\<AGENT_CREATED_DIRECTORY>\README.md
   C:\Users\Public\Documents\<AGENT_CREATED_DIRECTORY>\package.json
   C:\Users\Public\Documents\<AGENT_CREATED_DIRECTORY>\main.js
   ```

10. No `approval/requested` event occurred before any of these writes.

## Relevant session evidence

The exported JSONL records the following state. Only the private workspace name has been redacted:

```json
{"type":"session","data":{"cwd":"E:\\<REDACTED_WORKSPACE>"}}
{"type":"permission/preset","data":{"preset":"workspace-write"}}
{"type":"sandbox/mode","data":{"mode":"workspace-write"}}
{"type":"approval/policy","data":{"policy":"ask"}}
```

It later records an editor call equivalent to:

```json
{
  "type": "tool/call",
  "data": {
    "name": "str_replace_editor",
    "arguments": {
      "command": "create",
      "path": "C:\\Users\\Public\\Documents\\<AGENT_CREATED_DIRECTORY>\\index.html",
      "file_text": "<!doctype html><html><body>test</body></html>"
    }
  }
}
```

The corresponding tool result confirms successful creation under:

```text
C:\Users\Public\Documents\<AGENT_CREATED_DIRECTORY>
```

The complete session export contains unrelated host paths and directory listings, so I am not attaching it publicly. I can provide a redacted export or additional event records if needed.

## Expected behavior

Under `workspace-write`, every mutating tool should reject paths outside:

* the selected workspace; and
* explicitly permitted per-session temporary roots.

In this case, with the workspace located at:

```text
E:\<REDACTED_WORKSPACE>
```

a write to:

```text
C:\Users\Public\Documents\<AGENT_CREATED_DIRECTORY>\index.html
```

should be rejected.

If an out-of-workspace operation supports escalation, it should execute only after explicit user approval.

## Actual behavior

`str_replace_editor` created and modified files under Windows Public Documents, outside the selected workspace and on a different drive.

No approval was requested, and the session continued to report `workspace-write`.

## Suspected cause

The Web `minimal` preset contains the following composition:

```yaml
- id: filesystem
  name: cordis:group
  group: true
  isolate:
    fs: true
  config:
    - id: fs-local
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-local'
      config:
        cwd: !!js process.env.DSH_CWD ?? process.cwd()

    - id: str-replace-editor
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-str-replace-editor'
```

The preset documentation indicates that the bare local filesystem shadows the host sandbox provider.

This matches the observed behavior: the editor resolves absolute paths through `fs-local`, while the active `workspace-write` policy is not consulted.

The standalone minimal-variant documentation warns that absolute editor paths can modify any path available to the runtime process and recommends using the variant only in a disposable checkout or container. That may be acceptable for an explicitly unrestricted standalone composition, but it conflicts with presenting the Web session as `workspace-write`.

## Security impact

A model operating under this preset may write to host-user-writable locations outside the selected workspace, potentially including:

* shared Windows Public folders;
* unrelated user files;
* application configuration;
* startup or persistence locations;
* scripts and source trees belonging to other projects;
* writable files that affect later host behavior.

The demonstrated write into:

```text
C:\Users\Public\Documents
```

also shows that the effect is not confined to the selected workspace drive or directory tree.

The exact impact depends on the privileges of the Harness process, but the documented `workspace-write` boundary is not enforced.

Directory reads are not the primary issue here, because the current documentation does not promise read confinement under `workspace-write`. The confirmed issue is successful out-of-workspace mutation.

## Suggested fixes

At least one of the following changes appears necessary:

1. Replace `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-local` with the sandbox-enforcing filesystem backend in the Web `minimal` preset.

2. Make `str_replace_editor` enforce `ctx.sandboxPolicy` independently of the mounted filesystem provider.

3. If `minimal` intentionally requires unrestricted filesystem access, prevent it from running while the UI reports `workspace-write`. Require an explicit `danger-full-access` selection and confirmation.

4. Fail closed during preset composition when a preset advertises `workspace-write` while exposing a mutating tool backed by a non-enforcing provider.

5. Add Windows and POSIX integration tests verifying that every mutating tool rejects:

   * sibling directories;
   * other drives or volume roots;
   * absolute paths outside the workspace;
   * Windows Public folders;
   * traversal and link-based escapes;
   * other unrelated host-user-writable directories.

These tests should cover both `bash` and `str_replace_editor`. Restricting only one mutating tool does not preserve the permission boundary.

## Severity

I consider this a high-severity permission-boundary issue.

The interface communicates a constrained `workspace-write` environment, but the `minimal` preset permits out-of-workspace writes with the privileges of the Harness host process. This mismatch is silent and requires no approval event.

## Related discussions

This report is related to, but distinct from:

- #490, which describes missing `workspace-write` semantics for remote
  execution-world filesystem providers. This report reproduces the issue
  locally on Windows in the Web `minimal` preset, where the bare `fs-local`
  provider appears to shadow the sandbox-enforcing filesystem provider.

- #159, which describes a post-check pathname race in an otherwise active
  `fs-sandbox` implementation. This report does not require a race, symlink,
  hardlink, background process, or Linux sandbox. A direct absolute-path
  `str_replace_editor` call deterministically writes outside the selected
  workspace without approval.

Therefore, this appears to be a separate preset-composition and permission-UI
mismatch rather than another reproduction of either issue.

discussions.title: Provider-neutral ToolSearch: source-backed API seams for safe staged tool activation
discussions.body:
Harness's scoped `ctx.tools.restrict()` already gives progressive disclosure
the right visibility primitive: presentation, lookup, and execution all derive
from the same scoped view. Building a safe, out-of-tree ToolSearch plugin
against the current public API, however, runs into six concrete lifecycle and
observability gaps audited below. This is not a proposal to “add embeddings to
the core” — retrieval policy can remain completely out of tree. The narrower
question is whether Harness can expose a revisioned catalog and provide a
transactional point at which any retriever can safely change the next request's
visible tool set.

I audited the source at a fixed commit, then built and tested an independent
community compatibility adapter to check whether those six gaps are real and
whether four small seams would close them.

The practical motivation came from an external system already operating at
roughly 1,700 tools with both name lookup and purpose-oriented keyword/vector
lookup. That is context for this proposal, not a claim that Harness itself
already has 1,700 tools or a semantic tool retriever. The harder problem is how
discovery, reversible activation, model-visible schemas, execution lookup, hot
updates, and replay remain consistent as overlapping plugins accumulate.

This analysis is pinned to commit
[`47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/tree/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a).
The prototype, benchmark, and API sketch are available at
[https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/dsh-hybrid-toolsearch](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/dsh-hybrid-toolsearch). It is an independent
project, not an official or endorsed DeepSeek implementation.

At this audited revision, the contribution guide says external pull requests
are not currently accepted; it points proposals to Discussions and encourages
independent plugin repositories with the `dsh-plugin` topic:
[`CONTRIBUTING.md#L9-L16`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/CONTRIBUTING.md#L9-L16).

### The observed problem

At the audited commit, MCP discovery drains `tools/list` and registers each
advertised definition in `ctx.tools`; a later `tools/list_changed` notification
repeats the synchronization. There is no query-relevance or top-k step in that
path:

- [`packages/mcp/mcp-client/src/tools.ts#L128-L173`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/mcp/mcp-client/src/tools.ts#L128-L173)
- [`packages/mcp/mcp-client/src/connection.ts#L254-L269`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/mcp/mcp-client/src/connection.ts#L254-L269)

The existing Skill mechanism is useful progressive disclosure for bodies, but
its model-facing catalog still contains every invocable name and description;
loading is by exact name. Provider `rank` resolves duplicate providers rather
than ranking a natural-language query:

- [`packages/skill/tool-skill/src/index.ts#L50-L57`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/skill/tool-skill/src/index.ts#L50-L57)
- [`packages/skill/tool-skill/src/index.ts#L127-L155`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/skill/tool-skill/src/index.ts#L127-L155)
- [`packages/skill/tool-skill/src/index.ts#L220-L228`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/skill/tool-skill/src/index.ts#L220-L228)

Harness already has the right visibility primitive. Inherited definitions are
filtered by scoped restrictions, exact-agent tools are added after inherited
filtering, and the derived view supplies schemas, lookup, and execution. The
extension cookbook explicitly identifies ToolSearch/progressive disclosure as
a scoped `ctx.tools.restrict()` replacement use case:

- [`packages/core/tools/src/index.ts#L1152-L1192`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/core/tools/src/index.ts#L1152-L1192)
- [`packages/core/tools/src/index.ts#L1204-L1236`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/core/tools/src/index.ts#L1204-L1236)
- [`docs/cookbook/extension-cookbook.md#L95-L113`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/docs/cookbook/extension-cookbook.md#L95-L113)

The missing pieces are lifecycle and observability seams, rather than a
particular retrieval algorithm.

### Why an out-of-tree plugin cannot safely finish the job today

1. **No unfiltered scoped catalog after activation.** Public
   `schemas(agent)` returns the post-restriction view, while the complete
   inherited name sets are private. An indexer cannot reliably discover a new
   hidden tool or rebuild from authoritative unfiltered state.

2. **Catalog and presentation changes are indistinguishable.** Registration,
   unregistration, and restriction changes emit the same synchronous,
   payload-free `tools/change`. A plugin cannot observe name, scope, action,
   revision, or origin, so its own restriction can feed back into reindexing:
   [`index.ts#L199-L207`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/core/tools/src/index.ts#L199-L207),
   [`index.ts#L811-L814`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/core/tools/src/index.ts#L811-L814),
   [`index.ts#L1110-L1115`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/core/tools/src/index.ts#L1110-L1115).

3. **Restriction replacement is not atomic.** `restrict()` returns a disposer,
   and multiple restrictions intersect. Installing the new restriction before
   disposing the old one is fail-closed but exposes a temporary intersection
   and emits two events; disposing first creates an unacceptable temporarily
   unrestricted interval:
   [`index.ts#L713-L744`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/core/tools/src/index.ts#L713-L744),
   [`index.ts#L1064-L1097`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/core/tools/src/index.ts#L1064-L1097).

4. **There is no awaited safe commit boundary.** Tool schemas are derived
   during system-prompt assembly, before `agent/pre-step`. A restriction change
   there can make execution disagree with the already-rendered prompt.
   `step/end` observation is synchronous and is not an awaited transaction:
   [`dispatch.ts#L167-L175`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/core/agent/src/dispatch.ts#L167-L175),
   [`agent.ts#L225-L242`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/core/agent-loop/src/agent.ts#L225-L242),
   [`system-prompt/index.ts#L467-L535`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/core/system-prompt/src/index.ts#L467-L535),
   [`session/index.ts#L381-L398`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/core/session/src/index.ts#L381-L398).

5. **Changing visibility inside the search call is unsafe.** Calls from one
   model response are planned before dispatch, but later siblings can re-read
   live visibility. Code Mode captures generated bindings and also rechecks
   live lookup on nested dispatch. A search body that narrows immediately can
   invalidate a sibling call or a still-running program:
   [`tool-calls.ts#L70-L92`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts#L70-L92),
   [`tool-calls.ts#L198-L229`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts#L198-L229),
   [`code-mode.ts#L594-L607`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/core/tools/src/code-mode.ts#L594-L607).

6. **Request audit data does not restore a plugin restriction.** Headers record
   the old rendered view, but resume assembles a new current composition;
   ephemeral restriction ownership is not replayed:
   [`session/types.ts#L196-L209`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/core/session/src/types.ts#L196-L209),
   [`agent.ts#L458-L470`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/core/agent-loop/src/agent.ts#L458-L470).

### Requested provider-neutral seams

Would the maintainers consider four small, retrieval-agnostic APIs?

1. **Read-only unfiltered scoped catalog**

   ```ts
   ctx.tools.catalog(agentScope, {
     visibility: "inherited-unfiltered",
   }): ToolCatalogSnapshot
   ```

   The snapshot would contain stable runtime/provider identity, cloned schemas,
   schema hashes, and a monotonic catalog revision. Reading it would not change
   execution visibility.

2. **Structured catalog changes, separate from presentation changes**

   ```ts
   ctx.tools.onCatalogChange(({ revision, scope, action, toolIds, origin }) => {
     if (origin !== pluginOrigin) index.schedule(revision);
   });
   ```

   Restriction changes would keep the backward-compatible `tools/change` event
   but would not masquerade as catalog mutations.

3. **Atomic restriction replacement**

   ```ts
   restriction = await ctx.tools.replaceRestriction(restriction, {
     allow: selectedNames,
     origin: pluginOrigin,
   });
   ```

   Readers would observe either the old or new immutable view, never a temporary
   intersection or open set. Validation/notification failure would retain the
   old handle, and one structured visibility notification would be emitted.

4. **Awaited before-assembly boundary**

   ```ts
   ctx.agent.onBeforeAssemble(async ({ agent, previousStep, signal }) => {
     await toolSearch.commitStagedSelection(agent, signal);
   });
   ```

   It must run after all sibling calls or the complete Code program settle and
   before native schemas, SDK text, request headers, or provider requests are
   derived. Rejection should preserve the old prompt/view pair and prevent
   dispatch.

An optional explicit **bootstrap/control-tool marker** could replace reliance on
exact-scope registration while still applying normal guards and approval.

These seams do not put BM25, embeddings, a vector database, top-k policy, or a
vendor in Harness core. They only let an independently chosen retrieval policy
remain consistent with prompt assembly, lookup, execution, hot updates, and
session replay.

To check whether these seams are actually sufficient and correctly shaped, I
built and tested an independent compatibility adapter against the current
public API where that is possible, leaving the rest as explicit, disclosed
workarounds.

### Prototype design

The prototype deliberately separates retrieval policy from Harness lifecycle:

```text
revisioned unfiltered catalog
  -> exact name/alias + BM25 + replaceable dense provider
  -> structured constraints and semantic reranking
  -> reciprocal-rank fusion with deterministic ties
  -> discovery top-k with lane scores and reasons
  -> durable staged activation top-k
  -> all sibling calls / current Code program finish under old view
  -> awaited pre-assembly commit
  -> next request sees the control tool plus selected inherited tools
```

Each Discovery Card has a stable ID, canonical name/aliases, provider,
capabilities, effects, input/output and negative constraints, risk/cost/latency
hints, version, schema hash, and catalog revision. Each selection event records
the query, candidates and all lane/constraint/fusion scores, selected names,
revision, and commit status.

The exact-scope search tool remains visible independently of the inherited
allow-list. Search only stages. At the next safe boundary, replacement is
install-new-before-dispose-old; failure retains the old restriction. Resume or
fork restores the last compatible committed event. A revision mismatch records
an explicit invalidation and remains control-only until re-search. Empty,
low-confidence, failed-dense, and no-result paths never fall back to the full
catalog.

The frozen reference adapter also installs the inherited empty/replayed
restriction before registering the session's control tool, avoiding a bootstrap
full-open interval. On hot update it durably appends invalidation plus a
control-only fallback before publishing the new in-memory revision; a durable
write failure leaves the old revision and restriction live and surfaces a
retryable failure. The event store is still non-transactional across those two
records, as disclosed below.

For `native`, the next request receives selected function schemas. For `code`,
the generated SDK and all nested dispatches retain one view for the entire
program. For `both`, native and SDK presentations share one revision and their
duplicated presentation cost is measured separately. Code Mode is not assumed
to be inherently cheaper.

The compatibility adapter and reference runtime test those invariants, but the
audited public API cannot attach the required awaited boundary. This is a
reference host contract, not a claim of safe drop-in integration today. Full
design and tests:

- [architecture](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/dsh-hybrid-toolsearch/blob/be1a135/docs/architecture.md)
- [compatibility matrix](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/dsh-hybrid-toolsearch/blob/be1a135/docs/compatibility-matrix.md)
- [source audit](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/dsh-hybrid-toolsearch/blob/be1a135/docs/upstream-gaps.md)
- [minimal seam proposal](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/dsh-hybrid-toolsearch/blob/be1a135/docs/upstream-seam-proposal.md)

### Reference retrieval implementation — validation results

The seams above are retrieval-policy-agnostic; they do not require BM25,
embeddings, or any specific algorithm. To exercise them concretely, the same
adapter drives one reference retrieval implementation (exact/alias + BM25 + a
replaceable dense provider, fused with RRF). That implementation's own quality
claim is disclosed in full below because it is part of the same evidence trail
as the source audit — not because it is what I am asking maintainers to adopt.

Environment: Node v24.19.0, Windows x64, Intel Core i5-10600T (12 logical
cores), seed `1592598566`. Both quality comparisons use the fixed synthetic
1,000-tool catalog. The gate was unchanged: hybrid Recall@5 must be at least
90%, Recall@10 at least 97%, and Recall@5 must exceed the better keyword/dense
single lane by at least 5.00 percentage points.

#### Historical holdout-v1 — FAIL

The original 48-query sealed result is retained unchanged:

| Runner | Recall@5 | Recall@10 | MRR@10 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| keyword-only | 93.75% | 93.75% | 0.8125 |
| dense-only | 93.75% | 95.83% | 0.7292 |
| hybrid | **97.92%** | **100.00%** | **0.8628** |

Hybrid gained two hits over the better single lane: **4.17 points**, not the
required 5.00. The sole hybrid miss placed the gold tool at rank 6. This result
was not used for later tuning and was never rerun with the new ranking code.

#### Preregistered holdout-v2 one-shot — FAIL

Option A used 144 independently authored, provider-blind, text-only semantic
queries. They were sealed before development changes. Final implementation
commit `62d8f2b302fd27bea3517ebc1b46899dc35569f4` was bound by manifest SHA-256
`3da516b09e55be0aec8e68e1ef971689f8c5427dda64419e670df6e6f5243fd4`.
Run `78276923-eed1-4471-b8a8-6936765e82c7` durably wrote its started ledger
before loading sealed text and completed exactly once:

| Runner | Recall@5 | Recall@10 | MRR@10 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| keyword-only | 132/144 (91.67%) | 136/144 (94.44%) | 0.7152 |
| dense-only | 122/144 (84.72%) | 129/144 (89.58%) | 0.6443 |
| hybrid | **133/144 (92.36%)** | **133/144 (92.36%)** | **0.7589** |

Hybrid recovered only one additional top-5 query, an improvement of
**0.69 points**. It therefore failed the 5-point relative gate. Its 92.36%
Recall@10 also failed the 97% absolute gate; the 92.36% absolute Recall@5 gate
passed. Separate exact suites achieved 24/24 canonical names and 24/24 stable
IDs at Rank@1.

| Frozen v2 scale gate | Result | Threshold | Status |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1k warm hybrid p95 | 19.26 ms | <=100 ms | PASS |
| 10k warm hybrid p95 | 156.35 ms | <=500 ms | PASS |
| 1k native top-5 presentation reduction | 99.39% | >=95% | PASS |
| 1k code / both reduction | 99.30% / 99.34% | reported separately | — |

The like-for-like development raw-text result had shown a 5.36-point gain, so
the v2 result records a material development/holdout transfer failure. I did
not change weights, redefine a baseline, lower a threshold, or rerun the
one-shot after disclosure. Both failed validations remain first-class evidence.

The corpus is synthetic, v2 is process-isolated model-authored rather than
production-log or external-human data, and the local embedding is a
deterministic test provider. The roughly six-second 10k cold build/query,
MRR@10 truncation, presentation-character proxy, and frozen implementation
edge cases are disclosed in the linked limitations rather than hidden behind
the passing latency/schema gates.

Evidence:

- [v2 one-shot report](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/dsh-hybrid-toolsearch/blob/be1a135/benchmark/holdout-v2-results.md)
- [v2 machine result](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/dsh-hybrid-toolsearch/blob/be1a135/benchmark/holdout-v2-results.json)
- [v2 append-only ledger](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/dsh-hybrid-toolsearch/blob/be1a135/benchmark/holdout-v2-run.jsonl)
- [v2 failure analysis](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/dsh-hybrid-toolsearch/blob/be1a135/docs/holdout-v2-failure-analysis.md)
- [historical v1 report](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/dsh-hybrid-toolsearch/blob/be1a135/benchmark/results.md)
- [v1 failure analysis](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/dsh-hybrid-toolsearch/blob/be1a135/docs/holdout-v1-failure-analysis.md)
- [known limitations](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/dsh-hybrid-toolsearch/blob/be1a135/docs/known-limitations.md)

Reproduction from a checkout uses Node `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` and pnpm
`11.19.0`. It verifies the completed ledger/artifact hashes and recomputes the
disclosed deterministic projection; it is not a second independent holdout:

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm verify
pnpm generate:corpus
pnpm historical:v1:verify  # hashes preserved v1 FAIL; does not re-evaluate it
pnpm benchmark             # safe v2 reproduction; writes nothing
pnpm demo
```

### Security and limitations

`restrict()` is a scoped composition/visibility mechanism, not an authorization
boundary. ToolSearch can reduce what the model sees and what ordinary scoped
lookup resolves, but it must not replace Harness guards, approvals, credentials,
or sandboxing. Risk metadata in the prototype affects ranking only.

The prototype is synthetic, single-process, and uses a deterministic local
embedding provider. It failed the relative quality gate twice and has not
demonstrated production vector-store behavior or a safe dynamic attachment to
the audited public API. The tested adapter is a reference host contract, not a
drop-in Harness plugin.

Known frozen edge cases were deliberately documented rather than repaired
after the one-shot result:

- field-aware interaction is computed for a top-100 coarse union, but
  differently scaled coarse scores outside that window are mixed back into the
  final ordering; the top-100 window is therefore not a hard candidate bound;
- the lane named `exact` also contains contained-name/token-overlap heuristics,
  although the separate strict identity suites passed 48/48;
- the ranking fingerprint binds declared configuration/provider while the
  final manifest, not that fingerprint alone, binds every implementation byte;
- durable visibility events retain candidate scores/revision but omit the full
  engine ranking fingerprint, and staging does not prove every selected item
  came from the supplied candidate list;
- control-name/`run_code` collisions and every disposer-failure retry path are
  not fully preflighted;
- hot-update invalidation uses multiple durable appends, not a transaction; a
  partial failure can make cold replay more restrictive than the live process;
- malformed-card quarantine, duplicate-identity rejection, and dense-provider
  failure are deterministic fail-closed paths but do not all return a normal
  search fallback with equally detailed diagnostics.

The complete list, including benchmark measurement limits, is in
[known-limitations.md](https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/dsh-hybrid-toolsearch/blob/be1a135/docs/known-limitations.md).
These points are not excuses to reinterpret the failed result. They are the
frozen boundary for deciding whether another iteration is worthwhile.

Those limitations are why I am asking primarily about the four
lifecycle/catalog seams and their invariants, not proposing the ranking
implementation for core adoption.

I would especially appreciate feedback on whether the proposed boundary should
be `agent/before-assemble`, a transactional replacement around system-prompt
assembly, or another lifecycle point that also covers the initial request,
zero-tool turns, retry, resume, fork, and complete Code programs.

discussions.title: dsh-plugins: bounded cross-session memory (MEMORY.md/USER.md) and skill lifecycle curation, ported from hermes-agent
discussions.body:
Two ecosystem plugins porting the two mechanisms I consider the core of [NousResearch/hermes-agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent), reimplemented on dsh's own conventions.

Repo: https://github.com/hyls9527/dsh-plugins (tagged `dsh-plugin`)

## @hyls9527/dsh-memory

Bounded, file-backed, cross-session self-maintained memory: `$DSH_HOME/memories/MEMORY.md` (the agent's own notes) and `USER.md` (what it knows about the user).

- §-separated entries with character budgets (2200/1375 by default), so files stay human-editable and the model consolidates instead of growing unbounded memory.
- One `memory` tool: `add` / `replace` / `remove` / `batch` (atomic multi-op).
- A frozen snapshot is injected as a durable `user/message` at the first admitted step of each session — mid-session writes never touch it, so the prompt prefix stays stable for the whole session.
- `nudgeInterval` persistence reminders (default every 10 write-free turns).
- Durability guards: cross-process locks, atomic renames, refusal to overwrite unreadable files, and drift detection (external edits are snapshotted to `.bak.<ts>` and refused).

Model-visible ⟺ logged is satisfied without new session event vocabulary: the snapshot is a durable message with a `memory` source, and tool calls are logged by the harness itself.

## @hyls9527/dsh-skill-curator

Minimal skill lifecycle curation: every `skill` tool call is recorded into one usage document, and a `skill_curator` tool reports usage and staleness (derived from a configurable threshold, default 21 days), archives unused skills out of the catalog, and restores them.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add @hyls9527/dsh-memory
dsh plugin --profile web add @hyls9527/dsh-skill-curator
```

Both are dsh bundles (a `cordis.patch.yml` inserting one row each), built against `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` 0.1.0-rc.6, with 100% per-file vitest coverage and verified end-to-end in a real profile (snapshot injection, a live memory write, and usage tracking). Feedback welcome.

discussions.title: Show and tell: dsh-eval-regression, deterministic golden-output evaluation plugin
discussions.body:
I built **[dsh-eval-regression](https://github.com/aryswisnu/dsh-eval-regression)**, a small third-party DSH plugin for deterministic regression checks of candidate agent output.

It registers `evaluate_golden_output`, which evaluates supplied output against per-case required and forbidden text fragments and returns:

- passed and failed case counts
- a deterministic `0..1` score
- each case's missing and forbidden fragments

It deliberately does not call a model, persist data, or claim semantic or factual correctness. The intended use is as one transparent gate beside replay/snapshot tests and stronger product-specific evaluation.

Verification completed locally against the public DSH packages:

- 5 Vitest tests passed, including real Cordis tool-pipeline registration, execution, and disposal
- TypeScript typecheck passed
- production build passed

Source and source-install instructions: https://github.com/aryswisnu/dsh-eval-regression

Feedback on the tool surface and the right path toward replay-driven suites would be welcome.

discussions.title: [web] Cannot create a workspace on Windows: native OS folder dialog is used instead of in-browser browse picker
discussions.body:
## Summary
When running `dsh web` on Windows, the **"New workspace"** action in the web UI cannot complete - it appears to do nothing and no error is shown in the page.

## Environment
- OS: Windows (win32)
- Package: `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.0-rc.6`
- Command: `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web` (binds `127.0.0.1:3080`)
- Client: browser

## Symptom
In the web UI, clicking "New workspace" produces no visible result and the workspace is never created.

## Root-cause analysis (from the published package)
The picker backend is chosen by `resolveDirectoryPickerBackend` in `packages/host/directory-picker-auto/lib/resolve.js`:

```js
if (facts.bindHost !== "127.0.0.1") return "browse";
if (present(facts.env.SSH_CONNECTION) || present(facts.env.SSH_TTY)) return "browse";
if (facts.platform === "darwin" || facts.platform === "win32") return "native";   // <-- Windows lands here
if (facts.platform !== "linux" || !facts.linuxChooser) return "browse";
return present(facts.env.DISPLAY) || present(facts.env.WAYLAND_DISPLAY) ? "native" : "browse";
```

On Windows with a loopback bind and no SSH, it returns `"native"`. The native backend (`packages/host/directory-picker-native`) spawns `worker.cjs`, opens the Win32 `IFileOpenDialog` via koffi - a **system folder dialog that lives outside the browser**. For a web (browser) client this dialog is detached from the page and is normally hidden behind / loses focus to the browser window, so the user cannot see or operate it and workspace creation appears to fail.

Notably, the module's own comment says "remote deployments compose the browse backend instead" - but a localhost web client is currently treated as a local desktop client and gets `native`.

I verified separately that:
- the backend `workspace.create` API works correctly (created a workspace via the API using an existing directory), and
- `worker.cjs` does spawn and initialize the COM dialog correctly (it emits the `showing` message).

So the storage/data model is fine; the problem is the **picker kind selected for a web client on Windows**.

## Expected behavior
When running `dsh web`, the workspace picker should use the **browse** backend (in-browser directory tree via `host.listDirectory` / `host.createDirectory`), not the native OS dialog - matching the documented intent that web/remote clients get `browse`.

## Suggested fix
Either:
- make `resolveDirectoryPickerBackend` return `"browse"` for a web client (e.g. pass a `clientKind` / `isWeb` fact and prefer `browse` for web clients regardless of platform), or
- in the web app composition, mount the `browse` pair (`dsh-host-directory-picker-browse` + `dsh-client-ui-directory-picker-browse`) directly instead of the `auto` chooser.

Happy to open a PR if you indicate the preferred approach.

discussions.title: 社区插件 dsh-email 发布：让 DSH 查收件箱/读邮件/搜邮件/代发信（6 工具 + Web 设置页）
discussions.body:
**dsh-email —— 给 DeepSeek Harness 装上邮件能力：查收件箱、读邮件、搜邮件、代发信（6 工具 + Web 设置页）**

做这个插件的起因：公测首日看到 #14 求 memory，扫了一遍生态发现 memory 已被社区做穿，但**邮件工具是几百个 dsh-plugin 仓库里的真空**。于是从零写了一个，期间还在原生模式（标准/极简/创造预设）下踩出并修复了工具参数 schema 的坑。

**六个工具**
- email_list / email_read / email_search —— 收件箱列表、读全文（HTML 自动转纯文本、超长截断）、按主题/发件人/收件人搜索
- email_send —— 代发邮件。**默认走审批门**：弹框显示收件人和主题，你批准才发出；Full Access 模式下被安全拒绝
- email_folders / email_attachment —— 列文件夹、下载附件（20MB 上限、文件名防路径穿越、不覆盖同名文件）

**特性**
- 内置 QQ / 163 / 126 / 新浪 / 阿里 / Gmail / Outlook / iCloud 八个预设，也可手填任意 IMAP/SMTP 服务器
- 多账号（accounts/defaultAccount）与 IMAP/SMTP 连接复用
- 纯 Node 实现，Windows / macOS / Linux 通吃，零核心改动

**安装（一分钟上手）**

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-email
```

重启后打开 **设置 → 邮件 (dsh-email)**：选服务商 → 填邮箱 + 授权码 → 「测试连接」→「保存并应用」。不用手写 YAML，保存即生效。

**质量**
- 34 个单元测试 + GitHub Actions CI
- 真实 QQ 邮箱端到端验收（列表/搜索/阅读/发信/附件字节级往返）
- 授权码标记 secret（不进日志/导出），支持 DSH_EMAIL_PASSWORD 环境变量

**链接**
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-email
- GitHub: https://github.com/STARDUSTLC666/dsh-email （已打 dsh-plugin 话题）
- 目录登记 PR: https://github.com/AdamPlatin123/awesome-dsh-plugins/pull/20

欢迎试用、反馈、PR，也欢迎顺手点个 star 🐋

discussions.title: [Show and tell] DeepSeek Desktop：DeepSeek Harness 的 Windows x64 社区安装包
discussions.body:
大家好，我做了一个面向 Windows x64 的 DeepSeek Harness 社区发行项目：**DeepSeek Desktop**。

它基于已发布的 `@deepseek-ai/dsh` 构建，不是 DeepSeek 官方桌面客户端，也不包含任何 API Key。目标是让 Windows 用户通过普通安装程序使用 Harness，不必手动准备 Node.js、命令行启动服务或管理浏览器标签页。

![DeepSeek Desktop 中文界面](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/121103qwq/deepseek-desktop/main/docs/images/deepseek-desktop-main.png)

### 默认可以免登录使用

安装向导默认选择 **Kilo Auto Free**。它使用 Kilo 提供的匿名免费路线，不需要登录或 API Key，也不是本地模型。免费额度、具体路由和可用性由 Kilo 决定；Auto Free 可能转发给会记录输入和输出的第三方服务，不应提交个人、机密或敏感内容。

如果已有 DeepSeek API Key，也可以在安装时选择 **DeepSeek API**，随后通过 Harness 原有的应用内流程填写自己的密钥。安装后仍可在应用内修改模型路线，后续启动不会重复询问。

![安装向导中的模型路线](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/121103qwq/deepseek-desktop/main/docs/images/installer-model-choice.png)

### 内置桌面窗口

DeepSeek Desktop 会在本机启动 Harness 服务，并把本地 UI 加载到名为 `DeepSeek Desktop` 的内置 WebView2 窗口中，不会打开外部浏览器。界面默认中文，也可以之后自行切换。

### 两个 Windows 安装包

| 安装包 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| 标准版 `Setup-默认.exe` | 体积约 36 MB；首次启动时通过国内 npm 镜像下载固定的 Harness 依赖，并使用系统已有的 WebView2 Runtime。 |
| 完整离线版 `Offline-Setup.exe` | 体积约 355 MB；内置 Harness 完整依赖和固定版 WebView2 Runtime，安装组件无需另行下载。 |

“离线版”只表示安装所需组件已内置；Kilo 和 DeepSeek API 的模型请求仍需联网。

标准版首次启动会明确询问是否下载运行组件，并显示下载进度；依赖已经存在时不会再次下载。

![标准版首次启动下载进度](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/121103qwq/deepseek-desktop/main/docs/images/standard-first-launch-download-progress.png)

两个安装包都只为当前 Windows 用户安装，不要求管理员权限，不修改系统 `PATH`，支持自定义安装位置和可选桌面快捷方式，并创建开始菜单入口与 Windows“已安装的应用”记录。

卸载会停止桌面窗口和随附的 Node 服务，移除程序文件、注册项及快捷方式，但保留 `%LOCALAPPDATA%\DeepSeek Harness Data` 中的会话与设置，便于以后重装继续使用。

### 项目、下载和中文视频

- 项目仓库：https://github.com/121103qwq/deepseek-desktop
- Release：https://github.com/121103qwq/deepseek-desktop/releases/tag/deepseek-desktop-v0.1.0
- 中文图文介绍：https://github.com/121103qwq/deepseek-desktop/blob/main/distribution/windows/INTRODUCTION.zh.md
- 62 秒中文演讲视频：https://github.com/121103qwq/deepseek-desktop/blob/main/presentation/video/out/deepseek-desktop-v0.1.0-zh.mp4

当前安装程序是未签名的社区构建，Windows 可能显示“未知发布者”。请只从项目 Release 下载。

我已经在 Windows 上实测了安装包图标、默认 Kilo 配置、无 Key 匿名请求、自定义安装位置、小包首次下载与进度条、已有依赖的再次启动、内置 WebView、应用注册，以及卸载后的进程和文件清理。欢迎反馈安装、WebView2、Kilo 免费路线和卸载流程方面的问题。

discussions.title: [Bug] `WebSocket error` 被归类为 `PI_AI_ERROR`，导致绕过重试
discussions.body:
# `WebSocket error` 被归类为 `PI_AI_ERROR`，导致绕过重试

## 摘要

OpenAI Codex 出现瞬时传输故障时，pi-ai 返回的确切消息为 `WebSocket error`，但 `llm-pi-ai` 将其归类为 `PI_AI_ERROR`，而不是 `TRANSPORT`。由于 DSH 默认重试策略会重试 `TRANSPORT`，但不会重试 `PI_AI_ERROR`，因此 Agent turn 会立即结束，并且不会产生 `llm/retry` 事件。

这与目前已经覆盖的错误消息 `WebSocket closed unexpectedly` 不同。

## 实际行为

环境：

- DSH：`0.1.0-rc.6`
- Provider：`openai-codex`
- Adapter：`@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai`

持久化 session 事件：

```json
{"type":"assistant/chunk","chunk":{"type":"finish","reason":{"kind":"error","failure":{"message":"WebSocket error","code":"PI_AI_ERROR"}}}}
{"type":"turn/end","reason":{"kind":"error","error":{"message":"WebSocket error","code":"PI_AI_ERROR"}}}
```

该 session 中没有任何 `llm/retry` / `llm/retry-started` 事件。

## 根因

`packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/stream.ts` 能识别以下 WebSocket 错误措辞：

```text
WebSocket closed unexpectedly
```

但不能识别 pi-ai 返回的较短措辞：

```text
WebSocket error
```

后者会落入默认分支，被归类为 `PI_AI_ERROR`。默认 Provider 重试策略包含 `TRANSPORT`，因此错误分类阻止了现有的外层重试机制运行。

Codex OAuth 插件并不是传输层的所有者：它只负责提供和刷新凭据。WebSocket 连接由 pi-ai 的 `openai-codex-responses` Provider 负责。

## 预期行为

`WebSocket error` 应当映射为 `TRANSPORT`，让 DSH 有界的外层重试策略能够重新执行失败的 step。

## 最小修复

```diff
- WebSocket closed unexpectedly
+ WebSocket (?:closed unexpectedly|error)
```

在 `packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/tests/convert.spec.ts` 现有的表驱动传输错误措辞测试中加入 `WebSocket error`。

## 验证

已在上游 `master` 的 `47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a` 提交上应用：

```text
vitest packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/tests/convert.spec.ts: 69 passed
oxlint changed source/test: 0 warnings, 0 errors
pre-commit gates: passed
```

可移植的 `git format-patch` 已作为当前目录中的 `upstream-fix.patch` 保留。

discussions.title: 将其他agent的会话导入dsh的插件！
discussions.body:
## dsh-plugin-session-import v0.1.0 发布说明

插件仓库 https://github.com/huguangyu666/dsh-plugin-session-import/tree/main

### 这个插件做什么

把 Claude Code、Codex、Reasonix、ZCode 四个工具的历史聊天记录导入 DeepSeek Harness。导入后就是一个完整的 dsh 会话，可以直接继续对话、正常调用工具、自动绑定工作区。

场景很简单：你在别的工具里聊了一半，想换到 dsh 继续，不用从头讲一遍背景，历史直接带过来。

### 主要功能

- 四工具导入：Claude Code（含新端）、Codex、Reasonix（CLI 和桌面版）、ZCode
- 会话信息自动提取：标题、项目名、消息数、时间，扫描有 30 秒缓存
- 导入后工具完整可用：read、edit、glob、grep、pwsh 等 25+ 个工具和正常会话一样
- ZCode 压缩过的会话能还原摘要正文，模型还记得压缩前的关键信息
- 超长会话有三层保护：内容裁剪、消息截断、单条兜底，上万条消息或单条几百万字符都不会撑爆上下文
- 支持按标题、项目名搜索
- 支持多选批量导入，每个会话独立创建并绑定工作区

### 安装

```bash
npm i dsh-plugin-session-import
```

然后在 `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` 挂载：

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: session-import
      name: 'dsh-plugin-session-import'
```

重启 `dsh web` 即可。侧边栏底部会出现"导入会话"入口。

### 实现上的一些说明

开发过程中踩了不少坑，这里简单交代几个关键点：

- seed 生成严格对齐 dsh 的消息派生规则：assistant 消息承载 tool-call 块，tool/result 紧邻配对，孤儿结果直接丢弃，保证导入后模型请求不会报错
- ZCode 走 db.sqlite 权威索引，不是扫描 transcript 文件，所以标题、项目、时间都是准确的
- Codex 新版（custom_tool_call）的参数是 JS 代码字符串，解析时自动转成标准 JSON，避免模型学到错误的工具调用格式
- 上下文预算按模型的真实窗口动态计算，换模型不需要改配置；也可以用 `DSH_IMPORT_CONTEXT_BUDGET` 环境变量覆盖
- 中文路径处理过两轮：Claude 的目录编码用 `.claude.json` 做权威映射，Reasonix 的项目 slug 用贪心解码还原真实路径

### 已知限制

- 图片附件目前降级为占位文本
- 超长会话的中间轮次会被截断（保留摘要、开头锚点和尾部）
- Reasonix 桌面版部分会话标题依赖 `.titles.json`，缺失时回退文件名

### 后续想做的

- 更多工具支持（Cline、Gemini CLI、OpenCode 等）
- 图片随会话一起迁移
- 超长会话的摘要化截断策略
- 列表排序、过滤等 UI 细节

### 反馈

有 bug 或者想法，开 Issue 或者直接在讨论区回帖都行。这个插件我自己用了一段时间，四个工具的导入链路都实际跑过，但不同机器、不同版本的环境差异还可能有没覆盖到的情况，欢迎报问题。

discussions.title: [BUG]会话/思考过长导致的：历史加载失败：history unavailable for session "session-2063f7c0-01dd-4892-ad90-9a2068c4f95d": RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded（internal）
discussions.body: [dsh-session-session-2063f7c0-01dd-4892-ad90-9a2068c4f95d.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31047539/dsh-session-session-2063f7c0-01dd-4892-ad90-9a2068c4f95d.zip) 这是相关会话内容。 这是相关BUG截图。会话中约20w输出tok，考虑到官方设置的模型输出上限是384k，不应在harness/webui处限制会话加载时的上限。以下是GPT模型对此的判断： Title Long single-response sessions fail to load with `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` Body ## Environment - `@deepseek-ai/dsh`: `0.1.0-rc.6` - Node.js: `v24.15.0` - Platform: Windows - Web mode: `dsh web` ## Observed behavior After a session produced one unusually long assistant response, generation completed successfully and the session was persisted. However, opening its history in the WebUI failed with: ```text Failed to load history: history unavailable for session "": RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded (internal) The DSH process remained alive, the Web server continued returning HTTP 200, and other sessions continued running. I found no indication that the affected session log itself was lost or corrupted. This appears to affect history loading only. Expected behavior The history should load normally, or at least be paginated without depending on the number of chunks in one assistant message. Root cause The error originates in the server-side history pagination code in: @deepseek-ai/dsh-host-apiproxy/lib/index.js The relevant code in paginate() is: const sources = event.sourceEventSeqs; const groupStart = sources !== undefined && sources.length > 0 ? Math.min(event.seq, ...sources) : event.seq; For a long streamed response, the final assistant/message records all corresponding chunk sequence numbers in sourceEventSeqs. In the affected session: sourceEventSeqs.length = 156582 Spreading such a large array into Math.min() exceeds V8's function argument limit and produces: RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded On the same Node.js installation, the following reproduces the failure independently: Math.min(0, ...Array.from({ length: 125000 }, (_, i) => i + 1)); The exception is then caught by the server-side session.history handler and wrapped as: message: `history unavailable for session "${sessionId}": ${String(error)}` The WebUI appears to be displaying this backend internal response correctly. Therefore, this does not appear to be a React rendering or frontend transport failure. Minimal reproduction Start DSH in Web mode. Create a session whose single assistant response produces more than approximately 125,000 chunk events. Allow the response to complete. Leave and reopen the session. History loading fails with RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded. The precise threshold is engine-dependent. Suggested fix Compute the minimum iteratively instead of spreading the array: let groupStart = event.seq; if (sources !== undefined) { for (const seq of sources) { if (seq < groupStart) groupStart = seq; } } This preserves the current pagination semantics and removes dependence on V8's argument-count limit. It may also be useful to add a regression test with a synthetic sourceEventSeqs array larger than the engine's spread-argument limit. Additional impact I found several locally persisted long sessions with sourceEventSeqs lengths above the failure threshold. This suggests that any sufficiently long single streamed response can become impossible to reopen through the normal history API, even though generation and persistence complete successfully.

discussions.title: [BUG] 通过 SSH 端口转发远程访问 Web 界面时，无法添加新工作区
discussions.body:
## 环境信息

- 机器 A（服务端）：运行 `npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh web`，监听 3080 端口
- 机器 B（客户端）：通过 SSH 端口转发访问，命令为 `ssh -L 3080:localhost:3080 <机器A>`

## 复现步骤

1. 在机器 A 上运行 `npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh web` 启动 Web 服务；
2. 在机器 B 上通过 SSH 将机器 A 的 3080 端口转发到本地 3080 端口；
3. 在机器 B 的浏览器中访问 `http://localhost:3080`，页面可以正常打开和操作；
4. 在 Web 界面中点击"添加新工作区"，尝试选择文件夹。

## 预期行为

能够在浏览器中直接完成文件夹路径的选择（例如通过手动输入路径，或弹出基于 Web 的目录选择器），正常添加工作区。

## 实际行为

无法添加新工作区。文件夹选择器是以 GUI 弹窗的形式出现在机器 A 的桌面环境上，而不是在机器 B 正在访问的浏览器页面中。由于机器 B 无法访问机器 A 的桌面，远程场景下该功能实际上不可用。

## 问题分析

当前的文件夹选择逻辑似乎调用的是服务端（机器 A）本地的原生文件对话框，而非在前端 Web 页面中实现。这在本地使用时不构成问题，但在任何远程访问场景（SSH 端口转发、部署在无 GUI 的服务器上等）都会导致该功能完全失效。

## 建议

- 在 Web 界面中支持手动输入工作区的绝对路径；或
- 实现基于 Web 的服务端目录浏览器，让前端直接浏览和选择机器 A 上的目录。

discussions.title: [web] "Open file" opens on the host machine and fails silently (no feedback)
discussions.body:
## Summary
In the web UI, clicking a file path (e.g. a file mentioned in a conversation, or the "open file" action on a tool result) does not open the file on the **user's** machine. It instead triggers `host.openPath` which opens the file on the **host server** machine, and the call is wrapped in a silent catch so the user gets no feedback at all.

## Evidence (from the published package, line numbers from the bundled build)
- `dsh-client-ui-conversation/lib/client.js` ~line 9731-9734: `openFile` calls `workspaces.openPath(resolveWorkspacePath(cwd, path)).catch(() => {})` — the `.catch(() => {})` **swallows every error silently**.
- `dsh-client-runtime/lib/client.js` ~line 9993-9996: `openPath` invokes `api.host.openPath({ path })`, which on the host runs a native "open with default app" (`openNativePath` in `dsh-host-apiproxy/lib/index.js` ~line 2346-2365).

## Impact
- On a **localhost** deployment the host *is* the user's machine, so it may work by accident — but still silently.
- On a **remote web** deployment the file is opened on the server, which the user cannot see/access — the click appears to do nothing. Combined with the silent catch, there is zero feedback.

## Suggested fix
- Web clients should not map "open file" to a host-native open. Options:
  - open the path in a workspace-relative view / offer "copy path" + "download", or
  - at minimum remove the `.catch(() => {})` and surface a clear message ("opened on host" or "use the desktop client").
- The open semantics should be explicit per client kind (web vs desktop).

Happy to PR if you point at the preferred behavior.

discussions.title: [web] Windows path separator mishandled in resolveWorkspacePath (mixed back/forward slashes)
discussions.body:
## Summary
`resolveWorkspacePath` always joins with a forward slash, producing mixed-separator paths like `C:\Users\foo/bar` on Windows. It relies on the host's tolerance for mixed slashes, which is fragile.

## Evidence (from the published package)
`dsh-client-runtime/lib/client.js` ~line 10302-10306:
```js
function resolveWorkspacePath(cwd, path) {
  if (path.startsWith("/") || /^[A-Za-z]:[/\\]/.test(path) || path.startsWith("\\\\")) return path;
  if (cwd === void 0 || cwd === "") return path;
  return `${cwd.replace(/[/\\]+$/, "")}/${path.replace(/^[/\\]+/, "")}`;
}
```
The final `/` is hardcoded and not platform-aware.

## Impact
On Windows workspaces, relative file paths are resolved to `C:\a/b` style strings. `host.openPath` / tools that consume the path may mishandle the mixed separators depending on the downstream API, causing "file not found" or wrong-file bugs that are hard to trace.

## Suggested fix
Pick the separator from the host platform (or from `cwd`'s drive), or better: send the raw `cwd` + relative `path` to the host and let it `path.resolve` on the correct platform. Avoid hardcoding `/` in the client.

(Note: the host-side `dsh-host-directory-picker-browse` already uses platform-correct `join`/`resolve`, so the normalization belongs there.)

discussions.title: [web] Transport errors hide host error details, making web failures hard to diagnose
discussions.body:
## Summary
When the host returns a non-2xx (e.g. 500) or a network error, the web client throws a generic "transport failure ... HTTP 500" message with no server-side detail, making web failures very hard to diagnose.

## Evidence (from the published package)
`dsh-client-connection/lib/client.js` ~line 6190-6199:
```js
if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`transport failure for ${path}: HTTP ${response.status}`);
```
The response body (which often contains the actual error / stack) is never read.

Business errors are correctly returned as `200 + { result: { ok: false, error } }` and surfaced properly — the gap is only at the transport layer (5xx / network). But in practice web-only problems (picker failures, workspace creation hanging behind a hidden OS dialog, `host.openPath` issues) are exactly the ones that land here and become undebuggable.

## Impact
Web users and maintainers cannot tell *why* an action failed; they only see a generic HTTP status. Combined with web-specific flows (see the directory-picker discussion), this turns routine failures into black boxes.

## Suggested fix
On `!response.ok`, read `await response.text()` (or JSON) and append it to the thrown error so the cause propagates to the UI / logs. Optionally include the request path and method.

Happy to PR.
