discussions.body:
**dsh-read-confine**：读取隔离插件——补上自带沙箱"读取始终放行"的缺口。

仓库：https://github.com/SummerXaa-Z/dsh-read-confine （MIT，macOS）

动机：自带 provider 只围栏写入——`dsh-fs-sandbox` 明示"所有模式都允许读取"，自带 Seatbelt profile 没有读规则。OS 用户能读的文件 agent 都能读：SSH 私钥、云凭据、浏览器状态。可达鸭用工作区外诱饵文件实测证实（read 工具和 bash 双路径均成功）。

本包在两条面向模型的路径上同时加读取围栏：

- `dsh-read-confine`（替换 `sandbox`）：Seatbelt profile 增加 `(deny file-read* (subpath $HOME))` + 白名单回允，内核级拦截。
- `dsh-read-confine/fs`（替换 `fs-sandbox`）：继承官方 `SandboxedFileSystem`，为 readText/streamText/readBytes/listDir/stat 加 $HOME 读围栏，拒绝走结构化 `FS_SANDBOX_DENIED`，模型看到的拒绝标记与写围栏同款。

威胁模型的刻意取舍：只围栏 $HOME（系统库/工具链保持可读），`danger-full-access` 不拦。软链按真实目标判定（先 canonicalize 再决策），默认白名单含 `~/Workspaces` 以兼容软链 skill 库。

rc.6 实测：诱饵文件 read/bash 双路径均被拒；工作区写+执行回归正常；项目级 skill 发现（含软链库）正常。

与 [dsh-credentials-keychain](https://github.com/SummerXaa-Z/dsh-credentials-keychain)（#1129）互补：一个管 dsh 自己的凭据，一个管用户的机密。

discussions.title: [Control flow] Hook continue:false is recorded but does not halt agent runs
discussions.body:
## Summary

Both `@deepseek-ai/dsh-hooks-codex` and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-hooks-claude-code` parse and durably record a hook response containing `{"continue": false}`, but official `master` does not act on the merged stop request. A PreToolUse hook can therefore request a hard halt, produce a `hook/result` with decision `stop`, and still allow the tool and the rest of the turn to run.

I reproduced the control-flow mismatch with failing regression tests and prepared a tested fix in a public fork. Since the upstream repository does not expose external pull-request creation, I am sharing the complete patch here according to the repository's contribution workflow.

## Reproduction

Configure either bridge with a PreToolUse command hook that prints:

```json
{"continue": false, "stopReason": "halt"}
```

Then run an agent turn whose first model response calls the matched tool.

Before the fix, both bridge regressions failed on official `master` at the same assertion:

```text
expected tool execution flag to be false, received true
```

The session log contained `hook/result.decision === "stop"`, yet the tool ran and the turn completed normally. The targeted failing commands were:

```bash
pnpm exec vitest run packages/hooks/hooks-codex/tests/coverage-prompt.spec.ts -t 'continue.*false.*PreToolUse hook halts'
pnpm exec vitest run packages/hooks/hooks-claude-code/tests/coverage-context.spec.ts -t 'continue.*false.*PreToolUse hook halts'
```

## Root cause

`mergeHookOutputs()` correctly folds the first `continue:false` into `MergedHookOutcome.stop` and preserves `stopReason`. Each bridge then maps permission decisions and context but ignores `merged.stop`; the source carried an explicit `TODO(hook-continue-false)` saying that a run-level halt mechanism was still needed.

The agent loop now exposes that mechanism through `Agent.cancel({ kind: 'hook', reason })`, including a durable aborted turn reason. The bridge code had not been updated to use it.

## Impact

Hook authors commonly use `continue:false` for policy, safety, or automation stop conditions. Recording the request without enforcing it can execute a tool the hook explicitly intended to prevent, issue another model request after a post-tool halt, or force continuation from a Stop hook whose result also requested termination. The audit log and actual behavior disagree at a security-sensitive control boundary.

## Proposed fix

The patch adds a shared `createHookHaltController()` in `dsh-hook-protocol` and applies it consistently in both bridges:

- UserPromptSubmit cancels before the first model request.
- PreToolUse cancels the run and denies tool dispatch.
- PostToolUse preserves the already-produced tool result, then prevents another model request.
- Stop cancellation takes precedence over block steering, so it cannot accidentally force another step.
- Detached SessionStart results cancel an active first request; if they arrive while the agent is idle, a weakly keyed one-shot halt is consumed at the first pre-step instead of being lost to the intentional idle no-op of `Agent.cancel()`.
- Claude SubagentStart/SubagentStop halts target the scoped delegating parent when the lifecycle carrier exposes it, rather than an already-settled child.
- `stopReason` becomes the durable hook cancellation reason, with `stopped by <Event> hook` as a deterministic fallback.

`continue:false` takes precedence over deny/ask/context output at the same point. Integration coverage verifies all active boundaries, preserved post-tool results, absence of subsequent model requests, the SessionStart timing path, scoped subagent cancellation, and the exact aborted turn reason. The shared idle latch also has focused unit coverage.

## Patch

- Commit: [`8e79b5390632a40abb31b8d3b2070346d3bd151d`](https://github.com/Lzb-gzist/deepseek-harness/commit/8e79b5390632a40abb31b8d3b2070346d3bd151d)
- Full comparison against official master: [deepseek-ai:master...Lzb-gzist:agent/hooks-honor-continue-false](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/compare/master...Lzb-gzist:agent/hooks-honor-continue-false?expand=1)
- Fork branch: `agent/hooks-honor-continue-false`

## Validation

- Initial Codex and Claude Code regression tests failed on official master because the tool still executed.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/hooks/hook-protocol/tests packages/hooks/hooks-codex/tests packages/hooks/hooks-claude-code/tests` — 19 files, 217 tests passed.
- `pnpm run typecheck` — passed, including the pre-push rerun.
- `pnpm run lint` / final `pnpm run lint:contracts-ready` — passed.
- `pnpm run duplication` — zero clones.
- `pnpm run doc-sync` — 28/28 gates passed.
- Repository pre-commit translation pairing, staged lint, whitespace, and vendor guard — passed.

I would appreciate maintainer feedback on whether this cancellation mapping matches the intended Codex and Claude Code compatibility semantics.

discussions.title: Bug: tool calls crash with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')" after profile plugin install (dual dsh-tools copy)
discussions.body:
## Summary

On 0.1.0-rc.6, **every tool call in a session fails** after a profile installs plugins via `pnpm install`. The turn ends with:

```
Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')   (code: UNKNOWN)
```

No `tool/result` is ever produced; the failure happens right after the `tool/call` event is appended.

## Repro

1. Desktop app (host bundles `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools@0.1.0-rc.5`).
2. Install profile plugins: `cd ~/.dsh/profiles/web && pnpm install` — this lifts `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools@0.1.0-rc.6` (plus `cordis`, `dsh-subprocess`, `dsh-commands`) into `~/.dsh/profiles/web/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/`.
3. Start a session and ask the agent to call any tool (e.g. `bash`). The turn fails immediately.

Works fine before the profile install and in the `headless` profile (no profile `node_modules`).

## Root cause

`TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER` is a non-global `Symbol` (`packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:466`). `dsh-agent-loop` (host copy, rc.5) imports it from its own copy, while `ctx.tools` is a `ToolRuntime` built from the profile copy (rc.6). `ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER]` is therefore `undefined`, and `startCall` throws at `packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts:169` (`ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER].prepare(call.exec)`).

`cordis` already uses `Symbol.for('cordis.isolate')` for cross-copy isolation; `dsh-tools` does not follow that pattern.

## Proposed fix (branch available)

`tsonglew/deepseek-harness@fix/tool-runtime-scheduler-symbol-for` changes `TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER` and `createExecutionToken()` to `Symbol.for(...)`. Since external PRs are currently not accepted, I am sharing it here for the team to pick up.

## Independent observation

In the same environment, profile plugins (`dsh-worktree`, `dsh-find-plugin`, ...) fail to load with `cannot get property "tools" without inject` when they resolve `@deepseek-ai/cordis` from the profile copy. A boot-time version-drift check between host and profile `@deepseek-ai/*` packages would surface both failure classes with a clear message.

discussions.title: Make network access a separate sandbox permission
discussions.body:
## Problem

The local sandbox has a clear filesystem policy, but network access is outside its enforcement contract. That makes `workspace-write` mean different things on different platforms.

On platforms where the restricted process keeps normal network access, a model can reach arbitrary hosts even though its file writes are limited. On Windows, the current restricted-token backend can remove outbound access entirely, as reported in [#1157](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1157). A user who needs `npm install`, `git fetch`, or a local development server should not have to switch the whole call to `danger-full-access` just to get network access.

Loopback also needs its own rule. [#250](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/250) shows why a sandboxed process reaching the Harness control plane is different from reaching a package registry.

## Proposal

Make process network access a separate sandbox permission. A tool call should be able to request `workspace-write` together with a bounded network policy.

A first contract could distinguish:

- `inherit`: preserve today's platform behavior
- `deny`: block outbound and loopback connections
- `allow`: permit declared destinations and deny everything else

Loopback should be explicit rather than included in a broad network grant. Providers should report whether they enforced the requested policy fully, partially, or not at all. A profile should also be able to fail closed when the selected backend cannot enforce it.

## How I would implement it

I would split this into two stages.

The first stage would add the provider-neutral policy, enforcement reporting, approvals, and a reliable `deny` mode. This gives every consumer one contract and removes silent platform differences.

The second stage would add destination allowlists through a local network broker. The sandboxed process would only reach the broker, and the broker would enforce host, port, DNS resolution, and loopback rules. That avoids putting domain matching into Seatbelt, Landlock, Windows ACL, or every shell integration separately.

The same policy should cover Bash, PowerShell, persistent terminals, Code Mode workers, and workflow children. Host-side tools such as `web_search` can keep their own policy because they do not run inside the model-side process sandbox.

## Acceptance criteria

- `workspace-write` plus `deny` cannot reach public addresses or the Harness loopback control plane.
- A bounded grant can allow an approved destination without widening filesystem access.
- Loopback requires a separate grant.
- Unsupported enforcement is visible in the tool result and can fail closed by profile policy.
- Bash, PowerShell, terminals, Code Mode, and workflow children apply the same network contract.
- The sandbox documentation includes a platform matrix for filesystem and network enforcement.

The current filesystem-only scope is documented in [the sandbox subsystem](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/subsystems/sandbox.md). This proposal keeps that boundary explicit while adding a separate capability for network access.

discussions.title: Run workflows as managed jobs with progress and cancellation
discussions.body:
## Problem

The `workflow` tool runs in the foreground and returns only after its worker finishes. While it is running, the parent agent cannot do other work. Cancellation also loses the partial result, and there is no supported way to inspect the active phases or continue from a completed phase.

This is a rough edge for the kind of fan-out work the tool is designed for. A ten-minute research or review workflow should not make the parent session look stuck.

## Proposal

Let a workflow run as a managed job through the existing jobs subsystem.

An optional background mode could return a job id immediately. The existing job tools could then expose status, recent logs, the active phase, completed branches, failures, and the final result. Killing the job should cancel the worker and every child agent, then settle the job once.

Foreground behavior should remain unchanged for callers that want one blocking result.

## How I would implement it

1. Add a workflow job producer that owns the worker and its child agents.
2. Emit structured progress records for phase start, phase completion, agent start, agent completion, log output, and the final result.
3. Store bounded recent output in the job snapshot, with the full durable trace in the session log.
4. Route cancellation through the jobs lifecycle so owner teardown and explicit `job_kill` use the same cleanup path.
5. Persist completed `phase()` outputs as checkpoints. Arbitrary JavaScript stacks cannot be resumed safely, so the first resumable contract should restart only from an explicit phase boundary.

The existing [jobs subsystem](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/subsystems/jobs.md) already owns most of the lifecycle rules. The workflow package would become a producer instead of inventing another background-task API.

## Acceptance criteria

- Background workflow start returns a job id without blocking the parent turn.
- `job_read` and `job_wait` expose the current phase, branch outcomes, and bounded logs.
- `job_kill` cancels the worker and all live children without duplicate completion notices.
- Session or service teardown waits for cleanup and leaves no orphan children.
- The final background result matches the current foreground result shape.
- Foreground workflow behavior remains compatible.
- A workflow written with explicit `phase()` boundaries can restart from the last completed checkpoint after interruption.

The current behavior is described in the [workflow tool README](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/packages/workflow/tool-workflow/README.md).

discussions.title: Add a session doctor and versioned migrations
discussions.body:
## Problem

The session format is still version `0`, and the persistence layer correctly refuses formats it cannot read. That is safe, but there is no user-facing migration or recovery path yet.

Recent reports show the practical cost of this gap. A malformed or interrupted JSONL log can make a session unreadable, and in some cases one bad session can stop a workspace from loading. Examples include [#496](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/496), [#647](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/647), [#1452](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1452), [#1473](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1473), and [#1497](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1497).

Fixing each writer is necessary, but users also need a supported way to inspect and recover durable history before the format starts changing between releases.

## Proposal

Add an offline session doctor and a versioned migration pipeline.

Possible commands:

```text
dsh session doctor <session-id> --check
dsh session doctor <session-id> --repair --output <new-path>
dsh session migrate <session-id> --to <version> --output <new-path>
```

Repair and migration should write a new artifact by default. They should not overwrite the source log. The command should produce a machine-readable receipt listing the detected invariants, applied repairs, dropped or synthesized events, source hash, and output hash.

## How I would implement it

The doctor should use the same event decoder and invariants as normal persistence. It can classify failures such as a torn tail, duplicate sequence, gap, unsupported event type, invalid synthetic closer, or a version mismatch.

Repairs should be explicit transforms with narrow preconditions. A transform that cannot prove a safe result should stop and explain the remaining problem instead of guessing.

Format migrations should be pure, versioned `SessionEvent` transforms. Each migration should be repeatable, tested against frozen fixtures, and able to emit the same audit receipt as a repair.

At workspace startup, one unreadable session should be quarantined and reported rather than preventing unrelated sessions from loading. The UI can then offer the doctor command or export the failing log.

## Acceptance criteria

- `--check` never changes data and reports the first broken invariant plus its event position.
- `--repair` and `migrate` preserve the source and write a separate output artifact.
- Every change appears in a JSON receipt with source and output hashes.
- Repairs are deterministic and covered by fixtures for known JSONL failure modes.
- An unreadable session does not prevent the rest of the workspace from loading.
- A format bump ships with an explicit migration from the previous supported version.

The current refusal behavior is documented in [the persistence subsystem](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/subsystems/persistence.md).

discussions.title: Bug + tested fix: truncated tool-call arguments permanently poison a session (llm-deepseek serializer)
discussions.body:
**The bug:** when a tool call'\''s generation is truncated mid-arguments (or the model emits malformed JSON), `serializeAssistant` in `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/serialize.ts` replays `block.arguments` verbatim on every subsequent turn. Servers that re-parse tool calls while rendering the chat template then reject **every later request of that session** — vLLM with `Expecting '\'','\'' delimiter` and llama.cpp with `[json.exception.parse_error.101]` — so no retry can ever succeed and the session is permanently stuck in an error loop. Observed in production with a ~13.6k-char subagent tool call truncated mid-string.

**The fix (tested):** validate arguments with `JSON.parse` at serialization and substitute `"{}"` when unparsable; valid arguments pass through untouched. The paired tool result already records what happened, and previously-poisoned sessions become usable again on their next request.

Since PRs and issues appear to be closed on this repo, the full change (plus a regression test in `tests/serialize.spec.ts`; suite passes 28/28) is on this branch:
https://github.com/brianmswheart/deepseek-harness/tree/fix/sanitize-replayed-tool-call-arguments — happy to reformat it however contributions are meant to flow.

*Written with assistance from Claude Code.*

discussions.body:
"## 中文版（主）

# 实测：DSH WebUI 长任务下 100% 缓存命中

## 环境

- **DSH 版本**：0.1 开发者预览版（2026-08-13 开源）
- **运行模式**：`dsh web`（Web UI）
- **模型**：`deepseek-v4-flash`（High reasoning effort）
- **权限**：`Full access`
- **任务**：单次长会话，含 3 轮 / 231 步工具调用

## 数据截图

![DSH WebUI long task: 100% cache hit rate (3 turns / 231 steps / 33.9M input tokens)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ccch713/dsh-feedback-assets/main/cache-hit-100-webui-231steps.png)

截图右下角指标：

| 指标 | 数值 |
|---|---|
| 轮次 | 3 |
| 步数 | 231 |
| LLM 推理耗时 | 24m 21s |
| 工具调用耗时 | 8m 58s |
| 首 token 延迟 | 平均 1.3s |
| 输出吞吐 | 141 tok/s |
| **缓存命中率** | **100%** |
| 累计输入 token | 33.9M |

## 观察

1. **缓存命中 100%** 在 231 步的长任务中保持稳定，无任何一次 cache miss。说明 DSH 的"运行期间永不重新读取"不变量（README §"前缀稳定缓存"）在 WebUI 模式下也成立。
2. **首 token 1.3s 平均延迟** —— 比预想快。可能因为 prefix cache 命中后 KV cache 已预热，无需重新计算 attention。
3. **141 tok/s 输出** —— 与 deepseek-v4-flash 在裸 API 调用下的速率一致，说明 prefix cache 没有影响生成速度。
4. **LLM 24m / 工具 8m** —— 工具调用时间占比约 27%，对长任务而言可控。

## 建议（可选）

- 考虑在 WebUI 任务栏把"缓存命中率"做成可点击下钻 —— 跳转到该会话的事件日志（session/event log），按 `turn/*` 和 `step/*` 维度分别统计，区分"prompt prefix cache"和"tool-result cache"。
- 当前"缓存命中 100%"是无单位指标，建议标注是 `cached_tokens / total_input_tokens`，方便用户估算成本节省。

## 复现步骤

1. `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web`
2. 选择 `deepseek-v4-flash`，reasoning effort 设为 `High`
3. 启动一个长任务（建议 ≥ 100 步），观察右下角指标

---

## English version (summary)

# Measured: 100% cache hit rate on long WebUI task

## Setup

- **DSH version**: 0.1 developer preview (released 2026-08-13)
- **Mode**: `dsh web` (Web UI)
- **Model**: `deepseek-v4-flash` with `High` reasoning effort
- **Permission**: Full access
- **Workload**: single long session, 3 turns / 231 steps

## Numbers (see attached screenshot)

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Turns | 3 |
| Steps | 231 |
| LLM time | 24m 21s |
| Tool time | 8m 58s |
| First-token latency (avg) | 1.3s |
| Output throughput | 141 tok/s |
| **Cache hit rate** | **100%** |
| Cumulative input tokens | 33.9M |

## Observations

The "never re-read during a run" invariant holds in WebUI mode — no cache miss across 231 steps. First-token latency stays at ~1.3s average, suggesting the prefix cache keeps the KV cache warm across turns.

## Suggestions

- Make the "cache hit rate" clickable to drill into the session event log, broken down by `turn/*` and `step/*`.
- Add unit (currently unitless) — e.g. `cached_tokens / total_input_tokens` — so users can estimate cost savings.

cc @deepseek-ai — feedback on the 0.1 preview."

discussions.title: [Control flow] Claude Stop hooks can force unbounded continuations
discussions.body:
## Summary

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-hooks-claude-code` currently lets a blocking `Stop` hook force another model request without tracking consecutive blocks. An unconditional hook can therefore keep the same turn alive indefinitely, consuming model requests and tokens until some external limit intervenes. The payload also always reports `stop_hook_active: false`, so a hook cannot detect that it is running because of its own prior block.

Claude Code's documented behavior marks Stop-hook re-entry with `stop_hook_active` and overrides the hook after eight consecutive blocks by default. I reproduced the mismatch against official `master` and prepared a tested fix in a public fork. Since this repository does not expose external pull-request creation, I am sharing the complete patch here according to the repository's contribution workflow.

## Reproduction

Configure a `Stop` command hook that always exits with code 2:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "keep working" >&2
exit 2
```

Run an agent with nine otherwise-completing mock model responses, then assert that the bridge performs at most nine requests: the initial request plus eight forced continuations.

On official `master`, the regression failed because the bridge attempted a tenth request and stopped only when the mock response script was exhausted:

```text
AssertionError: expected [ ...10 requests... ] to have a length of 9 but got 10
```

The focused failing command was:

```bash
pnpm exec vitest run packages/hooks/hooks-claude-code/tests/coverage-stop.spec.ts -t 'caps an unconditional Stop hook'
```

## Root cause

The `agent/turn-stopping` listener runs the `Stop` point and calls `agent.steer()` after every blocking result, but it retains no per-agent or per-turn continuation state. `stopPayload()` also hardcodes `stop_hook_active: false`. Consequently, each forced stopping boundary is indistinguishable from the first one and no block cap can be enforced.

## Proposed fix

The patch:

- tracks consecutive blocking Stop results in a `WeakMap`, scoped to the exact agent and open turn;
- sends `stop_hook_active: false` on the first attempt and `true` on re-entry;
- resets the chain after a non-blocking result or a new turn;
- allows the turn to stop after eight consecutive blocks by default and records a warning;
- adds a validated positive-integer `stopHookBlockCap` plugin setting for deployments that need a different bound.

The configuration difference is explicit: this bridge uses `stopHookBlockCap`; it does not claim to consume Claude Code's `CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP` environment variable. The cap warning is currently logger-visible rather than injected into user chat.

## Verification

New regression coverage verifies:

- an unconditional Stop hook runs eight times and the turn completes after nine model requests;
- re-entry payloads are `[false, true]` and a later user turn resets to `[false, true]`;
- a configured cap of 1 is honored;
- zero, negative, fractional, and `NaN` cap values fail at load.

Full validation completed successfully:

```text
Hook protocol + Claude bridge tests: 13 files, 149 tests passed
lint: passed
typecheck: passed (including pre-push hook)
doc-sync: 28 passed, 0 failed
duplication: 0 clones
git diff --check: passed
```

## Patch

- Compare: https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/compare/master...Lzb-gzist:agent/hooks-stop-loop-guard
- Commit: https://github.com/Lzb-gzist/deepseek-harness/commit/9fa02a9d149d203057dc0e0cfd0ca1036d59a327
- Branch: `Lzb-gzist:agent/hooks-stop-loop-guard`

The behavior is based on Claude Code's official hook documentation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks

discussions.title: [Windows] Directory picker unusable: native win32 dialog worker crashes; browse backend's client UI never renders
discussions.body:
# [Windows] Directory picker unusable: native win32 dialog worker crashes, and the browse backend's client UI never renders

## Summary

On Windows, the workspace directory picker is completely unusable in the web UI (both `web` and any flow that adds a workspace). Clicking "Add workspace" / "Select workspace" surfaces an error instead of a picker. Switching the backend from `-auto` to `-browse` via `cordis.patch.yml` loads the browse backend correctly (confirmed via `--dump-config`), but the in-app directory-browser dialog still never renders in the client.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 (build 10.0.26200.9168), zh-CN locale
- Node: v24.18.0, pnpm 11.21.0
- dsh: 0.1.0-rc.5 (built from source at `deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness`, commit 2026-08-13)
- Launch: `pnpm dsh web` (default `web` profile)

## Steps to reproduce

1. `pnpm dsh web` → open http://127.0.0.1:3080
2. Click the "Add workspace" button in the sidebar (or "Select workspace" under the hero title)

## Actual behavior

A dialog appears with:

```
无法打开文件夹 (Cannot open folder)
directory picker failed: win32 folder dialog worker exited before reporting a result
```

The native win32 folder dialog worker process exits before returning a result, so no directory can ever be selected. Workspace creation via the GUI is impossible.

## Root cause analysis (so far)

**Layer 1 — `directory-picker-auto` always picks `native` on Windows.**

`packages/host/directory-picker-auto/src/resolve.ts` only consults a Linux chooser probe (`zenity`/`kdialog`); on any other platform (incl. Windows) it resolves to `native`. The native backend spawns a "win32 folder dialog worker" which crashes on this machine (the exact spawn/exit reason is not surfaced by the error message).

**Layer 2 — the `browse` backend mounts, but its client UI never renders.**

As a workaround I pinned the backend in `packages/bundle/web-app/cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: directory-picker
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-directory-picker-browse'
```

Verified the running config tree actually loads browse:

```
$ pnpm dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep -A1 'id: directory-picker'
- id: directory-picker
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-directory-picker-browse'
```

Service is healthy (HTTP 200, no errors in the server log; `apps/web` rebuilt). Yet clicking "Add workspace" produces no dialog, no DOM dialog element appears (`document.querySelectorAll('dialog,[role=dialog]')` → 0), and the browser console shows no JS errors. The client's directory-flow UI (`ui-workspace` holes) appears not to mount for the `browse` capability.

## Expected behavior

- Windows users should be able to add a workspace from the GUI (either the native dialog works, or the in-app directory browser opens), or at minimum the auto resolver should fall back to `browse` when the native worker fails.

## Suggested fixes

1. **`directory-picker-auto`: probe the native backend health on Windows** (e.g. try spawning the dialog worker once at boot; on failure fall back to `browse`). Right now Windows can never fall back because the resolver hard-codes `native`.
2. **Surface the native worker's real exit reason** — the current error string (`win32 folder dialog worker exited before reporting a result`) hides whether it's a spawn failure, a missing dependency, or a worker crash. A diagnostic payload (exit code + stderr) would help.
3. **Investigate why the browse client UI doesn't mount** when the backend is `browse` — `ui-workspace`'s directory-flow contribution seems to not activate, so users on Windows have *no* working path to add a workspace through the GUI.

## Workaround (for other Windows users)

For now, Windows users cannot add a workspace via the GUI. A CLI/config-level way to register a workspace (or a `--cwd` on session create) would be an acceptable interim.

Happy to provide more logs or run diagnostics if useful. Thanks for the great project — the plugin architecture is genuinely impressive.

discussions.title: Agent preset selection is silently lost when switching workspace on the new-session screen
discussions.body:
# Agent preset selection is silently lost when switching workspace on the new-session screen

## Summary

On the new-session screen, picking a non-default agent preset and then switching the workspace **before** creating the session silently discards the pick: the session is created with the deployment default preset instead. The preset chip may keep showing the picked preset (state/display desynchronization), so the user sees "selected" while the session actually runs the default — there is no error anywhere.

## Environment

- dsh `0.1.0-rc.6` (web profile)
- Browser: Chrome 151, driven via chrome-devtools-mcp 1.7.0 (CDP) for the reproduction
- A user-authored preset exists at `~/.dsh/.agent-presets/v4-mcp-test/` (one `dsh-mcp-client` row, serverName `testp`), so the preset picker has a non-default option

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the new-session screen (workspace picker + preset chip are side by side).
2. Click the preset chip (default "标准模式" / standard) and pick a non-default preset (e.g. `v4-mcp-test`). The chip label updates.
3. Click "选择工作区" (choose workspace) and switch to a different workspace.
4. Type a first message and send it (this creates/activates the session).
5. Inspect the created session's persisted header (`session.jsonl.zstd` first line) → `"agentPreset":"standard"`, **not** the picked preset.

Control run with the reversed order works: switch workspace **first**, then pick the preset, then send → the session header records the picked preset.

## Expected vs actual

Expected: the session is created with the preset picked on the new-session screen, regardless of the order of workspace switching.

| Order of operations | Persisted `agentPreset` |
|---|---|
| switch workspace → pick preset → send | picked preset ✅ |
| pick preset → switch workspace → send | default (`standard`) ❌ |

Network evidence (CDP request log during the failing sequence): `agentPreset.list` is called (roster re-reads), but **`agentPreset.select` is never called** — not on the pick, not on the workspace switch, not on session creation. The session-creating call `session.prompt` carries no preset field at all — the preset is expected to reach the session through the front-end staged state.

## Evidence (inline)

Failing session — persisted header created by the "pick → switch workspace → send" sequence (event stream contains only this line; no `agent-preset/selected` event):

```json
{"type":"session","version":0,"id":"session-47ffa312-c1cf-41a8-a598-751780f86c07","createdAt":1786724713886,"cwd":"F:\\Project\\DeepSeekHarness\\dsh-project-mcp-bridge","delegationDepth":0,"agentPreset":"standard"}
```

Control session — same user preset via the host default path (`agent-presets.default`), header records it:

```json
{"type":"session","version":0,"id":"session-1354ac64-1aa7-4b21-b500-cde83d40f3f6","createdAt":1786723481633,"cwd":"F:\\Project\\DeepSeekHarness\\mcp-v4-test","delegationDepth":0,"agentPreset":"v4-mcp-test"}
```

Session-creating request during the failing sequence — no preset field; the only preset-related traffic was `agentPreset.list`, never `agentPreset.select`:

```json
{"type":"client-request","rpcId":"baeec506-d26d-445e-81e7-04655650c191","method":"session.prompt","payload":{"sessionId":"session-47ffa312-c1cf-41a8-a598-751780f86c07","mode":"queue","content":[{"type":"text","text":"你好"}],"clientTimeZone":"Asia/Shanghai"}}
```

## Likely cause (front-end, `dsh-client-ui-agent-preset`)

The new-session preset chip is driven by the seat controller, whose contract is "stage a pick for the NEXT session, apply it when a (blank) session becomes current" (see `AgentPresetSeatController` docs: "The new-session screen has no session, so a pick is staged rather than applied. It reaches a session when one becomes current and is still blank… The stage is forgotten once applied.").

The stage is consumed (or silently dropped) by the apply path:

```js
async apply() {
    const staged = this.staged;
    const session = this.currentSession();
    if (staged === void 0 || session === void 0) return;
    if (!session.blank || session.agentPreset === staged) {
        this.staged = void 0;   // silently discarded, display NOT reverted
        return;
    }
    await this.api.agentPresets.select({ sessionId: session.id, agentPreset: staged });
}
```

Switching the workspace changes the current-session placeholder (each workspace has its own blank "new session"), which can fire the list-change applier against a placeholder judged unservable — the stage is cleared without a `select` call. Depending on the interleaving with `load()` (which re-reads the roster after the switch), the chip either reverts to the default or keeps showing the staged pick while the stage is already gone — hence the "selected but not applied" illusion and the intermittent display behavior observed during reproduction.

## Impact

Users who pick a preset and then switch the workspace (a natural order — the two controls sit side by side) get a session running the default preset with zero feedback. The chip display can lie (still showing the picked preset), so the mismatch may go unnoticed until the session's behavior shows it.

## Workarounds

- Pick the preset **after** switching the workspace (verified stable).
- Use `settings` → agent-presets default (`agent-presets.default`), resolved by the host at session creation and unaffected by the staged-state path.

discussions.title: DeepSeek Harness Desktop：已签名公证的 macOS 包 / 零添加的壳 / 想把「↑ 翻历史」提给上游
discussions.body:
> A signed & notarized macOS build of a minimal desktop shell for dsh — plus one composer feature I'd like to upstream if you want it.

桌面壳这两天已经有很多位在做了，我这个的不同点只有三处，说完就走。

## 1）macOS 包已签名并通过 Apple 公证

不会弹「无法验证开发者」，普通用户双击即用。Windows 包目前**没有**签名，SmartScreen 会拦一次（我在下载页和文章里都写明了）。

- macOS · Apple Silicon：https://pub-add8d85a6fb44ae89097b7abb5a05ca9.r2.dev/v0.1.0/dshd-0.1.0-arm64.dmg
- Windows · x64：https://pub-add8d85a6fb44ae89097b7abb5a05ca9.r2.dev/v0.1.0/dshd_0.1.0_x64-setup.exe
- 源码（自官方 fork）：https://github.com/Octo-o-o-o/deepseek-harness-desktop

壳用 Tauri。**特意没有去实现 `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-19-gui-layering-and-rpc-protocol` 里给将来 Electron 应用预留的 IPC 载体**——那个座位是官方的，我只包住今天已经发布的 web 形态。官方桌面端出来之后，这个壳就该退役。

## 2）除了壳必须干的活，一个功能都没加

审批时的系统通知、手机连接桌面、快速截图、剪贴板监听、技能导入导出——都不难做，我一个都没做。仓库里的取舍纪律很清楚，给它做壳的人应该守同一条线：壳只让人坐得舒服，不替内核做决定。

## 3）唯一的例外是一个键，也正是我想提给上游的东西

在输入框最开头按 `↑`，从新到旧召回本会话自己发过的提问；`↓` 往回走并恢复开始召回时的草稿。实现在 `packages/client/ui-conversation`（`src/client/input/prompt-history.ts`），契约已按仓库惯例写进包 README 的中英双语正文：

- 触发菜单打开时箭头归菜单，只有菜单交回按键才表示召回
- 召回一旦开始，光标位置不再参与判断；停在最旧一条不回绕
- 编辑草稿或发送即结束本次召回
- steering 消息计入提问；纯图片与纯空白跳过；相邻重复合并
- 只读或处于 pending lock 的输入框拒绝召回

**如果你们觉得这个值得进主干，我按仓库门禁（测试 + Agent Note + 翻译配对）整理成 PR 提上来；不需要的话我就留在自己的 fork 里，不占你们的时间。**

---

最后：这是非官方社区项目，与 DeepSeek 无关联，内核是官方 MIT 代码、能力与插件体系一概不动。用它遇到的问题请先发我的仓库；只有能用 `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web` 复现的，我才会整理成最小复现来这里报，不给讨论区添噪音。

另有一篇我读完设计文档之后写的分析，讲我理解的「为什么官方此刻还没做桌面端」：https://blog.octoooo.com/posts/deepseek-harness-desktop/

discussions.title: [Lifecycle] Duplicate waiting subagent tool names can roll back late providers
discussions.body:
## Summary

Two live `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent` instances can currently declare the same model-facing `toolName` while both selected providers are absent. Both plugin fibers activate successfully and retain provider-lifecycle listeners. The conflict is discovered only later, when the second provider arrives and its listener attempts the duplicate tool registration.

That turns a local configuration error into a load-order-dependent provider-registration failure: a `provider-added` listener is allowed to unwind the provider registration transaction. I reproduced the missing early rejection against official `master` and prepared a tested fix in a public fork. Since this repository does not expose external pull-request creation, I am sharing the complete patch here according to the repository's contribution workflow.

## Reproduction

1. Load `dsh-system-prompt`, `dsh-tools`, and `dsh-subagent`.
2. Load `dsh-tool-subagent` with `{ provider: 'later-a', toolName: 'shared_subagent' }` while `later-a` is absent.
3. Load a second instance with `{ provider: 'later-b', toolName: 'shared_subagent' }` while `later-b` is absent.
4. Require step 3 to fail at its own plugin boundary, before either provider lifecycle is involved.

On official `master`, both instances activated. The focused regression failed with:

```text
AssertionError: expected 'undefined' to contain
'toolName "shared_subagent" is already reserved by another tool-subagent instance'
```

`undefined` is the captured load error: no error was raised. The focused command was:

```bash
pnpm exec vitest run packages/subagent/tool-subagent/tests/tool-subagent.spec.ts \
  -t 'reserves a toolName while providers are absent'
```

## Root cause

`dsh-tool-subagent` registers `subagent/provider-added` and `subagent/provider-removed` listeners before checking whether its selected provider exists, which is correct for sibling load-order independence. However, it does not reserve the eventual tool name at apply time. The only duplicate-name check is inside `ctx.tools.register()` in `mount(provider)`, so two waiting instances remain latent until provider arrival. At that point the error escapes the addition listener and can roll back the provider that triggered it.

Continuable instances happen to reserve a related prompt-section name, but one-shot instances have no equivalent early ownership record. Name validity should not depend on background mode or provider timing.

## Proposed fix

The patch adds an app-scoped intent registry for live `tool-subagent` names:

- a `WeakMap<Context, Set<string>>` is keyed by `ctx.root`, so separate applications in one process do not share names;
- each plugin fiber reserves its `toolName` before observing provider lifecycle events;
- a duplicate fails at the second plugin's apply boundary with an actionable error;
- the fiber's effect disposer releases exactly its reservation, preserving HMR and replacement;
- the ordinary tool registry remains the final backstop for collisions with other tool packages.

This keeps the existing reactive provider design: the model-facing tool still appears only while its selected provider exists, and its wording is still re-derived after provider reload.

## Verification

The new regression proves that:

- two absent-provider instances cannot reserve the same `toolName`;
- the earlier instance still mounts normally when its provider arrives;
- a later provider remains registered after the rejected duplicate instance;
- disposing the owner removes the tool and releases the name;
- a replacement instance can immediately reuse the released name and bind the already-present provider.

Full validation completed successfully:

```text
tool-subagent tests: 2 files, 69 tests passed
lint: passed
typecheck: passed (including pre-push hook)
doc-sync: 28 passed, 0 failed
duplication: 0 clones
git diff --check: passed
```

## Patch

- Compare: https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/compare/master...Lzb-gzist:agent/subagent-toolname-intent-reservation
- Commit: https://github.com/Lzb-gzist/deepseek-harness/commit/a0128dd2b03fe542150b0f09fb2f024723b26180
- Branch: `Lzb-gzist:agent/subagent-toolname-intent-reservation`

discussions.title: [Windows] subprocess-local 无 Job Object 保护：宿主死亡后子进程（rg 等）孤儿化，taskkill 事后补救不可靠
discussions.body:
## 现象

开发/长驻运行环境下，rg.exe 进程偶发大规模堆积（历史记录单次 4000+ 个，伴随等量 conhost.exe，提交内存逼近 100%）。仓库根目录的 watch-rg.ps1 / rg-watchdog.ps1 即为该事故的应急看门狗。

## 证据链

### 证据 1：grep 的 rg 走无沙箱的普通 spawn 路径

packages/fs/tool-fs-search/src/search-core.ts:184,227

    * The spawn is unconfined (a plain ctx.subprocess call), so --no-config ...
    handle = ctx.subprocess.spawn({
      argv: [await resolveRgPath(), "--no-config", ...argv],
      ...
    })

发行版基座 packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:164 将 subprocess seam 挂载为
@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-local —— 即 dsh web 宿主中 grep 的 rg 必然走 subprocess-local。

### 证据 2：沙箱路径有防孤儿机制，普通路径没有

| 路径 | 防孤儿手段 |
|---|---|
| 沙箱路径（runner.js） | ✅ kill-on-close Job Object：packages/sandbox/sandbox-windows-acl/src/spawn.ts:224-238，JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE，注释原文 "When the caller dies with the job handle open, Windows terminates every process in the job — the orphan-child backstop" |
| 普通路径（subprocess-local） | ❌ 无任何 Job Object 代码（grep 证实全源码零处 JobObject）；Windows 分支仅 spawn.ts:359-360（detached: platform !== "win32"）+ taskkill 事后补救 |

### 证据 3：事后补救本身有两个洞

packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/spawn.ts

    // 276-282
    export function taskkillProcessTree(pid: number): void {
      if (pid <= 0) return
      // Outcome deliberately unchecked: an already-absent tree (status 128), exit
      // races, and a missing taskkill binary (spawnSync reports, never throws) ...
      spawnSync("taskkill", ["/PID", String(pid), "/T", "/F"], { stdio: "ignore" })
    }

    // 386-389（treeAlive 的 Windows 分支）
    // Windows has no group-liveness probe; the direct child exit is the
    // observable boundary (taskkill /T already took the tree with it).

问题：① taskkill 失败（PID 复用、中间进程已退出导致树快照失真、二进制缺失）不重试、不记日志；
② treeAlive() 直接假设 taskkill 一定成功，失败时误判树已死。

## 泄漏机制

宿主 node 进程被 TerminateProcess（开发期 dev:web tsdown watch 重建、dsh web 宿主重启、扩展宿主重启、系统强杀）→ 无 Job Object 的 rg 收不到任何"父进程死亡"信号，立即孤儿化并永久存活。Windows 无父进程死亡信号，唯一根治手段是内核级 kill-on-close Job Object —— 沙箱路径已有，普通路径没有。

## 量级吻合性

- 本仓库 8 万+ 文件，rg 全仓搜索可运行数十秒，与宿主重启窗口碰撞概率高
- 每个孤儿 rg 是控制台子系统进程，Node 以管道 stdio spawn 时各拖一个 conhost —— 与历史观察 "+4000 conhost" 吻合
- 仅靠 taskkill 偶发失败无法堆积到四位数；宿主反复死亡才能解释该量级

## 已实证 / 未实证边界

- ✅ 已实证：上述三处代码缺口（行号级）；堆积现象（watch-rg.ps1 记录）；rg 由 harness 经 subprocess seam spawn（打包版 @vscode/ripgrep）
- ⏳ 未实证：某次堆积与某次宿主死亡的直接对应 —— 下次触发时运行 powershell -File watch-rg.ps1 -FindParents（按父进程分组，父进程 exited 即为孤儿铁证）

discussions.title: [Bug] Windows native folder picker truncates paths at characters whose UTF-16 low byte is 0x00 (e.g. 销 U+9500)
discussions.body:
环境: Windows · dsh 0.1.0-rc.6（最新版，master 分支同样存在）· web profile

现象: 在"新建项目"的 Windows 原生文件夹对话框中选择 ，报 workspace-invalid-path: cannot create a workspace at ENOENT。

复现: 任意含"销"(U+9500)、"一"(U+4E00)、"刀"(U+5200) 等码点以 00 结尾字符的目录名，经原生对话框选择后路径在该字符处被截断。

根因: packages/host/directory-picker-native/src/win32-dialog-bindings.ts 的 readUtf16 逐字节扫描 UTF-16 字符串，只检查低字节 bytes[end] !== 0（步长 2），把低字节为 0 的字符（如 销 = UTF-16LE 0x00 0x95）误判为结束符。

修复建议（已验证）: 检查完整 code unit：

while (end + 1 < bytes.length && (bytes[end] !== 0 || bytes[end + 1] !== 0)) end += 2

discussions.title: Proposal: integrate persistent token-usage tracking into DeepSeek Harness
discussions.body:
## Proposal

I built **[dsh-token-usage](https://github.com/LeemanCheung/dsh-token-usage)**, an MIT-licensed DeepSeek Harness plugin that provides persistent, privacy-preserving token-usage analytics. I would like to propose integrating this capability into the official project—either as an officially maintained optional plugin or as a built-in feature.

![Token usage dashboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LeemanCheung/dsh-token-usage/main/assets/token-usage-settings.png)

## What it provides

- Records the complete usage buckets: uncached input, output, cache read, and cache write tokens. `reasoningTokens` is already part of output usage and is not double-counted.
- Aggregates usage by provider/model, session, and UTC day across normal requests, retries, and context compaction.
- Avoids duplicate accounting when streaming usage is followed by final-message usage.
- Backfills readable historical sessions asynchronously without delaying startup.
- Adds a compact **Settings → Token usage** dashboard with summary cards, per-model totals, searchable session records, and a 30-week activity heatmap.
- Stores only aggregate usage buckets, dates, and model routes—never prompts, responses, or session contents.

## Why upstream integration could help

Token usage is fundamental observability for both personal and team DSH deployments. A first-party implementation would make the data model stable across providers, eliminate the need for each user to install and maintain a separate plugin, and give users visibility into cache effectiveness and consumption trends without compromising session privacy.

The plugin is already packaged as a standard DSH host projection plus Web settings UI and can be installed today with:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add github:LeemanCheung/dsh-token-usage
```

## Suggested path

1. Review it as an official optional plugin first, so the feature can evolve independently.
2. If appropriate, move the usage projection/event contracts into official packages and retain the dashboard as a maintained UI surface.
3. Define the desired data-retention, migration, and aggregation APIs together to ensure compatibility with future providers and clients.

I am happy to contribute the implementation, adapt it to the project conventions, split it into reviewable PRs, or transfer ownership if that makes integration easier. Feedback on the preferred scope and architecture would be very welcome.

Source: https://github.com/LeemanCheung/dsh-token-usage

discussions.title: dsh-instruction-audit: privacy-minimal receipts for effective workspace instructions
discussions.body:
I built [dsh-instruction-audit](https://github.com/1052326311/dsh-instruction-audit), an independent community bundle that records which `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` changes Harness actually injected into a session.

It observes the existing durable `agent-instructions` message source. Receipts contain only session/event metadata, logical scope, display path, action, and the source producer's digest. The bundle does not read instruction files, persist instruction text, modify a workspace, or change prompt assembly.

Release: [v0.1.0](https://github.com/1052326311/dsh-instruction-audit/releases/tag/v0.1.0)

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/1052326311/dsh-instruction-audit/releases/download/v0.1.0/dsh-instruction-audit-0.1.0.tgz
```

Verification used the packed release artifact in a fresh `DSH_HOME`: installed it with the plugin CLI, booted the real loopback Web profile, appended an `agent-instructions` user message through the real `SessionStore` publication path, and read the resulting receipt through the installed CLI. A distinct instruction-text sentinel was confirmed absent from persisted JSONL.

The project is tagged [`dsh-plugin`](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin). Feedback on the receipt shape or coverage of instruction-boundary cases is welcome.

discussions.title: [Bug] pwsh tool crashes with 0xC0000142 when falling back to Windows PowerShell 5.1 under the Windows ACL sandbox
discussions.body:
## 摘要 / Summary

Windows 上未安装 PowerShell 7 时，DSH 的 pwsh 工具会按 `resolvePwshPath` 的兜底逻辑回退到 Windows PowerShell 5.1（`C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe`）。在 Windows ACL 沙箱（`workspace-write` / `read-only`）下，5.1 **每次启动都以 `0xC0000142`（STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED）崩溃**：零输出、命令从未执行、前台与后台 100% 复现。沙箱外 5.1 运行完全正常。

## 环境 / Environment

- DSH 核心版本：`0.1.0-rc.6`（`@deepseek-ai/dsh`、`@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-windows-acl`、`@deepseek-ai/dsh-pwsh-local`）
- DSH Desktop 版本：`0.1.4`（DeepSeek Harness Desktop.exe）
- 操作系统：**Windows 11 专业版 Build 26200**（10.0.26200.0；与沙箱 README 的验证版本一致）
- PowerShell 7：**未安装**（`C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7` 不存在）；调查过程中安装过商店版（MSIX），见「补充证据」
- Windows PowerShell 5.1：正常（沙箱外 `powershell.exe -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command "Write-Output ok"` 正常输出 `ok`，排除 5.1 本身损坏）

## 复现步骤 / Repro

1. Windows 机器上不安装 PowerShell 7；
2. 在 DSH 任意会话中调用 pwsh 工具，任意命令（例如 `Write-Output "hi"`）；
3. 结果：退出码 `3221225794`（`0xC0000142`），无任何 stdout/stderr；
4. `run_in_background: true` 的后台调用同样崩溃。

## 根因分析 / Root cause

1. **解析链静默回退到 5.1**：`packages/shell/pwsh-local` 的 `resolvePwshPath` 依次探测「PowerShell 7 安装位置 → PATH 条目 → Windows PowerShell 5.1 兜底」。本机无 PS7，因此实际执行的是 `powershell.exe`（5.1），且无任何提示。
2. **崩溃码确属 5.1 自身**：沙箱 runner（`packages/sandbox/sandbox-windows-acl/runner.js`）以受限令牌 `CreateProcessAsUserW`（`dwCreationFlags=0`）spawn 子进程并**镜像子进程退出码**（runner 自身失败会以 `127` + `windows-acl-run:` 签名退出并被识别为 `SandboxUnavailableError`，本场景未出现）。所以 `0xC0000142` 是 powershell.exe 的崩溃码，崩溃发生在**早期 DLL 初始化阶段**（命令执行之前）。
3. **`0xC0000142` 是沙箱文档化的已知边界**：`sandbox-windows-acl/README.md`「已验证边界 → 控制台隔离不可用」一节记载——「在受限令牌下，以 `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` / `CREATE_NEW_CONSOLE` 创建的子进程在 DLL 初始化期间以 `STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED`（`0xC0000142`）死亡」；`spawn.js` 注释同样写明 "hidden-console children die with STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED (0xC0000142) — verified empirically"。
4. **沙箱从未对 5.1 兜底做过验证**：该沙箱的 restricting-SID 列表、keep-alive 组（logon SID + Everyone）等都是针对 **pwsh 7（.NET 5+/CoreCLR）** 调优的（代码注释中的崩溃模式均为 pwsh 的 `0xC0000142` / `0xE0434352`）；README 与测试均未提及 `powershell.exe` / Windows PowerShell 5.1。.NET Framework 的 5.1 在早期初始化上触发了这条受限令牌边界。
5. **结果**：未安装 PS7 的用户每次调用 pwsh 工具都拿到一个无含义的崩溃码，完全无法定位。

## 期望行为 / Expected

- 未安装 PowerShell 7 时给出**明确、可操作的错误**（例如「pwsh 工具需要 PowerShell 7，请运行 `winget install --id Microsoft.PowerShell`；Windows PowerShell 5.1 兜底在沙箱下不可用」），而不是静默崩溃 `0xC0000142`；
- 或：将 5.1 兜底纳入沙箱兼容验证；
- 或：在文档/工具描述中明确声明「Windows 沙箱下仅支持 PowerShell 7」。

## 建议修复 / Suggested fixes

1. `resolvePwshPath` 回退到 5.1 且沙箱启用时，检测并抛出清晰的错误（可复用 `SandboxUnavailableError` 的呈现路径）；
2. 将「5.1 兜底 + 沙箱」组合加入回归测试，或显式标记 unsupported；
3. 工具描述 / README 注明沙箱仅支持 PowerShell 7。

## 附加信息 / Additional

- 崩溃在前台/后台路径一致，非偶发，与具体命令无关（`Write-Output` 即崩）；
- 安装 PowerShell 7（MSI）后问题消失（解析到 `C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe`，沙箱验证过的路径）；
- 相关社区反馈：https://linux.do/t/topic/2754213 （「deepseek harness 在 windows 下 pwsh 好多问题」）。

## 补充证据：微软商店版（MSIX）pwsh 同样不可用（两条路径都失败）

调查中先安装了商店版 PowerShell 7（MSIX，经 `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WindowsApps\pwsh.exe` 执行别名运行）。实测该版本**无法作为 DSH 的 pwsh 使用**，无论沙箱开关：

1. **无沙箱（danger-full-access）**：`Error: spawn ...\WindowsApps\pwsh.exe ENOENT` —— DSH 宿主（Node/libuv）无法 spawn Windows 商店执行别名（reparse point）；用户自己的终端可正常执行（cmd/Explorer 走系统 CreateProcess 解析）。
2. **沙箱内（workspace-write）**：runner 报 `windows-acl-run: CreateProcessAsUserW failed (Win32 2)`，同样无法解析/启动该别名。

（附带观察：解析器命中商店版后，工具错误从「静默 0xC0000142」变为「runner 失败 + 提示切换 danger-full-access」，信息量改善，但结论不变。）

**阶段性结论**：Windows 上 DSH 的 pwsh 工具最可靠的路径是 MSI 版 PowerShell 7（`C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe` 真实 exe）；5.1 兜底在沙箱下 `0xC0000142` 崩溃成立；商店版在**包注册损坏**时不可用（ENOENT / Win32 2），`winget --force` 重装修复注册后可正常使用（见「验证结果」）。建议：
- 解析器在「5.1 兜底 + 沙箱」或「商店版别名」场景下给出明确、可操作的错误（如「请安装 MSI 版 PowerShell 7：`winget install --id Microsoft.PowerShell --source winget --force`」）；
- 或将这两条路径纳入沙箱回归测试 / 文档明确声明。

## 验证结果 / Resolution（2026-08-15 实测）

`winget install --id Microsoft.PowerShell --source winget --force` 成功（重装/修复了商店包注册）后，**pwsh 工具完全恢复可用**：

- `PSVersion=7.6.4`，`PSHOME=C:\Program Files\WindowsApps\Microsoft.PowerShell_7.6.4.0_x64__8wekyb3d8bbwe`
- 前台命令、中文 UTF-8 输出、管道、`run_in_background` 后台任务全部正常（exit 0）
- 此前商店别名 ENOENT 的根因：包注册不完整（早期 msixbundle 下载失败留下的坏状态），winget --force 重装后别名可正常 spawn

**注意**：本次验证在 `danger-full-access`（无沙箱）策略下进行。「PowerShell 7 + workspace-write 沙箱」组合在桌面应用环境下**未验证**——若用户恢复沙箱后 pwsh 7 仍报 `0xC0000142`，说明该控制台/DLL 初始化边界对桌面壳（无控制台宿主）是普适的，本报告需按此升级（标题与根因将改为「任何 PowerShell 在桌面壳 + 受限令牌下 DLL 初始化失败」）。

discussions.title: 🧩 dsh-plugin-manager — DSH 设置面板内嵌的插件管理器(MCP / Skills / 内置插件包,改动热生效)
discussions.body:
## 🧩 dsh-plugin-manager

在 DeepSeek Harness **设置面板里内嵌**的图形化管理器,让你像操作普通 App 一样管理 **MCP 服务 / Skills / 内置插件包**,开关、删除**实时热生效,无需重启 dsh web**。

> Everything is a Plugin —— 但插件多了以后,管理和排查全靠手改 `cordis.patch.yml`,门槛高还容易出错。这个插件把最常见的三类管理操作变成了可视化开关。

### ✨ 功能特性

| 能力 | 说明 | 生效方式 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 🎛️ MCP 开关 | 一键禁用/启用任意 MCP 服务(写入 `disabled: true` 或移除) | 实时热生效,无需重启 |
| 🗑️ MCP 删除 | 从 `cordis.patch.yml` 删除整个 MCP 条目(上方注释保留) | 实时热生效,无需重启 |
| 📚 Skills 管理 | 浏览全部 skill 及描述;删除 = 移入 `.trash-*` 目录,可恢复 | 立即生效 |
| 📦 插件包浏览 | 只读查看 DSH 本体 160+ 内置插件包的名称/版本/说明 | 只读 |
| 🛡️ 自动备份 | 每次写操作前自动备份配置为 `cordis.patch.yml.bak-<时间戳>` | — |
| 🔌 零额外进程 | 后端内嵌在 dsh web 宿主里,同源 API,不占端口、无 CORS 暴露 | — |

### 📸 界面预览

管理页位于 **DSH 设置 →「插件管理」**,三个标签页:

![MCP 服务](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/liqichen/dsh-plugin-manager/main/docs/screenshots/manager.png)

![Skills](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/liqichen/dsh-plugin-manager/main/docs/screenshots/manager-skills.png)

![内置插件包](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/liqichen/dsh-plugin-manager/main/docs/screenshots/manager-plugins.png)

### 🚀 安装

```bash
git clone https://github.com/liqichen/dsh-plugin-manager.git
mkdir -p ~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-plugin-manager
cp -r dsh-plugin-manager/{index.js,client.js,package.json} ~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-plugin-manager/

dsh plugin --profile web add ~/.dsh/plugins/dsh-plugin-manager
```

编辑 `~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json` 的 dependencies 加入:

```json
"dsh-plugin-manager": "file:../../plugins/dsh-plugin-manager"
```

在 `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` 的 plugins 列表加入:

```yaml
- id: plugin-manager-ui
  name: dsh-plugin-manager
```

重启 dsh web,打开 **设置 → 插件管理** 即可使用。

### 🛠️ 用 DSH 开发(吃自己的狗粮)

本项目**就是用 DeepSeek Harness 开发出来的** —— 整个开发过程由运行在 DSH 里的 AI 编码智能体完成:逆向研究官方双端插件的扫描与注入机制、反复实验验证「配置改动 → 宿主 HMR 热生效」链路、用 Playwright 自动化截图,最终产物又作为标准 DSH 插件被安装回 DSH,用来管理 DSH 自己 —— **DSH 管理 DSH 自己**。

### ⚠️ 注意事项

- 操作的是真实配置,每次写前自动备份,出问题可用最近的 `.bak-*` 恢复
- MCP 删除 ≠ 卸载包(只删配置条目);Skill 删除是移入 `.trash-*` 而非真删

discussions.title: dsh-doctor: an offline diagnostic for the failure classes this community keeps reporting
discussions.body:
# dsh-doctor: an offline diagnostic for the failure classes this community keeps reporting

> Show-and-tell + community asset. A small, dependency-free CLI that checks a profile's env / profile / session state **before** you boot or install — 19 checks mapped to 18 discussions, each one a failure this community has hit and traced.

## TL;DR

Over the last few days this community produced a cluster of reproducible failure reports around the plugin/profile/session surfaces. Almost all of them are **detectable offline** — the broken state lives in local files (`package.json`, `cordis.patch.yml`, `node_modules`, session logs, PATH) long before boot or the next install. I mined the discussions, grouped them into checkable classes, and built a single zero-dependency CLI (`dsh-doctor.mjs`) that catches them ahead of time.

## 1. Method

For each of the ~15 candidate discussions, asked one question: *is the failure state visible in local state that an offline script can inspect?* If yes → turned into a check. If it needs a live host (e.g. runtime registry collisions like #1415) → out of scope, noted.

## 2. The failure-class catalog (what the checks map to)

| # | Check | Discussion | What it detects |
|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | tool availability | [#1270](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1270) | `node`/`pnpm`/`zstd` missing from PATH (session creation / `dsh plugin` / log decode) |
| E2 | `.env` type | [#71](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/71) | `.env` is a directory → `failed to load .env: EISDIR` |
| E3 | node version | [#113](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/113), [#1313](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1313) | `--expose-internals`-dependent boot paths (HMR/headless) |
| P1 | bundle entry resolvable | [#917](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/917), [#1377](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1377), [#880](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/880) | `dsh.profile.bundles` entries that can't resolve (failed remove leftovers, silently disabled bundles, boot fail-fast) |
| P2 | bundle vs user-patch id collision | [#1404](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1404) | duplicate loader entry id → boot crash |
| P3 | patch insert `name:` resolvable | [#1197](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1197), [#880](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/880) | unresolvable `cordis.patch.yml` insert names (asymmetric resolution) |
| P4 | `file:` deps intact | [#1197](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1197) | dangling `file:` links (vanished node_modules link) |
| P5 | no top-level `@deepseek-ai/*` duplication | [#1486](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1486) | duplicate module instances → `Symbol` mismatch → tool layer crash |
| S1 | orphan `tool_call` | [#1363](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1363) | assistant `tool_calls` without tool results → `INVALID_REQUEST` on resume |
| S2 | unclosed turns | [#466](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/466), [#1265](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1265) | session stuck "running" after an abnormal host kill |

Known out of scope (need a live host): #1415 (runtime registry collision), #1486's runtime manifestation (we only detect the *condition*), IME issues (#1051/#629/#1417/#1281).

## 3. The tool

- **File**: `dsh-doctor.mjs` (~14 KB, zero npm dependencies; uses `node:fs`/`node:child_process`, shells out to `zstd` only for `.zstd` session logs)
- **Usage**:
  ```
  node dsh-doctor.mjs                      # everything
  node dsh-doctor.mjs --profile web        # profile checks only
  node dsh-doctor.mjs --session <path>     # session checks (default: latest session)
  node dsh-doctor.mjs --env                # env checks
  node dsh-doctor.mjs --json               # machine-readable output
  ```
- **Exit codes**: 0 = all pass · 1 = fixable problems found · 2 = usage/environment error
- **Verified**:
  - Healthy profile (web, 0.1.0-rc.6): all 10 checks pass, exit 0
  - Negative tests: the pre-fix broken profile from #1404 correctly flags `modlens, better-sidebar` under P2; a synthetic orphan fixture correctly flags S1
  - `--json` round-trip works

## 4. Where this fits

This community already has several doctor proposals — [#649](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/649) (one-command env doctor), [#432](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/432) (surface silent patch failures), [#1380](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1380) (plugin doctor), [#1518](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1518) (session doctor + migrations), [#738](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/738) (Windows doctor). This one is intentionally the **offline, zero-dependency, three-surface (env/profile/session)** slice — a stopgap that runs anywhere `node` exists, and a seed the official `dsh doctor` (per the advisory in [#1496](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1496)) can absorb.

It complements the user-side security checklist in the dsh-handbook chapter 13 (which already lists our earlier `check-dsh-profile.mjs`).

## 5. Call to action

- **Try it** — if you've hit any of the 18 discussions above, run the matching check and confirm it catches your case (or add the missing one);
- **Extend it** — the structure is "one function per check"; natural next candidates: port-in-use (#602), interrupted plugin-creation leftovers (#1131), `pnpm-lock` vs `file:` consistency;
- **Adopt it** — happy to hand this over as the seed for an official `dsh doctor` implementation.

*Author note: built while chasing #1404/#1197/#1486/#1363 in a real profile; the catalog is from the discussions above (2026-08-14 era, 0.1.0-rc.6).*


---

---

---

---

## Source & maintenance

The tool's canonical home is the public repo: **https://github.com/moonquake2004/dsh-doctor** (MIT).

```bash
# latest, no clone needed (node + zstd on PATH)
npx --yes github:moonquake2004/dsh-doctor
# or clone
git clone https://github.com/moonquake2004/dsh-doctor
```

The repo README keeps the current check↔discussion table, the S11 materialization-metric calibration (measured heap model + `DSH_DOCTOR_HEAP_MB`), and Windows-compat notes. This post intentionally no longer embeds the full source — an embedded copy goes stale as the tool evolves with the threads (it already did twice); the discussion history here is the design/verification log, the repo is the code.

discussions.title: macOS native host of official `dsh web` (WKWebView): working pattern + host bugs
discussions.body:
Field report from hosting the **official** Web UI in a native macOS WKWebView. Not a fork and not a desktop-shell announcement.

## Setup

- `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.0-rc.6`
- Official `dsh web` at `http://127.0.0.1:3080`
- Loaded in WKWebView
- Official package stays in Application Support (npm update of `@deepseek-ai/dsh` only). We do not change DSH source.

Official UI comes up in a Mac window. Document title is `DeepSeek Harness`.

## Host friction (reproduced against official `dsh web`)

1. **Web UI assumes browser chrome.** Cmd+V does nothing until the *host* provides an Edit menu (Paste). The page has no paste affordance that works in WKWebView.
2. **`npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web` hangs** on this host path. A pinned Application Support install of `@deepseek-ai/dsh`, then that `dsh web`, is reliable.
3. **A broken `~/.dsh` profile can block `dsh web`.** An isolated `DSH_HOME` unblocks it.
4. **Occupied `:3080`.** If something else is already listening, attach when it is healthy official `dsh web`, or bind the next port. Do not kill the stranger.

Related native-dialog / clipboard threads (mostly Windows or in-browser; same class may apply when the official UI is hosted in WKWebView, not Chrome):

- https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1503 — folder picker not frontmost; picker crash when the service is orphaned
- https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1523 — Windows directory picker unusable
- https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/702 — macOS “add workspace” picker delay / not frontmost
- https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1494 — copy button no-ops when `navigator.clipboard.writeText` is permission-denied

## Ask

A short **embedded-host contract** for people wrapping official `dsh web` (not forking it):

- localhost / `127.0.0.1` vs `localhost` (also https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/764 and https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/322)
- paste / clipboard in a WebView with no browser chrome
- native file dialogs in WKWebView
- a documented boot-health signal (we used `__DSH_BOOT__` as a ready check)

Most host reports here are Windows. A Mac official-UI host path is under-documented. Happy to answer follow-ups on the official CLI + WKWebView side only.

discussions.title: [Bug] Settings save fails forever with "暂时无法保存确认状态" after a killed process orphans the writer lock
discussions.body:
# Bug report: settings write fails permanently with "暂时无法保存确认状态，请重试" after a process dies holding the writer lock

> Post this under **GitHub Discussions → Bug Reports** for `deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness`.
> (Upstream does not accept external PRs per `CONTRIBUTING.md`, so this is the official channel. A proposed fix is included at the bottom for the team to adopt.)

## Summary

On Windows, if a `dsh` process is killed or crashes while holding the
settings writer lock, every subsequent save fails forever with:

```
settings-rejected: atomic-write: timed out waiting for the writer lock at <home>/settings.yaml.lock
```

In the UI this shows as **"暂时无法保存确认状态，请重试"** (cannot save
confirmation state, please retry) — but retrying never works, because the
orphaned lock is never released by anyone.

## Root cause

`packages/util/atomic-write/src/index.ts` — `withFileLock`:

- The lock is an exclusive `wx` create of `<file>.lock` that records the
  owner `process.pid`.
- On losing the race (EEXIST), the contender only backs off and retries until
  a 2s deadline, then throws. **It never inspects or removes the existing lock.**
  The code comment is explicit: *"orphan recovery is an operator action"*.

So a process that dies while holding the lock leaves a permanent lock. Every
later write times out.

### How it triggered in practice

A `dsh web` process stalled inside the `rename` of the settings write — the
`rename` was blocked by Windows Defender realtime scanning holding a handle on
`settings.yaml`. `withFileLock` only releases the lock in its `finally`, which
runs only after `operation()` returns; a stuck `rename` means the lock is held
indefinitely. Once the process was killed, the lock became an orphan that no
live writer would ever release.

> Note: the data was actually written successfully before the stall — the
> `welcomeNoticeVersion` value in `settings.yaml` was already correct. The error
> is purely about the orphaned lock, not data loss.

## Why the fix is safe

The lock already stores the owner PID. When the exclusive create loses the
race, read that PID and, if the process is dead (`process.kill(pid, 0)` →
`ESRCH`), remove the orphan and retry. A **live** owner is still respected:

- the 2s timeout still protects a genuinely slow writer (e.g. a `rename`
  stalled behind antivirus scanning);
- PID liveness is re-checked at removal time, so a PID reused by a new live
  process is left untouched — a strict improvement over the old age-based rule
  that could never tell a dead owner from a slow one.

This does **not** break a lock held by a *live but hung* writer — doing so
would risk two concurrent writers and silent data loss. The mitigation for a
hung write remains excluding the harness home from realtime antivirus
(operator action), unchanged.

## Proposed fix (for the team to adopt)

```ts
import { kill } from 'node:process'

function isEEXIST(error: unknown): error is NodeJS.ErrnoException {
  return error instanceof Error && (error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === 'EEXIST'
}

async function tryRecoverOrphanLock(lockPath: string, deadline: number): Promise<boolean> {
  if (Date.now() >= deadline) return false
  let raw: string
  try {
    raw = await readFile(lockPath, 'utf8')
  } catch {
    return false // lock vanished (raced) or unreadable; caller retries the create
  }
  const pid = Number.parseInt(raw.split(/\r?\n/)[0] ?? '', 10)
  if (!Number.isInteger(pid) || pid <= 0) return false
  let alive = false
  try {
    kill(pid, 0)
    alive = true
  } catch (error) {
    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== 'ESRCH') return false
  }
  if (alive) return false // genuinely held by a living process; respect the timeout
  if (Date.now() >= deadline) return false
  // PID is dead: only now is it safe to clear the orphan. Re-check liveness
  // right before removal so a PID reused by a new live process is left untouched.
  try {
    kill(pid, 0)
    return false
  } catch (error) {
    if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== 'ESRCH') return false
  }
  await rm(lockPath, { force: true })
  return true
}
```

And in the `withFileLock` retry loop, after the EEXIST branch:

```ts
    } catch (error) {
      if (!isEEXIST(error)) throw error
      if (await tryRecoverOrphanLock(lockPath, deadline)) continue
    }
```

`withFileLock` has exactly 3 call sites (settings-file ×2, credentials-local ×1),
all semantically "hold lock → atomic replace", so the recovery is safe and
beneficial for each.

## Workaround (until adopted)

- Delete the orphaned `<home>/settings.yaml.lock` and restart `dsh`.
- Add the harness home (e.g. `C:\Users\<you>\.dsh`) to Windows Defender
  exclusions to stop the `rename` stalls that produce the orphans.

## Reproduction

1. Start `dsh web`; let it write settings at least once.
2. Kill the `dsh` process (or simulate by writing a dead-PID into
   `settings.yaml.lock` and leaving it).
3. Restart `dsh`; any settings save now fails with `settings-rejected`
   until the orphan lock is manually removed.

## Test plan (unit, already passing locally)

- A lock orphaned by a dead process is recovered and the operation runs.
- A lock held by a live process still times out (never broken).
- `vitest run packages/util/atomic-write` — 7 passed.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10
- `dsh` from `deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness` (developer preview)
- Antivirus: Windows Defender realtime protection

discussions.title: Out-of-repo plugins cannot mark session events `ignorable` — every log they touch becomes unreadable (extensibility gap + minimal fix)
discussions.body:
# Out-of-repo plugins cannot mark session events `ignorable` — every log they touch becomes unreadable (extensibility gap + minimal fix)

> Posted for the DeepSeek Harness team. We hit this while building a third-party plugin (`dsh-agent-teams`) that records its own session events.

## Scenario

- A plugin appends its own session events (`agent-teams/team-created`, `task-created`, `message-sent`, …) into the captain's session log via `session.append(type, data)`, so the web client can fold a team tree from the log (same mechanism as `tool-workflow/*`).
- Those event types are out-of-repo, so they are not in the generated `KNOWN_SESSION_EVENT_TYPES`.
- The persistence coordinator therefore refuses to interpret **any** log containing them unless the event carries `ignorable: true`:
  `session "…" contains event type "agent-teams/task-created" (seq …) unknown to this harness and not marked ignorable; refusing to interpret the log — it was likely written by a newer harness`.

## Root cause

`SessionEvent.ignorable?: true` is a documented envelope field (`packages/core/session/src/types.ts`) and the read path honors it — but `Session.append()` only accepts `SurfaceIntent` opts for surface events (`user/message`, `assistant/message`, `tool/result`). **For non-surface events — exactly the case of a plugin vocabulary — there is no public way to pass `ignorable: true`.** `known-event-types.ts` explicitly defers a registration surface "until such a consumer exists"; this consumer now exists.

Consequence: every session a plugin touches becomes unreadable to the harness (history load + `session.list` fail). Rewriting logs to inject the marker is a whack-a-mole workaround while the plugin keeps writing.

## Minimal fix (implemented locally, working)

1. `packages/core/session/src/index.ts` — `Session.append`: for non-surface events accept an optional `{ ignorable?: true }` opts argument and include it in the envelope (read-side validation already allows the field; ~5 lines).
2. The plugin then calls `session.append(type, data, { ignorable: true })`; verified end-to-end that new events carry the marker and logs stay readable.

## Questions for the team

1. Is this minimal form acceptable as the deferred registration surface (allow out-of-repo events to be marked ignorable through the public API)?
2. Or do you prefer a runtime registry where out-of-repo plugins declare their event types (so projections could still fold them, keeping events "known")? That is a bigger design, but we are happy to follow your direction.
3. We understand external PRs are not currently accepted (per CONTRIBUTING) — if that changes, happy to prepare a proper PR with tests + agent note; otherwise the diff is available on request.

discussions.body: ### 问题描述 当 Agent 调用 `ask_user_question` 提问时，如果用户在问题回答框中输入了一部分文字，但还没有提交，此时切换到其他会话，再切换回来，之前输入的文字会消失。 该问题似乎只影响 `ask_user_question` 的结构化问题回答框。普通聊天输入框中的草稿可以在切换会话后正常保留。 ### 复现步骤 1. 打开会话 A。 2. 让 Agent 调用 `ask_user_question` 提出一个需要输入文字回答的问题。 3. 在问题回答框中输入一部分文字，但不要提交。 4. 切换到会话 B。 5. 再切换回会话 A。 6. 查看问题回答框中的内容。 ### 实际结果 问题回答框变为空白，之前输入但尚未提交的文字已经丢失。 ### 预期结果 未提交的回答草稿应当按会话保存。切换回会话 A 后，之前输入的文字应该恢复，行为应与普通聊天输入框一致。 ### 复现频率 可以稳定复现。 ### 补充说明 - 普通聊天输入框的草稿在“会话 A → 会话 B → 会话 A”的切换过程中可以正常保留。 - 只有 `ask_user_question` 问题回答界面中的草稿会丢失。 - 切换会话前没有提交回答。 - 已确认该问题并非特定桌面端插件导致，更换插件后仍然可以复现。 - 问题发生在 DeepSeek Harness Web GUI 中。 ### 运行环境 - 操作系统：Windows - 使用界面：DeepSeek Harness 桌面端（https://github.com/anywhere-labs/deepseek-harness-desktop.git）

discussions.title: [Hooks] SessionStart context can miss the first model request
discussions.body:
## Summary

`SessionStart` runs detached in both hook bridges and injects its context only after the hook promise resolves. If the first prompt reaches `agent/pre-step` and claims the inbox first, the model request can be sent without the startup context. The late `agent.inject()` then targets a later step instead.

This is observable in `hooks-claude-code`, and `hooks-codex` has the same detached `.then(... agent.inject(...))` structure. The existing Codex regression test avoids the race by polling `agent.inbox.nextStep` before sending the prompt, while the Claude coverage test explicitly described first-request delivery as best-effort.

## Deterministic reproduction

I added a barrier-based regression test on the current `master` (`47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a`):

1. A `SessionStart` script touches a `started` marker, waits for a `release` marker, then emits `additionalContext: "late ctx"`.
2. The test waits until the hook process is definitely running and blocked.
3. It immediately submits the first user prompt.
4. After giving the old bridge a chance to send the request, it releases the hook and checks the first model request.

The unmodified bridge fails because the request contains only the prompt:

```text
FAIL packages/hooks/hooks-claude-code/tests/coverage-edge-paths.spec.ts
AssertionError: expected '[{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"g…' to contain 'late ctx'

Expected: "late ctx"
Received: "[{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"go"}],"source":{"kind":"user"},...}]"

Test Files  1 failed | 1 passed (2)
Tests       1 failed | 22 passed (23)
```

## Root cause

`agent/session-start` is an emit-shaped extension point, so the bridge correctly does not block agent creation. However, the continuation currently calls `agent.inject(context)`. `agent/pre-step` atomically claims the current `next-step` and `next-turn` inputs before the model request. If the detached continuation resolves after that claim, its injection cannot join the already-proposed step.

The lifecycle ownership and delivery guarantees are therefore conflated: startup must remain non-blocking, but first-request context still needs an awaited boundary before the request is sent.

## Proposed fix

I prepared an independently reviewable branch based on the current official `master`:

- Compare: https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/compare/master...Lzb-gzist:agent/hooks-session-start-first-request-gate
- Commit: https://github.com/Lzb-gzist/deepseek-harness/commit/e7f72a346eaf125470336f4bb6b9e3cee66a9044
- Branch: https://github.com/Lzb-gzist/deepseek-harness/tree/agent/hooks-session-start-first-request-gate

The change:

- starts `SessionStart` immediately and keeps the run owned by `createDetachedRuns()`, so agent creation remains non-blocking and disposal still aborts/drains the hook;
- stores the resulting context promise per agent;
- joins it only after `UserPromptSubmit` and downstream `agent/pre-step` policy return `enter`, before the first model request;
- prepends startup context to preserve the former inbox-injection order before the user prompt;
- keeps the result when a proposal is rejected or its wait is cancelled, so the next accepted prompt can still consume it;
- adds `waitForTrackedRun()` to cancel only the turn-owned wait without cancelling the tracker-owned hook;
- applies the same lifecycle contract to both Claude Code and Codex bridges;
- updates the English/Chinese package docs, Agent Note, generated config catalog, and translation-pairing sidecars.

## Regression coverage and gates

New coverage includes:

- a barrier-held `SessionStart` result cannot be missed by the first request;
- startup context remains ordered before the original prompt;
- downstream rejection does not consume startup context;
- turn cancellation cancels only the wait and preserves context for the next prompt;
- executor failure yields no startup context and does not stop the agent;
- the shared wait helper preserves the exact abort reason, leaves the tracked run alive, handles pre-aborted signals, and cleans up listeners.

Validation on the pushed commit:

```text
Hook suites: 18 files passed, 210 tests passed
pnpm run typecheck: passed (also rerun by pre-push)
pnpm run lint: passed
pnpm run doc-sync: 28 passed, 0 failed
pnpm run duplication: 0 clones
git diff --check: passed
```

I searched the latest 100 official Discussions (titles and bodies, newest #1538 through oldest #1439) before posting; the related keyword matches concern Windows subprocess cleanup, Stop-loop control, `continue:false`, and subagent model selection, not this SessionStart first-request race.

Would this delivery contract be acceptable for the two bridges, or would maintainers prefer a new awaited core startup extension point instead?
