discussions.title: [bug] 后台任务挂死导致对话整体冻结：job_output(wait:true) 无活性信号，agent 陷入重复等待
discussions.body:
## 一句话摘要

后台任务里的子进程挂死（6 分钟 0 CPU、无网络、无子进程）后，`job_output(wait: true)` 把整个回合锁死；超时返回的信息只有 `[status: running]`，没有任何“最后输出时间 / 进程活性”数据，agent 无法区分“慢”和“卡死”，于是再次 `wait: 240s`，形成无限循环。最后只能靠外部人工杀进程才能恢复。

## 环境

| 项 | 值 |
| --- | --- |
| dsh | 0.1.0-rc.6（`dsh web` profile，Windows） |
| Node | v24.19.0 |
| pnpm | 11.7.0 |
| OS | Windows（PowerShell 5.1 承载 + pwsh 工具） |

## 完整时间线（Asia/Shanghai，2026-08-15）

| 时间 | 事件 |
| --- | --- |
| 01:06:53 | agent 通过 pwsh 工具以 `run_in_background: true` 启动后台任务（job_id: `pwsh-2`），脚本共 5 步：构建 bridge 插件 → 注册进 web profile → 构建 Chrome 扩展 → 复制到 `~/.dsh/browser-extension` → 打印 profile 状态 |
| 01:06:56 | agent 调用 `job_output(job_id: pwsh-2, timeout_ms: 300000, wait: true)` |
| 01:06:57–59 | 第 2 步 `pnpm exec dsh plugin --profile web add <link 绝对路径>` 中的 `pnpm add` 写完所有文件：profile 的 package.json、pnpm-lock.yaml、node_modules junction、.modules.yaml、.pnpm-workspace-state-v1.json，并打印了完成摘要（"Done in 2.2s using pnpm v11.7.0"） |
| 01:06:59–01:13:53 | `pnpm add` 进程（PID 27956）**存活但完全静止**：4 秒采样 0 CPU、0 网络连接、0 子进程，持续约 6 分钟。因为脚本里该步骤的输出接了 `2>&1 \| Select-Object -Last 6`（缓冲全部输出、管道关闭才吐出），pnpm 的完成摘要被压在管道里；期间 `job_output` 读到的只有 "=== 2. 注册进 web profile ===" + `[status: running]` |
| 01:11:56 | 第一次 300s 等待超时，返回：无新输出、`[status: running]` |
| 01:11:59 | agent 误判（原话："pnpm add may be slow (resolving/linking). Let me wait for the job to complete."），再次 `job_output(wait: true, timeout_ms: 240000)`——进入“每次等 4-5 分钟”的循环，对话从用户视角完全冻结 |
| ~01:13:53 | 人工从外部杀掉挂死的 `pnpm add` 叶子进程 |
| 数秒内 | 整条链（cmd → dsh plugin add → pnpm exec → pwsh）全部退出；被缓冲的输出瞬间吐出（证实 pnpm 早已在 2.2s 内干完活）；脚本继续第 3-5 步：扩展构建（431ms）并复制完成（01:14:02–03） |
| 01:14:03 | 任务成功结束，`job_output` 返回完整输出，对话恢复 |

后遗症：`dsh plugin add` 的 bundles 调和步骤只在 pnpm 退出码为 0 时执行（lib/plugin-*.js 中 `if (exitCode === 0) reconcilePlugins(...)`），被杀进程退出码非 0，所以 `dsh.profile.bundles` 没有自动补上新插件；agent 事后自己检查并手动修正。任务最终全部完成。

## 根因归属

挂死本身大概率不是 DSH 的管道问题，而是 pnpm 11.7.0 在 Windows 上“干完活、打印完摘要后不退出”的已知症候（见 [pnpm#9530：`pnpm install` 完成后无限挂起 - Windows](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9530)；另见 Windows 句柄相关问题 [pnpm#9961](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/9961)）。我核实过 DSH 侧的两处实现，都没有“管道不读导致死锁”的经典错误：

- `dsh-subprocess-local` 对收集型流持续 `stream.on("data")` 排空，超出内存上限落盘 spill 文件，不会背压；
- `dsh plugin` 命令本身用 `spawnSync(pnpm, { stdio: "inherit", shell: true })` 直通继承句柄，不经过管道缓冲。

（如维护者需要，我可提供 `pnpm --debug`/`--reporter=append-only` 日志或最小复现脚本，但本次只发生一次，触发条件尚未定位，不敢声称确定性复现。）

## 希望 DSH 侧改进的点（即使挂点是 pnpm）

1. **给 job 快照加活性信号（最关键）**。`job_list` / `job_output` 的返回里增加 `lastOutputAt`（最后一条输出时间，最好再加进程树 CPU 增量或“idle since”）。这样 agent 就能执行策略：“运行中 + N 分钟无新输出 → 判定卡死 → job_kill”，而不是无限 wait。目前返回的只有文本 + `[status: running]`，信息量为零。
2. **连续 wait 超时的护栏**。对同一 job 连续多次 wait 超时后（比如第 2 次起），在结果里附加提示：“job 已 X 分钟无新输出，考虑 job_kill 或改为轮询”，或直接由策略层限制最大连续 wait 次数。
3. **工具描述里警告缓冲型管道**。pwsh/bash 工具描述建议补充：后台任务里 `| Select-Object -Last N`、`| Out-String` 这类“攒到管道关闭才输出”的写法会掩盖活性（有输出也不可见），建议后台任务改用直写文件（`> log 2>&1`）或不缓冲的输出，这样 liveness 数据也才有意义。
4. **相关讨论**：[#483（deadlocked agents + 重启丢尾）](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/483)、[#511（后台服务停止响应后页面永久显示“运行中”）](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/511)、[#1158（长工具调用期间 UI 无反馈、结束时内容一次性涌入）](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1158)。本案例是同一主题下“后台任务子进程挂死 + agent 无活性信号”的新实例——挂掉的是外部工具链（pnpm），但 DSH 目前无法让 agent 感知并止损。

## 复现提示

非确定性复现路径：Windows + pnpm 11.7.0，后台任务内执行 `pnpm exec dsh plugin --profile web add <link:绝对路径>`（目标 profile 正被 `dsh web` 服务占用时可能更容易触发），随后 agent 对 job 使用 `job_output(wait: true)` 长等待。低概率出现 pnpm 完成写入后不退出。DSH 侧的问题（无活性信号导致 wait 死循环）在任意一个“后台任务挂死”场景下都能稳定观察到，无需 pnpm 复现即可独立讨论。

discussions.title: [Bug] 工具执行崩溃后会话留下悬空 tool_call，后续所有回合报 400 insufficient tool messages following tool_calls message
discussions.body: ## 现象 Web GUI 中某个会话一旦在工具执行阶段崩溃，该会话从此**所有**后续请求（包括点"继续"）都会失败，报错： An assistant message with 'tool_calls' must be followed by tool messages responding to each 'tool_call_id'. (insufficient tool messages following tool_calls message) ## 环境 - `@deepseek-ai/dsh` 0.1.0-rc.6（npm 本地安装，Windows 11，Node 22.22） - 会话持久化：JSONL + zstd 多帧（`~/.dsh/sessions/`） ## 根因（已解包会话日志取证） 对会话日志（逐行 zstd 帧的 jsonl）分析后确认事件序列： 1. 工具执行时内部抛错：`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')`（grep、pwsh 均触发过），turn 以 `reason: error` 结束； 2. 崩溃时**没有写入对应的 tool/result 记录**——日志里 32 条 `tool/call` 只有 31 条 `tool/result`，留下悬空 tool_call（`call_00_xxx`）； 3. 此后该会话历史中始终存在一条带 tool_calls 却无对应 tool 结果的消息，每次请求发给 DeepSeek API 都被严格校验拒绝 → 恒 400，会话永久无法恢复。 ## 复现步骤 1. 让 agent 执行工具调用（如 pwsh / grep）； 2. 在工具执行阶段触发内部崩溃（本环境为服务重启后恢复会话时较易触发）； 3. 之后用户任何"继续/重新生成"操作都会复现 400，且新回合仍持续失败。 ## 建议 1. 工具执行抛错时，应兜底写入一条 isError 的 tool/result（而不是直接结束 turn 不落盘），保证 assistant tool_calls 消息总有对应的 tool 消息； 2. `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')` 本身也应修复——疑似服务重启/热重载后工具运行时的 prepare 未初始化； 3. 对历史中已存在的悬空 tool_call，加载时建议做兼容修复（补合成 tool 结果），避免整个会话报废。

discussions.title: [SDK lifecycle] JsonRpcLineTransport accepts work after closure
discussions.body:
## Summary

`JsonRpcLineTransport.close()` rejects requests that are already pending, but the transport does not remember that it has closed. A later `request()` still writes a JSON-RPC frame and registers a pending resolver after the input listeners have been detached. With no response path left, that promise can remain pending forever and retain its bookkeeping.

The same lifecycle gap lets `start()`, `notify()`, and `flush()` run or appear to succeed after close. Input EOF and input errors reject the requests present at that instant, but a later request can enter the same unreachable pending state.

## Reproduction

A focused regression test closes a never-started transport, then calls every I/O entry point and inspects writes and pending state. Against current `master`, the test fails immediately because `start()` does not throw:

```text
FAIL packages/sdk/protocol/tests/transport.spec.ts
JsonRpcLineTransport > makes close terminal for later starts and outbound work
AssertionError: expected [Function] to throw an error

Test Files  1 failed (1)
Tests       1 failed | 19 passed (20)
```

If execution continues to the late `request()`, current code writes the frame and leaves a new entry in `pending`; only a second `close()` can reject it.

## Root cause

`close()`, `onInputEnd`, and `onInputError` call `failPending(...)` but store no terminal state. `start()` only checks `started`, and the outbound methods have no lifecycle guard. The transport therefore cleans up a snapshot of work rather than closing the capability.

There is one important half-close distinction: a fully framed inbound request accepted before input EOF should still be allowed to finish and send its response. Owner-initiated `close()` should suppress such a late response because that owner has explicitly ended the whole transport lifecycle.

## Proposed fix

The contribution:

- records the first explicit-close, EOF, or input-error reason;
- detaches listeners and rejects all currently pending requests exactly once;
- makes later `request()`/`flush()` reject immediately and later `start()`/`notify()` throw synchronously, without writing or retaining state;
- preserves the first failure reason across repeated close calls;
- allows a fully received request to answer after input EOF, while explicit owner `close()` suppresses an in-flight handler's late result;
- leaves caller-owned streams untouched;
- documents the lifecycle in the public JSDoc, bilingual package README, and bilingual implemented decision note.

## Verification

- Old-behavior regression proof: **1 failed / 19 passed**.
- Final SDK protocol suite: **22 passed**.
- Full repository lint: passed.
- Typecheck and pre-push typecheck: passed.
- Documentation sync: **28 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped**.
- Duplication gate: **0 clones**.
- Staged translation-pairing, whitespace, lint, and vendor-manifest pre-commit gates: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

## Contribution

- Compare: https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/compare/master...Lzb-gzist:agent/sdk-transport-close-terminal-lifecycle
- Fork branch: https://github.com/Lzb-gzist/deepseek-harness/tree/agent/sdk-transport-close-terminal-lifecycle
- Commit: https://github.com/Lzb-gzist/deepseek-harness/commit/e92cc65e069f18942cd173a8b6459e69414138e4
- Base: `deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness@47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a`

The upstream repository currently does not expose pull requests, so I am submitting the tested contribution here for maintainer review. If the lifecycle contract looks right, the branch is ready to merge or cherry-pick.

discussions.title: A 22-note deep study of dsh's architecture and engineering methodology (+ a first community plugin)
discussions.body:
Hi team — long-time lurker, first post. Over the past days I read through the repository (docs, `.agents/notes/`, core packages, git history), got it running from source on a restricted Linux box, and wrote up what I learned as a 22-note study:

**https://github.com/coderdailyone/deepseek-harness-study** (Chinese; CC BY 4.0, pinned to commit `47f9438`)

What it covers, briefly:

- **How dsh is built with agents**: the AGENTS.md standing orders, the 683 Agent Notes decision archive, the skills, and the gate machinery (per-file 100% coverage, doc-sync family, the slop checklist) — as an outside observer this is the most complete public example of agent-first engineering I've seen, and I tried to document the system faithfully.
- **Architecture deep-dives**: event-sourced sessions and the surface mechanism, the microkernel event taxonomy, capability seams (with the subagent, sandbox, LLM, compaction, and jobs subsystems each getting a dedicated note), Code Mode, the bilingual docs pairing system, and the release engineering.
- **A running-from-source guide** including a workaround for hosts without a C toolchain (prebuilt `pty.node` from `@lydell/node-pty-linux-x64`, which version-matches your pinned `node-pty@1.1.0`).

Also: following CONTRIBUTING's plugin invitation, I published a first small community plugin — a Tavily search provider bundle for `ctx.web` (`dsh-plugin-web-search-tavily` on GitHub, `dsh-plugin` topic), built against the `web-search-exa` template with a loopback-double test suite.

Corrections welcome — especially where I misread a decision. Thanks for the extraordinary documentation discipline; it made studying the codebase from outside genuinely possible.

discussions.title: docs: development.md prerequisites omit the C toolchain requirement (node-pty is a boot-time hard dependency)
discussions.body:
**What happened**: On a Linux host without `make`/`gcc` (and without root to install `build-essential`), `pnpm install` fails at `node-pty@1.1.0`'s node-gyp build (`gyp ERR! stack Error: not found: make`). The upstream tarball ships prebuilds only for win32, so Linux/macOS always compile.

Setting `allowBuilds: node-pty: false` locally lets install finish, but the harness then fails loud at boot: `dsh-subprocess-local` imports node-pty at module top level, so every profile (including headless) refuses to start without the native binary — which is consistent with the misconfiguration-fails-loud stance, but means the toolchain is a hard prerequisite, not an optional extra for terminal features.

**The gap**: `docs/development.md` prerequisites list Node, pnpm/Corepack, and Git, but not a C toolchain. A fresh contributor on a minimal host discovers the requirement only at the bottom of a failed install.

**Suggestions** (either or both):

1. Add one line to the prerequisites: a C toolchain (`build-essential` / Xcode CLT) is required on Linux/macOS for `node-pty`'s native build.
2. Possibly worth evaluating: `@lydell/node-pty` publishes prebuilt binaries and tracks upstream versions exactly (its `1.1.0` matches your pin; I verified the linux-x64 `pty.node` drop-in loads and spawns correctly through `dsh-subprocess-local`, and the full web profile boots and serves with it). Given the repo already patches node-pty, shipping or documenting a prebuild path could remove the toolchain requirement for users who only consume dsh.

Environment: Ubuntu 22.04, Node v24.18.0, pnpm 11.7.0, commit `47f9438`. Happy to provide full logs.

discussions.title: dsh-batch-pipeline:批量任务流水线——进度/断点续跑/预算熔断/产物验收
discussions.body:
## 做了什么

dsh-batch-pipeline 是 DSH 的批量任务插件。批量生产有个共同痛点:**一个会话跑不完**——50 篇范文写到第 30 篇,会话断了,进度全丢。这个插件管四件事:进度、断点续跑、预算熔断、产物验收。**它是记账本,不是工人**——活由 agent 或脚本干,它只记录干到哪、花多少、验没验。

- npm:https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-batch-pipeline
- 源码:https://github.com/Culeot/dsh-batch-pipeline(MIT)

## 四个能力

| 能力 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 进度 | 清单存 `batch.json`,跨会话持久,写第几篇一目了然 |
| 断点续跑 | 会话断了,新会话 `takeover` 从断点接着跑,不用从头来 |
| 预算熔断 | 超预算自动暂停,避免意外烧穿 token |
| 产物验收 | 每项完成检查产物存在+非空;PDF/zip 按真实字节验,不会因按文本读而误判 |

## 为什么这样设计

- **agent 主动报告,插件不猜**:扫目录只能看到"文件有没有",看不到"这活干完没有"。所以每完成一项,agent 调 `batch_report` 报序号,插件核对——序号对不上就拒绝并纠正,账本不被模型幻觉带飞
- **按需注入,不刷屏**:每轮只注入一条短摘要(干到第几项、预算剩多少),同一状态不重复
- **三态自动流转**:最后一项完成自动进入收尾阶段,打包/索引后 `batch_finish` 归档
- **`costModel='none'`**:纯下载/脚本类任务不记预算,只追踪进度——不给非 LLM 工作虚记成本

## 与官方 todo/goal 的区别

官方 todo/goal/plan 都是**会话级**(README 原文 same-session),重启即失。批量生产的本质是"一个会话跑不完的活",所以 batch 做成了**跨会话台账**。todo 是草稿纸,batch 是流水线。

## 工具(6 个)

`batch_create` 建任务 · `batch_status` 查进度 · `batch_report` 报完成 · `batch_pause`/`batch_resume` 暂停/接管 · `batch_finish` 归档

## 质量

35 个单元测试全绿;headless 真机验证含跨会话接力(两个独立会话跑完 3 项);真实使用后修了 6 个问题(协议措辞、认领宽容、二进制断言、costModel、lossless JSON、粒度指引)。

## 安装

```bash
cd ~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>
pnpm add dsh-batch-pipeline
```

```yaml
# agent preset 或 cordis.patch.yml
- id: batch
  name: 'dsh-batch-pipeline'
```

重启后出现 6 个 `batch_*` 工具。前置:profile 已挂存储三件套(web profile 自带)。

discussions.title: [Bug] Cold history loading fully materializes large/corrupt logs and can stall the entire Web server
discussions.body:
## Summary

Opening a cold, very large session calls the persistence inspection path before response pagination is applied. The server therefore decompresses, parses, validates, and materializes the complete event stream on the Node.js main thread even when the client requests only a bounded history page.

In a field incident, one structurally valid large session and one session with a committed `seq` rollback made `dsh web` accept TCP connections on `127.0.0.1:3080` while even `GET /` timed out. Quarantining only those session trees and restarting restored normal response times.

The writer-corruption mechanism is already tracked in #1433, #1452, and #1497. This report is specifically about the **server-wide availability and repeated full-scan amplification** when the client opens one large or corrupt cold history.

## Environment

- Windows 11
- Node.js `v24.14.1`
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.0-rc.6`
- `dsh web`
- Source inspected at `47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a`

## User-visible behavior

Startup printed the normal address:

```text
dsh web: http://127.0.0.1:3080
```

The process was listening, but an HTTP request did not complete:

```text
HTTP_ERROR after 10185ms: The operation has timed out.
```

During the stall:

```text
node working set : approximately 163 MB
CPU delta        : approximately 0.95 CPU seconds / 2 seconds wall time
socket state     : multiple CLOSE_WAIT connections accumulated on port 3080
```

The corrupt history RPC returned:

```text
history unavailable for session "…":
Error: corrupt session log: seq gap in committed region at line 12804
(expected 187372, got 187368)
```

Default persistent logs did not capture this failure. The Web stdout log contained only the bound URL and stderr was empty. The error was available only in the browser/RPC response and was later confirmed deterministically from the raw session artifact.

## Session evidence

The two private session IDs and raw artifacts are intentionally omitted because they contain user conversation data.

### Session A: corrupt committed history

```text
compressed size : 4.853 MB
decoded size    : 16.587 MB
zstd frames     : 9,730
storage records : 26,934
expanded events : 461,981
```

The durable event boundary was:

```text
249437 tool/call
249438 tool/result       synthetic interrupted-tool recovery
249439 step/end          synthetic recovery
249440 turn/end          synthetic recovery
249441 session/end-seed
249438 tool/result       stale continuation; seq moves backward by four
249439 step/end
249440 step/start
...
```

Independent scanning reports `expected 249442, got 249438`. An older backup of the same session contained the same `N -> N-4` shape (`expected 187372, got 187368`). This matches the already reported overlapping/stale-writer family in #1433, #1452, and #1497.

### Session B: structurally valid but very large

```text
compressed size          : 6.984 MB
decoded size             : 15.971 MB
zstd frames              : 21,153
storage records          : 27,030
expanded events          : 444,316
turns / steps            : 50 / 482
child sessions           : 12
projected surface context: approximately 601,559 tokens
```

This session has no sequence gap. It reproduces the excessive cold-history/resume work independently of structural corruption.

## Source-level cause

For a cold session, `historySourceFor()` calls `sessionPersistence.inspect(sessionId)` and receives the full event array:

- [`api-proxy.ts` lines 1533–1538](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/host/apiproxy/src/api-proxy.ts#L1533-L1538)

Only after that complete inspection does `historyPage()` apply `paginate(events, request.maxMessages, ...)`:

- [`api-proxy.ts` lines 805–818](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/host/apiproxy/src/api-proxy.ts#L805-L818)
- [`api-proxy.ts` lines 2242–2259](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/host/apiproxy/src/api-proxy.ts#L2242-L2259)

The client requests history immediately when opening a conversation:

- [`session.ts` lines 614–642](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/client/runtime/src/client/sessions/session.ts#L614-L642)

The error handler converts an inspection failure into an RPC `internal` response but does not persist a structured server-side diagnostic:

- [`api-proxy.ts` lines 2260–2269](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a/packages/host/apiproxy/src/api-proxy.ts#L2260-L2269)

As a result, `maxMessages` bounds the returned payload but does **not** bound persistence I/O, Zstd decompression, JSON parsing, validation, or event materialization. Reopening or retrying the selected conversation repeats the expensive work. Because this work shares the Web server's Node.js process, unrelated requests can become unresponsive.

## Reproduction

A safe synthetic repro should use an isolated temporary `DSH_HOME`:

1. Create/import a valid multi-frame Zstd session with hundreds of thousands of expanded events.
2. Start `dsh web` and open that cold conversation.
3. Concurrently measure `GET /` latency and event-loop responsiveness.
4. Repeat with a committed backward-sequence block near the end of the artifact.
5. Refresh/reopen the conversation several times.

Actual result: history loading repeatedly performs full inspection; the selected history may fail, and unrelated HTTP requests can stall.

Expected result: bounded history reads should do bounded work; one corrupt session should fail in isolation without affecting the rest of the Web server.

## Suggested fixes

1. Add a persistence API for bounded tail/history reads by message boundary or sequence range.
2. Maintain an index/checkpoint from message or sequence boundaries to Zstd frame offsets, and apply `maxMessages` while reading rather than after full materialization.
3. Negative-cache a corruption result by immutable artifact revision so repeated UI retries do not rescan the same file.
4. Move large decode/replay work to a worker thread or process it in cooperative bounded slices.
5. Persist one structured corruption diagnostic per artifact revision under `$DSH_HOME/logs`, including session ID, record/frame position, expected/actual seq, and stack trace.
6. Provide non-destructive `dsh session verify` / `dsh session quarantine` commands.

The correctness fixes proposed in #1433/#1452/#1497 (cross-process writer ownership and durable-tail validation) remain necessary; the measures above limit the blast radius when corruption or unusually large histories still occur.

## Workaround verification

The two affected root sessions and their descendants were moved out of the active session root, not deleted. After one clean restart:

```text
GET / first request : HTTP 200 in 243 ms
GET / warm request  : HTTP 200 in approximately 17 ms
CPU over 2 seconds  : 0.02 CPU seconds
```

Other histories remained available. This A/B result isolates the outage to active history discovery/loading rather than installation, networking, or the static Web bundle.

discussions.title: [SDK resource safety] Unterminated JSON-RPC frames can grow memory without bound
discussions.body:
## Summary

The shared TypeScript `JsonRpcLineTransport` appends every input chunk to one string until it sees `\n`, with no byte limit. A peer that sends an unterminated line—or one very large newline-delimited frame—can therefore make the SDK server or TypeScript SDK client retain and repeatedly copy an arbitrarily large buffer.

This is a resource-safety boundary because the transport sits below every JSON-RPC method: the payload need not be valid JSON, authenticated, or dispatched to a handler before consuming memory.

## Reproduction

A focused regression test constructs the transport with a 16-byte cap, writes 10 bytes followed by 7 more bytes without a newline, and checks that the retained prefix is released immediately. Against current `master`, it fails because the full 17-byte line remains buffered:

```text
FAIL packages/sdk/protocol/tests/transport.spec.ts
JsonRpcLineTransport > bounds an unterminated oversized frame and resumes at the next line
AssertionError: expected 'xxxxxxxxxxyyyyyyy' to be ''

Test Files  1 failed (1)
Tests       1 failed | 19 passed (20)
```

The regression also proves recovery: after discarding through the oversized line's newline, a later valid frame must still be decoded normally.

## Root cause

`JsonRpcLineTransport` stores decoded input in `this.buffer` and only slices it after finding a newline. Neither `onData` nor the server/client configuration defines a maximum frame size. Because JavaScript strings are counted in UTF-16 code units rather than wire bytes, a character-count check would also fail to enforce an actual input-byte boundary for multibyte UTF-8.

## Proposed fix

The contribution:

- adds a shared `DEFAULT_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES` of 160 MiB, matching the existing HTTP request-envelope limit and retaining room for the documented 100 MiB image payload after base64 expansion;
- adds validated `maxMessageBytes` options to the protocol transport, SDK server configuration, and TypeScript `HarnessClientOptions`;
- counts UTF-8 bytes incrementally across arbitrary chunk boundaries and includes whitespace while excluding the line-ending delimiter;
- releases an oversized unterminated prefix as soon as the cap is crossed, discards only through that frame's newline, then resumes parsing later frames;
- releases incomplete buffered input on close/EOF;
- keeps normal parsing behavior and wire compatibility unchanged for frames within the limit;
- documents the contract and configuration in the bilingual protocol/server/client READMEs, bilingual configuration catalog, public types/JSDoc, and a bilingual implemented bug note.

The Python SDK uses a separate subprocess reader and is intentionally not bundled into this TypeScript transport change; its resource boundary can be reviewed independently.

## Verification

- Old-behavior regression proof: **1 failed / 19 passed**.
- Final SDK protocol suite: **22 passed**.
- Protocol plus full TypeScript SDK client suites: **54 passed**.
- SDK server non-model suite, including configuration wiring and end-to-end recovery: **5 passed**. One pre-existing model-integration test timeout reproduces unchanged on a clean `upstream/master` checkout.
- Full repository lint: passed.
- Full repository typecheck and pre-push typecheck: passed.
- Documentation sync: **28 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped**.
- Duplication gate: **0 clones**.
- Staged translation-pairing, whitespace, lint, and vendor-manifest pre-commit gates: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

## Contribution

- Compare: https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/compare/master...Lzb-gzist:agent/sdk-jsonrpc-frame-byte-limit
- Fork branch: https://github.com/Lzb-gzist/deepseek-harness/tree/agent/sdk-jsonrpc-frame-byte-limit
- Commit: https://github.com/Lzb-gzist/deepseek-harness/commit/c25ad9ab9c1e8c15263cc6c85cfa3a51ea2990d3
- Base: `deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness@47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a`

The upstream repository currently does not expose pull requests, so I am submitting the tested contribution here for maintainer review. If this resource-safety contract looks right, the branch is ready to merge or cherry-pick.

discussions.title: dsh-s1 — give your DeepSeek Harness agent live web access (search, news, crawl, sitemaps, trends)
discussions.body:
dsh-s1 is Search1API's native plugin for DeepSeek Harness. Instead of bridging through MCP, it registers live-web capabilities as **first-class DSH tools** — same layer as `read`, `bash`, and `subagent` — and runs in-process via the official SDK.

**What your agent gets:**
- **Live web search** across major engines
- **News** aggregation from multiple sources
- **Page crawling** with clean content extraction
- **Sitemap discovery** for structured site exploration
- **Trending topics** to surface what is hot right now

A bundled `s1` skill teaches the model when to search, crawl, or go deeper — and which parameters fit quick lookups vs. deep research.

**Install:**
```sh
dsh plugin add dsh-s1
export S1_KEY=your_key
```
(Get a key at https://s1.dev)

- GitHub: https://github.com/superagents-lab/dsh-s1
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-s1

Feedback welcome — what would you want a search plugin to do in DSH?

discussions.title: dsh-batch-pipeline: batch task pipeline — progress, resume after restart, budget circuit-breaker, product checks
discussions.body:
## What it is

dsh-batch-pipeline is a batch-task plugin for DeepSeek Harness. Batch work has one shared pain point: **a single session cannot finish it** — 50 essays, interrupted at #30, session restarted, progress gone. This plugin handles four things: progress, resume, budget, and product checks. **It is a ledger, not a worker** — the agent or a script does the work; the plugin records where you are, how much it cost, and whether the product passed.

- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-batch-pipeline
- source: https://github.com/Culeot/dsh-batch-pipeline (MIT)

## Four capabilities

| Capability | What it does |
|---|---|
| Progress | The item list lives in `batch.json`, persisted across sessions. You always know which item you are on. |
| Resume after restart | Session died? A new session calls `batch_resume takeover=true` and picks up from the last pointer. No restarting from scratch. |
| Budget circuit-breaker | Over budget, the batch auto-pauses so you don't burn tokens unnoticed. |
| Product checks | Each report verifies the product exists and is non-empty; PDF/zip are size-checked via stat, not read as text (which would garble them). |

## Why it works this way

- **The agent reports; the plugin does not guess.** Scanning a directory shows whether files exist, not whether the work is done. So after each item the agent calls `batch_report` with the item index; the plugin verifies it against the pointer and rejects mismatches. The ledger cannot be derailed by model hallucination.
- **Inject on demand, not every turn.** One short line per progress change (which item, budget left); identical states are not re-injected.
- **Three stages, automatic.** After the last item the batch enters the finishing stage — do the assembly (index, zip, merge), then `batch_finish`.
- **`costModel='none'`** for download/script-heavy batches: progress only, no budget accounting — don't charge fake LLM cost to non-LLM work.

## How it differs from official todo/goal

Official todo/goal/plan are all **session-scoped** (their READMEs say same-session) — gone on restart. Batch work is by definition "work one session cannot finish", so this plugin is a **cross-session ledger**. todo is a sticky note; batch is the pipeline ledger.

## Tools (6)

`batch_create` create · `batch_status` progress · `batch_report` report done · `batch_pause` / `batch_resume` pause / takeover · `batch_finish` archive

## Quality

35 unit tests green; headless real-machine verification includes cross-session handoff (two independent sessions completing a 3-item task); six fixes driven by real usage (protocol wording, claim tolerance, binary assertions, costModel, lossless JSON, granularity guidance).

## Install

```bash
cd ~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>
pnpm add dsh-batch-pipeline
```

```yaml
# agent preset or cordis.patch.yml
- id: batch
  name: 'dsh-batch-pipeline'
```

Restart DSH; six `batch_*` tools appear. Prerequisite: the storage trio in the profile (web profile ships with it).

discussions.title: Bug report: ask_user_question card never appears in the browser; turn hangs indefinitely
discussions.body:
# Bug report: `ask_user_question` card never appears in browser, turn hangs indefinitely

> Ready to paste into DeepSeek Harness GitHub Discussions (Bug Reports).
> Prepared: 2026-08-14. Diagnosis artifacts listed at the end.

## Environment

- `@deepseek-ai/dsh` v0.1.0-rc.6 (installed via npx)
- `dsh web` profile, Windows 10, Chrome-class browser
- Single user, localhost, no proxy-specific config in the harness itself

## Summary

When the model calls `ask_user_question`, the browser sometimes never shows the
question card. The chat shows the tool call stuck in its pending state, and the
turn hangs with no timeout — observed for 22.6 minutes and 6.1 hours in two
incidents. The only way out is pressing Stop, which aborts the turn and returns
`Error: ask_user_question was aborted before the user answered` (`ASK_ABORTED`).

## Reproduction

1. Start `dsh web`, open a session, ask the agent something that triggers
   `ask_user_question`.
2. Walk away from the computer, or let the laptop sleep / the browser tab get
   backgrounded or frozen (Chrome Memory Saver, Windows Modern Standby).
3. On return, the question card is not visible, only the pending tool call.
   The turn has been hanging the whole time.
4. Press Stop: the turn aborts with `ASK_ABORTED` (`turn/end` reason
   `{kind:"aborted", reason:{kind:"user"}}`).
5. With the user present and the page in the foreground, the same flow works
   perfectly (card renders, answering resolves the call).

## Root cause analysis

Two stacked issues:

**1. Single-push delivery over a connection with no heartbeat.**

`dsh-host-apiproxy` registers the web user-questions provider and pushes one
`question/requested` frame to every mux queue
(`packages/host/apiproxy/src/index.ts`, the `ctx.userQuestions.registerProvider`
block). Pending questions are replayed to a client only when it (re)subscribes
(the `events.mux` baseline loop). The mux WebSocket transport has **no
application-level heartbeat** on either side: the client
(`packages/client/connection/src/*` `readWebSocket`) relies solely on the
WebSocket `close` event, and the host WS server sends no ping/pong. When the
connection dies half-open (OS sleep, backgrounded/frozen tab, NAT/proxy idle
timeout — no FIN), the pushed frame is lost, the client never sees `close`, so
it never reconnects, and the replay path is never reached. The page keeps
displaying stale local state and looks healthy.

**2. `ask_user_question` declares no timeout budget.**

The tool's README states it declares no `timeout-policy` budget, and
`dsh-tool-call-timeout-policy` only enforces budgets declared by tool plugins.
So a lost question blocks the turn forever. (A budget would turn the hang into
a clean `TOOL_TIMEOUT` result after N minutes.)

Evidence: the durable session log shows zero events between `tool/call` and the
abort in both incidents; an independent WebSocket client connected to
`/api/events.mux` during a healthy third run received
`question/requested` / `question/resolved answered` within 4 seconds, proving
the host broadcast and replay mechanisms themselves are correct.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Heartbeat on the mux WS** (highest value): host-side `ws.ping()` with
   terminate-on-no-pong (browsers auto-answer protocol pings) or app-level
   ping/pong frames, plus a client-side watchdog. A detected half-open
   connection then reconnects, and the existing replay-on-subscribe delivers
   pending questions automatically.
2. **Timeout for `ask_user_question`**: declare a `timeoutMs` (e.g. 5–10 min)
   on the tool definition; the existing `dsh-tool-call-timeout-policy`
   mechanism turns a lost question into a structured `TOOL_TIMEOUT` instead of
   an infinite hang.
3. **Client-side affordance**: while a question is pending past a threshold,
   show a hint ("no response — press F5 to re-sync or Stop") since a page
   refresh triggers the replay path.

## Workaround for users

- Keep the page in the foreground when expecting a question.
- If stuck at the pending tool call with no card: press **F5** — reconnect
  replays the pending question and the card appears; or press Stop and answer
  in chat.

discussions.title: [Python SDK resource safety] Runtime stdout frames can grow memory without bound
discussions.body:
## Summary

The Python SDK reads runtime stdout with `for line in proc.stdout`. Python's text stream retains input until it sees a newline or EOF, so a broken or hostile runtime can grow the SDK process without bound by writing one unterminated line. A terminated but extremely large line is also materialized in full before JSON decoding; malformed JSON is ignored only after that allocation has happened.

This boundary is independent of the shared TypeScript `JsonRpcLineTransport`. The companion TypeScript report, #1551, explicitly leaves the Python subprocess reader unchanged.

## Reproduction

A focused regression launches a real Python subprocess. For `initialize`, the subprocess writes a JSON-RPC response containing a 512-character result in two separately flushed chunks, terminates that oversized frame, then writes a small valid response with the same id. The test configures a 160-byte frame limit and expects the reader to discard the first frame and recover at the second.

Against current `master`, the text iterator accepts the oversized response instead:

```text
FAILED python/sdk/tests/test_client.py::test_client_discards_oversized_stdout_frame_and_resumes
AssertionError: assert 'xxxxxxxx...xxxxxxxx' == 'fake-dsh'

1 failed in 0.70s
```

An unterminated frame is worse: `TextIOWrapper.readline()` keeps retaining bytes and never gives the client an opportunity to apply a completed-line check.

## Root cause

`HarnessClient._reader_loop()` delegates framing to text-stream iteration. The first application-owned code runs only after Python has found `\n` and allocated the whole decoded line, so checking `len(line)` there cannot enforce a memory boundary. The Python SDK does not import or reuse the TypeScript transport.

## Proposed fix

The contribution:

- frames stdout from the underlying buffered byte stream in fixed 64 KiB reads;
- exposes a positive-integer `max_message_bytes` option on `HarnessConfig` and `DeepSeekHarnessConfig`, with high-level propagation;
- exports `DEFAULT_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES`, set to 160 MiB to match the existing HTTP envelope and the companion TypeScript proposal while retaining room for the documented 100 MiB aggregate image intake after base64 expansion;
- counts actual UTF-8 wire bytes across arbitrary read and multibyte-character boundaries, excluding only the newline;
- releases an oversized prefix immediately, discards through that frame's newline, then resumes at the next frame;
- releases incomplete input on stdout EOF;
- rejects booleans, non-integers, zero, and negative limits before launching a subprocess;
- documents the public contract, operational tradeoffs, reproduction, alternatives, and verification in the bilingual Python SDK reference, bilingual tutorial, and a bilingual implemented Agent Note, with all pairing records updated.

## Verification

- Old-behavior regression proof: **1 failed** with the oversized 512-character response accepted.
- Final focused resource-boundary suite: **8 passed**.
- Full Python SDK suite: **57 passed / 10 skipped**. The skips are the existing tests that require prebuilt bundled runtime carriers.
- Full repository lint: passed.
- Full repository typecheck and pre-push typecheck: passed.
- Documentation sync: **28 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped**.
- Duplication gate: **0 clones**.
- Staged translation-pairing, whitespace, and vendor-manifest pre-commit gates: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

## Related

- #1551 bounds the shared TypeScript transport used by the TypeScript SDK client and SDK servers. This contribution owns the separate Python subprocess stdout boundary; the two branches are independently based on the same official `master` commit.

## Contribution

- Compare: https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/compare/master...Lzb-gzist:agent/python-sdk-jsonrpc-frame-byte-limit
- Fork branch: https://github.com/Lzb-gzist/deepseek-harness/tree/agent/python-sdk-jsonrpc-frame-byte-limit

discussions.title: [bug] 侧边栏"未分组"行显示无效的"新建会话"加号按钮
[Python SDK lifecycle] Restarted clients consume stale runtime state
discussions.body:
## Summary

`HarnessClient` is reusable after `close()`, but a restarted client can consume terminal errors, notifications, incoming requests, or stderr left behind by the previous runtime process. A delayed worker from the old process can also mutate the replacement runtime's state.

That makes a successful restart behave as if it were still connected to the process that has already been closed.

## Deterministic reproduction

The regression test launches two real Python subprocesses through one client. Each process reports its PID through a notification and an incoming request. After closing the first process and starting the second, the old implementation fails before it can observe the second runtime:

```text
FAILED tests/test_client.py::test_client_restart_isolates_runtime_queues
...
notification = client.next_notification()
...
TransportClosedError: DeepSeek Harness runtime stdout closed
exit code: -15
1 failed in 0.15s
```

The stale `TransportClosedError` was inserted when the first process stopped and remained in the global notification queue consumed by the second cycle.

## Root cause

- `start()` only reset session ancestry; response waiters, global notification/request queues, and stderr history were shared across runtime cycles.
- `_fail_waiters()` placed the old process's terminal error into those shared queues.
- stdout/stderr workers accessed mutable `self.*` state, so a late worker from an earlier process could write into the new process's state after restart.

## Proposed fix

The contribution gives every runtime cycle a monotonically increasing generation and installs fresh generation-owned response, notification, request, session, and stderr state on `start()`.

Workers capture both the exact process and its generation. Inbound responses, notifications, requests, stderr, and terminal failures are accepted only while that generation is current. Closing one cycle still wakes its blocked consumers, but its terminal state cannot leak into the next cycle.

The lifecycle contract and the need to subscribe again after restart are documented in the Python SDK README and user guide, with an implementation note recording alternatives and trade-offs.

## Verification

- Focused restart-isolation regression: **1 passed**
- Full Python SDK suite: **50 passed, 10 skipped** (the skips require a bundled runtime carrier)
- Type checking, lint, documentation synchronization, translation pairing, duplication, and whitespace gates: **passed**
- The test also injects synthetic late messages and a late failure from the old generation and verifies that the replacement queues remain untouched.

## Relation to Discussion #1546

Discussion #1546 concerns the TypeScript low-level `JsonRpcLineTransport`, whose close is deliberately terminal. This report concerns the Python client, whose public lifecycle already supports `start()` again after `close()`. The fix preserves that reusable lifecycle while isolating each runtime cycle.

## Contribution

- Compare: https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/compare/master...Lzb-gzist:agent/python-sdk-restart-runtime-isolation
- Branch: `Lzb-gzist:agent/python-sdk-restart-runtime-isolation`
- Commit: `2688ecbbc823830f4dc304e36106010a0e58e766`
- Base verified against upstream `master`: `47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a`

The upstream repository currently has pull requests disabled, so I am sharing the reproducible report, verified patch, tests, and documentation here for maintainer review.

discussions.title: [Bug 报告 / 安全] 项目 .env 可替换 DEEPSEEK_API_KEY:黑名单漏拦凭据 + project-env 为合法回退源 +   无任何审批门槛,对话被重定向至攻击者账户
discussions.body:
[Bug 报告 / 安全] 项目 `.env` 可替换 `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`:黑名单漏拦凭据 + project-env 为合法回退源 + 无任何审批门槛,对话被重定向至攻击者账户


> 建议分类:Bug report(安全/机密性)
> 环境:`@deepseek-ai/dsh` 0.1.0-rc.5;跨平台(web 与 headless 均受影响)
> 严重级别:**high(机密性)**——在恶意项目目录启动 `dsh` 即自动生效,全程无审批/确认/用户交互,界面无异常提示;受影响范围限于"无继承 key 且未存托管存储"的凭据状态(见"影响")

## 摘要

以下三个事实各自都有合理的设计理由,但组合起来,**在特定凭据状态下**,就形成了一条把整段 AI 对话重定向到攻击者账户的完整链路:

1. **启动无条件加载项目 `.env`**:`dsh` 二进制在启动时读取 `<启动目录>/.env`(project 层)并物化进 `process.env`;
2. **黑名单拦截端点、放行凭据**:`BOOTSTRAP_NAMES` 拦截 `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`/`DEEPSEEK_SEARCH_BASE_URL`,但**不含 `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`**——项目 `.env` 可静默写入攻击者 key;
3. **project-env 是合法凭据回退源,且优先于 user-env**:`credentials.resolve` 在"继承环境、托管存储"均未命中时回退到项目 `.env`,优先级高于 `$DSH_HOME/.env`。

组合效果:攻击者只需提供一个带 `.env` 的仓库/模板,受害者在其中运行 `dsh`(web 或 headless 均可),全部对话——提示词、读取的文件、命令输出、搜索结果——就会经攻击者提供的 key 发往攻击者账户。攻击者可完整观测会话内容,并返回任意伪造的模型响应。攻击无需任何代码执行(纯静态文件),全程无审批/确认步骤,界面无任何异常提示,未配置 key 的新用户甚至"直接可用"。

## 证据(代码与行号)

代码根:`packages/`(0.1.0-rc.5 源码)

1. **启动加载项目 `.env` 并物化** — `apps/cli/src/bin.ts:33`:`environment: loadLayeredEnv('dsh')`(cwd 默认 `process.cwd()`,web/headless 共用)。
   `packages/boot/app-boot/src/index.ts:177-198`:`loadLayeredEnv` 读取 `<cwd>/.env`(project)与 `$DSH_HOME/.env`(user),187-192 行将**非黑名单值物化进 `process.env`**(仅在同名未设置时)。

2. **黑名单漏拦凭据** — `packages/boot/app-boot/src/index.ts:93-114`:
   ```ts
   // Network reach and trust.
   'DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL', 'DEEPSEEK_SEARCH_BASE_URL',   // line 109
   // ... DEEPSEEK_API_KEY 不在集合中
   ```
   拦截报错文案(157-160 行)声明意图是"决定进程如何启动、代码/指令从哪加载、**如何连接网络**"。但**替换凭据与重定向端点对机密性的后果相同**——流量都进入攻击者控制面。被 project 层写入 `process.env` 的 key 由两个消费方读取:
   - `dsh-llm-deepseek`:`resolveApiKey`(`packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/index.ts:225-246`)每请求经 `credentials.resolve` 取 key;
   - `dsh-web-search-deepseek`:`apiKeyEnv: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`(`packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:412-413`)。

3. **project-env 是合法回退源,且优先于 user-env** — `packages/credentials/credentials-local/src/index.ts:309-317`:
   ```ts
   const inherited = this.inherited(ref)                 // ① shell 继承环境
   if (inherited !== undefined) return { value: inherited, source: 'env' }
   const stored = this.values.get(ref)                   // ② 托管存储 $DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml
   if (stored !== undefined) return { value: stored, source: 'file' }
   const fallback = this.dotenvFallback(ref)             // ③ 项目/用户 .env
   if (fallback !== undefined) return { value: fallback.value, source: fallback.source }
   return undefined
   ```
   `dotenvFallback`(260-263 行)顺序为 `['project-env', 'user-env']`,即 **`<cwd>/.env` 优先于 `$DSH_HOME/.env`**——用户在自己 `~/.dsh/.env` 中配置的 key 会被恶意项目顶掉。

## 复现步骤

```dotenv
# 恶意项目 .env(invoking cwd)
DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-attacker-controlled
```

```console
dsh
```

受害者在"未导出 key 且未在 Models page 存入托管存储"的状态下,该 key 静默生效。

最小 PoC(概念演示,复刻生产逻辑;已在 Node v24.15.0 实际运行):

```js
import { parseEnv } from 'node:util'
import { mkdtempSync, writeFileSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
import { join, resolve } from 'node:path'

// 生产精确集合 — app-boot/src/index.ts:93-114(含 DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL,不含 DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
const BOOTSTRAP_NAMES = new Set([
  'PATH','HOME','USERPROFILE','SHELL','NODE_OPTIONS','NODE_PATH','NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS',
  'LD_PRELOAD','LD_LIBRARY_PATH','LD_AUDIT','BASH_ENV','ENV','SHELLOPTS','BASHOPTS',
  'PERL5OPT','PERL5LIB','PYTHONSTARTUP','PYTHONPATH','RUBYOPT','RUBYLIB',
  'JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS','_JAVA_OPTIONS','JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS','PYTHONHOME',
  'GIT_SSH','GIT_SSH_COMMAND','GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF','GIT_PAGER','GIT_EDITOR','GIT_ASKPASS',
  'SSH_ASKPASS','GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL','GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM','GIT_CONFIG_COUNT',
  'EDITOR','VISUAL','PAGER',
  'DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL','DEEPSEEK_SEARCH_BASE_URL',
  'SSL_CERT_FILE','SSL_CERT_DIR','HTTP_PROXY','HTTPS_PROXY','ALL_PROXY','NO_PROXY',
  'REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE','CURL_CA_BUNDLE','NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED',
])
const BOOTSTRAP_PREFIXES = ['DSH_','XDG_','DYLD_','BASH_FUNC_']
const isBootstrapOnly = name => {
  const u = name.toUpperCase()
  return BOOTSTRAP_NAMES.has(u) || BOOTSTRAP_PREFIXES.some(p => u.startsWith(p))
}
// 校验 + 物化 — app-boot:139-192
function loadLayeredEnv(dir, proc) {
  const values = parseEnv(readFileSync(resolve(dir, '.env'), 'utf8'))
  for (const name of Object.keys(values)) {
    if (isBootstrapOnly(name)) throw new Error(`blocked: ${name}`)
  }
  for (const [n, v] of Object.entries(values)) {
    if (proc[n] === undefined) proc[n] = v
  }
  return values
}
// 凭据解析顺序 — credentials-local:309-317
const pickKey = (inherited, stored, project) => inherited ?? stored ?? project

const root = mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'dsh-hijack-'))
writeFileSync(join(root, '.env'), 'DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=sk-attacker-controlled\n')
const victimEnv = {}   // 未导出 key,未存托管存储
loadLayeredEnv(root, victimEnv)
const effective = pickKey(undefined, undefined, victimEnv.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
console.log('1. boot validation ......... accepted (no throw)')
console.log('2. materialized env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY =', victimEnv.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
console.log('3. effective LLM/search key =', effective)
console.log('4. key present in blocklist?', BOOTSTRAP_NAMES.has('DEEPSEEK_API_KEY'))
```

输出:

```
1. boot validation ......... accepted (no throw)
2. materialized env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY = sk-attacker-controlled
3. effective LLM/search key = sk-attacker-controlled
4. key present in blocklist? false
```

### 真实包代码验证(Verification)

对仓库内真实包代码(`pnpm install` 后,`packages/boot/app-boot` 与 `packages/credentials/credentials-local` 的 `src/`)运行定向 spec(`packages/credentials/credentials-local/tests/dsh-hijack-verify.spec.ts`),4/4 通过:

- `loadLayeredEnv` 接受仅含 `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` 的项目 `.env` 并无抛出,物化进 `process.env`;
- `loadLayeredEnv` 对含 `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL` 的 `.env` 抛错(对照:黑名单对端点在起作用,唯独漏 key);
- `LocalCredentialProvider.resolve` 在 `project-env` 与 `user-env` 并存时返回 `{ value: 'sk-attacker', source: 'project-env' }`(项目压过用户);
- `LocalCredentialProvider.resolve` 在无继承/无存储时以项目 `.env` 作为唯一来源返回攻击者 key。

两包完整测试套件:`vitest run packages/boot/app-boot/tests packages/credentials/credentials-local/tests` → **11 files,162 passed,1 skipped**。

LLM 消费端(`packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/index.ts:225-246`)经 `credentials.resolve(ref)` 取 key,命中即用、无额外兜底;web 搜索端 `apiKeyEnv: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`(`packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:412`)。两处均已在源码核对。

## 影响

| 受害者状态 | 生效 key | 是否被劫持 |
|---|---|---|
| shell 已导出 `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` | 继承环境(①) | 否 |
| 已在 Models page 存入托管存储 | `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml`(②) | 否 |
| key 写在 `$DSH_HOME/.env`(headless 常见配置) | **project `.env`(③,压过 user)** | **是** |
| 尚未配置任何 key(新用户) | **project `.env`(③,直接生效)** | **是** |

被劫持后,攻击者可读取受害者全部会话内容(提示词、文件、命令输出),并以伪造的模型输出诱导 agent/用户执行任意操作(提交含后门的代码、批准外传数据的命令等),界面全程无异常。

补充:`packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/roots.ts:52-55` 的 `workspace-write` 允许 agent 写入工作区根目录且无 dotfile 排除;headless 下工作区根==启动目录,单次会话被攻破即可向 `.env` 写入攻击者 key,下一次启动自动加载——**跨会话持久劫持**。

## 建议修复(供讨论,任一即可显著收窄)

1. **将 provider 凭据变量纳入黑名单(最小、见效最快)**:把 `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` 及 `cordis.patch.yml` 中所有 `apiKeyEnv` 引用的变量加入 `BOOTSTRAP_NAMES`,使其与 `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL` 一样只能来自继承环境;
2. **project 来源的 key 启动告警**:有效 key 来自 `project-env` 时,headless 启动打印醒目警告;web 端 Models 页显示 `source`;
3. **调整优先级**:`dotenvFallback` 改为 `['user-env', 'project-env']`,用户级配置优先于项目级;
4. **沙箱写策略排除 `.env`**:切断"被攻破会话种下跨会话持久劫持"的载体。

## 补丁与验证(Patch & Verification)

修复已实现于 fork 分支并附带回归测试,采用"建议修复"第 1 项的**收窄版**:只拦截 **project 层**(`<cwd>/.env`)的凭据,**user 层**(`$DSH_HOME/.env`)与继承环境不受影响——避免破坏 `$DSH_HOME/.env` 配置 key 的合法用法(#981 场景依赖该配置)。

- Fork 分支:`https://github.com/IHateTheWorld-LYK/deepseek-harness/tree/fix/project-env-credential-hijack`
- 提交:`0de34dd` — `https://github.com/IHateTheWorld-LYK/deepseek-harness/commit/0de34dd31c930cc83983cadec76baa5d3e47d217`
- 对比(`47f9438...0de34dd`):`https://github.com/IHateTheWorld-LYK/deepseek-harness/compare/47f9438...0de34dd`
- 拉取请求入口:`https://github.com/IHateTheWorld-LYK/deepseek-harness/pull/new/fix/project-env-credential-hijack`

**改动**:

1. `packages/boot/app-boot/src/index.ts`:新增 `PROJECT_PROTECTED_NAMES = new Set(['DEEPSEEK_API_KEY'])`(与 `cordis.patch.yml` 的 `apiKeyEnv` 引用对齐);`readEnvLayer` 增加 `project` 标志,仅对 project 层拒绝受保护凭据。原 bootstrap-only 拦截逻辑与文案(`/only the launching environment may set/`)不变;
2. 新增 `packages/boot/app-boot/tests/credential-protection.spec.ts`:project 层拒绝 key、大小写不敏感、原 bootstrap 文案不变、parse-before-apply(拒绝时零物化)、user 层仍接受 key;
3. `packages/credentials/credentials-local/tests/dsh-hijack-verify.spec.ts` 改写为端到端修复验证:恶意 project `.env` 在启动即被拒,`resolve()` 再也拿不到攻击者 key;合法 `$DSH_HOME/.env` key 经真实启动快照端到端解析正常。

**验证(真实包代码,`pnpm install` 后)**:

- 修复后:两包套件 `pnpm vitest run packages/boot/app-boot/tests packages/credentials/credentials-local/tests` → **12 files,166 passed,1 skipped**。修复前基线为 11 files / 162 passed / 1 skipped;净增 4 = 新增保护测试 +5、原"接受 key"证据测试改写 −1;
- 上方"真实包代码验证"记录的是修复前基线(证明漏洞存在);该证据测试现已改写为"拒绝 key"断言,即修复后的回归防线。

> 与既有讨论的区别:本报告是**恶意项目替换用户凭据**(对话重定向);#962 方向相反(代理窃取 key 外传)、#981 为空值遮蔽、`#190` 为黑名单导致启动失败——与本报告共享黑名单机制但方向相反(它关心"拦得太狠",本报告关心"拦得不够")。

discussions.title: [Python SDK resource safety] Runtime stderr lines can grow memory without bound
discussions.body:
## Summary

The Python SDK retains only the latest 400 runtime stderr lines, but one line has no size limit. A broken or hostile runtime can therefore grow the SDK process without bound by writing diagnostic bytes without a newline. A completed oversized line is also materialized in full before the 400-line deque can evict anything.

This is a separate input boundary from JSON-RPC stdout: stderr is human-facing diagnostic text, but it is still read by the long-lived SDK process and attached to transport exceptions.

## Deterministic reproduction

The regression launches a real Python subprocess that writes one 65,537-byte stderr line, then a useful diagnostic line, and exits. On the official implementation, the transport error contains the entire first line:

```text
FAILED test_client_bounds_oversized_stderr_line_and_keeps_following_diagnostics
...
assert len(error_text) < 1024
E  AssertionError: assert 65641 < 1024
```

`deque(maxlen=400)` limits completed line count only; `for line in proc.stderr` has already retained and decoded the entire physical line by that point.

## Proposed fix

- Read stderr from the underlying buffered byte stream in fixed 8 KiB chunks.
- Add a positive-integer `max_stderr_line_bytes` option, defaulting to 64 KiB, to both high- and low-level Python SDK configuration.
- Release an oversized prefix immediately, discard through its newline, append one compact omission marker, then resume with the next diagnostic line.
- Count raw UTF-8 bytes, preserve exact-limit and unterminated EOF behavior, and reject invalid values before starting a subprocess.
- Export `DEFAULT_MAX_STDERR_LINE_BYTES` and document the memory/debugging trade-off in the SDK reference, tutorial, and bilingual implementation note.

The runtime is not terminated because stderr is not protocol input. A newline is a deterministic resynchronization point, so dropping only the malformed diagnostic preserves later useful context.

## Verification

- Old-behavior regression: **fails with a 65,641-character exception**
- Fixed regression: omission marker present, following useful diagnostic preserved, complete exception below 1 KiB
- Full Python SDK suite: **57 passed, 10 skipped** (the skips require a bundled runtime carrier)
- Exact boundary, UTF-8 byte accounting, valid neighboring lines, unterminated EOF, invalid configuration, exported default, and high-level propagation: **covered**
- Repository lint, type checking, 28 documentation gates, translation pairing, duplication, whitespace, and pre-push checks: **passed**

## Relation to Discussion #1555

Discussion #1555 protects newline-delimited JSON-RPC messages on Python runtime **stdout**, where legitimate structured payloads can be large and the proposed default is 160 MiB. This report protects human-facing runtime **stderr**, whose diagnostic tail should remain compact. Separate limits avoid shrinking valid protocol traffic merely to protect logs.

## Contribution

- Compare: https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/compare/master...Lzb-gzist:agent/python-sdk-stderr-frame-byte-limit
- Branch: `Lzb-gzist:agent/python-sdk-stderr-frame-byte-limit`
- Commit: `62ac170897278207950c4e5832f481321156b83c`
- Base verified against upstream `master`: `47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a`

I searched the latest 100 official Discussions before posting. The closest report is #1555, but it covers the distinct stdout JSON-RPC boundary described above.

The upstream repository currently has pull requests disabled, so I am sharing the reproducible report, verified patch, tests, and documentation here for maintainer review.

discussions.title: dsh-computer-use-windows:Windows Computer Use for DSH — 窗口绑定、验证闭环、纯 OCR 模式(填补 Windows 空白)
discussions.body:
### TL;DR

为 DeepSeek Harness 发布 **Windows 版 computer use 插件**(参考实现阶段):窗口绑定截图/OCR、按文字点击 + 验证闭环、可插拔视觉模型、**纯 OCR 模式零外部依赖**。生态里已有 macOS 的 [Anionex/dsh-computer-use](https://github.com/Anionex/dsh-computer-use),Windows 侧此前是空白 —— 我们补上了。

Repo: https://github.com/Altairpaca/dsh-computer-use-windows (MIT)

### 背景:一次真实实验的教训

在 Windows 上操作保险"云助理"客户端(Chromium 内嵌手机视图)提取客户数据时,"截图 → VLM 报坐标 → 点击"工作流反复失败:点击系统性偏移(识别偏上、行为偏下)、点错入口、全屏截图混入其他窗口文字、窗口句柄失效。复盘(见 repo `docs/experiment-findings.zh.md`)得出四个根因,全部指向"盲坐标"工作流。

### 设计:四条原则

1. **窗口绑定** —— 所有截图/OCR/点击在目标窗口坐标空间内进行,点击自动回加窗口偏移;句柄动态解析,点击前校验前台窗口;
2. **文字即坐标** —— `computer_click_text`:OCR 定位文字中心再点击,模型不再猜坐标;
3. **验证闭环** —— 点击后自动截图+OCR 校验期望状态,失败按偏移网格重试,返回证据,"盲试"变"可证明";
4. **感知可配置** —— 视觉模型任意 OpenAI 兼容端点可插拔;`mode:"ocr"` 纯 OCR 模式下全部操作零外部 API,适合无 key/内网/隐私敏感场景。

### 现状与路线图

- ✅ 实验复盘 / 设计文档(含完整 config schema:`vision` provider、`ocr` 预处理/模糊匹配/窗口过滤、`verify` 偏移网格、`dpi` 校准)
- ✅ `helper/cu.ps1` v2 参考实现(已在本机冒烟测试:DPI-aware、窗口枚举、窗口截图、OCR 全部通过)
- 🚧 Bundle 化(plugins/ 骨架)与一键安装 —— 调研期后定稿
- 📋 跨平台调研计划(Claude/OpenAI/Gemini/UFO/OmniParser/UI-TARS…)已公开在 repo `docs/research-plan.zh.md`

### 求反馈

1. Windows 上大家怎么处理 VLM grounding 偏差?(偏移网格?编号标注?UIA 树?)
2. 纯 OCR 模式 + 验证闭环够用吗?还是需要语义树(UIAutomation)?
3. 愿意一起做 Windows 版"语义优先"第二代的,欢迎来 repo 讨论。

### 致谢

设计借鉴 [Anionex/dsh-computer-use](https://github.com/Anionex/dsh-computer-use)、[ezpzai/codex-computer-use-windows](https://github.com/ezpzai/codex-computer-use-windows)、[ysr666/dsh-vision-router](https://github.com/ysr666/dsh-vision-router)。

discussions.title: 非官方社区：DeepSeek Harness 生态大全（mydsh.dev）诚邀共建
discussions.body:
# 给 DeepSeek Harness 加一个「定时任务」能力:到点自动跑(社区插件)

DeepSeek Harness 的 agent 跑起来很能干活,但有个场景一直要人盯着:**
想在固定时间自动做点什么**——比如每天凌晨整理一次工作区、定期跑个巡检脚本、到点提醒自己某件事。之前只能靠外部 cron,或者人肉记住。

我们做了一个社区插件 **`dsh-schedule-tasks`**,把定时任务直接做进了 DSH:

## 它做了什么

- **5 段式 cron 解析**:`17 4 * * *` 这种标准写法,也支持自定义,不依赖系统 cron
- **侧边栏任务面板**:在 Web GUI 侧边栏直接「新建 / 编辑 / 启停 / 删除 / 手动触发」定时任务,可视化看列表和日志
- **host + headless 都能跑**:web profile 和 headless profile 都验证激活过,独立进程也能定时干活
- **动作可扩展**:目前支持 shell 命令触发,可以定时跑脚本、发通知
- **持久化**:任务配置存在 `$DSH_HOME/storages`,重启不丢

## 几个实际用法

```bash
# 每天 04:17 自动跑数据刷新
17 4 * * *  /path/to/refresh_data.py

# 每 30 分钟巡检一次服务状态
*/30 * * * *  /path/to/healthcheck.sh
```

## 插件是这么来的

这个插件是我们(MyDSH,一个**非官方**社区,mydsh.dev)在日常维护社区站时被真实需求逼出来的——每天凌晨要自动刷新插件数据,手动记着太容易忘,干脆做成了插件。现在它也在插件大全里(mydsh.dev/plugins 搜「schedule」能找到)。

如果你也有「到点自动跑」的需求,或者想要更丰富的动作类型(比如定时发消息、定时触发 agent 任务),欢迎在评论区聊聊你的场景,也可以去 mydsh.dev 反馈页告诉我们——说不定下一个功能就是你提的。

discussions.title: dsh-no-console-flash:Windows 弹窗修复补丁(整合 #1344 + #1102,已验证)
discussions.body:
## 问题

DSH 在 Windows 上执行命令(沙箱 pwsh/bash、普通子进程)时,如果宿主没有控制台(桌面启动、后台服务),Windows 会给每个子进程新建一个可见控制台窗口,闪一下再关闭,打字都被打断。

已有讨论:[#1344](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1344)(沙箱弹窗+修复方案)、[#1102](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1102)(无控制台宿主弹 PowerShell 窗口)、[#1142](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1142)(频繁弹 CMD 窗口)。

## 为什么不能直接隐藏窗口

不能加 `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`:DSH 的 Windows ACL 沙箱用受限令牌跑子进程,隐藏控制台会让子进程死于 `0xC0000142`(DLL 初始化失败,[#810](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/810) 有记录)。

正确做法是 **#1344 的方案**:保持 `dwCreationFlags = 0`,用 STARTUPINFO 的 `STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW` + `SW_HIDE` 把新控制台设为隐藏。

## 补丁内容(两处,均已实测)

| 文件 | 改动 | 来源 |
|---|---|---|
| `dsh-sandbox-windows-acl/lib/types-*.js` | 两处 spawn:`dwFlags` 256→257(加 `STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW`),新增 `wShowWindow: 0`(`SW_HIDE`) | #1344 |
| `dsh-subprocess-local/lib/index.js` | spawn 加 `windowsHide: true` | #1102 |

## 验证结果(本机实测)

- 补丁前后沙箱命令输出一致(无功能回归)
- 隐藏窗口子进程检测:`hwnd=0 visible=no-window`
- 补丁脚本幂等,重跑全部 skip,有 `.noconsole.bak` 备份
- 升级 DSH 后重跑一次即可(幂等)

## 使用

```bash
node patch.cjs   # 默认补 ~/.dsh,可传 DSH_HOME 路径
```

仓库:https://github.com/Culeot/dsh-no-console-flash(README 中英双语)

欢迎官方采纳此改动进正式包(两个包的 spawn 路径都漏了窗口隐藏,`dsh-native-command`/`dsh-host-directory-picker-native` 等组件已有 `windowsHide`)。

discussions.title: [Show & Tell] topology: visualize your dsh plugin dependency graph (+ how to ship a third-party plugin)
discussions.body:
# Topology: visualize your dsh plugin dependency graph (and a third-party plugin integration walkthrough)

> A show-and-tell + integration guide for shipping an *external* plugin into the DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) monorepo.

## TL;DR

I built **`topology`**, a plugin that renders a live SVG dependency graph of your running `dsh` instance: every loaded plugin as a node, every `inject` dependency as an edge, and every service as a hub. While wiring it in, I hit (and solved) the three real gotchas that any third-party plugin author will hit. This post is the guide I wish I had.

Repo: https://github.com/qidiai/dsh-contrib-topology — feedback wanted on the integration contract below. (Please associate the repo with the `dsh-plugin` topic so others can discover it.)

---

## 1. What `topology` does

`dsh` is "everything is a plugin", which means the *runtime shape* of your agent is a graph: plugins depend on services (`ctx.llm`, `ctx.tools`, `ctx.sessions`…), services are provided by other plugins, and `inject` declarations form the edges.

`topology` exposes one Host Remote method, `graph()`, that scans `ctx.loader.entries()` and returns a `TopologySnapshot`:

- **plugin nodes** — grouped by their Cordis `group` (core / contrib / third-party), with their `fiber` lifecycle phase (`pending → active → disabled`)
- **service nodes** — every key a plugin `inject`s becomes a hub
- **edges**:
  - `depends-on` — a plugin → a service it injects
  - `provides` — a service → the plugin that declares it (reversed from the hub)
  - `contains` — the Cordis parent/child link between plugins
  - `disabled` edges are rendered dashed (a disabled plugin still has `inject`s wired)

The client side is a `Settings → Plugins → Topology` tab that fetches the snapshot and draws the SVG. No backend beyond the standard Host Remote round-trip.

---

## 2. The integration contract (the part that matters)

`dsh` does **not** auto-discover third-party plugins. To make one first-class you must touch **three** places, plus handle one TypeScript composite-project trap.

### Wiring A — root `tsconfig` references (both faces)

Add your package to **both** project graphs so `tsc -b` type-checks it:

```jsonc
// tsconfig.host.json
{ "references": [ { "path": "./packages/contrib/topology" } ] }

// tsconfig.client.json
{ "references": [ { "path": "./packages/contrib/topology/tsconfig.client.json" } ] }
```

### Wiring B — the `dsh-api-remotes` assembly (only if you expose a Host Remote)

If your plugin has a Host Remote face (mine does — `graph()`), the client can't call it unless the remote is registered in the central assembly. Two edits in `packages/api/remotes/package.json`:

```jsonc
"peerDependencies":   { "@deepseek-ai/dsh-contrib-topology": "workspace:^", ... },
"devDependencies":    { "@deepseek-ai/dsh-contrib-topology": "workspace:^", ... }
```

…and in `packages/api/remotes/src/client/index.ts`:

```ts
import topologyRemote from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-contrib-topology/remote'
// ...
for (const contribution of [ /* ...existing... */ topologyRemote ]) {
  // aggregated into TypertClientRemote so ctx.remote.topology resolves
}
```

Without this, `ctx.remote.topology` simply does not exist at type level.

### Wiring C — the web roster (the "it compiles but there's no tab" trap)

This is the one nobody tells you. The web client does **not** statically import your plugin. `packages/bundle/web-app/cordis.patch.yml` holds an explicit *roster* of browser plugins; the loader loads each entry's host face into the host bundle and client face into the client bundle. If your package isn't in that list, it builds fine and **silently never appears in the UI**.

```yaml
# packages/bundle/web-app/cordis.patch.yml
- id: topology
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-contrib-topology'
```

The `name` is the package name; dual-face packages need only one entry (host + client come from the same package's `.` and `./client` exports).

### Trap — TS5055: dual-face shared types overwrite

A dual-face package compiles the *same* `src/types.ts` into both the host and client faces, both emitting to `lib/types/`. If you blow away `lib` and rebuild, one face's `tsc` run overwrites the other's `types.d.ts` → `TS5055`.

Fix: give each face its own incremental build info and let incremental builds coexist:

```jsonc
// tsconfig.json (host face)
{ "compilerOptions": { "tsBuildInfoFile": "lib/tsconfig.host.tsbuildinfo" } }
// tsconfig.client.json (client face)
{ "compilerOptions": { "tsBuildInfoFile": "lib/tsconfig.client.tsbuildinfo" } }
```

And import the shared types by **relative path** (`'../types.ts'`), never via the package name cross-face — that triggers `TS6307`.

---

## 3. Build & serve notes

Client bundles (`lib/client.js`) are produced per-package via `tsdown --env.DSH_BUILD_FACE client` (each client package needs its own `tsdown.config.ts` using the `clientBundle` preset). The web build (`pnpm build:web`) does **not** inline plugins — they're served at runtime by `dsh web`.

Two things to know about the serve endpoint:

- **Manifest IDs are full package names.** The correct URL is
  `GET /plugins/@deepseek-ai/dsh-contrib-topology/client.js`
  not `/plugins/topology/client.js`. (Every official plugin follows the same rule — a 404 here almost always means you used the short id.)
- `dsh web` reads the plugin set at startup; after editing the roster, restart the server.

> **Build environment note (Windows):** a full `pnpm build:lib` with rolldown writing ~200 packages in parallel can trip `os error 5` (access denied) on freshly-written `.js` files when real-time antivirus locks them. Building packages **serially** (`RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1`, one `tsdown` invocation per package) sidesteps it cleanly. On CI / Linux this doesn't bite.

---

## 4. What's next

This is the P2 milestone of a larger plan: I'm exploring how to bring a config-driven, multi-tool *orchestration* layer (Bayesian routing across coding agents, an observe/proxy, an MCP bridge) into `dsh` as a set of plugins. `topology` is the visualization foothold.

**I'd love feedback on:**

1. Is registering third-party Host Remotes in `dsh-api-remotes` the intended path, or is there a cleaner extension point I missed?
2. Should the web roster (`cordis.patch.yml`) support a `cordis.yml`-style patch so external plugins don't require a core-ish edit? (This feels like the biggest friction for the plugin ecosystem.)
3. Naming / scope for the orchestration plugins.

Repo: https://github.com/qidiai/dsh-contrib-topology (associate it with the `dsh-plugin` topic to help others discover it). The package lives as source on GitHub for now — publishing under `@deepseek-ai/*` isn't possible from a community account, so the repo is the distribution channel. Happy to turn section 2 into official docs if useful.

discussions.title: [TypeScript SDK resource safety] Runtime stderr lines can grow memory without bound
discussions.body:
## Summary

The TypeScript SDK keeps only the newest 400 runtime stderr lines, but the *current* line was accumulated with `stderrBuffer += chunk` until a newline arrived. A runtime that emits one very large or never-terminated diagnostic line can therefore grow the SDK process memory without bound before the 400-line retention limit has any effect.

I reproduced this deterministically with a scripted runtime that writes a 65,537-byte stderr line, then a useful diagnostic line. Before the fix, the captured error text reached 65,606 characters even when the configured per-line budget was 1 KiB.

## Root cause

The line-count limit applies only after newline splitting. It does not constrain the in-progress string, and JavaScript string length is not a reliable raw-byte limit for UTF-8 process output.

## Proposed fix

The contribution replaces the unbounded string accumulator with a raw-buffer stderr framer that:

- defaults to a 64 KiB per-line byte budget;
- exposes `maxStderrLineBytes` through both the low-level client and `DeepSeekHarness` launch options;
- validates the limit before spawning the runtime;
- releases an oversized prefix immediately, discards through the next newline, and records a bounded omission marker;
- resumes normally so later useful diagnostics are preserved;
- handles exact-limit, multibyte UTF-8, fragmented chunks, and final unterminated lines.

## Verification

- The old deterministic regression failed with 65,606 captured characters under a 1 KiB limit.
- The fixed SDK client suite passes: 51 tests.
- Package lint and TypeScript compilation pass.
- Repository lint, full typecheck, documentation sync, translation pairing, duplication, and diff checks pass.

## Relationship to recent reports

- #1560 applies the same resource-safety contract to the **Python SDK process stderr reader**. This report covers the independent **TypeScript SDK client implementation**.
- #1551 bounds **JSON-RPC stdout protocol frames** in the TypeScript SDK transport. Runtime stderr is a separate diagnostic channel with a much smaller default budget and different recovery behavior.

I searched the latest 100 Discussions before posting and found no existing report for the TypeScript SDK stderr path.

## Contribution

- Compare: https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/compare/master...Lzb-gzist:agent/typescript-sdk-stderr-byte-limit
- Branch: `agent/typescript-sdk-stderr-byte-limit`
- Commit: `777a3518a111e993241da1f908a6c62b64b60acd`
- Base: `47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a`

The official repository currently has Pull Requests disabled, so I am sharing the reproducible case, verified fix, and compare link here for maintainer review.

discussions.title: [TypeScript SDK lifecycle] start() reports success after terminal close
discussions.body:
## Summary

The high-level TypeScript `DeepSeekHarness.start()` can report success after the harness has been permanently closed. If one handshake succeeded before `close()`, a later `start()` returns the memoized resolved Promise even though the owned runtime process has already been reaped and the low-level client is terminal.

This makes the public readiness boundary misleading: callers proceed as if a runtime were available, and only discover the lifecycle error in a later operation.

## Deterministic reproduction

1. Construct `DeepSeekHarness` against the scripted runtime.
2. Await `harness.start()` so `initialize` succeeds and is memoized.
3. Await `harness.close()` so the runtime is shut down and reaped.
4. Await `harness.start()` again.

Before the fix, step 4 resolves to `undefined`; the regression fails with `promise resolved "undefined" instead of rejecting`.

## Root cause

`start()` consulted `this.initialized` before enforcing `this.closed`. The cached successful Promise therefore outlived the resource whose readiness it represented. The low-level `HarnessClient` already refuses reuse correctly, but it was never reached on this path.

## Proposed fix

The contribution makes the high-level terminal state authoritative before the handshake cache. Every `start()` after `close()` now rejects with the exported `TransportClosedError`, including after a previously successful initialization. Successful memoization while open and fresh-client retry after a failed handshake remain unchanged.

The bilingual SDK lifecycle documentation now states this contract explicitly.

## Verification

- The deterministic old-behavior regression fails by resolving stale success and passes after the fix.
- The TypeScript SDK client suite passes: 48 tests.
- Package lint and TypeScript compilation pass.
- Repository lint, full typecheck, documentation sync (28 gates), translation pairing, duplication, pre-commit, pre-push, and whitespace checks pass.

This is related to #1546, which made low-level transport closure terminal. This report covers the independent high-level readiness cache that could bypass that state.

I searched the latest 100 Discussions before posting and found no existing report for this high-level start-after-close path.

## Contribution

- Compare: https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/compare/master...Lzb-gzist:agent/sdk-start-after-close-terminal
- Branch: `agent/sdk-start-after-close-terminal`
- Commit: `23d375d29869b48f82b997bb8204b510efba0a59`
- Base: `47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a`

The official repository currently has Pull Requests disabled, so I am sharing the reproducible case, verified fix, and compare link here for maintainer review.
