discussions.title: Bug: KV cache hit rate collapses to 0–3% after session resume — system-prompt section ordering drift (cordis preset)
discussions.body:
# Bug Report: KV cache hit rate collapses after session resume — system-prompt section ordering drift

> Status: Confirmed (official source evidence + runtime data + deterministic reproduction)
> Scope: `cordis` (creative) mode + frequent restart/resume users — full miss on the first round after resume
> Keywords: `system-prompt`, `KV cache`, `prompt section order`, `resume`

---

## 1. Summary

DeepSeek Harness collapses the **KV cache hit rate from ~99% to 0.3%–3% on the first model request after a session resume / restart**, re-billing the entire cached prefix at full price and adding significant token cost and latency.

Root cause: **unstable ordering of system-prompt prompt sections**. The official `dsh-system-prompt` uses a stable sort by `order`; when two sections share the same `order`, their order depends on the **plugin registration (insertion) order** — which is not stable across session resume/restart (host-layer vs preset-layer mount order can differ). The same-`order` sections can swap positions after restart, changing the **system-prompt prefix bytes → invalidating every provider KV cache key → full miss.**

> This only affects users on the **`cordis` (creative) preset**: it mounts both `tool:workflow` (universal) and `tool:cordis` (creative-mode-only), two `order: 115` sections that queue next to each other. Other presets lack the second `order: 115` and are not affected.

## 2. Environment

- DSH version line: `0.1.0-rc.6`
- Relevant packages:
  - `@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt@0.1.0-rc.6` (at fault)
  - `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-workflow@0.1.0-rc.6` (conflict A, universal tool guidance, order 115)
  - `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-cordis@0.1.0-rc.6` (conflict B, creative-mode-only tool guidance, order 115)
- **Reproduction environment**:
  - Must be on the **`cordis` (creative) preset** — it mounts both `dsh-tool-workflow` (universal) and `dsh-tool-cordis` (creative-mode-only), producing **two `order: 115` sections** that queue adjacently;
  - Other presets (`code` / `standard` / `minimal`) mount only `dsh-tool-workflow`, so there is **no second `order: 115`** and this root cause cannot trigger;
  - The session must be **restarted / resumed** (triggering `session/end-seed` + `request/header reason=resume`), and that particular restart must actually flip the registration order.
- Evidence sources: session run logs (`.jsonl.zstd`), official source static analysis, deterministic runtime experiment.

## 3. Impact

- Affects **`cordis` (creative)-mode users who restart/resume frequently**.
- After each resume, the first request's cached prefix (measured up to **460k–590k tokens**) is fully missed and re-billed at full price.
- Token cost and latency rise significantly under long-session / frequent-restart workflows.
- Evidence: `cacheReadTokens` drops from ~99% (e.g. `cacheRead=294784 / input=146`) to ~1% (e.g. `cacheRead=8704 / input=286440`).

## 4. Reproduction

1. Start a long session on the **`cordis` (creative) preset** (accumulate tens to hundreds of thousands of tokens).
2. Record the normal hit rate (expected ~99%).
3. **Restart DSH / resume the session** (triggers `session/end-seed` + `request/header reason=resume`).
4. Observe the first resumed request's `usage.cacheReadTokens`: **hit rate collapses to 0.3%–3%**.
5. Without restart the hit rate stays 99%+; after restart it only collapses if the section ordering flipped — **flip → collapse**.

### Measured data (first 14 restarts, first-round hit rate)

| # | First-round hit rate | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3.3% | ❌ full miss |
| 2 | 99.6% | ✅ |
| 3 | 1.4% | ❌ full miss |
| 4 | 100.0% | ✅ |
| 5 | 0.8% | ❌ full miss |
| 6 | 1.1% | ❌ full miss |
| 7 | 99.8% | ✅ |
| 8 | 0.0% | ❌ full miss (compaction-associated) |
| 9 | — (no request) | — |
| 10 | 97.4% | ✅ |
| 11 | 32.3% | ⚠️ partial miss (compaction-associated) |
| 12 | 2.9% | ❌ full miss |
| 13 | 97.5% | ✅ |
| 14 | 99.5% | ✅ |

7 of the first 14 were affected (6 full misses + one 32.3%), i.e. **~50% flip rate**. After applying the fix, 3 consecutive restarts hit 99.9% / 99.9% / 100%.

**Steady-state hit rate (excluding abnormal rounds, cold start, and not-yet-recovered rounds, but including normal compaction/change rounds) = 99.60%**, stable across four different exclusion criteria. Roughly 3/4 of the 0.4% miss is normal per-round cache loss (0.1–1% each); the rest is residual gap damage.

## 5. Root Cause

### 5.1 Official sort algorithm

`packages/core/system-prompt/src/index.ts` (official source, line 504):

```ts
const sectionDefinitions = [...sectionByName.values()].sort((a, b) => a.order - b.order)
```

- `Array.prototype.sort` is **stable**: with equal `order`, it keeps the iteration order of `sectionByName.values()` (i.e., the **insertion order** of `NamedEntries`).
- Insertion order = the **registration order** of each plugin calling `ctx.systemPrompt.section()`.
- **Registration order is unstable across resume/restart**: host-layer (`dsh-base`) vs preset-layer plugin mount order can differ → same-`order` sections swap.

### 5.2 The two conflicting official plugins both register order=115

**Conflict A (universal tool guidance)**: `packages/workflow/tool-workflow/src/index.ts` (lines 212–214) — the `workflow` tool (large multi-agent orchestration), **mounted by every preset**:

```ts
ctx.systemPrompt.section({
  name: 'tool:workflow',
  order: 115,
  text: `Use the ${toolName} tool ONLY when the user explicitly asks for a workflow...`
})
```

**Conflict B (creative-mode-only tool guidance)**: `packages/extensions/tool-cordis/src/index.ts` (line 36) — the dynamic Cordis plugin toolset (`cordis_inspect_*` / `cordis_define` / `cordis_run` / `cordis_stop` / `cordis_undefine`), **mounted only by the `cordis` (creative) preset**:

```ts
ctx.systemPrompt.section({ name: 'tool:cordis', order: 115, text: CORDIS_SYSTEM_PROMPT })
```

Both are `order: 115`. Under a stable sort, whichever registers first comes first; when the registration order flips across restart, the two swap positions (measured line 34 ↔ line 140), and everything after the swap point misaligns.

> **Key**: `tool:workflow` is universal, `tool:cordis` is creative-mode-only — so **only the `cordis` (creative) preset mounts both `order: 115` sections**. Other presets lack the second `order: 115` and cannot trigger this root cause (see 5.5).

### 5.2a Breakpoint location (byte-by-byte evidence)

Comparing a normal round vs the immediately following resume round byte-by-byte:

| | Normal (before restart) | Resume (after restart) |
|---|---|---|
| Total tokens | 294,930 | 295,144 |
| Cache hit | 294,784 (99.95%) | **8,704 (2.95%)** |
| `Use the workflow tool ONLY...` | **line 34** | pushed to line 140 |
| `# Dynamic Cordis Plugins` | after workflow | moved earlier |

- The two rounds are **almost identical in content and total tokens** — this is an **ordering change, not a content change**.
- Breakpoint = token 8,704 = inside the system prompt's "tool guidance zone" (the order-115 conflict point).
- The other 5 full-miss rounds break at 2,560 / 3,968 / 4,224 / 5,760 / 8,704 tokens — all in the front tool-guidance zone, consistent with "break at the `tool:cordis`/`tool:workflow` swap point".

### 5.2b All 17 restarts verified individually (swap ↔ hit rate)

Comparing each resume against its preceding normal round (using the character positions of `Use the workflow tool` and `Dynamic Cordis` inside the `request/header` system prompt):

| resume# | prev order | this order | swap? | first-round hit | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | cordis-first | workflow-first | 🔁 | 3.3% | ❌ collapse |
| 2 | workflow-first | workflow-first | same | 99.6% | ✅ |
| 3 | workflow-first | cordis-first | 🔁 | 1.4% | ❌ collapse |
| 4 | cordis-first | cordis-first | same | 86.7% | ✅ |
| 5 | cordis-first | workflow-first | 🔁 | 0.8% | ❌ collapse |
| 6 | workflow-first | cordis-first | 🔁 | 1.1% | ❌ collapse |
| 7 | cordis-first | cordis-first | same | 99.8% | ✅ |
| 8 | cordis-first | cordis-first | same | 0.0% | ❌ (compaction-associated, not a swap) |
| 9 | cordis-first | workflow-first | 🔁 | 97.4% | ✅ (swap near tail) |
| 10 | workflow-first | cordis-first | 🔁 | 97.4% | ✅ (swap near tail) |
| 11 | cordis-first | workflow-first | 🔁 | 32.3% | ⚠️ partial |
| 12 | workflow-first | cordis-first | 🔁 | 2.9% | ❌ collapse |
| 13 | cordis-first | cordis-first | same | 97.5% | ✅ |
| 14 | cordis-first | cordis-first | same | 99.5% | ✅ |
| 15–17 | cordis-first | cordis-first | same | 99.9/99.9/100% | ✅ (after fix) |

**Correlation**: 5 full misses + 1 partial among 8 swaps; only 1 miss among 9 non-swaps (and that one was compaction-related). **Swap ↔ collapse is strongly correlated; root cause confirmed.**

### 5.2b-2 Regression matrix (`system` / `tools` hashed separately)

Per a community suggestion (discussion #2141 comment), for the 17 resume rounds that produced requests we hashed `request/header.system` and `request/header.tools` separately, to isolate "prompt drift" from "tool change":

| resume | system hash | tools hash | 1st-round hit | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | changed | unchanged | 3.3% | ❌ collapse |
| 2 | unchanged | unchanged | 99.6% | ✅ ok |
| 3 | changed | unchanged | 1.4% | ❌ collapse |
| 4 | unchanged | unchanged | 86.7% | ✅ ok |
| 5 | changed | **changed** | 0.8% | ❌ collapse |
| 6 | changed | unchanged | 1.1% | ❌ collapse |
| 7 | unchanged | unchanged | 99.8% | ✅ ok |
| 8 | changed | unchanged | 0.0% | ❌ collapse |
| 9 | changed | unchanged | 97.4% | ✅ ok (tail-only) |
| 10 | changed | **changed** | 32.3% | ⚠️ partial |
| 11 | changed | unchanged | 2.9% | ❌ collapse |
| 12 | unchanged | unchanged | 97.5% | ✅ ok |
| 13 | unchanged | unchanged | 99.5% | ✅ ok |
| 14–17 | unchanged | unchanged | 99.9%+ | ✅ ok (after fix) |

**Conclusions**:
- 8 rounds with a `system` change → 6 full collapses + 1 partial + 1 tail-only; 9 rounds without a `system` change → **all normal**.
- `tools` changed only twice (#5, #10), and in both of those the `system` also changed — **`tools` never independently caused a collapse**; `system` is the only independent variable.
- After the fix (deterministic tie-breaker), both `system` and `tools` stay stable and hit rate is 99.9%+.

### 5.2c Hit-rate magnitude: a fingerprint of breakpoint location

- **Breakpoint inside the system prompt (ordering drift) → 0–3% hit** (only the first ~34 lines of the system prompt still hit).
- **Breakpoint in the tool zone (after the system prompt, e.g. tool add/remove) → 10%+ hit** (the whole system prompt still hits).

All 6 full misses reproduced here fall in **0–3.3%** — the unique fingerprint of "breakpoint inside the system prompt", distinct from the community-reported "tool-change → ~11%" scenario (see section 8).

### 5.3 The mechanism is officially acknowledged (but this case is not covered)

Official `packages/core/system-prompt/README.md`:

> **KV Cache effect**: Any change may invalidate reuse from the **first changed system-prompt token**.

The official fix `2026-07-21-compaction-summary-prefix-cache-reuse.md` already addressed **compaction-round** prefix reuse (moving the compaction instruction to the tail message), but **does not cover section-ordering drift in ordinary turns**.

### 5.3b Another gap source: compaction

Log review shows **compaction (session summarization) is itself also a gap trigger**:

```
After 1st compaction → first-round 0.0% (full miss)
After 2nd compaction → first-round 32.3%
After 3rd compaction → first-round 58.3%
```

Because compaction replaces history messages with a summary → the request prefix token sequence changes → cache key invalidates. This is a normal cost of the feature itself, but it shows that **any DSH-internal behavior that changes the request prefix** (compaction, ordering drift, conditional tool registration) can break the KV cache.

### 5.4 General risk: anything that changes the prefix breaks the cache

> Any factor that changes system-prompt prefix **content or ordering** across resume (same-`order` conflicts, conditional tool registration, dynamically injected content) can break the cache. This is a systemic weakness in DSH's prompt assembly "cross-resume stability".

### 5.5 Why this has not been found before (scope & discoverability)

1. **Narrow trigger**: only the `cordis` (creative) preset mounts both `tool:workflow` (order 115, universal) and `tool:cordis` (order 115, creative-only). Other presets have no second `order: 115`, so they never trigger this root cause.
2. **Masked by other factors**: community reports of cache misses are mostly attributed to **tool add/remove** (#935, #963), **compaction** (#1944), or **`--port 0` port change** (#2136) — all "obvious what changed" causes. Ordering drift is an "**internal order change with nothing visibly changed**" — it can only be found by byte-comparing the full system prompt of the round before and after restart (this report located it via character-position comparison in `request/header`).
3. **Different hit-rate magnitude**: tool-zone breakpoints still hit 10%+; this root cause's breakpoint is inside the system prompt, dropping the hit rate to 0–3% — a different magnitude and different breakpoint location from the community's "11%" case.

## 6. Deterministic Reproduction

Register two `order: 115` sections in a real runtime and observe `assemble()` under different registration orders:

| mode | registration order | order values | result | flips? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `same-ab` | A then B | both 115 | `A < B` | — |
| `same-ba` | B then A | both 115 | `B < A` | ❌ flips |
| `fix-ab` | A then B | A=115, B=114 | `B < A` (114 first) | ✅ stable |
| `fix-ba` | B then A | A=115, B=114 | `B < A` (114 first) | ✅ stable |

**Conclusion**: with equal `order`, ordering is fully determined by registration order; with different `order`, it is deterministic. This determines the fix direction.

## 7. Suggested Fix

### Official (root fix): add a deterministic tie-breaker

Change the comparator in `packages/core/system-prompt/src/index.ts` so same-`order` sections are ordered by **static fields**, not runtime registration order:

```ts
// current (unstable):
.sort((a, b) => a.order - b.order)

// fix (deterministic):
.sort((a, b) => a.order - b.order
  || a.name.length - b.name.length          // same order → by name length
  || (a.name < b.name ? -1 : a.name > b.name ? 1 : 0))  // same length → lexicographic
```

**Benefits**:
- Depends on no runtime state (registration order, plugin load order); pure, static.
- One change covers all future same-`order` conflicts.
- `tool:cordis` (11 chars) is always before `tool:workflow` (13 chars); prefix stays stable.

> Note: the official CONTRIBUTING.md says external PRs are **not accepted**; reports should go to GitHub Discussions.

> Community plugin (early share, for reference): `dsh-prompt-order-fix` (npm package **`@tiyirt/dsh-prompt-order-fix`**) — an **AI-written** plugin that subclasses `SystemPrompt` and overrides `assemble()` with the deterministic tie-breaker above, as a default-export class drop-in replacing the `system-prompt` row.
>
> ✅ **Tested**: core function verified in a real environment — 3 consecutive restarts after install returned 99.9%+ first-round hit rate; the fix works.
> ⚠️ **Not covered**: the **standalone npm one-command install path** (`npm install` + `dsh plugin add`) has not been verified; evaluate before installing. Once officially fixed, this plugin can be retired (remove the patch row to restore official behavior).

## 8. References

- Official sort source: `packages/core/system-prompt/src/index.ts:504`
- Conflict A: `packages/workflow/tool-workflow/src/index.ts:212-214`
- Conflict B: `packages/extensions/tool-cordis/src/index.ts:36`
- Official mechanism doc: `packages/core/system-prompt/README.md` (KV Cache effect)
- Official fixed: `.agents/notes/implemented/bug-fix/2026-07-21-compaction-summary-prefix-cache-reuse.md`
- Related community discussions (public):
  - `deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness` discussion #935 — tool add/remove → 97%→11% (tool-zone breakpoint, different magnitude from this report's system-prompt-internal breakpoint)
  - #963 — dynamic plugin tool registration breaks cross-session cache (tool-layer breakpoint)
  - #1944 — compaction request misses prefix cache (confirmed and fixed by a contributor)
  - #2136 — cache miss after restart (suspected `--port 0` port URL change; not concluded)

discussions.title: Bug：会话恢复后 KV 缓存命中率暴跌到 0–3% —— system-prompt section 排序漂移（cordis 创造模式）
discussions.body:
# Bug Report：DSH 会话恢复后缓存命中率暴跌（system-prompt section 排序漂移）

> 状态：已确认（含官方源码证据 + 运行数据 + 受控复现）
> 影响面：`cordis`（创造）模式 + 频繁重启的用户，在 resume/重启后第一轮全量 miss
> 关键词：`system-prompt`、`KV cache`、`prompt section order`、`resume`

---

## 1. 摘要（Summary）

DeepSeek Harness 在**会话恢复（resume / 重启）之后的第一轮模型请求**，KV 缓存命中率会从正常的 **~99% 暴跌到 0.3%~3%**，导致整个已缓存的历史前缀被全量重算，产生大量不必要的输入 token 计费与延迟。

根因是 **system prompt 的 prompt section 排序不稳定**：官方 `dsh-system-prompt` 用稳定排序按 `order` 排序，当两个 section 拥有相同的 `order` 值时，先后顺序取决于**插件注册（插入）顺序**；而注册顺序在会话恢复/重启时不稳定（host 层与 preset 层插件挂载顺序可能不同），导致同 order 的 section 在重启后互换位置。**system prompt 前缀字节变化 → provider KV 缓存 key 全部失效 → 全量 miss。**

> 该问题**仅影响 `cordis`（创造）模式**的用户：该模式同时挂载 `tool:workflow`（通用）与 `tool:cordis`（创造模式专属）两个 order=115 的 section；其他 preset 因缺少第二个 order=115 而不触发。

## 2. 环境（Environment）

- DSH 版本线：`0.1.0-rc.6`
- 相关包：
  - `@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt@0.1.0-rc.6`（问题所在）
  - `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-workflow@0.1.0-rc.6`（冲突方 A，通用工具引导，order 115）
  - `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-cordis@0.1.0-rc.6`（冲突方 B，创造模式专属工具引导，order 115）
- **触发环境（复现条件）**：
  - 必须使用 **`cordis`（创造）模式** preset —— 该模式同时挂载 `dsh-tool-workflow`（通用）与 `dsh-tool-cordis`（创造模式专属），产生**两个 order=115 的 section** 相邻排队；
  - 其他 preset（`code` / `standard` / `minimal`）只挂 `dsh-tool-workflow`，**没有第二个 order=115**，不受此根因影响；
  - 会话需**重启 / 恢复**（触发 `session/end-seed` + `request/header reason=resume`），且该次注册顺序恰好翻转。
- 复现载体：会话运行日志（`.jsonl.zstd`）+ 官方源码静态分析 + 受控动态实验

## 3. 影响（Impact）

- **影响面**：使用 **`cordis`（创造）模式**、且频繁重启/恢复会话的用户（该模式同时挂载两个 order=115 的 section）。
- 每次会话恢复后，第一轮请求携带的历史前缀（实测可达 **46 万 ~ 59 万 token**）全部 miss，按全价重新计费。
- 在长会话/频繁重启工作流下，token 成本与延迟显著上升。
- 命中率证据：`cacheReadTokens` 从正常轮次的 ~99%（如 `cacheRead=294784 / input=146`）跌到 ~1%（如 `cacheRead=8704 / input=286440`）。

## 4. 复现步骤（Reproduction）

1. 在 `cordis`（创造）preset 下开始一个长会话（积累到数万 ~ 数十万 token）。
2. 记录正常轮次命中率（预期 ~99%）。
3. **重启 DSH / 恢复会话**（触发 `session/end-seed` + `request/header reason=resume`）。
4. 观察恢复后第一轮请求的 `usage.cacheReadTokens`：**命中率暴跌到 0.3%~3%**。
5. 若无重启，命中率持续 99%+；重启后若 section 排序未翻转，则命中率正常——**翻转才暴跌**。

### 复现数据（实测，12 次 resume 对应表）

| resume# | system 是否变化 | 恢复后首请求命中率 | 备注 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | （首次） | 3.3% | 冷启动 |
| 2 | 同 | 99.6% ✅ | 未翻转，不跌 |
| 3 | 变 | 1.4% ❌ | 翻转 |
| 4 | 同 | 86.7% | 未翻转 |
| 5 | 变 | 0.8% ❌ | 翻转 |
| 6 | 变 | 1.1% ❌ | 翻转 |
| 7 | 同 | 99.8% ✅ | 未翻转，不跌 |
| 8 | 变 | 0.0% ❌ | 翻转 |
| 9 | 变 | 97.4% ✅ | 变但变化在尾部，不跌 |
| 10 | 变 | 97.4% ✅ | 同上 |
| 11 | 变 | 32.3% | 半跌 |
| 12 | 变 | 2.9% ❌ | 翻转 |

> 结论：**不是每次 resume 都暴跌，只有 system prompt 前缀变化（section 排序翻转）时才暴跌**；变化发生在前缀关键区（如 order 冲突的 section 交换）→ 全量 miss；发生在尾部 → 影响小。

### 最新量化（复查，同源会话日志）

**前 14 次重启的"恢复后第一轮"命中率**：

| # | 第一轮命中率 | 判定 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3.3% | ❌ 全 miss |
| 2 | 99.6% | ✅ |
| 3 | 1.4% | ❌ 全 miss |
| 4 | 100.0% | ✅ |
| 5 | 0.8% | ❌ 全 miss |
| 6 | 1.1% | ❌ 全 miss |
| 7 | 99.8% | ✅ |
| 8 | 0.0% | ❌ 全 miss（compaction 伴生） |
| 9 | （无请求） | — |
| 10 | 97.4% | ✅ |
| 11 | 32.3% | ⚠️ 部分 miss（compaction 伴生） |
| 12 | 2.9% | ❌ 全 miss |
| 13 | 97.5% | ✅ |
| 14 | 99.5% | ✅ |

**前 14 次中 7 次受影响（6 次全 miss + 1 次 32.3%），漂移率 ≈ 50%。** 修复后 3 次重启第一轮 = 99.9% / 99.9% / 100%。

**稳态命中率（排除异常轮次 + 冷启动 + 断层未恢复轮，含正常压缩/改动轮）= 99.60%**，该数字在"只抠第 1 轮 / 抠前 4 轮 / 抠全部未恢复轮 / 保留总结轮"四种口径下均一致，稳健。0.4% miss 中约 3/4 为每轮 0.1~1% 的正常缓存损耗，其余为断层残留。

## 5. 根因分析（Root Cause）

### 5.1 官方排序算法

`packages/core/system-prompt/src/index.ts`（官方源码，第 504 行）：

```ts
const sectionDefinitions = [...sectionByName.values()].sort((a, b) => a.order - b.order)
```

- `Array.prototype.sort` 是**稳定排序**：order 相同时，保持 `sectionByName.values()` 的迭代顺序（即 `NamedEntries` 的**插入顺序**）。
- 插入顺序 = 各插件调用 `ctx.systemPrompt.section()` 的**注册顺序**。
- **注册顺序跨 resume/重启不稳定**：host 层（`dsh-base`）与 preset 层（agent preset）的插件挂载顺序可能不同 → 同 order 的 section 插入顺序翻转。

### 5.2 冲突方：两个官方插件注册了相同的 order=115

**冲突方 A（通用工具引导）**：`packages/workflow/tool-workflow/src/index.ts`（官方源码，第 212-214 行）—— `workflow` 工具（大规模多 agent 编排），**所有 preset 都会挂载**：

```ts
ctx.systemPrompt.section({
  name: 'tool:workflow',
  order: 115,
  text: `Use the ${toolName} tool ONLY when the user explicitly asks for a workflow...`
})
```

**冲突方 B（创造模式专属工具引导）**：`packages/extensions/tool-cordis/src/index.ts`（官方源码，第 36 行）—— 动态 Cordis 插件工具集（`cordis_inspect_*` / `cordis_define` / `cordis_run` / `cordis_stop` / `cordis_undefine`），**仅 `cordis`（创造）模式挂载**：

```ts
ctx.systemPrompt.section({ name: 'tool:cordis', order: 115, text: CORDIS_SYSTEM_PROMPT })
```

两者都是 `order: 115`。稳定排序下，谁先注册谁在前；注册顺序跨重启翻转时，两个 section 在 system prompt 中的位置互换（实测第 34 行 ↔ 第 140 行），前缀从交换点起全部错位。

> **关键**：`tool:workflow` 通用、`tool:cordis` 为创造模式独有 —— 因此**只有 `cordis`（创造）模式会同时挂载这两个 order=115 的 section**，其他 preset 因缺少第二个 order=115 而不会触发此根因（详见 5.5）。

### 5.2a 断点定位（逐字节对比证据）

对同一会话中某一正常轮与紧随其后的 resume 轮做逐字节对比：

| | 正常轮（重启前） | resume 轮（重启后） |
|---|---|---|
| 总 token | 294,930 | 295,144 |
| 缓存命中 | 294,784（99.95%） | **8,704（2.95%）** |
| `Use the workflow tool ONLY...` | **第 34 行** | 被推到第 140 行 |
| `# Dynamic Cordis Plugins` | 在 workflow 之后 | 被提前 |

- 两轮**内容几乎相同、总 token 几乎一致**（不是内容变化，是**顺序变化**）。
- 断点 = 第 8,704 token 处 = system prompt 内"工具引导区"（order 115 冲突处）。
- 其余 5 次全 miss 轮的断点 token 数（2,560 / 3,968 / 4,224 / 5,760 / 8,704）全部落在 system prompt 前部工具引导区，与"断点在 `tool:cordis`/`tool:workflow` 交换处"一致。

### 5.2b 全部 17 次重启逐一验证（顺序互换 ↔ 命中率）

对每次 resume 与其前一个正常轮对比两个 section 的顺序（依据 `request/header` 内 system prompt 中 `Use the workflow tool` 与 `Dynamic Cordis` 的字符位置）：

| resume# | 前轮顺序 | 本轮顺序 | 互换? | 第一轮命中率 | 判定 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | cordis前 | workflow前 | 🔁 | 3.3% | ❌ 暴跌 |
| 2 | workflow前 | workflow前 | 同 | 99.6% | ✅ |
| 3 | workflow前 | cordis前 | 🔁 | 1.4% | ❌ 暴跌 |
| 4 | cordis前 | cordis前 | 同 | 86.7% | ✅ |
| 5 | cordis前 | workflow前 | 🔁 | 0.8% | ❌ 暴跌 |
| 6 | workflow前 | cordis前 | 🔁 | 1.1% | ❌ 暴跌 |
| 7 | cordis前 | cordis前 | 同 | 99.8% | ✅ |
| 8 | cordis前 | cordis前 | 同 | 0.0% | ❌（compaction 伴生，非互换）|
| 9 | cordis前 | workflow前 | 🔁 | 97.4% | ✅（互换在尾部）|
| 10 | workflow前 | cordis前 | 🔁 | 97.4% | ✅（互换在尾部）|
| 11 | cordis前 | workflow前 | 🔁 | 32.3% | ⚠️ 部分 |
| 12 | workflow前 | cordis前 | 🔁 | 2.9% | ❌ 暴跌 |
| 13 | cordis前 | cordis前 | 同 | 97.5% | ✅ |
| 14 | cordis前 | cordis前 | 同 | 99.5% | ✅ |
| 15–17 | cordis前 | cordis前 | 同 | 99.9/99.9/100% | ✅（修复后）|

**相关性**：8 次互换中 5 次全 miss + 1 次部分；9 次未互换仅 1 次暴跌（且为 compaction 因素）。**互换 ↔ 暴跌强相关，根因确认。**

### 5.2b-2 回归矩阵（`system` / `tools` 分开 hash）

响应社区建议（discussion #2141 评论），对 17 次有请求的 resume 分别对 `request/header.system` 与 `request/header.tools` 做 hash，隔离"提示词漂移"与"工具变化"两类原因：

| resume | system hash | tools hash | 恢复后首轮命中 | 判定 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 变化 | 不变 | 3.3% | ❌ 暴跌 |
| 2 | 不变 | 不变 | 99.6% | ✅ |
| 3 | 变化 | 不变 | 1.4% | ❌ 暴跌 |
| 4 | 不变 | 不变 | 86.7% | ✅ |
| 5 | 变化 | **变化** | 0.8% | ❌ 暴跌 |
| 6 | 变化 | 不变 | 1.1% | ❌ 暴跌 |
| 7 | 不变 | 不变 | 99.8% | ✅ |
| 8 | 变化 | 不变 | 0.0% | ❌ 暴跌 |
| 9 | 变化 | 不变 | 97.4% | ✅（尾部变化）|
| 10 | 变化 | **变化** | 32.3% | ⚠️ 部分 |
| 11 | 变化 | 不变 | 2.9% | ❌ 暴跌 |
| 12 | 不变 | 不变 | 97.5% | ✅ |
| 13 | 不变 | 不变 | 99.5% | ✅ |
| 14–17 | 不变 | 不变 | 99.9%+ | ✅（修复后）|

**结论**：
- `system` 变化的 8 次 → 6 次全 miss + 1 次部分 + 1 次尾部；`system` 不变的 9 次 → **全部正常**。
- `tools` 仅 2 次变化（#5、#10），且这 2 次 `system` 也同时变化——**`tools` 无任何独立造成暴跌的案例**；`system` 是唯一独立变量。
- 修复后（确定性 tie-breaker）`system` 与 `tools` 均稳定，命中 99.9%+。

### 5.2c 命中率量级：断点位置的指纹

- **断点在 system prompt 内部（排序漂移）→ 命中率 0~3%**（只剩 system prompt 前 ~34 行命中）
- **断点在工具区（system prompt 之后，如工具增删）→ 命中率 10%+**（system prompt 整段仍命中）

本报告复现的 6 次全 miss 全部落在 **0~3.3%**，是"断点在 system prompt 内部"的独有指纹——区别于社区报告的"工具变化导致 11% 量级"场景（见 8. 参考资料）。

### 5.3 官方已承认该机制（但未覆盖此场景）

官方 `packages/core/system-prompt/README.md`：

> **KV Cache effect**: Any change may invalidate reuse from the **first changed system-prompt token**.

官方已在 `2026-07-21-compaction-summary-prefix-cache-reuse.md` 修复**压缩轮**的前缀缓存复用（把压缩指令从 system prompt 移到末尾消息），但**未覆盖普通对话轮次中 section 排序漂移**的问题。

### 5.3b 另一个断层源：compaction（压缩总结）

复查日志发现 **compaction（会话压缩总结）本身也是断层触发源**：

```
第 1 次压缩后 → 恢复后第一轮 0.0%（全 miss）
第 2 次压缩后 → 恢复后第一轮 32.3%
第 3 次压缩后 → 恢复后第一轮 58.3%
```

原因：compaction 把历史消息替换成 summary → 请求前缀 token 序列变化 → 缓存 key 失效。这是"压缩功能本身"的代价（机制上正常），但说明**任何改变请求前缀的 DSH 内部行为**（压缩、排序漂移、条件注册工具）都会打穿 KV 缓存。官方已修 compaction 的前缀复用（把压缩指令移到 system prompt 末尾消息），但**未覆盖普通轮次的 section 排序漂移**。

### 5.4 同类风险：任何改变前缀的因素都会打穿缓存

> 结论：**任何导致 system prompt 前缀内容或顺序在 resume 前后变化的因素**（同 order 冲突、条件注册工具、动态注入内容）都会打穿缓存。这是 DSH prompt 组装在"跨恢复稳定性"上的系统性薄弱点。

### 5.5 为何此前未被发现（影响范围与可发现性）

1. **触发条件苛刻**：仅 `cordis`（创造）模式同时挂载 `tool:workflow`（order 115，通用）与 `tool:cordis`（order 115，创造模式专属）两个 section；其他 preset 无第二个 order=115，永不触发此根因。
2. **现象被其他因素遮蔽**：社区报告的缓存 miss 多归因于**工具增删**（如 #935、#963）或 **compaction**（如 #1944）或 **--port 0 端口变化**（如 #2136），均为"能直接看出什么变了"的显性原因；而排序漂移是"system prompt 内部顺序变化"——**必须对比重启前后两个请求的完整 system prompt 才能发现**（本报告即通过 `request/header` 内 system prompt 的字符位置对比定位）。
3. **命中率量级不同**：工具区断点仍有 10%+ 命中；本根因断点在 system prompt 内部，命中率直接掉到 0~3%，与社区报告的"11%"场景是不同量级、不同断点位置。

## 6. 受控复现实验（Deterministic Reproduction）

在真实运行环境中注册两个 `order: 115` 的 section，用不同注册顺序观察 `assemble()` 结果：

| 模式 | 注册顺序 | order 值 | 排列结果 | 是否翻转 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `same-ab` | 先 A 后 B | 都是 115 | `A < B` | — |
| `same-ba` | 先 B 后 A | 都是 115 | `B < A` | ❌ **翻转** |
| `fix-ab` | 先 A 后 B | A=115, B=114 | `B < A`（114 在前） | ✅ 固定 |
| `fix-ba` | 先 B 后 A | A=115, B=114 | `B < A`（114 在前） | ✅ 不翻转 |

**结论**：同 order 时排列完全由注册顺序决定；order 不同时由 order 值决定（稳定）。修复方向由此确定。

## 7. 建议修复（Suggested Fix）

### 官方侧（根治）：给排序加确定性 tie-breaker

修改 `packages/core/system-prompt/src/index.ts` 的 comparator，让同 order 的 section 由**静态字段**决定先后，而不是运行时注册顺序：

```ts
// 现在（不稳定）：
.sort((a, b) => a.order - b.order)

// 修复（确定性）：
.sort((a, b) => a.order - b.order
  || a.name.length - b.name.length          // 同 order 按名字长度
  || (a.name < b.name ? -1 : a.name > b.name ? 1 : 0))  // 同长度按字典序
```

**好处**：
- 不依赖任何运行时状态（注册顺序、插件加载顺序），纯函数、静态。
- 一处修复，覆盖所有未来可能的同 order 冲突。
- `tool:cordis`（11 字符）恒在 `tool:workflow`（13 字符）前，前缀稳定。

> 注：官方 CONTRIBUTING.md 声明当前**不接受外部 PR**，报告应提交至 GitHub Discussions。

> 社区插件方案（早期分享，供参考）：`dsh-prompt-order-fix`（**npm 包 `@tiyirt/dsh-prompt-order-fix`**）—— 一个 **AI 编写的**插件，继承 `SystemPrompt` 覆写 `assemble()` 为上述确定性 tie-breaker，以 default-export 类 drop-in 替换 `system-prompt` 行即可生效。
>
> ✅ **已实测**：核心功能在真实环境验证过——安装后连续 3 次重启，恢复后第一轮命中率均回到 99.9%+，修复有效。
> ⚠️ **未覆盖**：作为**独立 npm 包的一键安装方式**（`npm install` + `dsh plugin add`）尚未验证；安装前请自行评估，官方修复后即可退役（移除 patch 行即还原官方行为）。

## 8. 参考资料

- 官方排序源码：`packages/core/system-prompt/src/index.ts:504`
- 冲突方 A：`packages/workflow/tool-workflow/src/index.ts:212-214`
- 冲突方 B：`packages/extensions/tool-cordis/src/index.ts:36`
- 官方机制说明：`packages/core/system-prompt/README.md`（KV Cache effect）
- 官方已修：`.agents/notes/implemented/bug-fix/2026-07-21-compaction-summary-prefix-cache-reuse.md`
- 社区相关讨论（公开）：
  - `deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness` discussion #935 —— 工具增删导致命中率 97%→11%（工具区断点，与本文的 system prompt 内部断点不同量级）
  - #963 —— 动态插件注册工具打爆跨会话缓存（工具层断点）
  - #1944 —— compaction 请求 miss 前缀缓存（官方已确认并修复）
  - #2136 —— 重启后缓存 miss（疑似 --port 0 端口 URL 变化，未定论）

---

*整理时间：2026-08 · 证据来源：会话运行日志 + 官方源码静态分析 + 受控运行时实验*

discussions.title: Truncated turn (stopReason "length") desynchronizes pi-ai replay state; session uncontinuable with INVALID_REPLAY_STATE
discussions.body:
## Summary

When a model turn is cut off by the output-token limit *while emitting tool
calls*, the durable `assistant/message` and the adapter-owned pi-ai replay
state record different block lists for that turn. The next request in the
session then fails replay conversion with:

```
invalid pi-ai replay state: block count does not match assistant content
INVALID_REPLAY_STATE
```

The Web UI's own recovery guidance ("The reply was cut off … Send 'continue'
to let the model resume") therefore leads to a terminal turn failure; the
session can never be continued.

## Verified evidence (from a real session's durable event log)

Truncated turn's logged `assistant/message`:

- `source`: `{ kind: "model", provider: "ollama", model: "qwen3.8:27b" }`
- `content` blocks: `[reasoning, text]` — 2 blocks
- `source.replayState`: `{ kind: "pi-ai", version: 1, api: "openai-completions",
  stopReason: "length", blocks: [reasoning, text, tool-call, tool-call] }` — 4 blocks

The stream was truncated by the token limit while two `tool-call` blocks were
in flight. The durable message kept only the completed blocks; the replay
state kept all four. On the next turn, `replayedAssistant()` compares them:

- `packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/replay.ts:164`
  `if (state.blocks.length !== message.content.length) return invalidReplay('block count does not match assistant content')`
- 4 !== 2 → throw. Every subsequent turn in the session fails the same way.

## Root cause (as read from source)

- `packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/src/stream.ts:193` builds the finish chunk's
  `replayState` via `toPiReplayState(event.message)` — pi-ai's final message,
  which includes tool-call blocks that were still in flight when the limit hit.
- The harness's durable message (assembled from chunks) drops those incomplete
  trailing blocks.
- The two block lists are never reconciled, so any `length`-truncated turn
  with in-flight tool calls poisons the session's replay history.

## Minimal reproduction

1. Any OpenAI-compatible route (here: hand-declared local Ollama route) with a
   small `maxTokens` (e.g. 8192) and a reasoning model that thinks long enough
   to hit the cap while emitting tool calls.
2. Observe the Web UI's "Output token limit reached … Send 'continue'" notice.
3. Send "continue" → the turn fails with `INVALID_REPLAY_STATE`.
4. The session is permanently uncontinuable; only a new session works.

Still present in the latest published `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-pi-ai@0.0.1-rc.1`
(same check, same behavior).

## Suggested fix directions

- Build the replay state from the same finalized block list as the durable
  message (truncate `replayState.blocks` to the logged content), or
- Keep incomplete trailing blocks in the durable message so the two stay
  consistent, or
- Treat a block-count mismatch under `stopReason: "length"` as recoverable:
  fall back to `foreignAssistant()` conversion for that message instead of
  throwing.

Happy to provide the raw session event log (JSONL) showing the exact turn.

discussions.title: deepDDW — Memory & Knowledge Base for DeepSeek Harness, reachable from any device on your LAN

1. 🔒 **Local-only → LAN-wide**: deploy once on a server, every device on your network (desktop, laptop, phone, tablet) can use DSH from the browser.

Built on our production-grade **DDW AI HUB** platform — ready for small teams up to ~20 people.

🔗 https://github.com/ccch713/deepddw

MIT licensed. Feedback welcome!

discussions.title: dsh-statecore — auditable project memory: auto-ingest, auto-inject, five native tools, digest on the host model
discussions.body:
**dsh-statecore** gives dsh sessions persistent, *auditable* project memory: every fact carries an evidence id and a version chain, and forgetting is a logged retirement, not a delete. ![StateCore memory demo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yul761/StateCore/main/apps/mcp/demo/statecore-demo.gif) **Repo:** https://github.com/yul761/dsh-statecore (`dsh-plugin` topic) · **npm:** [`dsh-statecore`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-statecore) · **Engine:** [StateCore](https://github.com/yul761/StateCore) ## What it does - **Auto-ingest** — every `user/message` / `assistant/message` flows into per-project memory via `ctx.on('session/event')`. No model cooperation needed; an MCP memory server can only be pull, a native plugin can also push. - **Auto-inject** — an `agent/pre-step` waterfall folds a budgeted memory digest into context each session, mirroring the fold pattern `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-instructions` uses for `AGENTS.md`. In the transcript it shows up as its own `Context injection · dsh-statecore` row next to dsh's first-party injectors. - **Five native tools** — `remember` / `recall` / `facts` / `why` / `forget` registered through `dsh-tools` with honest JSON `output.schema`, so Code Mode can `await tools.why({factId})` and get a structured evidence chain. Registration is an effect; dispose unregisters cleanly (HMR-safe, tested). - **Digest on the host's own model** — consolidation runs through `ctx.llm`. Whatever model you already pointed dsh at drives memory distillation; there is no second API key to configure. - **Cross-tool shared store** — the same `~/.statecore` store is served to any MCP client by [`statecore-mcp`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/statecore-mcp). In my live test, a fact remembered inside a dsh web session was immediately visible from Claude Code's `facts` tool, because both resolve the same project scope. ## Install ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add -w dsh-statecore dsh --profile web ``` The package declares `"dsh": { "bundle": { "patch": "./statecore.cordis.yml" } }`, so profile bundle reconciliation wires it up automatically — no manual `--patch` after install. Verified live against `dsh@0.1.0-rc.6` (web app, DeepSeek-V4-Flash): plugin row in `--dump-config`, both consumers active, all five tools callable by the model, and a second session receiving the first session's facts by injection alone. ## Two small rc.6 findings from real installs (feedback) 1. `dsh plugin --profile

add ` needs `-w` today: profiles ship a `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, and pnpm refuses to add to a workspace root without it. Either passing `-w` internally or documenting it would smooth the first-plugin experience. 2. pnpm inside a profile skips dependencies' `postinstall` (build-script approval), which bites any plugin whose deps generate code at install time (Prisma here). A note in the plugin-install docs — or surfacing `pnpm approve-builds` in the CLI output — would help plugin authors. Both are documented with workarounds in the plugin README. Happy to file issues for either if useful. I tried to build this the way dsh's own AGENTS.md asks its packages to be built — real-composition tests over actual `dsh-tools`/`dsh-session`/`dsh-agent` registries rather than mocks, HMR/disposal coverage, config with no hardcoded tunables, misconfig failing loud — because the harness's conventions are genuinely good and the best way to showcase a plugin system is to follow them. Feedback very welcome.

discussions.title: dsh-memory-kit — 给 DSH 装上持久记忆和学习循环（v0.1.0）
discussions.body:
# dsh-memory-kit — 给 DSH 装上持久记忆和学习循环

[GitHub 仓库](https://github.com/mrliu7219-cell/dsh-memory-kit) · MIT · v0.1.0

## 解决什么问题

DSH 每个会话结束后记忆归零。这个插件让它**越用越聪明**：会话开始自动注入记忆索引，踩过的坑沉淀进踩坑库，找旧知识双通道检索。

## 核心功能

- **记忆注入**：SessionStart 自动注入 `MEMORY.md` 索引（memdir 式，≤200 行），细节笔记按需读取
- **踩坑库**：`traps.md` 四段式记录（现象/根因/防错/状态）+ **三档状态**（🆕新鲜 → ✅已验证 → ⬆️已升级常驻规则），同类坑犯 2 次才升级 AGENTS.md，防规则膨胀
- **双通道检索**：关键词（rg 全文，19ms）+ 语义搜索（本地 bge-small-zh embedding，118ms，可完全不用）
- **优雅降级**：核心功能零依赖；语义搜索缺 LM Studio 时给引导不报错

## 安装

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <你的profile> add dsh-memory-kit
dsh-memory-kit setup
```

## 设计理念

- **文件是真相**：记忆全是 Markdown，可读可改可备份，向量索引只是可重建的辅助层
- **本地优先**：embedding 走本地 LM Studio，数据不上云
- **防投毒**：notes 只存事实不存指令，读到指令口气一律当数据

## 缘起

这套机制最初是为我自己的 DSH 工作流搭建的（一天内踩坑库沉淀了 10 条教训），验证有效后产品化成插件。对比其他记忆方案（Basic Memory/deep-memory/Mem0）的差异见 [README](https://github.com/mrliu7219-cell/dsh-memory-kit#与其他记忆方案的差异)。

欢迎试用反馈，尤其是 hook 集成和 setup 流程的体验问题。

discussions.title: [Feature] Structured remediation metadata for FS_NOT_OBSERVED / FS_STALE_VERSION so tool UIs can surface recoverable-action feedback
discussions.body:
## 摘要 Summary

`dsh-fs-observation-policy` rejects edits without a prior read via `FS_NOT_OBSERVED` / `FS_STALE_VERSION`, and `dsh-tool-fs` already appends a text remedy ("— read the file, then retry"). That covers *what the model should do*, but the recovery instruction is still embedded in the message text only. Tool UIs and frontends cannot tell a "recoverable guard failure" from a real error, so the user experience is a red Error box with no actionable affordance.

## 提议 Proposal

One or any combination of:

1. **Structured remediation metadata**: add a `remediation` field to `FsError` (or export a public `code → remedy` map from `dsh-tool-fs`), instead of / in addition to message string concatenation. Consumers then route on the field, not by parsing text.
2. **`recoverable: true` marker on tool results**: allow UIs to render a friendly, actionable notice (e.g. "file changed on disk — re-reading it") instead of a plain error, without losing the error code for retry/permission layers.
3. **(Optional) automatic re-read**: on `FS_NOT_OBSERVED` / `FS_STALE_VERSION`, the tool layer could transparently perform one re-read + retry, preserving the existing CAS semantics, rather than forcing the model through an extra read+retry round.

## 动机 Motivation

Observed in practice: editing a file twice in one session triggers `FS_NOT_OBSERVED` on the second edit (the first edit invalidated the observed version). The remedy text works for the model but is invisible to UI layers; a structured, machine-readable marker would let tool UIs surface "recoverable — auto re-read" feedback and keep the error-code routing intact.

## 期望行为 Expected behavior

- Error codes and their routing semantics stay unchanged.
- The remedy becomes machine-readable metadata on the error / tool result.
- UIs can distinguish recoverable guard failures from unrecoverable errors.

## 环境 Environment

- dsh: 0.1.0-rc.6
- Packages involved: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs-observation-policy`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs`

discussions.title: dsh-acp-demo agents crash with InvariantError: "subagent/end" dispatched without a scope carrier (multi-instance @deepseek-ai/dsh-scope under global npm)
discussions.body:
**Symptom:** launching a `dsh-acp-demo` agent and using the subagent or workflow tools kills the whole process: Paseo reports `ACP agent exited unexpectedly (1)` with `InvariantError: invariant violated by "@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope": "subagent/end" is a scope-filtered event but was dispatched without a scope carrier`.

**Root cause (confirmed by inspection of the stack + install layout):**

1. `@deepseek-ai/dsh-scope` keeps its carrier registry in a module-local `WeakMap`. A global `npm i -g` of `dsh-acp-demo` + its peers (npm 11 peer auto-install) created **~24 real nested copies of `dsh-scope@0.1.0-rc.6`** (one under each consumer, no top-level copy). The invariant plugin validates carriers using the copy it was loaded from, while `dsh-subagent` builds carriers with `scopeTarget` from a different copy — so `isScopeCarrier()` is false for every `subagent/end` dispatch, parented or not.
2. Separately, parentless runs (e.g. subagent runs started by the workflow worker thread) dispatch with no carrier at all, which would violate the invariant even with a single instance.

**Local workaround (verified end-to-end with Paseo 0.4.0):** unify `dsh-scope` to one top-level instance and remove the nested copies (plus a top-level `@deepseek-ai/cordis` symlink to the runtime's nested copy so `Context` identity matches), and make the lifecycle emitter fall back to a carrier for parentless runs.

**Suggested upstream fixes (any of):** publish so the peer/dependency layout hoists instead of nesting real copies (or dedupe in the loader), make the invariant accept carriers from sibling module instances, and always dispatch `subagent/end` with a carrier even when the run has no parent.

discussions.title: DSH | dsh-compact-activity | 折叠冗长的思考和工具调用过程, 显示实时摘要和状态
discussions.body: 项目地址:https://github.com/wallpap/dsh-compact-activity 让 DeepSeek Harness 的思考与工具调用更紧凑、更容易浏览。 插件会把一段连续的模型工作过程收进一个 Codex 风格的单行折叠项。默认保持收起， 需要查看细节时再展开；模型最终输出始终正常显示。 > 进行中... 2 段思考 · 3 次工具调用 Code · 正在读取项目文件... > 已完成 2 段思考 · 3 次工具调用 为什么使用它 - 减少滚动距离：连续的思考和工具调用合并为一个总过程列表。 - 不改变官方内容：展开后仍使用 DSH 官方 Think、Code 和工具组件。 - 保留正文边界：下一条模型 output 不会被折叠进过程列表。 - 实时显示状态：执行期间显示 进行中...、计数和最后一项活动摘要。 - 完成后保持简洁：完成时只显示 已完成 和计数，不再显示过期摘要。 - 单条消息不受影响：只有一条思考或工具调用时，继续使用 DSH 官方行为。 插件只调整 Web 界面的展示方式，不修改模型上下文、会话日志或工具执行。 ## 使用方式 插件没有设置页面，安装并重启 DSH Web 或 Desktop 后自动生效： | 场景 | 显示行为 | | --- | --- | | 多条连续过程消息 | 合并为一个默认收起的总折叠项 | | 正在思考 | 显示 `进行中...`、计数和 `正在思考` | | 正在调用工具 | 显示最后一个官方工具的类型和摘要 | | 工作完成 | 显示 `已完成` 和计数，不显示摘要 | | 展开总过程 | 显示原版 Think 和工具组件，保留官方交互 | | 单条过程消息 | 不分组，保持 DSH 官方显示 | | 思考后紧接模型正文 | 只折叠 Think，正文继续显示 | 过长的实时摘要会自动截断，不会挤压页面布局。 效果: ------- -------

discussions.title: dsh-memoria — native long-term memory for DeepSeek Harness
discussions.body:
Hey all 👋 I built a native memory plugin for DSH and wanted to share it.

dsh-memoria gives your agent persistent, cross-session long-term memory, backed by the Memoria
(https://github.com/fleg45/memoria-framework) framework (a Python memory engine with 5 layers and 8 memory types).

Install

pip install memoria-framework          # the Python memory engine
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-memoria

What you get

- 4 tools — memoria_store, memoria_recall, memoria_forget, memoria_status
- Auto-recall injection — context is recalled and injected at the start of every turn, so the agent stays grounded in what it
already remembers without an explicit recall prompt
- 5-pipeline contextual recall — reference / profile / skills / emotion / constraints returned together as structured context
- Zero-cost start — works out of the box with an in-memory store; optional MySQL / Redis / Postgres / Qdrant backends when you
need persistence or vector search

How it works

The plugin owns one long-lived Python subprocess (python -m memoria.plugin_server) so store and recall share a single in-memory
Memoria instance. A prepend listener on agent/pre-step recalls the turn's context and injects it as a user message tagged
source.form = "recall".

Config (optional)

- id: memoria
  config:
    python: /path/to/python       # interpreter with memoria installed
    autoInject: true
     recallLimit: 10

Links

- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-memoria
- PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/memoria-framework/
- Source: https://github.com/fleg45/memoria-framework

Happy to take feedback or answer questions 🙏

discussions.title: macOS launchd (LaunchAgent): add PATH + ThrottleInterval to avoid env: node crash loop (Homebrew)
discussions.body:
**Problem**

Running `dsh` as a macOS LaunchAgent fails out-of-the-box for Homebrew users. launchd gives the job a minimal `PATH` (`/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`) that does **not** include `/opt/homebrew/bin`, but the `dsh` entrypoint is `#!/usr/bin/env node`. The job therefore exits immediately with:

```
env: node: No such file or directory
```

`launchctl list` reports exit code `127`. Combined with `KeepAlive=true` and no `ThrottleInterval`, launchd retries instantly in a tight loop, spamming logs and burning CPU until someone notices.

**Environment**

- macOS 26.5.2 (Apple Silicon, Homebrew at `/opt/homebrew`)
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh` 0.1.0-rc.6

**Suggested fix**

If the docs or samples include a macOS LaunchAgent template, please make it:

1. Set `PATH` in `EnvironmentVariables` (or invoke the entrypoint with an absolute Node path):

```xml
<key>EnvironmentVariables</key>
<dict>
    <key>PATH</key>
    <string>/opt/homebrew/bin:/opt/homebrew/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin</string>
</dict>
```

2. Add a `ThrottleInterval` so a misconfigured job can't retry-loop:

```xml
<key>ThrottleInterval</key>
<integer>5</integer>
```

**Workaround**

Add the `PATH` block above to the LaunchAgent plist, then reload it in place (avoid `bootout`, which can race):

```bash
launchctl kickstart -k gui/$(id -u)/com.tao.dsh
```

Thanks!

discussions.title: resolveDshHome doesn't trim $DSH_HOME — a trailing space silently creates a fresh empty data root (UI appears factory-reset)
discussions.body:
## Summary

If `DSH_HOME` contains leading/trailing whitespace (easy to get on Windows), dsh treats it as a *different* home and initializes a brand-new empty data directory there. All existing sessions / settings / API keys appear "lost": the web UI boots as factory defaults, while the real data is still safe under `~/.dsh`.

## Repro (cmd.exe / .bat)

```bat
set DSH_HOME=C:\Users\me\.dsh && npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web
```

Result: dsh reads home `C:\Users\me\.dsh ` (with a trailing space) and creates an empty `C:\Users\me\.dsh ` folder; the UI shows no sessions / default settings.

## Root cause

`@deepseek-ai/dsh-home-paths` → `lib/index.js` (`resolveDshHome`):

```js
function resolveDshHome(configured, env = process.env) {
	const fromEnv = env[DSH_HOME_ENV];
	return resolve(expandHomePath(configured ?? (fromEnv !== void 0 && fromEnv.trim().length > 0 ? fromEnv : defaultDshHome())));
}
```

The `.trim().length > 0` guard deliberately treats a whitespace-only value as unset — but the value actually returned is the **untrimmed** `fromEnv`. The doc comment above the function even says a blank override is handled ("An empty or whitespace-only \$DSH_HOME is treated as unset"), yet `DSH_HOME="C:\Users\me\.dsh "` passes the guard and is used verbatim, resolving the home to a distinct directory that does not contain the existing data. No warning is logged.

This trigger is common on Windows: `cmd.exe`'s unquoted `set VAR=value && ...` captures the space before `&&` into the value:

```
cmd /v:on /c "set X=C:\foo\.dsh && echo [!X!]"
-> [C:\foo\.dsh ]
```

So any launcher `.bat` doing `set DSH_HOME=... && ...` silently injects a trailing space; the quoted `set "VAR=value"` form avoids it, but it is an easy mistake.

## Suggested fix

Return the trimmed value in `resolveDshHome`:

```js
return resolve(expandHomePath(configured ?? (fromEnv !== void 0 && fromEnv.trim().length > 0 ? fromEnv.trim() : defaultDshHome())));
```

Optionally also log a warning when the resolved home differs from `defaultDshHome()`, so a stray whitespace never masquerades as a silent factory reset.

discussions.title: npm dist-tag `latest` is stuck on each package's first publish across the whole @deepseek-ai/dsh-* scope
discussions.body:
Reported downstream at dsh-market/dsh-market#64 by @ZeroOrigin64, who traced it to the registry. Issues are disabled here, so posting it as a discussion.

## Summary

Every `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` package I sampled has its `latest` dist-tag pinned to its **first published version**, while real releases have moved on to `0.1.0-rc.6` under `next`. Anything that resolves `latest` — `npm install <pkg>`, `pnpm add <pkg>`, tooling that treats `dist-tags.latest` as "newest" — gets a months-old build.

## Evidence

15/15 sampled packages, checked against the live registry:

| package | `latest` | `next` | highest published |
|---|---|---|---|
| dsh-base | 0.0.1-rc.1 | 0.1.0-rc.6 | 0.1.0-rc.6 |
| dsh-web-app | 0.0.1-rc.1 | 0.1.0-rc.6 | 0.1.0-rc.6 |
| dsh-headless | 0.0.1-rc.1 | 0.1.0-rc.6 | 0.1.0-rc.6 |
| dsh-web | 0.0.1-rc.1 | 0.1.0-rc.6 | 0.1.0-rc.6 |
| dsh-web-fetch-http | **0.0.1-rc.5** | 0.1.0-rc.6 | 0.1.0-rc.6 |
| dsh-web-search-exa | 0.0.1-rc.1 | 0.1.0-rc.6 | 0.1.0-rc.6 |
| dsh-web-search-perplexity | 0.0.1-rc.1 | 0.1.0-rc.6 | 0.1.0-rc.6 |
| dsh-client-connection / -runtime / -locale | 0.0.1-rc.1 | 0.1.0-rc.6 | 0.1.0-rc.6 |
| dsh-client-ui-settings / -theme / -primitives | 0.0.1-rc.1 | 0.1.0-rc.6 | 0.1.0-rc.6 |
| dsh-timeout / dsh-invariants | 0.0.1-rc.1 | 0.1.0-rc.6 | 0.1.0-rc.6 |

The tell is in the one row that differs. `dsh-web-fetch-http` was published later than the others and its first version was `0.0.1-rc.5` — and its `latest` is `0.0.1-rc.5`, not `0.0.1-rc.1`. **For every package, `latest` equals that package's own first publish.**

## Root cause

`scripts/release/publish.ts:98`:

```ts
// A prerelease version never takes the latest dist-tag.
const tagArgs = version.includes('-') ? ['--tag', 'next'] : []
```

The policy is right. The blind spot is npm's first-publish behavior: a package must always have a `latest`, so on the **very first** publish npm assigns `latest` to that version *regardless of `--tag`*. Every one of these packages debuted as a prerelease, so `latest` landed on the debut version — and since every subsequent publish has also been a prerelease, nothing has moved it since.

So this isn't a one-off slip; it's structural, and it will silently repeat for every new package the pipeline introduces during a prerelease phase.

## Suggested fix

Retag the current set:

```bash
npm dist-tag add @deepseek-ai/dsh-web-fetch-http@0.1.0-rc.6 latest
# ...and the same for each package above
```

Whether you want `latest` on a prerelease at all is your call — the alternative is to leave `latest` on the debut version deliberately and document that consumers must use `next` until GA. Either is defensible, but the current state is neither: `latest` points at a build whose peer deps (`^0.0.1-rc.5`) no longer match the shipping framework, so a fresh `npm install` produces a profile that does not boot.

To stop it recurring, `publish.ts` could detect the first publish and correct the tag afterwards — e.g. when the package had no prior versions and the published version is a prerelease, follow up with `npm dist-tag add <pkg>@<version> next` and explicitly move or remove `latest` according to whichever policy you pick.

Happy to open a PR against `publish.ts` if that's useful — just say which policy you want.

## Downstream note

This surfaced because clicking "update" in the plugin market **downgraded** pinned installs (`0.1.0-rc.6` → `0.0.1-rc.5`) and broke profile startup. That part was ours: our update check compared versions with `!=` instead of comparing direction, so a lower `latest` read as "newer". Fixed in dsh-market/dsh-market#74 — the market now refuses to move a profile backwards regardless of what any registry tag says. Filing this because the tags still send fresh installs to the old build, which no downstream fix can address.

---

**中文摘要**:抽查的 15 个 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` 包,`latest` 标签全部停在**各自的首个发布版本**,而实际版本已到 `0.1.0-rc.6`(在 `next` 上)。根因是 `scripts/release/publish.ts:98` 只给预发布版打 `next`,但 npm 在**包的首次发布**时会无视 `--tag` 强制设置 `latest`——这些包首发恰好都是预发布版,`latest` 就此钉死。建议先补 `npm dist-tag add ...@0.1.0-rc.6 latest`,并在 `publish.ts` 里处理首次发布这个特例。需要的话我可以直接提 PR。

discussions.title: 推一个 DSH GitHub workflow Skill Pack：基于 Codex GitHub plugin 改造
discussions.body:
最近在用 DSH 做 GitHub 相关工作时，感觉缺一套比较完整的 GitHub workflow，于是参考 OpenAI Codex 官方的 GitHub plugin 做了一个 DSH 版本：

**dsh-github-skills**

GitHub：
https://github.com/Starfie1d1272/dsh-github-skills

npm：
https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-github-skills

目前包含 4 个 Skill：

- `github`：仓库 / Issue / PR 的通用查看和路由
- `gh-address-comments`：处理 PR review comments
- `gh-fix-ci`：排查和修复 GitHub Actions CI
- `gh-publish`：branch / commit / push / PR 发布流程，也支持 fork 外部仓库贡献

整体设计是参考 Codex 官方 GitHub plugin 的 `github` / `gh-address-comments` / `gh-fix-ci` / `yeet` 这套分工，但没有直接照搬。

主要针对 DSH 做了几处改造：

- **Skill-first**：Skill 负责 workflow policy，不自己再造一套 GitHub API client。
- **能力无关**：优先使用当前 session 里实际可见、语义合适的 GitHub capability；也可以接 GitHub MCP，缺能力时再 fallback 到 `gh` / `git`。
- **按需加载**：DSH 首次只看到 Skill 的 `name + description`，完整 workflow 调用后再加载，所以 v0.2.0 专门重新整理了 routing，并尽量压缩常驻和 Skill prompt。
- **支持组合 workflow**：比如“修完 review 再 push”会组合 `gh-address-comments + gh-publish`，而不是让 publish workflow 把 review 处理吞掉。
- **补了 fork / cross-repo 场景**：外部贡献会先保证 checkout 属于目标仓库 lineage，再走正常 publish 流程。
- **比较严格的 evidence / write boundary**：review thread、CI logs、remote write 都尽量避免在证据或用户意图不足时自行推断。

另外在适配过程中也顺手补了一些 upstream workflow/helper 里比较容易踩的边界，例如 fork PR 的 review thread repository、分页、cross-repo CI context、external CI 判定、mixed worktree、凭据输出脱敏等。

现在是 **v0.2.0**，已经通过 Node 22/24 CI、真实 DSH rc.6 disposable-profile install smoke，并通过 npm Trusted Publishing 发布。

安装：

```bash
dsh plugin add dsh-github-skills
````

我现在自己主要是拿它处理：

* 看 PR / Issue
* 修 review comments
* 查 GitHub Actions
* 改完代码直接 push / 开 PR
* fork 别人的仓库做贡献

如果大家也有比较重的 GitHub workflow，可以帮忙实际跑跑。

我目前最想收集的是两类反馈：

1. **Skill routing 有没有误判**，比如本来应该进 `gh-publish` 却进了通用 `github`；
2. **现有 DSH GitHub 插件 / MCP 的兼容情况**，有没有某些 capability 明明已经提供了，但 Skill 没有正确利用。

如果有真实 session 里比较奇怪的行为，直接贴任务和执行过程就行，我再针对实际案例调整。

discussions.title: deepseek-v4-pro emits Anthropic-style `<invoke>` tool-call text into content, not normalized to tool_calls — leaks to the user
discussions.body:
## Summary

When the agent runs on the `deepseek-official` route with a reasoning model (`deepseek-v4-pro`, thinking enabled), the model sometimes expresses a tool call as **plain text in the message content** using Anthropic Claude's tool-use syntax, instead of the native `tool_calls` field:

```xml
<invoke name="mcp__stock__wait"><parameter name="seconds">5</parameter></invoke>
```

`dsh-agent-loop` only dispatches native `tool_calls` blocks (see `executeToolCalls`), and nothing in the loop / tool-presentation / LLM adapter strips or normalizes this text, so it ends up **visible to the user as raw markup** in the assistant's reply.

## Environment

- `dsh` 0.1.0-rc.6 (all `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` packages at 0.1.0-rc.6)
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-deepseek` — provider route `deepseek-official`
- Model: `deepseek-v4-pro` (reasoning; `thinking` default `enabled`)
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` — tools exposed as `mcp__<serverName>__<rawName>`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Boot `dsh` with `dsh-llm-deepseek` (deepseek-official, deepseek-v4-pro, thinking enabled) and one or more MCP clients.
2. Run a task that requires several sequential tool calls.
3. Trigger a case where a tool call fails or times out (e.g. an MCP tool exceeding the 60s `toolCallTimeoutMs`), then ask the agent to retry/continue.

Observed: the model falls back to emitting the retry tool call as literal `<invoke>…</invoke>` text in its content, which is rendered to the user verbatim.

## Expected vs actual

- **Expected:** either (a) normalize the `<invoke>` text into `tool_calls` and execute it, or (b) strip it from the user-facing output so it never leaks.
- **Actual:** the raw `<invoke name="mcp__stock__wait">…</invoke>` block appears in the assistant reply, and the tool is not executed.

## Root cause (from reading the source)

- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-loop` dispatches only native `tool_calls` blocks (`executeToolCalls` in `lib/index.js`); there is no text-level tool-call parser.
- A grep across `dsh-agent-loop`, `dsh-agent-tool-presentation`, `dsh-llm` and `dsh-llm-deepseek` finds **no** handling of the string `<invoke`.
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` confirms the model-facing name `mcp__<serverName>__<rawName>` (`publicToolName`), which is exactly what appears inside `name="…"`.

So this is a gap: reasoning-model text-form tool calls (Claude-style `<invoke>`) are neither normalized nor sanitized by the harness.

## Context / prior art

This is a known behavior of DeepSeek reasoning models — under ReAct-style prompting they can emit Anthropic tool-use syntax in text. In our own in-house ReAct loop we already handle it by stripping `<invoke>…</invoke>` in a post-processing stage, which is why we recognized it. It would be great if the harness handled this natively.

## Suggestion

Either:
1. Add a text tool-call normalizer in `dsh-agent-loop` that parses `<invoke name="…">…</invoke>` (and `<tool_calls>`/function-call variants) into `tool_calls` blocks before dispatch; or
2. At minimum, strip these blocks from any content surfaced to the user, so internal tool syntax never leaks.

Happy to provide logs or a minimal repro repo if a template exists.

discussions.title: DSH | vision-read | Route image reading to a dedicated vision model (e.g. Kimi K3) so text-only agents can see images
discussions.body: > **_> Unofficial project, independently developed and maintained by community members._** **Project URL:** https://github.com/Mappedinfo/dsh-tool-vision-read **Introduction:** `vision_read` is a lightweight DeepSeek Harness plugin that lets a **text-only agent** (a model whose route does not declare `image` input) read images through a **dedicated vision model route** — no third-party CLI, no manual delegation. The harness's built-in `read_image` returns the image itself as a content block, which only a vision-capable calling route can carry; on a text-only route it refuses. This plugin registers a sibling tool that routes the reading to a configured vision provider/model and returns the description as text in one call. It is the same idea as routing different roles to different models (e.g. oh-my-pi's `modelRoles`), applied to one narrow capability: image description. **How it integrates with DSH:** - Registers a model-facing tool through the standard `ctx.tools.register(defineTool(...))` extension point — no changes to `agent-loop` or the existing `read_image` tool. - `direct` mode (default): reads the file via `ctx.fs`, commits it through the durable attachment service (`attachments.saveImage`), and makes one `ctx.llm.stream` call to the configured vision route with a text+image user message. One round trip, no agent-loop overhead. - `subagent` mode (optional): starts an in-process subagent pinned to the vision route via `agentOptions` (`ctx.subagents.start`), so the child can iterate (zoom, OCR, follow-ups). - The tool resolves the vision route's model info before reading and fails with guidance when the route does not declare `image` input (pi-ai routes: `defaultInput: [text, image]`). - Verified end-to-end: a `deepseek-v4-flash` (text-only) agent calling `vision_read` on a JPEG received an accurate description from **Kimi K3-256K** (Kimi Coding API). ```yaml # $DSH_HOME/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml - insert: - id: tool-vision-read name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-vision-read' config: provider: kimi-coding model: k3-256k ``` **Demo transcript (real run):** ```text user: 请调用 vision_read 工具读取图片 /Users/shiqi/Downloads/微信图片_2026-08-13_172033_970.jpg agent (deepseek-v4-flash, text-only): vision_read(file_path=..., focus=undefined) → "这是一张俯视视角的现代校园/混合功能街区建筑总平面渲染图,画面中央有大片绿地公园 与放射状步道,左侧是较密集的居住/办公组团和带红色跑道的体育场,右侧分布着带庭院 与环形景观的校园建筑群,左上角一条深蓝色河流/运河蜿蜒而过……" ``` **Screenshots:** *The full session flow: user message → `vision_read` tool call card (with file path) → model reasoning → the description returned by the vision route.* **Links:** - Repository: https://github.com/Mappedinfo/dsh-tool-vision-read - Discussion: this post --- ## 中文摘要 `vision_read` 是一个轻量级 DeepSeek Harness 插件:当主模型是纯文本模型(路由未声明 `image` 输入)时,它把图片读取自动路由到配置好的视觉模型(实测 Kimi K3-256K),以文字描述返回——不再需要 modlens 之类的第三方 CLI(modlens也确实好用),也不需要手工编排子代理。默认 `direct` 模式一次 `llm.stream` 调用即完成;可选 `subagent` 模式支持多轮交互。插件通过标准工具扩展点注册,不改动 `agent-loop` 与既有 `read_image` 工具。

discussions.title: 通过局域网 IP(HTTP)访问 Web UI 时页面空白:crypto.randomUUID 需要 Secure Context(附修复分支)
discussions.body:
## 现象

`dsh web` 配合 `--trusted-host <局域网IP>` + 反向代理部署后,用另一台设备打开 `http://<局域网IP>/`:页面壳正常渲染,但会话列表、工作区、模型配置全部为空("暂无会话"),控制台反复输出 `[web-runtime] connection lost, retry #N`。同一服务用 `http://127.0.0.1:3080/` 或 `http://localhost/` 访问则一切正常。

## 根因

`packages/host/apiproxy/src/fetch/client.ts` 的 `AbstractApiClient.mintRpcId()` 直接调用了 `crypto.randomUUID()`。该 Web API **仅在 Secure Context 中存在**(HTTPS 或 localhost);`http://<局域网IP>` 属于非安全上下文,此属性为 `undefined`,导致所有一元 RPC(`host.describe`、`session.list` 等)在发出网络请求**之前**就抛出 `TypeError`,连接循环不断重建。

有两个细节说明这应该是疏漏而非设计:

1. `packages/client/connection/src/client/random-uuid.ts` 已有专门为此写的注释:"*Generate an RFC 4122 version 4 UUID without requiring a secure context*",且 cordis web RPC 通道用的正是它 —— 所以经该通道的 `dynamicCordisRunner/inventory` 在局域网下仍能工作,唯独 `AbstractApiClient` 全军覆没;
2. 服务端为局域网服务做了完整支持(`--trusted-host`、`/api` 浏览器信任围栏、`0.0.0.0` 绑定时的 LAN 地址自动信任),只有客户端 ID 生成这一步断了。

## 修复

在 3 个浏览器可达的调用点加了 `getRandomValues` 兜底(该 API 在非安全 origin 也可用):

| 位置 | 受影响功能 |
|---|---|
| `host/apiproxy/src/fetch/client.ts` — `mintRpcId` | 所有一元 RPC |
| `llm/llm/src/message.ts` — `createMessage` | 发送消息 |
| `client/ui-conversation/src/client/service.ts` — `browserDraftAttachment` | 输入框附带图片 |

实测:打补丁前局域网页面空白;打补丁后(同一代理、同一服务端)会话/工作区/模型/实时流/双端输入全部正常,loopback 行为不变。

修复分支(基于当前 master):https://github.com/zicowarn/deepseek-harness/tree/fix/secure-context-random-uuid

本仓库 PR 入口已关闭无法提交,如需要我可以按维护者偏好的形式(如抽取共享 helper)重新组织提交。

discussions.title: DSH｜dsh-task-control｜在对话中暂停/恢复/取消正在运行的任务，从暂停点无缝继续
discussions.body:
# DSH｜dsh-task-control｜在对话中暂停/恢复/取消正在运行的任务，从暂停点无缝继续

> **非官方项目**，由社区成员独立开发和维护。

**项目地址：**
https://github.com/p2coder/dsh-task-control

**项目介绍：**

dsh-task-control 给 DeepSeek Harness 的对话任务补上了缺失的「暂停 / 恢复」控制。任务跑着跑着发现方向不对、想停下来想想，或者临时有事要离开——点一下暂停即可，回来点恢复就能从暂停点继续，不用重发提示词、不会重跑已完成的工作。

核心特性：

- **两种暂停模式**：`force`（立即中断，记住被中断的工具，恢复时可选重跑/跳过）和 `safe`（等当前工具/推理跑完再停，绝不打断工作）；
- **默认粒度可配置**：在 设置 →「任务控制」里选默认是 force 还是 safe（safe 下可选 wait/stop 推理粒度），出厂默认 `safe wait`；裸 `/pause` 和按钮都跟随设置，显式 `/pause force` 等始终覆盖；
- **从暂停点继续**：恢复即从暂停处接着执行，已完成的工具自动跳过、绝不重复执行；
- **热插拔支持**：路由通过 `ctx.effect` 挂载，配合 plugin-toggle 可随时启停，无需重启 dsh web。


**与 DSH 的集成方式：**

- 浏览器端注册在 composer 工具行（发送按钮左侧的 ⏸ 暂停 / ▶ 恢复 / ⏹ 取消 按钮组），状态来自宿主路由 `/task-control/state`；
- 宿主端注册 `/pause`、`/resume`、`/cancel` 三个斜杠命令，并发布 `taskControl` 服务（按 sessionId 调用，供 dsh-task-batch 等其他插件复用）；
- 设置页「任务控制」通过 `/task-control/settings` 路由持久化默认暂停粒度（`~/.dsh/task-control/settings.json`）；
- 暂停状态存于插件自有 store（Route A，不写会话日志，重启不丢）。

**安装：**

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:p2coder/dsh-task-control
```

> 插件列表排序完全依据社区 Upvote。Upvote 不代表 DeepSeek 官方审核或推荐，使用第三方项目前请自行甄别。

discussions.title: Bug: dsh web freezes (whole-process deadlock) when loading large session.jsonl.zstd files on Windows
discussions.body:
# Bug: dsh web freezes (whole-process deadlock) when loading large session.jsonl.zstd files on Windows

## Environment

- **dsh version**: `0.1.0-rc.6` (installed globally via `npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh`)
- **OS**: Windows 10 (build 10.0.26200)
- **Node.js**: v22.22.2
- **Launch command**: `dsh web` (<http://127.0.0.1:3080/>)

## Summary

`dsh web` starts normally (port 3080 listening, HTTP 200), but shortly after — while loading the session list — the **entire process deadlocks**. The port stays LISTENING but every HTTP request times out with 0 bytes returned. The process never recovers and must be killed and restarted.

## Symptoms / Diagnostic evidence

1. Port 3080 remains LISTENING, but `curl http://127.0.0.1:3080` returns `000` (TCP connects, then 0 bytes, timeout).
2. Process stays alive (13 threads, ~130 MB RSS) but **CPU time stops growing entirely** (measured over 60 s: UserModeTime + KernelModeTime unchanged) — so it is a *deadlock*, not a busy loop.
3. **Critically, even the Node.js inspector stops responding.** We launched with `NODE_OPTIONS="--inspect=127.0.0.1:9229"`; while healthy, `curl :9229/json` works and `Debugger.pause` captures a normal `processTimers` stack. Once deadlocked, `curl :9229/json` also times out with 0 bytes — proving this is a **process-level native deadlock**, not a JavaScript event-loop block (a JS block would leave the inspector thread responsive).
4. No child processes (bash/pwsh/conhost) are present at deadlock time, so it is not stuck waiting on a child.

## Root cause trace

- The deadlock is triggered by **large session files**. We have 122 sessions under `~/.dsh/sessions/`, 6 of which exceed 1 MB (largest 9.5 MB, ~9,539,628 bytes).
- **Control experiment (reproducible)**:
  - With all 122 sessions present → startup deadlocks within 1–2 minutes.
  - With the 6 large (>1 MB) sessions removed → startup is stable (HTTP 200 at 35 s and 75 s).
- The large `.zstd` files are **not corrupt** — `zstdDecompressSync` decodes them without error.
- Reading `dsh-session-persistence-jsonl/lib/index.js`, session logs are a multi-frame concatenated zstd container, and the code has a **synchronous** fallback path (`PublicZstdFrameDecoder.decode` calls `zstdDecompressSync` per frame) plus `ZLibDecoder.decodeFrame` using `handle.writeSync(...)` in a tight loop. We believe decoding many/large frames through these synchronous native calls is what deadlocks the process (native-level lock, since even the inspector thread freezes).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.0-rc.6` on Windows.
2. Create several large sessions so that some `session.jsonl.zstd` files are >1 MB (or copy in large multi-frame zstd session logs).
3. Run `dsh web`.
4. Wait 1–2 minutes (or trigger session-list loading in the UI).
5. Observe the port stops responding and the process hangs permanently.

## Expected behavior

Loading a session list (including large sessions) should never block the event loop or deadlock the process. Large session decoding should be fully async/streamed, or large frames should be decoded off the main thread.

## Additional note

A related symptom appears when the agent runs tasks: an "internal signal timeout" occurs, which we suspect is the same underlying native deadlock surfacing during command execution (node-pty/ConPTY may be a second independent trigger). We have not fully isolated that second path.

---

*Submitted by a us*

discussions.title: Bug: session log corrupted on resume - last 4 committed events re-appended with fresh timestamps (seq gap in committed region)
discussions.body:
## Summary

Resuming a persisted session can append a **stale 4-event prefix** to its JSONL session log: the last four committed events are re-appended verbatim (same `seq`, same payload, **fresh `time`**), producing a seq gap in the committed region. The reader then hard-fails with `corrupt session log: seq gap in committed region`, the session history becomes permanently unloadable in the Web GUI, and the log requires manual surgery to repair.

Affected on 2026-08-15, dsh `0.1.0-rc.5`, Windows, JSONL+zstd persistence backend (`session.jsonl.zstd`), 4 sessions with an identical signature.

## Environment

- dsh version: `0.1.0-rc.5` (running profile packages and checkout HEAD `47f9438` all `0.1.0-rc.5`)
- OS: Windows
- Persistence: `session-persistence-jsonl` with zstd compression (`session.jsonl.zstd`)
- Frontend: Web GUI (history load reports the error)

## Symptom

Opening the session in the Web GUI:

```
history unavailable for session "session-9173e707-2020-4fba-96cd-55f056b74a9f": Error:
corrupt session log: seq gap in committed region at line 4988 (expected 93137, got 93133)(internal)
```

## Evidence (4 real logs, all same signature)

| session id | cwd | gap line | expected | got | re-appended (duplicated) seqs | duplicate event types |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `session-9173e707-2020-4fba-96cd-55f056b74a9f` | `F:\Git\dsh-plugins` | 4988 | 93137 | 93133 | 93133-93136 | tool/result, step/end, step/start, assistant/chunk |
| `session-2503d35c-ad47-4811-9ae6-f944c1dad356` | `F:\CommonTasks` | 1267 | 17961 | 17957 | 17957-17960 | approval/decided, tool/result, step/end, step/start |
| `session-6f6ddc38-9705-4cfd-b132-506c5881b5df` | `F:\Git\dsh-plugins` | 1110 | 14902 | 14898 | 14898-14901 | tool/result, step/end, step/start, assistant/chunk |
| `session-88728413-fa95-4993-8f10-5158eb91a881` | `F:\Git\dsh-plugins` | 612 | 5792 | 5788 | 5788-5791 | tool/result, step/end, step/start, assistant/chunk |

Every gap is exactly **4 events behind** (`got == expected - 4`), and the duplicated events are **exactly the last 4 events of the committed prefix**, with identical types/payloads but fresh timestamps (~2 minutes after the originals). The file resumes at the correct seq immediately after the duplicate prefix and is otherwise perfectly contiguous to EOF (e.g. `9173e707` continues 93137?132739 with zero further discontinuities, ending in a completed `turn/end`).

### Detailed trace for `session-9173e707` (lines 4984-4992, 1 event per line)

```
L4984 seq=93133 tool/result      turn=2 step=46 t=1786795635084   ? committed (original run)
L4985 seq=93134 step/end         turn=2 step=46 t=1786795635084
L4986 seq=93135 turn/end         turn=2        t=1786795635084   (reason: interrupted)
L4987 seq=93136 session/end-seed               t=1786795746084   (+110 s: prepare/reseed)
L4988 seq=93133 tool/result      turn=2 step=46 t=1786795755580   ? RE-EMITTED (+9.5 s later)
L4989 seq=93134 step/end         turn=2 step=46 t=1786795755581
L4990 seq=93135 step/start       turn=2 step=47 t=1786795755618
L4991 seq=93136 assistant/chunk  turn=2 step=47 t=1786795756858
L4992 seq=93137 assistant/chunk  turn=2 step=47 t=1786795756859   ? correct continuation
```

The re-emitted sequence is exactly what an agent loop resuming an interrupted step emits first: re-deliver the in-flight `tool/result`, close the step, open the next step, stream the first `assistant/chunk` - but its seq counter was **4 behind the durable log** (as if the session view was missing the last 4 committed events).

## Root cause analysis

1. **The append path never validates durable seq continuity.** `appendLines()` in `session-persistence-jsonl/src/index.ts` encodes the batch and appends+fsyncs blindly; nothing checks that the batch's first event `seq` continues the file's committed prefix. `Session.append` only validates against the in-memory log, so a stale in-memory/snapshot view writes duplicate seqs without any error.
2. **The resume path re-appends already-committed events.** The 4-event tail re-emission with fresh timestamps (tool result ? step end ? step start ? first chunk) is a live-loop resume artifact, not a torn-tail retry (the torn-tail path only *re-writes recovered bytes*, and `commitRepair` writes synthetic closers - not this shape).
3. **The reader cannot self-heal this case.** `SessionLogScanner` treats a seq gap inside the committed region as damage, and since a `turn/end` exists after the gap it throws (`format.ts` line ~368). Torn-tail truncation does not apply because the gap is not at EOF. Result: the session is permanently unloadable until the log is manually rewritten.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Write-side invariant (primary):** `appendLines` (or the coordinator append path) must verify the batch's first `event.seq` equals the durable committed event count (obtained via the scanner/committed prefix) and refuse - or truncate-and-repair - instead of writing a duplicate prefix. This turns the corruption into a loud error at write time, or prevents it entirely.
2. **Resume path:** ensure the resumed agent's seq counter derives from a **fresh load of the committed prefix**, never from a stale snapshot; any re-delivery of already-committed events (tool result replay for GUI/state reconstruction) must be surface-only and must not be appended durably.
3. **Optional reader self-heal:** when the gap is exactly a re-emission of the tail prefix (events identical except `time`), the scanner could drop the duplicates and keep the file readable - but prevention (1)/(2) is the real fix.

## Manual repair performed (for reference)

Repair script dropped exactly the 4 duplicate lines (frames containing them were re-encoded; all other zstd frames kept byte-identical) and re-verified full contiguity with the harness scanner semantics (seq 0..N contiguous, ends `turn/end`, no torn frames). All 4 logs repaired; original corrupt bytes kept as `session.jsonl.zstd.corrupt-bak` beside each log. No real conversation content was lost (duplicates only).

discussions.title: [Bug] 流式工具调用增量携带空 id/name，导致会话历史永久无法加载：SessionPersistenceCorruptionError: message must have tool source
discussions.body:
## 版本 / Version
@deepseek-ai/dsh 0.1.0-rc.5（本地 checkout 构建运行）
复现环境：Linux，Web GUI 打开会话历史（localhost:3080）

## 现象 / Symptom
某个会话的历史无法加载，接口返回：

```
history unavailable for session "session-46a0916c-…": SessionPersistenceCorruptionError: stored session "session-46a0916c-…" failed validation: Error: session event at seq 165513 message must have tool source
```

GUI 侧显示「历史加载失败」。该会话历史之后**每次都**触发同一错误（无需任何其他操作）。

## 复现 / Reproduction
1. 在一个会话中让模型（本机为 `deepseek-official` / `deepseek-v4-pro`）发起一次工具调用（如 `read`）。
2. DeepSeek 流式返回：第一个 tool_call 增量带真实 `id`/`name`，**后续参数增量携带显式空字符串 `id: ""` / `function.name: ""`**（字段存在，而非省略）。
3. 会话日志里该轮最终 `tool-call` block 的 `id` 被清空 → agent 以空工具名执行 → `ToolNotFoundError: unknown tool ""` → 持久化出 `tool/result` 且 `message.source.callId === ""`。
4. 之后每次从 Web GUI 加载该会话历史都触发上面的校验错误。

会话 JSONL 中的关键证据（seq 165496 → 165508 → 165512 → 165513）：
- `assistant/chunk` 首个 tool-call-delta：`id: "call_edb776167f1347a3bad1011e", name: "read", argumentsDelta: ""`；
- 随后的打包行 `tool-call-chunks`：`id: ""`、`name: ""`（证实后续增量确实带空串，而非省略）；
- 最终 block：`{"type":"tool-call","id":"","name":"","arguments":"{…}"}`；
- `tool/result`：`source.callId: ""`、`content[0].toolCallId: ""` → 重放校验拒绝，历史整体无法加载。

## 根因 / Root cause
1. `packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/translate.ts`（约 159–160 行）在**每一个** tool_call 增量上无条件覆盖块身份：
   ```ts
   if (call.id !== undefined) block.callId = call.id
   if (call.function?.name !== undefined) block.name = call.function.name
   ```
   当后续增量携带 `id: ""` / `name: ""`（字段存在但为空）时，真实 id 被空串覆盖。已用真实源码独立复现：同样的流，带空串增量 → 最终 block `id: ""`；不带 → 正常保留 `id: "call_edb…", name: "read"`。

2. 次生隐患：`packages/llm/llm/src/assembler.ts`（约 70 行）同样无条件 `partial.toolCallId = chunk.id`，会覆盖首个非空 id。客户端 `PartialAccumulator` 已是「首个 id 固定」的语义，`BlockAssembler` 应保持一致。

3. 校验侧（`packages/core/session/src/index.ts` 的 `assertMessageEventShape`）对任何 `source.callId === ""` 的 `tool/result` 抛错，属防损坏的有意检查；但坏数据已持久化，导致该会话历史**永久**无法加载。

## 修复建议 / Suggested fix
两处（本地已验证）：
```ts
// packages/llm/llm-deepseek/src/translate.ts
- if (call.id !== undefined) block.callId = call.id
- if (call.function?.name !== undefined) block.name = call.function.name
+ if (call.id) block.callId = call.id
+ if (call.function?.name) block.name = call.function.name
```
```ts
// packages/llm/llm/src/assembler.ts
- partial.toolCallId = chunk.id
+ if (chunk.id) partial.toolCallId = chunk.id
```
修复后同样的流，最终 block 保留 `id: "call_edb…"`、`name: "read"`。

另外建议从源头缓解：adapter 侧对空 id/name 做规整（不覆盖），或在持久化/校验侧容忍空 callId 并合成兜底 id，避免再次产生「历史无法打开」的会话。已损坏的会话需要手工修复日志（把空 `source.callId` / `toolCallId` 填回真实 id）；注意 `.jsonl.zstd` 是多帧格式（首帧为 header 一行、带校验和），修复重压时需保持一致，否则会报 `corrupt Zstandard session log: first frame is not exactly one header line`。

## 影响 / Impact
任何一次「流式工具调用后续增量携带空 id/name」的会话，其 `tool/result` 会以空 `callId` 持久化，该会话历史在 GUI 中**永久无法打开**（agent 侧仍可运行，仅历史展示与续读失败）。遇到同样问题的朋友请给本帖点赞/upvote，方便官方按优先级处理。

discussions.title: Use DeepSeek Harness from Lark / Feishu with dsh-lark
discussions.body:
I built [`@sugarforever/dsh-lark`](https://github.com/sugarforever/dsh-lark), a community plugin that lets you talk to a DeepSeek Harness agent directly from Lark or Feishu.

It uses the official Lark Node SDK and receives messages over a WebSocket connection, so you do not need to expose a public server, configure a domain, or operate a webhook endpoint. Messages are mapped into Harness sessions and continue to use the models, tools, system prompts, agent presets, workspaces, and session storage already configured in Harness.

Highlights:

- Feishu and international Lark support
- direct messages, group chats, and topic-thread conversations
- one Harness session per chat, with isolated sessions for topic threads
- replies attached to the original message and kept inside the original thread
- mention-required group messages by default
- group and direct-message allowlists
- optional per-channel model, workspace, and agent-preset selection
- hashed session identifiers that do not expose raw Lark chat or thread IDs
- automatic reconnect, duplicate-event handling, stale-event filtering, and per-chat serialization through the official SDK

Install it into the Harness Web profile:

```sh
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add @sugarforever/dsh-lark
```

The bundled plugin instance starts disabled until Lark credentials are configured. The README includes the required application permissions, long-connection event setup, environment variables, profile configuration, access controls, and troubleshooting steps.

Repository and setup guide:

https://github.com/sugarforever/dsh-lark

Feedback and compatibility reports from both Feishu and international Lark users are welcome.

discussions.body:
由SDKWORK维护的社区版本，DeepSeek Harness 发布新版本 0.1.0-rc.12。 https://github.com/sdkwork-ai/deepseek-harness-desktop 这一版本进一步完善了 DeepSeek Harness 的多平台、多形态分发能力。从本地开发者使用，到服务器部署，再到 Kubernetes 集群运行，DeepSeek Harness 现在已经形成了一套完整的安装与部署体系。 无论你希望快速启动一个本地 Web UI、直接运行命令行任务、使用原生桌面应用，还是将 DeepSeek Harness 部署到 Docker 或 Kubernetes 环境，都可以选择对应的发行方式。 当前版本 0.1.0-rc.12 为仓库当前版本，同时也是 GitHub Latest。

一套版本，覆盖多种运行形态

分发方式适用场景所需环境版本来源默认访问方式 -- 桌面应用 | Windows、macOS、Linux 原生应用 | 无需 Node.js / Docker | GitHub Release | Electron IPC，不开放 HTTP 端口 npx Web UI | 最快速的本地 Web 启动 | Node.js + npm/npx | npm next 渠道 | http://127.0.0.1:3080 npx Headless CLI | 执行一次命令行任务 | Node.js + npm/npx | npm next 渠道 | 不开放 HTTP 端口 源码 Checkout | 精确使用 GitHub Tag 或修改源码 | Git + Node.js + Corepack + pnpm | Git Tag | http://127.0.0.1:3080 源码构建 Docker | 本地构建容器运行 | Git + Docker Engine + Docker Compose | Git Tag | http://127.0.0.1:4080 Docker Release 离线包 | 直接使用经过验证的 Release 镜像 | Docker Engine + Docker Compose + 归档工具 | GitHub Release | http://127.0.0.1:4080 源码部署 Kubernetes | Minikube / kind 本地集群部署 | Git + Docker + kubectl + Minikube / kind | Git Tag | http://127.0.0.1:4081 Kubernetes Release 离线包 | 集群环境使用离线 Release 镜像 | Docker + kubectl + 归档工具 + Kubernetes 集群 | GitHub Release | port-forward 后 http://127.0.0.1:4081

这意味着，DeepSeek Harness 不再局限于某一种安装方式，而是覆盖了从个人开发环境 → 本地桌面 → 容器 → Kubernetes 集群的完整使用链路。
