discussions.title: Feature request: in-place regenerate & a rewind event hook for session rollback
discussions.body:
Hi team,

First off, thank you for open-sourcing this — the Cordis plugin architecture and the agent preset composition mechanism are exceptionally clean, and building on it has been a great experience.

I've run into a capability gap I'd like to formally raise:

**1. In-place regenerate for the last assistant turn**

Currently, if a response is unsatisfying, the only option is to branch a new conversation. Branching makes sense for agentic tasks, but in long interactive sessions it's heavy: what the user usually wants is simply "retry the last turn in place." This could be implemented as a shortcut for fork + truncate, without changing the underlying session model.

**2. An event hook on rewind/branch/regenerate (the more important one)**

My use case: a plugin that maintains a project task board outside the conversation (SQLite: task states, dependencies, change log). When the user branches or retries, the conversation rolls back — but the plugin's external state has no way to know, so mutations get applied twice and the board drifts out of sync.

Since DSH already records the session into a single append-only log with fork/replay support, this shouldn't require a new mechanism — it would "just" mean broadcasting a Cordis event (e.g. `session/rewind`) on the existing fork/truncate path. A minimal payload like `{ sessionId, boundaryTurnId }` would let any plugin truncate or roll back its own external log accordingly.

This hook has general value for any plugin holding state outside the conversation: task boards, external resource managers, knowledge bases with write-back, etc.

**3. (Optional) Multiple candidate versions per assistant turn**

Similar to SillyTavern's swipe: keep several candidates for the same turn and let the user switch between them. I understand this is more of a chat-paradigm feature, so it's fine as the lowest priority.

Thanks for reading — happy to elaborate or help test any of these.

discussions.title: [Bug] 审批策略 never 时工具报错 "the user rejected tool X" 误导——实为策略自动拒绝，用户无任何可操作 UI
discussions.body:
# [Bug] 审批策略 never 时工具报错 "the user rejected tool X" 误导——实为策略自动拒绝，用户无任何可操作 UI

**Category: Bug report**（发布到 https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions ）

## 现象

当会话审批策略为 `never`（例如权限预设切到 `danger-full-access` 时）调用需要审批的工具（`issue_open` / `pr_create` / `issue_comment` 等），工具调用直接失败并返回错误文案：

```
Error: the user rejected tool "issue_open"
```

用户**从未看到任何审批界面、没有任何可点击的批准/拒绝按钮**——这个文案把「策略自动拒绝」表述成「用户拒绝」，误导性很强：模型会误以为用户明确拒绝了该操作，用户也会困惑「我什么都没点，怎么是我拒的？」。

## 复现

1. `/preset danger-full-access`（或 `DSH_PERMISSION_MODE=danger-full-access`）
2. 调用任意 `Requires approval` 的工具（如 `issue_open`）
3. 工具立即失败，报错 `the user rejected tool "..."`

## 根因

两处代码拼出的结果：

- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-user-approval`：`effectivePolicy === 'never'` 时直接返回 outcome `"rejected"`（无审批通道、无 UI）
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` 的审批 seam：outcome `"rejected"` → `reason: \`the user rejected tool "${exec.name}"\``（`resolveApprovalAsk` 的 switch 分支）

同类措辞还有：

- `dsh-sandbox`：`the user rejected escalating this ... to "..."`（never 模式下沙箱提权同样自动拒绝）
- `dsh-cordis-host-runner`：`The user rejected Cordis ...`

## 建议

按拒绝来源区分文案：

| 场景 | 建议文案 |
|---|---|
| 策略拒绝（policy = never，无人参与） | `tool "X" was rejected by policy (approval: never)` |
| 用户拒绝（审批弹窗点了拒绝） | 保留 `the user rejected tool "X"` |
| 取消 / 无通道 | 现有文案已区分（cancelled / unavailable），OK |

运行时上下文里的「Approval prompts are disabled in this session: actions that require approval are rejected automatically」是准确的，但工具报错与它自相矛盾——对齐后模型与用户都能立刻分清「策略拦的」还是「人拒的」。

discussions.title: Community review: deepseek-harness @ master (v0.1.0-rc.5) — findings & suggestions
discussions.body:
Hi maintainers! I spent some time reading through the public repo (master @ v0.1.0-rc.5) and, since issues are off here, I wanted to share a few things I noticed. The codebase is honestly in really good shape for a release candidate — I kept this short on purpose.

**Hooks can spin forever on a blocking Stop hook.** Both bridges hardcode `stop_hook_active: false` (`packages/hooks/hooks-codex/src/index.ts:257`, `packages/hooks/hooks-claude-code/src/index.ts:346`), so when a Stop hook blocks, the bridge tells the agent to keep going — and the hook never learns it already continued. A hook that always blocks therefore loops until something times out. The related `{"continue": false}` result is parsed but never actually stops the run either. A counter with a cap on forced continuations would fix the first one.

**Settings secrets can leak through the redactor.** If a secret field sits behind a union/intersection/transform schema, `redactSecrets` returns the value untouched and records nothing (`packages/settings/settings/src/redact.ts:86-91`). Since the seam promises every wire surface is redacted, rejecting such schemas at registration (fail closed) seems safer than the current fail-open behavior. Related: `settings-file` doesn't check file permissions the way `credentials-local` does (`assertOwnerOnly`), so a world-readable settings file containing secret fields gets served without complaint.

**Settings and credentials writes aren't crash-durable.** `writeFileAtomic` (`packages/util/atomic-write/src/index.ts:44`) renames the temp file into place without fsync, so a power cut can lose the most recent credentials or settings write. The JSONL session backend fsyncs; these two callers don't. An opt-in fsync there would close the gap.

**The published landlock-run packages link to a repo that isn't public.** All three `native/landlock-run/packages/*` packages have `repository.url` pointing at `github.com/deepseek-harness/deepseek-harness`, which 404s for npm users. It should be `deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness` — a one-line fix per package.

**The AGENTS.md layout has drifted a lot.** It's missing ~15 groups (client, host, jobs, sandbox, mcp, storage, workspace, …) and misnames two (`self-modification` → `extensions`, `support` → `test-support`). `packages/README.md` is accurate; linking to it instead of keeping a second list would stop this from drifting again. (`vitest.config.ts:175` still excludes the old `packages/self-modification/` name too.)

**The Python SDK has two concurrency rough edges.** `start()` checks `self._proc` outside the lock (`python/sdk/src/deepseek_harness/client.py:63-85`), so two concurrent starts can spawn two runtimes and orphan one. And the reader loop silently drops malformed JSON lines, which hides corrupted runtime frames from the caller.

That's everything I'd flag before release. I noticed a few smaller things as well — mostly i18n inconsistencies in the web UI, a stale ACP version string, and some tracked TODOs. Happy to share those too if useful, but I didn't want to bury the real items in noise.

discussions.title: [Bug][Windows] 目录选择器 readUtf16 提前截断低字节为 0x00 的汉字，含"开/一/丁"等字的文件夹无法认领为工作区
discussions.body:
## 环境
- 系统：Windows 10/11 x64（中文）
- dsh：0.1.0-rc.6（npm 全局安装）
- 相关包：`@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-directory-picker-native`
- 受影响文件（构建产物）：`lib/worker.cjs` 中的 `readUtf16`（源码区域标识为 `lib/types/win32-dialog-bindings.js`）

## 复现步骤
1. 在桌面新建文件夹 `软件开发`
2. Web 界面 → 工作区 → 添加工作区 → 在原生"选择文件夹"对话框中选中该文件夹（纯鼠标点选，不手动输入）
3. 点击"选择文件夹"后报错：

```
无法打开文件夹
workspace create failed: workspace-invalid-path: cannot create a workspace at
"D:\360MoveData\Users\Administrator\Desktop\软件":
ENOENT: no such file or directory, realpath 'D:\360MoveData\Users\Administrator\Desktop\软件'
```

- 预期：成功创建指向 `...\Desktop\软件开发` 的工作区
- 实际：路径被截断成 `...\Desktop\软件`（"开发"丢失），`fs.realpath` 报 ENOENT

## 根因
`readUtf16` 扫描 NUL 结尾的 UTF-16 字符串时，只判断每个单元的低字节：

```js
while (end + 1 < bytes.length && bytes[end] !== 0) end += 2;
```

任何码位低字节为 0x00 的字符都会让循环提前终止。例如 `开`（U+5F00，UTF-16LE 字节 = 00 5F）的低字节恰为 0，扫描到"开"即停止，"软件开发"被截成"软件"。同理 `一`（U+4E00）、`丁`（U+4E01）等大量常用汉字都会触发；ASCII 与低字节非 0 的汉字不受影响，因此 bug 相当隐蔽。

`IShellItem::GetDisplayName(SIGDN_FILESYSPATH)` 返回 `…\软件开发\0`，经 `readUtf16` 后变成 `…\软件`，随后 workspace 创建阶段的 `fs.realpath` 报 ENOENT。

## 修复建议
把终止条件改为"两个字节都为 0 才算结束"：

```js
while (end + 1 < bytes.length && (bytes[end] !== 0 || bytes[end + 1] !== 0)) end += 2;
```

## 验证
- 用新旧逻辑分别对 `D:\...\Desktop\软件开发` 的 UTF-16LE 字节做模拟：旧逻辑输出 `...\软件`（与报错完全一致），新逻辑输出完整路径。
- 本地修改 `lib/worker.cjs` 后，重新选择同一文件夹即可正常认领（选择器 worker 每次即时拉起，无需重启 dsh）。

## 影响面
Windows 平台上，任何路径包含低字节为 0x00 的 BMP 字符（"开、一、丁、些"等大量常用汉字）的目录都无法被认领为工作区，属于高频隐蔽 bug。

discussions.title: 一个通用 P2P 隧道方案：DSH 的 loopback 同源限制在远程访问下的处理
discussions.body:
DeepSeek Harness（DSH）将配置面板限制为 loopback 同源，用于防范 DNS rebinding，这一设计是合理的。但该限制对远程访问提出了额外要求：通过局域网 IP 直连时 /api 返回 403，通过域名或隧道访问时设置面板为空（设置仅存在于进程内存），--trusted-host 需要逐一枚举 IP 且不支持通配符，网络变更后需要重新配置。

此前常用的替代方案各有权衡。SSH 端口转发可用，但需要在每台设备上维护隧道及其保活；反向代理需要额外引入认证层。二者均未从根本上解决"服务只信任 loopback"这一约束。

kepos 是我开发的一个通用 P2P 隧道（Apache-2.0），其核心设计是：发布端分享任意 TCP 服务，订阅端以 *.localhost 域名或本地端口的形式访问，使浏览器、SSH、CLI 等客户端始终认为自己在访问本机。由于 DSH 的 browser-trust 围栏仅校验 Host 头，kepos 将服务挂载于 *.localhost 网关后，Host 即为 loopback，围栏原样放行。无需修改 --trusted-host，无需引入认证层，设置项正常持久化，刷新后不丢失。kepos 并未针对 DSH 做任何特殊适配，该能力是其通用设计的结果。

传输层方面，kepos 基于分布式哈希表（DHT）建立对等连接，并在此基础上实现端到端加密与多路复用。具体而言：HyperDHT 与 UDX 提供经过认证的对等连接、NAT 穿透、路径迁移、可靠有序的数据流；对等密钥对外层连接进行端到端加密认证。多路复用由 Protomux 承载——服务注册表、心跳控制、配对过程以及每个服务各自的独立通道，全部复用同一条持久化的外层连接；隧道本身是 UDX之上的分裂 TCP 字节流代理，OPEN、数据、半关闭、重置与背压均经由多路复用通道传递，而非传输原始 TCP 报文。


实际配置如下（订阅端）：

```toml
[subscriber]
enabled = true
gateway_port = 17480

[[subscriber.services]]
id = "dsh"
local_port = 13080
```

通过 http://127.0.0.1:13080 访问，语言与主题设置均可正常修改并持久化。SSH、Dagger 等 raw TCP 服务可复用同一条隧道，各自绑定独立本地端口。

访问控制方面：未知设备仍无法连接，发布端每个服务可独立配置 allowlist。

项目当前状态为 developer preview：Android 需侧载安装，macOS 也需要`xattr -d com.apple.quarantine`，UDP 不承载。

仓库：github.com/LamplitIsles/kepos
官网：https://kepos.guion.io/
集成文档：[docs/integrations/deepseek-harness.md](https://github.com/LamplitIsles/kepos/blob/main/docs/integrations/deepseek-harness.md)

discussions.title: dsh-web-search-ollama — web_search via Ollama, without DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
discussions.body:
# Draft — DeepSeek Harness Discussion / PR

**Title:** Ollama web search without DEEPSEEK_API_KEY (`dsh-web-search-ollama`)

## Problem

Running DSH against Ollama (custom OpenAI-compatible provider, e.g. `deepseek-v4-flash:cloud`) works for chat, but `web_search` still uses `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-search-deepseek`:

```
Error: DeepSeek search has no API key for "DEEPSEEK_API_KEY"; store it through the credentials service
```

`ollama launch dsh` is documented as pre-installing Ollama web search, but Ollama 0.32.4 does not expose a `dsh` launch target (`claude`, `hermes`, `opencode`, `pi`, … only).

## What we did

A profile bundle that:

- registers `ctx.web` search + fetch providers `id: ollama`
- sets `searchProvider` / `fetchProvider` to `ollama`
- disables `web-search-deepseek`
- calls the signed-in local host:
  - `POST http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/experimental/web_search`
  - fallback `POST /api/web_search`

Verified: headless `web_search` for “Ollama official website” returned `https://ollama.com/`.

Repo: https://github.com/mrmoradzekri-hub/dsh-web-search-ollama

Install:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add -w github:mrmoradzekri-hub/dsh-web-search-ollama
```

## Ask

1. Community plugin is enough for now, or do you want a first-party `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-search-ollama`?
2. If first-party: should it live next to `dsh-web-search-deepseek` / `dsh-web-search-exa`, selected via `DSH_WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDER=ollama`?
3. Please treat `/api/experimental/web_search` as a compatibility path until Ollama ships `ollama launch dsh` everywhere.

discussions.title: Proposal: task-conditioned Harness evolution with evaluable Plugin Packs
discussions.body:
## Summary

DSH can already inspect and change its own runtime through Cordis, and
developers can distribute those changes as plugins. The current specification
does not bind the developer's task, exact active composition, execution trace,
evaluation, and outcome into reusable evidence. The platform can distribute
plugin artifacts, but it cannot systematically accumulate evidence about how
they perform across tasks, models, and environments or use that evidence to
update Harness Recipes, Scorecards, and composition policies. This is the
missing link in the evolution of externalized Harness knowledge.

I propose a task-conditioned Harness evolution loop. The platform treats every
Plugin and Harness Recipe as a versioned data asset. Each asset declares a Task
Profile that defines its task family and applicability boundary, then ships a
representative evaluation suite. The platform runs those evaluations, maintains
independent Scorecards, and gives the AI evidence for searching the next
composition. Real task outcomes update that evidence.

Here, the platform is a logical registry and evaluation role. A local CI
system, an organization service, a community registry, or an official hosted
service could perform that role. It stores each trial result separately and
builds a Scorecard only from results produced under comparable versions and
conditions.

The proposed asset contract binds four records that are currently separate:
the exact artifact, its task claims and evaluation cases, platform-produced
scores, and the outcomes observed when a Harness used it.

```text
task
  -> retrieve compatible plugins and compositions
  -> search composition trajectories
  -> probe candidates against the current task and retention anchors
  -> issue a Selection Receipt and guarded CommitDecision
  -> activate an accepted harness for this task
  -> execute the task and record the outcome
  -> update shared evidence and future search priors
```

I will use **Harness Pack** as a provisional name for the publisher-owned
contract that attaches task claims, reproducible evaluation cases, graders,
and compatibility metadata to either a Plugin Asset or a Harness Recipe.
Platform-produced results, Scorecards, and real-task Outcomes remain separate
records. DSH already uses `Package` for an immutable version of a dynamic Cordis
Plugin, so the final name should avoid that collision.

## Related community foundations

Several community projects provide useful foundations:

- [#1597](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1597)
  and [#1760](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1760)
  provide natural-language plugin discovery.
- [#2282](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/2282)
  defines `use_when` / `not_for` capability declarations, recommends Top-K
  plugins before a task, and publishes a small B/C evaluation with scripts.
- [#1888](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/1888)
  proposes task-driven, session-scoped plugin assembly and cleanup.
- [#2276](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/2276)
  proposes machine discovery, trust metadata, and a shareable Compose unit
  containing plugin references and security declarations. Its comments also
  discuss runtime evidence for both plugins and compositions.
- [#2269](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/2269)
  connects marketplace records to machine-readable verification reports through
  fields such as `verifiedBy`, `verifiedAt`, and `reportUrl`.
- [#2088](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/2088)
  proposes real-host release lifecycle validation for packed plugins.
- [#524](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/524)
  examines retrieval and staged activation for large tool catalogs.

These discussions solve different boundaries. Discovery finds candidates.
Capability metadata explains when an author expects a plugin to help. Validation
checks whether an artifact installs and behaves as declared. Compose records a
reusable configuration. Session assembly applies a configuration to a task.

This proposal adds a platform-owned contract for task evidence, composition
search, outcome attribution, and Recipe promotion. It turns the discovery,
capability metadata, validation, Compose, and session-assembly work above into
one task-conditioned Harness evolution loop.

## What DSH provides today, and what is missing

DSH already has several prerequisites for an evolvable harness. They establish
the mechanics of change and observation, but they do not decide which change
will improve the current task.

| Current mechanism | What it establishes | Missing condition for self-evolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cordis composition and the dynamic package lifecycle | DSH can inspect, add, run, stop, replace, and dispose components without rebuilding the agent loop. | No task objective, candidate generator, search policy, or reward function chooses a composition. The model-facing dynamic package toolset is also opt-in and process-local. |
| Skill Registry | DSH can merge local, embedded, remote, and runtime skill catalogs and load a selected skill. | The registry has no standard task profile, evaluation suite, Scorecard, or evidence-based ranking for combinations. |
| Plugin inventory and inspection | DSH can report what is installed or running. | Inventory is an observation of the current runtime, not a searchable history of candidate recipes and their task outcomes. |
| Session Log and reconstructable request headers | DSH can preserve the exact model-visible history, tool calls, and changing tool catalog for a run. | The log does not bind a task outcome to an evaluated Harness Recipe or attribute the result to a composition change. |
| Feedback and session telemetry | A deployment can capture user feedback and export redacted execution records. | No evaluator consumes those records, updates a Scorecard, or changes the next composition search. Telemetry handoff alone does not create learning. |
| Plan Mode | DSH can inject planning guidance and require human review before execution. | Current Plan Mode is soft prompt guidance. It has no world model, reward, candidate tree, rollout, or automatic selection. |

The current architecture therefore provides **mutation**, **composition**, and
**observation**. Harness self-evolution also requires **search**, **evaluation**,
**selection**, and **retention**.

Here, retention means more than keeping a trace. A successful combination must
become a versioned asset with reproducible evidence, then influence the search
for later tasks.

## Upgrade 1: make task evidence part of the asset model

The platform could manage two related assets:

- A **Plugin Asset** is one installable capability.
- A **Harness Recipe** is an immutable, versioned artifact with a content
  fingerprint. It records the exact plugins, model settings, prompts, skills,
  and configuration needed to rebuild one Harness composition.

The second asset matters because plugin effects are not additive. Two useful
plugins can conflict, duplicate context, increase tool-selection errors, or
exceed a task's latency and token budget. DSH therefore needs evidence for both
individual plugins and complete harness combinations.

The core evaluation contract connects each asset to two records. The planner
also reads mutable Selection Facts, described in Upgrade 2.

### 1. Publisher-owned Pack

The immutable Pack contains declarations and reproducible evaluation inputs:

- task profile, including the task family, applicability boundaries, and
  expected outcomes;
- compatibility and permission requirements;
- representative evaluation suites and graders;
- exact plugin or recipe versions;
- known conflicts and declared side effects.

### 2. Platform-maintained evidence

The platform runs evaluations and stores the resulting Scorecard separately:

- exact Pack, model, environment, dataset, and grader versions;
- trial count and outcome distribution;
- quality, cost, latency, and safety metrics;
- comparison with the active baseline;
- retention anchors for historical tasks and protected capabilities;
- provenance and links to reproducible reports.

The publisher may contribute evaluation cases and graders. A publisher-supplied
`score: 95` should not become trusted platform evidence.

One successful trial should not broaden an asset's claimed applicability. The
Pack states the intended task family. Platform evidence determines where that
claim holds, while retention anchors protect earlier behavior when a Recipe
changes.

This split extends the evidence fields discussed in #2269. It also gives the
Compose work in #2276 a task-quality dimension rather than treating a
composition as useful solely because it can be shared and activated.

## A possible Pack shape

```yaml
pack:
  id: code-review-security
  version: 0.3.0
  kind: plugin # plugin | harness-recipe
  publisher: example-org

  artifact:
    plugins:
      - id: security-review
        version: 1.4.2

  task_profile:
    intents:
      - review a code change for security vulnerabilities
    inputs:
      - git_diff
      - repository_context
    expected_outcomes:
      - actionable findings with file and line evidence

  compatibility:
    models:
      - family: deepseek
    environments:
      - git_repository
    permissions:
      - filesystem_read
    conflicts: []

  evaluation:
    suites:
      - id: security-review-v1
        cases: ./evals/cases.jsonl
        graders: ./evals/graders.yaml
    required_metrics:
      - finding_precision
      - finding_recall
      - task_success
      - token_cost
      - latency
```

The existing Compose schema from #2276 may be the right base for
`harness-recipe`; a separate Harness Pack type may not be necessary. The point
is the contract between the asset, its task claims, and independently produced
evidence.

## Upgrade 2: build a task-conditioned Harness planner

The planner searches over Harness configurations instead of returning one
static recommendation:

- Its state contains the current task, active Harness Recipe, environment, and
  partial execution evidence.
- Its actions add, remove, replace, or configure Plugin Assets.
- Its objective combines task quality, cost, latency, safety, and user
  feedback.
- Its output is a versioned Harness Recipe supported by evidence for the
  current constraints.

Artifact identity alone is not enough for selection. Compatibility,
reachability, setup requirements, permissions, cost, risk, and evidence
references can change without changing the Plugin or Recipe itself. The
platform should store these as separately versioned **Selection Facts**. Each
choice should emit a **Selection Receipt** that pins the facts, constraints,
and evidence used for that decision.

An independent runner should handle exact-artifact execution binding as a
separate interoperability contract. Before it produces evaluation evidence,
the runner should resolve a versioned **RunnerBinding**. That document binds
the Selection Receipt to the selected candidate identifier, exact artifact
digest, artifact byte source, and named digest profile. The digest profile must
define portable JSON canonicalization and artifact byte-source rules, with
implementation-independent conformance vectors. The runner should place a
required `runnerBindingRef` in EvaluationEvidence so the evidence digest
commits to the binding. The evaluator or gate must reject unresolved,
invalid, or mismatched bindings before CommitDecision.

The Pack and evidence contracts should not prescribe one search algorithm. The
platform can begin with retrieval, constraint filtering, ranked candidate
generation, and a small number of probes. Later implementations may use beam
search, a contextual bandit, tree search, or a trained planning model.

Current DSH Plan Mode does not perform this search. It injects planning guidance
and collects human approval for one generated plan.

## Upgrade 3: close the task-to-evidence loop

For a request, DSH or a platform service could:

1. Classify the user's goal and current harness context against one or more Task
   Profiles.
2. Retrieve compatible Plugin Assets and Harness Recipes.
3. Resolve current Selection Facts, then filter candidates by model,
   environment, permissions, cost, risk, reachability, and conflicts.
4. Generate composition actions: keep, add, remove, replace, or reconfigure.
5. Rank candidate trajectories with evaluation evidence from similar tasks.
6. Run isolated task-specific probes when the evidence is weak or stale.
7. Select a candidate Recipe and emit a Selection Receipt that binds the exact
   facts, constraints, and evidence behind the choice.
8. An independent runner materializes the selected candidate and resolves a
   versioned RunnerBinding that binds the receipt to the exact artifact and
   named digest profile.
9. Evaluate that exact candidate in a controlled runtime against the current
   task, retention anchors, validity checks, and budget limits. Produce
   EvaluationEvidence with a required runnerBindingRef.
10. Emit a CommitDecision bound to the candidate, evidence, and policy digests.
   Activate the candidate through Cordis only when the decision accepts it.
11. Execute the real task and bind its trace, outcome, cost, and user feedback
    to that Recipe.
12. Update the Scorecard, applicability boundary, and retention evidence.
13. Register a successful composition as a new versioned Harness Recipe after
    it passes reproducibility, safety, and provenance checks.

The planner selects a better-supported harness under the current task, model,
environment, budget, and risk constraints.

The activation step can build on #1888. Candidate retrieval can build on #1597,
#1760, and #2282. The Pack and evidence records can build on #2276, #2269, and
#2088. Cordis supplies the mutation actions. The proposed addition is the
planner and the evaluation-driven feedback contract between those parts.

The platform should split work between two loops:

- **Offline evidence loop:** validate Packs, run repeatable suites, compare
  recipes against both current-task suites and retention anchors, and publish
  versioned Scorecards. This gives online search useful priors.
- **Online task loop:** search only a bounded compatible candidate set, run
  cheap probes where needed, emit a Selection Receipt, commit only an accepted
  candidate, and feed the observed outcome back into platform evidence.

Without the offline loop, every developer pays to rediscover the same
combinations. Without the online loop, the platform can only recommend a static
average that may not fit the current task.

## Why this fits DSH

Cordis already supplies the execution substrate: composition, inspection,
versioned dynamic packages, activation, update, teardown, and effect disposal.
The Skill Registry supplies a discovery surface. Session logs and telemetry can
provide execution evidence.

DSH already supports controlled mutation. The proposed layers add the missing
learning loop:

```text
Pack contract
  -> platform evaluation and Scorecard
  -> task-conditioned planner
  -> Selection Receipt
  -> isolated probe and retention checks
  -> CommitDecision
  -> Cordis activation
  -> real task outcome
  -> evidence update and Recipe promotion
```

With this loop, DSH can use past outcomes to improve future composition
decisions.

## Future direction: train DeepSeek for Harness search

The platform loop also creates training data:

```text
Task Profile
  + starting Harness Recipe
  + available Plugin Assets
  + Selection Facts and constraints
  + candidate composition actions
  + Selection Receipt
  + RunnerBinding
  + current-task and retention evidence
  + CommitDecision
  + final task outcome
```

DeepSeek could use these records to train a model specialized in Harness search
and planning. Given a task and the current recipe, the model could predict the
next composition action, estimate candidate value, or decide that the current
recipe is sufficient. Successful search traces provide supervised targets;
platform evaluation and real outcomes can provide reward or preference signals.

The model would accelerate candidate generation and reduce online probes. It
would not replace the Pack contract or external evaluation: the model proposes
and predicts, while the platform verifies and records the result. This is a
future direction, not a capability DSH currently provides.

## Related research

- The Cordis paper describes the temporal and spatial composition mechanisms
  needed to replace components safely:
  https://github.com/cordiverse/paper
- AlphaEvolve combines candidate generation, automated evaluators, a program
  database, and selection of promising candidates:
  https://deepmind.google/discover/blog/alphaevolve-a-gemini-powered-coding-agent-for-designing-advanced-algorithms/
- Anthropic's agent-evaluation guidance separates tasks, trials, graders,
  traces, and outcomes, and treats the evaluated agent as its model and harness:
  https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/demystifying-evals-for-ai-agents
- Voyager stores verified executable skills and retrieves them for later tasks:
  https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16291
- RAP shows that a planner can search reasoning trajectories with task rewards
  while balancing exploration and exploitation. It helps explain the problem;
  this proposal does not adopt RAP or require MCTS:
  https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.14992
- Harness Continual Learning separates candidate generation from guarded state
  commitment and checks current improvement, historical retention, and
  validity before committing a harness update:
  https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.19013

## Open questions

1. Should task and evaluation metadata extend the Compose work in #2276, extend
   the plugin manifest, or use a separate Pack contract?
2. Which evaluation inputs belong in the immutable asset, and which results
   belong in platform-maintained evidence?
3. What is the smallest useful first scope: one plugin, one complete Harness
   Recipe, or both?
4. Which graders can the platform run reproducibly across different plugin
   categories?
5. How should DSH compare results across models and environments without hiding
   the differences behind one aggregate score?
6. How should the platform handle private datasets, benchmark leakage,
   malicious graders, and score gaming?
7. Which parts should remain portable across harnesses, and which parts should
   describe Cordis-specific lifecycle rules?
8. Which search policy should the first planner use after retrieval and
   constraint filtering?
9. Where should candidate probes run so that failed or malicious combinations
   cannot mutate the user's active Harness?
10. Which records may be used to train a Harness planning model, and how should
    the platform preserve user and organization privacy?

Would it be useful to define a minimal shared schema that existing discovery,
Compose, verification, and session-assembly projects can all produce or consume?

If you would like the DSH team to evaluate these contracts and runtime hooks,
please upvote this Discussion. Use the comments for implementation evidence,
objections, and design feedback.

discussions.title: I built an image and video generation agent plugin for DeepSeek Harness like lovart
discussions.body:
Hello everyone, we have developed an agent plugin for image and video generation for DeepSeek Harness.

Our idea is that as foundational models and general-purpose Agent operating environments gradually mature, developing vertical Agents may no longer require building an Agent from scratch, but rather providing specialized APIs, domain-specific Skills and workflows.

I have provided APIs for various image, video and models here, along with a large number of best practices to help agents understand how to use these APIs in different image and video tasks.

It quickly helped me build a powerful agent for image and video generation, and it works really well for me.

https://github.com/weshopai/weshop-dsh-pluginhttps://github.com/weshopai/weshop-dsh-plugin

discussions.title: hygiene fails at master: rescope-vendor misreads cordis/* event channel names as package specifiers
discussions.body:
Title: `pnpm run hygiene` fails at master: rescope-vendor misreads `cordis/*` event channel names as package specifiers

## Bug

`pnpm run rescope-vendor:check` (the first gate in `pnpm run hygiene`) fails on current master (`47f943859b`):

```
rescope-vendor: residue: packages/api/remotes/src/remote-events.ts still carries a pre-rescope name token
rescope-vendor: residue: packages/extensions/cordis-host-runner/src/types.ts still carries a pre-rescope name token
... 26 files total
rescope-vendor: 26 problem(s); the mapping or an upstream site moved.
```

## Cause

Commit `4064198560` (feat(self-modification): add dynamic Cordis plugin runtime and UI) landed after the repository naming-contract rescope (`a2d0f7f411`). It emits events on the `cordis/` scope:

```ts
// packages/api/remotes/src/remote-events.ts
'cordis/request-run',
'cordis/request-run-resolved',
'cordis/dynamic-package',
...
```

The `rescope-vendor` token rule matches a quoted `'cordis/…'` string as a `cordis` package specifier with a subpath, so `--check` reports the file as un-rescoped residue. But these are wire event channel names emitted by the Loader's `cordis:` builtin — rewriting them to `'@deepseek-ai/cordis/request-run'` would break event matching between the Host and its consumers. The same files also use the bare `cordis` string as a UI/i18n namespace key (`PropsLocale<'cordis'>`, `NS = 'cordis'`), which is product data, not a package reference.

Affected files: 26, across `packages/api/remotes`, `packages/extensions/{cordis-host-runner,cordis-client-runner,tool-cordis,ui-cordis}`, `packages/client/ui-settings-plugin-inventory`, `docs/{event-producer-consumer*,subsystems/extensions*}`, and `scripts/gen-cordis-catalog.ts`.

## Reproduce

```sh
git checkout 47f943859b -- .   # master
pnpm install
pnpm run rescope-vendor:check  # exits 1 with the residue list above
```

## Fix

`GENERIC_SKIPS` in `scripts/rescope-vendor.ts` is the existing escape hatch for exactly this class of false positive — the agent-preset entries (`'cordis'` as a preset id) skip the bare name for the same reason. Adding the 26 files with `upstream: ['cordis']` makes the gate pass with no rewrites:

```
rescope-vendor: check over 4431 tracked files
rescope-vendor: post-state verified — no residue, every exact edit landed, idempotent.
```

Full `pnpm run hygiene` then passes locally, and `scripts/rescope-vendor.spec.ts` (3 tests) stays green.

Happy to share the patch (one-file change, skip-list entries + comment) if the team wants it. Per CONTRIBUTING.md I'm reporting here rather than opening a PR.

discussions.title: 【BUG】 代码分析过程中发现的一些问题
discussions.body:
各位好，

过去几天我通读这个仓库，过程中攒下七处**文档、设计记录或代码注释所声称的行为，与实际发出去的东西对不上**的地方。

---

## 一、非正的 hook `timeout` 会让 PreToolUse 拦截静默失效，而审计记录显示「通过」

这一条是四步组合起来的结果，每一步单独看都合理。

**第一步：`defaultTimeoutMs` 没有正数校验，而它的邻居有。**

`packages/hooks/hooks-claude-code/src/index.ts:98-100`：

```ts
const stderrSummaryMaxChars = config.stderrSummaryMaxChars ?? DEFAULT_STDERR_SUMMARY_MAX_CHARS
assertPositiveInteger('stderrSummaryMaxChars', stderrSummaryMaxChars)
const defaultTimeoutMs = config.defaultTimeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS
```

第 99 行校验了，第 100 行没有。schema 两者都是裸 `z.number()`（`:76-77`）。`hooks-codex` 同构。

**第二步：非正数传下去会抛错。** `packages/util/timeout/src/index.ts:51`：

```ts
if (requested !== undefined && (!Number.isFinite(requested) || requested <= 0)) {
  throw new Error(`${name} must be a positive finite number`)
}
```

**第三步：hook runner 把任何抛错都当成非阻塞错误。** `packages/hooks/hook-protocol/src/runner.ts:96`：

```ts
} catch (error: unknown) {
  // The executor rejects only on infrastructure faults (unusable workdir,
  // missing shell). A hook that cannot run is a non-blocking error: no exit
  // code, the failure on stderr for the record. The turn proceeds.
```

> 执行器只在基础设施故障（不可用的 workdir、缺失的 shell）时拒绝。一个跑不起来的 hook 属于非阻塞错误：没有退出码，失败信息记在 stderr 里。turn 继续。

这个判断对基础设施故障是合理的。但**配置错误也走同一条路**——而配置错误不是暂时性的，它每一次都会失败。

**第四步：审计记录把它记成通过。** `packages/hooks/hook-protocol/src/events.ts:86-87`：

> The recorded decision is the parsed decision, then `stop` for `continue:false`, else `pass`

**会出什么问题**

有人配了一个 PreToolUse hook 来拦危险操作，`timeout` 写成 `0`（或者某个计算出负数的表达式）。从此这个 hook **一次都没有启动过**，每次工具调用都畅通无阻。

没有报错，没有告警。事后追查「为什么没拦住」，翻持久审计记录，得到的答案是 **hook 跑了并且批准了**——日志本身给出了错误的结论。

触发条件：不需要特定平台，一个配置笔误即可。这类问题的危险之处在于它**不产生任何症状**，装的时候测一次「正常操作没被拦」看起来一切正常。

**把握程度**：四步链路都逐行验证过，确定。是否属于「有意的失败方向」需要你们判断——注释确实说明了非阻塞是设计选择，但它给的理由是基础设施故障，而不是配置错误。

**建议**：给 `defaultTimeoutMs` 加上和它邻居一样的 `assertPositiveInteger`；或者在 runner 的 catch 里把「配置类错误」和「基础设施故障」分开，前者 fail-closed。

---

## 二、`cordis-host-runner` 的 README 契约与实现不符，且会把宿主 stack trace 推给模型

**README 的声称**（`packages/extensions/cordis-host-runner/README.md:52` 与 `:56`）：

> Nothing directly: this package **registers no tool and injects no prompt**.

> Token effect — **None of its own**: every message above is carried by the calling tool's result.

**实际代码**：`src/index.ts` 里有 4 处 `agent.steer(createUserMessage(...))`（`:1043`、`:1056`、`:1081`、`:1107`）和 1 处 `agent.inject(createUserMessage(...))`（`:1153`），都是直接往模型历史里推 user 消息，`source` 标的是这个包自己：

```ts
agent.steer(createUserMessage({
  content: [{ type: 'text', text }],
  source: { kind: 'plugin', plugin: 'cordis-host-runner' },
}))
```

这些消息不是「由调用方的工具结果携带」的，是它自己的。所以「injects no prompt」和「Token effect: None of its own」两句都与实现不符。

另外 `:1262` 的失败格式化会把原始 stack 拼进文本：

```ts
+ (failure.stack === undefined ? '' : `\nstack:\n${failure.stack}`)
```

Node 的 stack trace 含绝对路径，开发机上通常包含用户名。

**会出什么问题**

两层。第一层是**成本口径**：任何人按 README 做 token 核算，都会把这个包算成零开销，而它实际会往历史里追加消息，且这些消息会留在会话里被后续每一轮重发。

第二层是**数据边界**：宿主的绝对路径（含用户名，可能还有目录结构）会进入模型请求。做合规评估时，如果依据 README 判断「这个包不产生模型可见内容」，这部分就不会被计入「离开本机的数据」。

Web 出厂组合默认挂载这个包。

**把握程度**：确定。拼接 stack 的 `formatErrorDetails` 在 `:1038`、`:1061`、`:1086`、`:1111`、`:1143` 被调用，而 `steer` / `inject` 在 `:1043`、`:1056`、`:1081`、`:1107`、`:1153` —— 每一个格式化调用后面紧跟着一个注入调用，所以带 stack 的文本确实会进模型历史。我没有穷举「哪些失败路径会带上 stack」，但只要带了就会进去。

---

## 三、`subagent_fork` 在默认 Web 路径上是 `continuable`，而这抵消了 fork 唯一的收益

这一条特殊：**你们的决策记录里有两篇 implemented note 结论相反，发行的 Web 路径跟的是较早那篇。**

**较晚的** —— `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-fork-children-stay-one-shot.md`：

> Every shipped composition binds the fork delegation tool to `backgroundMode: one-shot`: the base bundle, the ACP example, and the headless example.

理由在 Problem 段：

> Both live in the request head — the system block and the tool block precede every message — so a continuable forked child invalidates reuse before the first inherited turn and re-prefills the whole transcript it was forked to reuse. That composition pays fork's duplication cost and collects none of its benefit.

**较早的** —— `.agents/notes/implemented/feature/2026-07-27-web-subagent-conversations.md:80`，状态同样是 implemented，据我所见没有被撤回或标记为被取代：

> The shipped Web composition ... configures spawn and fork background delegation as continuable.

**实际配置**：

| 位置 | 取值 |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml` fork 行 | `backgroundMode: one-shot` |
| `packages/bundle/web-app/cordis.patch.yml` | 把这一行 `disabled: true` |
| `apps/cli/config/agent-presets/standard/agent.cordis.yml:192-198` | `backgroundMode: continuable` |
| `code` / `cordis` 两个 preset | 同样 `continuable` |
| `packages/bundle/web-app/cordis.patch.yml:424` | `default: standard` |

base 的绑定是对的，但 Web bundle 禁用了那一行，preset 又以 `continuable` 加回来。`standard` 是 `dsh web` 的默认，子代理还会通过 `composeFrom` 继承父代理的 preset（`packages/subagent/subagent/src/child-agent.ts:168`），所以这是默认路径。

08-10 那篇的 Accepted risks 提前写下了这个失败模式：

> The constraint lives in three configuration files and a code comment, not in a gate. A future bundle row or profile patch can set `backgroundMode: continuable` on a fork tool and silently reintroduce the prefix loss; nothing fails loud.

**两处旁证**：

1. `scripts/gen-tool-catalog.ts:451` 有一段硬编码字符串，写进了随发行版分发的 `docs/tool-catalog.md:35`：

   > `subagent_fork` stays `one-shot` and defaults them to foreground — see `packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml` and `examples/acp-agent/cordis.yml`.

   它点名引用的两份文件恰好是配置正确的那两份，但用户实际走的 Web 路径不是它们。

2. `packages/subagent/subagent-fork-in-process/src/index.ts:77` 的 TODO 注释写着「no shipped composition calls this」——按现在的 preset 配置这句已不成立。

**会出什么问题**

用户在跑了很久的会话里用 `subagent_fork` 派子代理。fork 的整个前提是「继承父前缀所以便宜」。实际是 `report` 工具 schema 加 `tool:report` 段落（order 117）落在请求头部，继承来的整段历史全部重新预填。

我量过这个头部增量：工具 description 521 字符 + 参数 description 94 字符 + system 段落 417 字符 ≈ 258 token，加 JSON schema 结构，量级在几百 token。用这几百 token 作废掉的是几万到几十万 token 的继承历史。

用户看到的是 **`subagent_fork` 比 `subagent`（spawn）还慢还贵**，跟设计意图相反，而且几乎不可能归因到组合配置上。

还有一处连带的行为差异：按 `2026-08-11-background-first-continuable-delegation.md:15`，`continuable` 会把「省略 `run_in_background`」的默认从前台翻成后台。所以同样一句 `subagent_fork` 调用，**在 Web 和在 ACP/headless 上语义不同**。

**把握程度**：配置事实确定。但「哪一篇 note 是当前决策」我判断不了——所以这条与其说是报问题，不如说是想请你们澄清：07-27 那篇是否应标为被 08-10 取代？如果是，preset 需要跟上；如果 08-10 才是该修订的那篇，`docs/tool-catalog.md` 里那段硬编码说明需要改。

---

## 四、主动压缩的阈值公式不减去输出预留，默认配置下这套策略几乎跑不到

阈值只按输入侧算 —— `packages/compaction/compaction-basic/src/config.ts:144`：

```ts
const thresholdTokens = Math.floor(contextWindow * policy.thresholdRatio)
```

公式里没有 `max_tokens` 这一项。而 `max_tokens` 会被自动写进每个请求（`packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts:740`），且这一层明确不做 clamp。

问题在于 `contextWindow` 的语义是**请求和响应合计** —— 你们自己的类型定义写得很清楚，`packages/llm/llm/src/types.ts:249`：

```ts
/** Maximum combined request and response context in tokens. */
contextWindow: number
```

所以真正能用于输入的上限是 `contextWindow − max_tokens`，而阈值算的是 `contextWindow × ratio`。两者比较时少了一项。

**我用真实 API 验证了这个前提。** 两次调用：

| prompt | max_tokens | 合计 | 结果 |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 690,989 | 256,000 | 946,989 | 成功 |
| 819,989 | 256,000 | 1,075,989 | **被拒** |

拒绝时的原文：

> This model's maximum context length is 1048576 tokens. However, you requested 1075989 tokens (819989 in the messages, 256000 in the completion). Please reduce the length of the messages or completion.

两个结论：求和**确实**被强制校验；以及**真实窗口是 1,048,576，而不是你们声明的 1,000,000**（`DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW`）。

**代入出厂默认值**：

| 项 | 值 |
| --- | ---: |
| 真实窗口 | 1,048,576 |
| 默认 `max_tokens` | 256,000 |
| 实际输入上限 | **792,576** |
| 主动压缩阈值（`floor(1,000,000 × 0.8)`） | **800,000** |
| 差额 | 7,424 |

阈值比上限高 7,424 token，约占窗口的 0.7%。

**这个差额很小，所以我不敢把话说满**：token 计量用的是 4 字符/token 的启发式（`packages/llm/token-meter`），估算误差很可能大于 0.7%。所以现实中主动压缩可能偶尔触发、偶尔不触发，取决于估算误差往哪边偏——这本身就不是一个好的状态。

**真正的问题是公式，不是这 7,424**。因为 API 允许 `max_tokens` 最大到 393,216（我实测的错误信息给出了这个范围），任何把它调高的部署都会让差额急剧扩大：

| `max_tokens` | 输入上限 | 阈值 | 差额 |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 256,000（默认） | 792,576 | 800,000 | 7,424 |
| 320,000 | 728,576 | 800,000 | 71,424 |
| 393,216（API 上限） | 655,360 | 800,000 | **144,640** |

差额越大，`thresholdRatio` / `retainRatio` 这套调好的策略就越彻底地变成死代码，长会话一律走 overflow 恢复。而 `compaction-basic/README.md` 自己描述那条路径粗暴得多：

> provider-confirmed overflow needs no capacity metadata: it bypasses normal pressure and retention, prunes, then attempts one maximal balanced head reduction while leaving the newest indivisible unit.

**会出什么问题**

长会话（大重构、读了几十个文件）在某次提问后先卡一下，然后要么看到上下文超限报错，要么静默经历一次远比配置激进的削减。之后 agent 明显失忆：重读十分钟前刚读过的文件、重复问已回答过的问题。

按配置本该保留 `retainRatio: 0.16` 对应的额度，实际只保留「最新的一个不可分割单元」。丢掉的上下文后面靠重新读文件补，又是新的输入 token。

对调过 `max_tokens` 的部署来说更明显：他们调高输出预算是为了让模型能写更长的回答，副作用却是把主动压缩彻底关掉了，而这两件事在文档里没有任何地方被联系起来。

**把握程度**：公式缺一项、`contextWindow` 是合计语义、求和被强制校验、真实窗口 1,048,576 —— 这四点确定（后两点是实测）。默认配置下那 7,424 会不会被估算误差淹没，我没有实测，所以上面按「几乎跑不到」而不是「一定跑不到」来写。

**已有的相关记录**：`2026-07-30-adapter-owned-max-token-defaults.md` 承认预留很大、小上下文部署要自己调低 `maxTokens`；`llm-deepseek/README.md:42` 说适配器不会拿这个预算和 `contextWindow` 做截断。`compaction-basic/README.md` 的 Known Limitations 有五条，没有一条涉及这个。我没找到任何地方把这两件事联系起来——如果有而我漏了，麻烦指路。

顺带一提：`DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WINDOW = 1_000_000` 比真实的 1,048,576 保守，这个方向是安全的，但它让上面这笔账更难算对。

---

## 五、`headless` profile 同时发出两套重叠的编辑器工具

`.agents/notes/implemented/simplification/2026-08-10-default-presets-single-editor.md:9`：

> The `standard`, `code`, and `cordis` presets exposed both the `read`/`write`/`edit` filesystem tools and `str_replace_editor`. The two interfaces overlap for ordinary file inspection and editing, so every request carried an additional tool schema without adding a distinct default capability.

Alternatives 段：

> **Keep both editing interfaces in the general-purpose presets.** Rejected because the overlapping model-visible schemas increase tool choice without supplying a separate default operation.

修改落到了 preset 上。但 `packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:384` 仍挂载 `tool-str-replace-editor`，`web-app` 在 `:318` 关掉，而 **`headless` 既没关也不挂 preset**：

| profile | 模型看到的编辑工具 |
| --- | --- |
| `web` | `read` / `write` / `edit` / `read_image` |
| `headless` | 以上**再加** `str_replace_editor` |

`docs/tool-catalog.md` 里 `str_replace_editor` 条目是 2,907 字节的 description + schema，约 700–750 token，headless 每个请求都带一遍。

这里可能还少了一道守卫。`2026-07-31-even-out-shipped-tool-rosters.md:41` 提到过一个测试：

> `apps/cli/tests/shipped-composition.e2e.ts` booted the shipped tree through the real Loader in a pseudo-terminal and read the tool names out of the `request/header` the session log persisted

这个文件在当前 commit 下不存在了（推测是随 TUI 下线一起删的）。`apps/web/tests/shipped-composition.e2e.ts` 还在，所以工具册断言只剩 Web 一侧。

**会出什么问题**

用 `dsh --profile headless` 跑无人值守任务时，每一步输入比 Web 多约 750 token，40 步下来约 3 万 token，换来的能力按 note 自己的判断是零。

编辑行为也在两个 surface 上不一致：模型有时用 `edit`、有时用 `str_replace_editor`，两者路径要求不同（后者要绝对路径）、输出截断规则也不同。用户大概率归因成「headless 的 prompt 不一样」。

**把握程度**：配置事实确定。是否有意为之需要你们判断——那篇 note 的 Alternatives 确实否决过「从每个发行组合移除 `str_replace_editor`」，但理由覆盖的是 `minimal` preset 和「显式部署」，而 `headless` 两者都不是，它是随发行版自动初始化的通用 profile。

---

## 六、`dsh-invariants` 的 README 声称了一条代码里不存在的检查

这条没有任何运行时症状，这正是我报它的原因。

`packages/runtime-diagnostics/invariants/README.md:39` 的覆盖表列了 **inbox FIFO conservation**：

> Session enclosure and call/result trace, agent-status transitions, **inbox FIFO conservation**, scoped subjects, and model-request reconstruction.

但据我查：

- `grep -rni "conservation" packages --include=*.ts` 零命中；
- 35 个可执行 companion 里没有一个观察 inbox；
- `dsh-agent` 的 companion（`packages/core/agent/src/invariant.ts`）只检查「状态上报不是重复的空转」。

**为什么没有症状也值得报**

inbox 的 splice 记录不只是遥测。`packages/core/agent/src/consumed-work.ts:68` 的 `foldConsumedWork()` 依靠它区分「某个 turn 领走了输入」和「工作被丢弃、从未运行」；`packages/subagent/subagent/src/lifecycle.ts:236` 用这个结果判定子代理的终止原因。

也就是说，如果守恒被破坏，一个**丢掉了待办工作的子代理会被报告成 `completed`**，父代理据此继续往下走。

用户能观察到的版本：你在 agent 工作时排队发了第二条消息，如果 splice 与 claim 交错把它丢了，**agent 就是不理那句话**。没有报错、没有异常日志，多数人以为模型没注意到，再发一遍。

我更在意第二层：有人读了这份 README，在 staging 挂上 `dsh-agent` 的 companion 期待它覆盖 inbox，跑出全绿，然后得出一个这次运行根本没验证过的结论。

（`apps/cli` / `apps/web` 出厂不挂 `dsh-invariants` 这件事，`2026-08-03-omit-invariants-from-shipped-config.md` 已写明，我不当作问题。）

另一个更小的点：`packages/core/agent/src/invariant.ts` 的 `lastStatus` 是空 `WeakMap`，从不从 `agent.status` 播种，所以某个 agent 的**第一次**状态上报即使是真空转也会通过。

**把握程度**：「README 声称的这条检查在代码里不存在」确定，可机械验证。README 是写给未来的目标还是已经过时，我判断不了。

---

## 小结

| # | 问题 | 性质 | 默认路径？ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | hook 超时非正数让拦截静默失效，审计显示「通过」 | 边界 | 配置笔误即触发 |
| 2 | `cordis-host-runner` 契约与实现不符，推送宿主 stack | 数据边界 + 成本口径 | 是（Web） |
| 3 | fork 发行成 `continuable` | 成本 | 是（`dsh web`） |
| 4 | 压缩阈值公式不减输出预留 | 成本 | 是 |
| 5 | `headless` 双份编辑器 | 成本 | 是（`headless`） |
| 6 | invariants README 声称的覆盖不存在 | 文档承诺 | 无症状 |

*说明：我维护一份独立的中文源码分析，上面的统计数字来自那里。链接请见[此处](https://github.com/plwslpld-arch/deepseek-harness-internals)。*

discussions.title: [Bug] Windows: koffi 3.1.4 导致 dsh web 工具调用时服务崩溃
discussions.body:
## 环境

- **dsh**: `0.1.0-rc.6`（npm latest）
- **OS**: Windows 10 Pro 10.0.19045
- **Node**: `v22.23.2`（另测 `v24.19.0`，同样复现）
- **安装**: 官方桌面安装器（dsh 本体在 `~/.dsh/profiles`，实际代码在 npm 缓存 `_npx/1e7f6d9597241db0`）
- **koffi**: `3.1.4`（dsh-session-persistence-jsonl / dsh-sandbox-windows-acl 依赖）

## 症状

1. 会话进行中，模型调用工具（`pwsh` 等）时，工具调用挂起较久，然后报：
   > The tool call was interrupted after it was recorded, but no result was durably recorded. Its outcome is unknown...
2. 随后 **dsh web 服务进程直接消失**，浏览器会话断开。
3. 服务**空闲时完全稳定**（独立启动 17+ 分钟、内存稳定 178MB、零错误）；**一执行工具调用必崩**（5 次全部复现）。
4. 服务进程消失时：**无 WER 崩溃记录、退出码为空、stderr 无错误输出**——即进程被强制终止（TerminateProcess）。

## 已排除的因素

| 因素 | 验证方式 | 结果 |
|---|---|---|
| 第三方插件 | 清理到官方 web profile（仅 `dsh-base`+`dsh-web-app`） | 仍复现 |
| 启动器/守护层 | 移除 WPF 启动器、托盘、watchdog | 仍复现 |
| sandbox 模式 | `workspace-write` 与 `Full access` 均测试 | 仍复现 |
| Node 版本 | `v22.23.2` 与 `v24.19.0` | 均复现 |
| 上游 API / 凭据 | opencode.ai 网关 HTTP 200，key 有效 | 正常 |
| 服务空闲稳定性 | 空闲 17+ 分钟 | 稳定 |

## 根因（最小复现）

dsh 写会话日志时，通过 `dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` 的 win32 持久化路径调用
`koffi.load("kernel32.dll")` + `MoveFileExW`。**koffi 3.1.4 的 `load()` 调用必段错误**：

```js
// koffi@3.1.4 → 段错误（退出码 139 / 0xC0000005）
const koffi = require('koffi');
const kernel32 = koffi.load('kernel32.dll'); // ← 这里崩溃
```

```js
// koffi@3.1.2 → 正常（退出码 0）
const koffi = require('koffi');
const kernel32 = koffi.load('kernel32.dll'); // OK
const MoveFileExW = kernel32.func('__stdcall', 'MoveFileExW', 'int', ['str16', 'str16', 'uint']);
MoveFileExW(src, dst, 8); // 成功，返回 1
```

**结论**：`koffi 3.1.4` 的 win32 prebuilt 损坏（社区已知 "broken koffi 3.1.3/3.1.4 prebuilts, pin koffi 3.1.2"）。
任何调用 `koffi.load()` 的路径（会话持久化 `MoveFileExW`、sandbox ACL）都会使 dsh 服务进程段错误崩溃。

## 修复

**降级 koffi 到 3.1.2** 后，`koffi.load()` 正常、`MoveFileExW` 正常、dsh 工具调用不再崩溃（已端到端验证）。

## 建议给 dsh 上游

1. **dsh 依赖固定 `koffi@3.1.2`**（或 `>=3.1.5` 的修复版），避开 3.1.3/3.1.4 损坏的 prebuilt。
2. koffi 上游排查 3.1.3/3.1.4 的 win32-x64 prebuilt 段错误问题。

---
## 附：完整诊断时间线（供复现参考）

- 会话日志 `tool/call` 后服务进程同一毫秒消失，会话记录注入 `interrupted-tool-result`
- 服务退出时 `Start-Process` 读到的 `ExitCode` 为空（进程被强制终止）
- 服务崩溃后残留未清理的 powershell 孤儿子进程（工具执行中途被杀）

discussions.title: Desktop UI: agent keeps running & billing after UI freeze; stop button unresponsive; forked sessions multiply input costs
discussions.body:
# Desktop UI: agent keeps running & billing after UI freeze; stop button unresponsive; forked sessions multiply input costs

## Environment

- DSH Desktop 0.1.0 (Windows, `DeepSeek-Harness-Desktop-0.1.0-Setup.exe`)
- Host: Node v24, profile `web`, plugins: `@liustack/modlens`, `@liustack/modsearch`
- Date: 2026-08-16 (Asia/Shanghai)

## Summary

Three related issues that combined into a surprise 15 CNY (~$2) bill for a single "failed" turn, draining my balance to negative:

1. **UI freeze while the agent keeps running in the background.** The desktop UI showed the turn as stuck/failed, the Stop button did nothing - but the host actually completed all 17 steps of that turn (verified in `session.jsonl.zstd`: full `assistant/message`, `tool/call`, `tool/result` events from 18:52 to 19:12). Every step was billed normally. The user sees "failure" while the API bill keeps growing.

2. **Session forking duplicates the accumulated context.** One conversation exists as 3 sessions, each carrying the full ~370K-token history. Resuming/continuing a session appears to seed a copy rather than reuse, tripling the base context that gets re-sent (and billed) on every step.

3. **Aggressive billing defaults with no cost guardrails.** Fresh install defaults to `deepseek-v4-pro` + `reasoningEffort: max`, with no budget cap, no low-balance warning, and no visible per-turn cost. Combined with the 1M context window (no auto-compaction), each step re-sends the whole history at full input price once the prompt cache expires (after a ~12h gap, cache hit rate dropped from ~99% to 0%).

## Steps to reproduce (issue 1)

1. Have a long session (~370K tokens of context, with images attached).
2. Leave it idle for ~12 hours (prompt cache expires).
3. Send a message; while the turn is running, the UI may freeze - clicking Stop has no effect.
4. The turn continues server-side to completion; all steps are billed.

## Evidence

Session log stats (from `~/.dsh/storages/session_projcache.json`):

```
turns: 21, steps: 190, llm calls: 184
uncachedInputTokens: 5,661,001
cacheReadTokens: 32,924,928
outputTokens: 226,856
```

Official usage export for 2026-08-16 matches:

```
deepseek-v4-pro: 182 requests, 5,560,957 cache-miss input,
                 33,151,616 cache-hit input, 205,668 output -> 18.75 CNY
```

The afternoon turn (18:51-19:12, 17 steps) alone cost ~15 CNY: every step re-sent a 370K-token context at the cache-miss price because the overnight gap had expired the prompt cache, while the UI showed nothing but a stuck turn.

## Expected behavior

- Stop button reliably aborts the in-flight turn (host cancels remaining steps; no further API calls).
- UI state reflects the actual host state, or at least recovers (replay event stream) instead of showing a silent dead turn.
- Resuming a session should reuse it, not fork a copy with duplicated history.
- Cost guardrails: opt-in default to a cheaper model/effort, a budget cap, or at least a low-balance warning before a turn starts.

## Workaround (for other users hitting this)

- In `~/.dsh/settings.yaml` (and the web profile's copy) set:
  `agent-default-model: { model: deepseek-v4-flash, reasoningEffort: medium }`
- Start a new session instead of continuing an old, huge one after a long idle gap.
- If the UI freezes, don't resend the message - each resend re-bills the full context.

Happy to provide the full `session.jsonl.zstd` exports privately if needed.

discussions.title: SDD 开发大型项目过程中如何解决目标漂移的问题
discussions.body:
各位好，

过去一段时间我在通读这个仓库，在想搞明白一个 harness 是怎么被造出来的过程中，发现更有意思的事：如何维护 `.agents/notes/`。

据我所知，**这是目前公开可读的、规模最大的一个 spec-driven development 实例**。不是「我们有个 ADR 目录」那种，而是：固定的文档结构、生命周期编码在路径里、格式由脚本强制生成的最佳实践。

但是，spec 和实际发出去的东西，结果上是一致性的吗？

读 `2026-08-10-fork-children-stay-one-shot.md` 时，它的 Decision 很明确：

> Every shipped composition binds the fork delegation tool to `backgroundMode: one-shot`

而 Accepted risks 段提前写了：

> The constraint lives in three configuration files and a code comment, not in a gate. A future bundle row or profile patch can set `backgroundMode: continuable` on a fork tool and silently reintroduce the prefix loss; nothing fails loud.

在 `47f9438` 上，三个出厂 preset 都把它设成了 `continuable`，而 Web bundle 把 base 里那条正确的行禁用了——也就是说默认路径正是这篇 note 说不该发出去的组合。

**更有意思的是**：`2026-07-27-web-subagent-conversations.md:80` 是一篇更早的、状态同样是 implemented、据我所见没有被撤回的 note，它写的是相反的结论（Web 组合把 spawn 和 fork 都配成 continuable）。

所以这不是简单的「配置漂移」，而是**决策记录内部有两篇结论相反的 implemented note，而发行路径跟的是旧那篇**。

我想问的是实践层面：在一个长期实践过程中，不可避免的出现目标漂移的问题，这种问题尤其在大型项目里非常常见，请问有什么解决此类问题的“like 银弹”的方法或者最佳实践吗？不然类似的问题不可避免的会对后续上下文造成污染，相信其他人也遇到过类似的问题，请问大家的看法是什么呢？

discussions.title: DSH | dsh-vision | Global image upload + configurable vision recognition with fallback for every session
discussions.body:
> **Unofficial project, independently developed and maintained by community members.**

**Project URL:** https://github.com/ariesy/dsh-vision

**Introduction**

`dsh-vision` is a dynamic Cordis plugin for **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)** that brings vision capabilities to *every* session:

- **Global upload button 📎** — an upload button appears in the composer toolbar of every session; picking an image attaches it as a draft thumbnail to the message and saves it to the session workspace's `uploads/` folder.
- **Automatic image recognition** — images in a message are recognized by a configurable vision model; the result is injected into the model context as a text note (`[uploaded image recognized by vision model <model>]`).
- **Pick any vision model** — the settings page auto-lists all models that declare `image` input support, so you can choose your primary recognition model.
- **Fallback chain** — if the primary model fails (error or empty result), it automatically falls back to a backup model (independently toggleable).
- **Sensible default** — with no config, it auto-selects a recognition model by name priority (`vl`/`vision`/`image` match), avoiding models that don't support vision.

**How it integrates with DSH**

- **Host half** (`src/host.js`): intercepts the `llm/stream` waterfall. When a request carries image blocks, each image is recognized by the vision model (no system message — some gateways only see the image when it rides in the same user message as the question), then the image block is replaced with a text note. Recognition is protected by an `inFlight` re-entrancy guard.
- **Client half** (`src/client.js`): registers two Slots — `conversation.input.left` (the upload button) and `settings.plugins.tab` (the "Image Recognition" settings page). Client and Host communicate only via package-private JSON-RPC (`host.call`).

**Install**

It ships as a dynamic plugin (no DSH restart needed): copy `src/host.js` and `src/client.js` as `code.host` / `code.client` when defining a dynamic plugin, run it, approve it, and refresh the page. A standard Cordis plugin packaging path is also documented in the README.

**Screenshots**

Running inside DeepSeek Harness — the 📎 upload button in the composer toolbar and the running `dsh-vision` plugin:

[DSH UI with dsh-vision running — the 📎 upload button in the composer toolbar and the running plugin:]

![dsh-vision screenshot](data:image/jpeg;base64,)


Plugin repo carries the `dsh-plugin` topic for discoverability: https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin

*Ranking here is purely by community upvotes; this is a third-party project, please evaluate carefully before using.*

discussions.title: [Bug Report] Win32 folder picker truncates paths at U+XX00 characters (e.g. 言)
discussions.body:
## Summary

On Windows, the native workspace directory picker returns a **truncated path** whenever the selected path contains a character whose UTF-16 low byte is `0x00` (any code point `U+XX00`), such as 言 (U+8A00) or 一 (U+4E00). This makes `workspace create` fail with `workspace-invalid-path: ENOENT`.

## Reproduction

1. Create a folder named `D:\高级程序语言`.
2. In the web GUI, click **Add workspace…** and select that folder with the native picker.
3. The picker returns `D:\高级程序语` (the trailing 言 is dropped).
4. Workspace creation fails:

```
workspace create failed: workspace-invalid-path: cannot create a workspace at "D:\高级程序语": ENOENT: no such file or directory, realpath 'D:\高级程序语'
```

ASCII digits and letters are unaffected because their low bytes are never `0x00`, which matches the reported symptom that digits are not truncated while CJK paths are.

## Root cause

`readUtf16` in `packages/host/directory-picker-native` (compiled to `lib/worker.cjs`) scans for the UTF-16 NUL terminator with:

```js
while (end + 1 < bytes.length && bytes[end] !== 0) end += 2;
```

This inspects only the **low byte** of each 16-bit code unit. A character whose code point is a multiple of `0x100` has a low byte of `0x00`:

| char | code point | UTF-16LE bytes |
|------|-----------|----------------|
| 语   | U+8BED    | `ED 8B`        |
| 言   | U+8A00    | `00 8A`        |

So 言 is mistaken for the terminator and the string is cut right before it.

## Fix

Check the full 16-bit zero instead of only the low byte:

```js
while (end + 1 < bytes.length && (bytes[end] !== 0 || bytes[end + 1] !== 0)) end += 2;
```

(or equivalently `bytes.readUInt16LE(end) !== 0`).

## Environment

- Package: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-directory-picker-native@0.1.0-rc.6`
- Source directory: `packages/host/directory-picker-native`
- OS: Windows
