discussions.title: agent-team persistence test asserts a timing-dependent sendMessage receipt status, failing under full-suite load
discussions.body:
`packages/experimental/agent-team/tests/persistence.spec.ts` pins a wakeup `sendMessage` receipt to `accepted` twice, at lines 215 and 313. That status is timing-dependent by design, so under full-suite load the test observes `queued` and fails a run in which nothing is actually wrong.

Seen on a Windows runner under full-suite parallelism:

```
FAIL  packages/experimental/agent-team/tests/persistence.spec.ts
  > reconciles a persisted child to active and a missing child to durable failed
AssertionError: expected 'queued' to be 'accepted'
```

## Why the status is not deterministic

For a `delivery: 'wakeup'` message to a live target, `dispatchOnce` calls `subagents.followup` and then `checkpointDelivered`, which flushes the target session and returns false when the followup is **not recorded yet**:

```ts
private async checkpointDelivered(root, target, messageId): Promise<boolean> {
  await this.ctx.sessions.flush(target)
  if (!this.targetRecorded(target, messageId)) return false   // -> 'queued'
  await this.markDelivered(root, messageId, target.id)
  return true
}
```

That false becomes `status: 'queued'`. It reports which side of a flush the observation landed on, not whether the message arrives — and the message is delivered either way, which the `vi.waitFor` calls immediately below the assertion already assert.

## One wrong turn worth flagging

The obvious reading is that the assertion is missing a `vi.waitFor`, like every neighbouring one. It is not: the receipt is a `readonly` value from an already-awaited call, so there is nothing left to wait on. Adding a wait there would be a no-op that looks like a fix.

## How it was isolated, without a reproduction

Fifteen consecutive isolated runs of the file all passed 10/10, so reproducing it standalone is not practical — it needs full-suite contention.

What worked instead: `dispatchOnce` has four `return false` sites, and three of them log a distinct warning (`cannot inspect Team message target`, `remains queued`, and the quiet-delivery path, which a wakeup cannot take). **None of those warnings appear anywhere in the failing log**, which leaves the one silent return in `checkpointDelivered` by elimination.

## Suggested fix

Accept both correct outcomes, and let the existing waits assert the invariant that matters:

```ts
expect(['accepted', 'queued']).toContain(receipt.status)
```

Applied at both sites in a fork at `eeced691d7`; the file has passed since. Happy to send it as a PR if useful.

discussions.title: DSH_SNAPSHOT=refresh rewrites unchanged fixtures because goldens embed raw session UUIDs
discussions.body:
`DSH_SNAPSHOT=refresh` rewrites snapshot goldens whose meaning has not changed, because the fixtures embed raw session UUIDs and every refresh bakes in fresh random ones. The result is a diff of pure noise that hides real changes.

Measured twice on the same corpus: **10 of 20 changed files** on one refresh, then **15 of 19** on the next. In both cases the great majority were re-baked ids.

The cost is not the churn itself, it is what the churn conceals: a genuine fixture change and a re-baked id look identical in review, so a refresh diff cannot be read.

## Cause

`defineAcpSnapshotSuite` compares a freshly produced fixture against the existing one and writes whenever they differ. The comparison is on raw text, so two fixtures that differ only in embedded session ids compare unequal and the file is rewritten.

`normalizeSessionLog` already tokenizes ids in the paths it knows about, but ids also appear embedded inside message payloads, where it does not reach.

## Fix that worked

Mask embedded ids for the purpose of the *comparison only* — the fixture written is still the real one:

```ts
const EMBEDDED_UUID_RE = /[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}/gi

function maskVolatileIds(fixture: string): string {
  return fixture.replace(EMBEDDED_UUID_RE, '{{id}}')
}
```

and in the write loop:

```ts
if (REFRESHING && existingFixture !== ''
  && maskVolatileIds(fixture) === maskVolatileIds(existingFixture)) return
```

One detail that cost time: masking must be applied to *both* sides. `normalizeSessionLog` also tokenizes the cwd, so masking only the new fixture makes `suite.spec.ts` fail with `expected '…' to contain '"cwd":"{{cwd}}"'`.

## What it buys, beyond a quieter diff

After the change, a full refresh on our runner changed **5 files, all churn and none real** — and those five come from `examples/headless-agent`, which writes its fixtures through its own snapshot files rather than `defineAcpSnapshotSuite`, so the conditional write never applies to them.

That number is the point. It means the statement "there is no hidden fixture drift in the corpus" can be made and checked. Before, with 15-20 files changing per refresh and three-quarters of it noise, no such claim was possible.

Applied in a fork at `a2a5f64c1c`. Happy to send it as a PR, including the headless-agent sites if wanted — those need the same conditional at six places across three files whose shapes differ, which is why they were left alone.

discussions.title: dsh-lsp-actions: LSP action surface for DeepSeek Harness (diagnostics, formatting, code actions, rename over real language servers)
discussions.body:
`dsh-lsp-actions` gives a DeepSeek Harness agent the feedback loop it needs while it writes and fixes code: eight `lsp_*` tools — diagnostics, formatting, completion, code actions, symbols, signature help, inlay hints, and rename — all served by the same language servers your IDE uses (official `ctx.lsp` seam first, with a built-in stdio client fallback). It also ships a stable editor action protocol (`lsp.actions.list` / `lsp.actions.run` / `lsp.events`) so editors like VS Code can consume those capabilities directly — the IDE integration backend.

**What problem it solves:** the official `ctx.lsp` seam covers navigation (go-to-definition, references, hover), but an agent that actually writes and fixes code also needs diagnostics, formatting, quickfixes, and rename. This plugin completes that action surface, with writes riding the official `fs/write-intent` waterfall and sandbox policy.

- Read-only by default: only `lsp_format` and `lsp_rename` write.
- No network; subprocess + filesystem only.
- Real-server verification: a real `typescript-language-server` run is part of the test suite (CI on Node 22/24 across Linux, Windows, macOS).

```sh
# from npm (published release, 0.3.4)
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-lsp-actions
# or latest main
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:PerryLink/dsh-lsp-actions#main"

discussions.title: [Plugin / 插件] dsh-composer-history — Terminal-style composer input history / 终端风格输入历史
discussions.body:
## 中文

大家好，我做了一个 Web 作曲器输入层插件 [`dsh-composer-history`](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-composer-history)：把终端的输入历史体验搬进 DeepSeek Harness 的 Web 输入框，并加入了跨会话的智能输入能力。

它解决的是 Web 输入框里的几件日常痛点：半输入的草稿被历史覆盖、找不到之前发过的指令、压缩（compaction）后上下文信息消失。这些都由浏览器本地接管——纯 UI 行为，不产生会话事件、不改 agent-loop、不发模型请求，召回的文字只有在你按 Enter 后才会进入对话。

功能：

- **边缘优先方向键召回**：裸 ↑/↓ 先移动光标，仅当光标位于首/末行时才触发历史召回；首次召回暂存 `{draft, caret}`，回到最新一条（或按 Esc）时精确还原，半截草稿永不丢失；
- **本地持久化历史**：每条已发送指令追加到有界的浏览器本地存储，刷新页面、跨会话都还在；
- **Ctrl+R 反向搜索**：在合并的历史、片段与模板上打开查询浮层；
- **智能输入层**：`/save`/`/load` 跨会话片段、带 `{{workspace}}`/`{{session}}`/`{{draft}}` 变量的提示模板、浏览器本地复用洞察；
- **滑动上下文感知**：压缩摘要以 `[compacted] …` 条目加入召回与搜索，压缩发生时弹一次性提示并可一键 `/compact` 填充。

安装：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-composer-history
```

- 源码与文档：https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-composer-history
- npm：https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-composer-history
- 当前版本：`0.5.3`，对齐 dsh `0.1.1-rc.2`
- License：Apache-2.0

---

## English

Hi! [`dsh-composer-history`](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-composer-history) brings terminal-style input history into the DeepSeek Harness Web composer, plus a smart cross-session input layer.

- **Edge-first arrow recall** — bare ↑/↓ move the caret first; recall triggers only at the first/last line. The first recall stashes `{draft, caret}` and reaching the newest entry (or `Esc`) restores both exactly.
- **Persisted history** — every sent message lands in a bounded browser-local store that survives reloads and reaches across sessions.
- **Reverse search** — `Ctrl+R` opens a query overlay over merged history, snippets, and templates.
- **Smart input layer** — `/save`/`/load` snippets, prompt templates with `{{workspace}}`/`{{session}}`/`{{draft}}` variables, and browser-local reuse insights.
- **Sliding-context aware** — compaction summaries join recall/search as `[compacted] …` entries, and a transient notice announces each compaction with a one-click `/compact` fill.

Pure UI behavior: no session events, no agent-loop changes, no model requests — recalled text only enters the composer draft.

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-composer-history
```

- Source and docs: https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-composer-history
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-composer-history
- Current release: `0.5.3`, aligned with dsh `0.1.1-rc.2`
- License: Apache-2.0

discussions.title: Draft Budget — see what your draft costs before you send it (`dsh-client-draft-budget`)
discussions.body:
Know before you send: how many tokens that half-written prompt will cost, and how much of your context window it's about to eat.

**Why:** The ContextMeter ring shows current occupancy, but nothing warns you that the draft you're typing will push the session to 90% — or blow past the window entirely. I checked the ecosystem (awesome list + this thread): usage dashboards are plentiful, but nothing does pre-send draft budgeting — so this fills the gap.

**What it does:**
- A tiny readout in the composer dock, right next to the stats line: `~1.2K tok · after send ~43%`
- The draft estimate mirrors the exact formula the built-in meter applies to a plain-text message — the number you see is the number the meter will charge when you hit send, not an invented approximation
- The after-send percentage is anchored to provider-reported usage (the same baseline ContextMeter uses); the heuristic only covers the draft's own increment
- Updates live as you type (250ms debounce) and disappears when the draft is empty; zero clicks, zero config, zero upstream changes — one slot entry plus public projections, nothing else

**Known limits (MVP):** every number carries a `~` — the app's own estimation is a character heuristic (roughly 4 chars/token plus overhead), which can diverge substantially from provider-reported usage, especially on CJK and JSON-heavy text (see #3514). Slash-command claims, @-mention chips, queued rows, and image attachments aren't counted — actual cost on send is ≥ what you see. The percentage mode needs the adapter to report a context window; without it you get tokens only.

**Where:** part of my fork-maintained plugin set → https://github.com/a137460387/deepseek-harness/tree/master/packages/extensions/draft-budget. Feedback welcome — especially on what else you'd want counted before you hit send.

Note: no demo GIF for now - the source tree linked above contains the implementation and usage notes.

discussions.body:
Postmortem 0003 (`docs/postmortem/0003-web-agent-gui-feedback-loop.md`, "Guardrails added") states that the Web launcher publishes both `$DSH_WEB_URL` and `$DSH_WEB_MODE`, and that the `app:web-surface` prompt section carries the actual production/development mode. In the current tree only `DSH_WEB_URL` is registered (`packages/bundle/web-app/src/index.ts`), and the surface prompt is a single static text with the client-plugin HMR receiver always mounted. `DSH_WEB_MODE` appears nowhere in source, only in comments:

```
$ grep -rn "DSH_WEB_MODE" packages apps
packages/bundle/web-app/cordis.patch.yml:309
apps/cli/config/agent-presets/code/agent.cordis.yml:45
apps/cli/config/agent-presets/standard/agent.cordis.yml:38
apps/cli/config/agent-presets/cordis/agent.cordis.yml:39
```

Separately, those four YAML comments say `apps/cli/src/web.ts` injects `shell-env` to publish these variables; that file no longer exists. The registration now lives in `packages/bundle/web-app/src/index.ts`.

If the mode distinction was deliberately simplified away (an always-active HMR receiver would make it moot), the four comments and the postmortem's guardrail claims may want a follow-up note so they match the current tree.

Found while reading the postmortems; happy to provide more detail if useful.

discussions.title: dsh-translate: vendor parameter translation + deterministic JSON repair for DeepSeek Harness
discussions.body:
Hi! I'm maintaining **dsh-translate**, an unofficial community plugin for DeepSeek Harness that translates vendor LLM parameters and deterministically repairs broken JSON tool output.

Repository: https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-translate
npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-translate

> This is a community-maintained plugin and is not an official DeepSeek or DeepSeek Harness component.

## What it does

Two independent surfaces, one bundle:

- **`/translate`** — a vendor parameter translation table: `temperature`, `top_p`, `max_tokens`, `stop`, `system`, and 8 more canonical parameters mapped across **11 vendors** (OpenAI, ERNIE, Qwen, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, Mistral, Cohere, xAI, Groq, Azure). Ask for a pairwise mapping, list vendors/params, or convert a whole standard request.
- **The repair layer** — a `tools/post-execute` listener plus the `fix_json` tool. When a successful tool result carries broken JSON as a string, it repairs deterministically: markdown-fence extraction, escape repair, trailing-comma removal, truncation closure, and required-field completion with explicit `null` placeholders. No value is ever invented — a result that still violates the schema fails closed, and failed tool results are never flipped into successes.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:PerryLink/dsh-translate#main"
# or from npm
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-translate
```

## Community listing

- awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin: https://github.com/awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin/pull/1783
- Already listed in AdamPlatin123/awesome-dsh-plugins and 0xsline/awesome-deepseek-harness.

discussions.title: dsh 升级 0.1.1-rc.2 后 web 打不开（127.0.0.1 拒绝连接）
discussions.body:
# [Bug Report] dsh 升级 0.1.1-rc.2 后 web 打不开（127.0.0.1 拒绝连接）

> 状态：🟢 已解决（pnpm hoisted 完整重装 + dsh 自愈机制重建 profiles/node_modules）

## 环境

- **工具/项目**: dsh（DeepSeek Harness）
- **版本**: `0.1.1-rc.2`（从 `0.1.0-rc.6` 手动升级）
- **OS**: Windows 10 Pro 10.0.19045
- **运行时**: Node `v22.23.2`
- **安装方式**: 手动升级（pnpm），dsh 本体在 `C:\Users\1\.dsh\profiles\node_modules\@deepseek-ai\dsh`
- **关键依赖**: pnpm `11.22.0`、koffi `3.1.6`

## 问题是什么

升级到 0.1.1-rc.2 后，浏览器访问 `http://127.0.0.1:3080` 报「127.0.0.1 拒绝了我们的连接请求」。
`dsh-web-ctl.ps1 start` 显示 `3080 监听=False`，dsh web 服务进程启动即退出。

## 怎么发现的（症状 + 复现）

1. 复现步骤：
   - 打开浏览器访问 dsh web（127.0.0.1:3080）→ 连接被拒
   - 用控制器 `dsh-web-ctl.ps1 -Action start` 反复启动 → `3080 监听=False`
2. 实际表现（错误日志 `storages/dsh-web-*.err.log`）：
   ```
   Error: dsh: plugin tree failed to load: loader entries failed to apply
   AggregateError: loader entries failed to apply
   Error: failed to import loader entry timer (@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-timer):
     Cannot find package '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-timer'
   ...（大量 @deepseek-ai/* 包：dsh-client-ui-message-feedback、dsh-base、
       dsh-web-app、dsh-agent、dsh-session 等 100+ 个全部 ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND）
   ```

## 已排除的因素

| 因素 | 验证方式 | 结果 |
|---|---|---|
| 端口占用 | `netstat -ano | grep 3080` | 无残留进程，端口空闲 |
| 配置损坏 | 对比 `_backup` 里升级前备份的 settings / cordis.patch / package.json | 配置本身正常 |
| store 包缺失 | `pnpm store/v11/links/@deepseek-ai/` 下 197 个包均在 | 正常（store 完整） |

## 根因

升级时 `profiles/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/` 被重建成了**隔离布局的 symlink 混搭**，
指向了三处不同来源：
- 60 个 symlink → pnpm store 里 dsh 主包的**依赖子集**（只有 dsh 直接依赖的 60 个包）
- 137 个 symlink → `pnpm-cache/dlx/` **临时目录**
- 5 个 symlink → 旧 npx 缓存 `_npx/1e7f6d9597241db0`

Node 解析 `@deepseek-ai/*` 时**跟随 symlink 落到 store 的隔离位置**，在那个位置向上
查找兄弟包时看不到完整插件集 → `cordis-plugin-loader` 加载所有 bundle 插件失败 →
插件树加载失败 → 服务进程退出 → 3080 无监听。

对比：升级前（8-16）`profiles/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/` 是 **195 个实体包**
（hoisted 平铺），所有兄弟包同层互见，所以正常。

关键机制（0.1.1-rc.2 新行为）：dsh 启动时 `healProfilesModuleFallback`
（`@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot/lib/index.js`）会**自动维护** `profiles/node_modules`——
按安装锚点（dsh 主包 package.json 所在目录）的依赖闭包 BFS，为每个包创建 **symlink**
指向其真实位置。**要求 `profiles/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh` 必须是 symlink**，
若是实体目录会报 `exists and is not a symlink; remove it so dsh can manage the installation fallback`。

## 解决方案

按 0.1.1-rc.2 的自愈机制修复，而不是手工复制实体目录：

1. 新建干净安装目录 `C:\Users\1\.dsh\install\dsh-0.1.1-rc.2`，
   `package.json` 依赖 `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.1-rc.2`，`pnpm-workspace.yaml` 设
   `nodeLinker: hoisted`，执行 `pnpm install --offline`（复用 store，秒装，koffi 3.1.6 正常）。
2. 删除损坏的 `profiles/node_modules`（损坏版已备份到
   `storages/profiles-node_modules-broken-20260823`，验证后清理）。
3. 运行 `node <安装目录>/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh/lib/bin.js --profile web --dump-config`
   触发 heal → 自动重建 `profiles/node_modules` 为指向该安装锚点的 symlink 集合
   （197 个 @deepseek-ai 包全部指向 `install/dsh-0.1.1-rc.2`）。
4. `dsh-web-ctl.ps1 -Action start` 正式启动。

## 验证

- `dsh-web-ctl.ps1 -Action start` → `3080 监听=True`，`netstat` 确认端口 LISTENING
- `curl http://127.0.0.1:3080/` → HTTP 200，页面标题 `DeepSeek Harness`
- 插件正常加载（日志出现 dsh-cost-meter / dsh-file-upload / GitHub MCP session connected）
- koffi 3.1.6 `koffi.load('kernel32.dll')` 无段错误

## 备注（教训）

- **不要手工复制实体目录覆盖 `profiles/node_modules`**——0.1.1-rc.2 由 heal 全权管理它，
  要求 dsh 是 symlink 而非实体。
- `profiles/node_modules` 的 symlink 应统一指向**一个完整安装锚点**
  （当前为 `C:\Users\1\.dsh\install\dsh-0.1.1-rc.2`），不要混指 store / dlx / npx 多处。
- 完整安装锚点不可删除，否则 dsh 会再次失效；更新 dsh 时在新目录重装并触发 heal 即可。
- 若上游有类似「升级后 web 拒连 / ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND」的 issue，可关联此文档。

discussions.title: dsh-test-drive — isolated install/smoke test drives for DSH plugins（隔离安装与冒烟实测驱动）
discussions.body:
## dsh-test-drive：给 DSH 插件做隔离的安装 + 冒烟实测

一个**批量验证 DSH 插件能否真正装得上、跑得起来**的测试驱动：把仓库或 npm 包安装进一次性 DSH_HOME 配置，校验 bundle patch 层与启动日志，输出结构化通过/失败矩阵（JSON/Markdown）供评分管线消费，并隔离清理所有自有临时目录。

- 📦 npm：https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-test-drive （0.2.3）
- 🐙 GitHub：https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-test-drive （开源，Apache-2.0，已打 `dsh-plugin` topic）

### 解决什么问题

插件榜单、市场与评分管线需要一个**可复现、不污染真实配置**的安装/冒烟验证手段。dsh-test-drive 把「装进临时 profile → 校验 patch 层 → 读启动日志 → 卸载 → 清理」做成结构化流程，输出机器可读的 `dsh-test-drive/v1` 结果矩阵，供雷达/评分/CI 直接消费。

### 安装

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-test-drive
```

装完重启 `dsh web` 即可；headless 或自定义 profile 把 `web` 换成对应 profile 名。

### 实测

- 本机 DSH 0.1.1-rc.2：`dsh plugin --profile headless add dsh-test-drive` 安装成功（+34 包），随后 `dsh --profile headless "hi"` 正常启动应答，无 plugin tree 加载错误。
- 已声明完整 `dsh.bundle.patch`（指向根 `cordis.patch.yml`），并携带 `dshWorkshop`（`omdsh-workshop-package/v1`）manifest。

### 已提交的生态收录

- AdamPlatin123/awesome-dsh-plugins：https://github.com/AdamPlatin123/awesome-dsh-plugins/pull/280
- awesome-dsh-plugin/awesome-dsh-plugin、0xsline/awesome-deepseek-harness：已收录

有任何问题欢迎回帖或提 issue。

---

**TL;DR (English):** `dsh-test-drive` is an isolated install-and-smoke test driver for DSH plugins — it installs a repo or npm package into a throwaway `DSH_HOME` profile, verifies the bundle patch layer and boot logs, emits a structured `dsh-test-drive/v1` pass/fail matrix (JSON/Markdown) for scoring pipelines, and quarantines every temp directory it owns. Install: `dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-test-drive`. Repo: https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-test-drive

discussions.title: failOnStartupError: false cannot cover a config validation failure, but its name and default promise it does
discussions.body:
`failOnStartupError` defaults to `false` and its name promises that a bad MCP entry degrades to "that server is unavailable". It does not cover a config **validation** failure, and the default makes that promise to every host that never sets it.

`boot()` sets `stage = 'plugin tree failed to load'` and calls `mountRootInclude`; any throw lands in the catch, disposes the whole context and rethrows. Validation of an entry's config happens *before* that entry activates, so `failOnStartupError` never gets a chance to apply — it governs a server that fails to **start**, not an entry that fails to **parse**.

For an embedding host the result is all-or-nothing: one malformed optional entry and the harness is gone. In the case that prompted this, an unset environment variable in one MCP server's `env` produced a dead harness with no listener rather than a harness missing one tool.

## Being fair to the design

An all-or-nothing mount is defensible, and the code is explicit that it is transactional — the comments around the mount reason clearly about a partially mounted tree being ambiguous. The problem is narrower than "make it lenient": the flag's name and default describe behaviour the flag cannot deliver.

## Three options, in the order the reporting consumer preferred them

1. **Make the flag cover the whole entry lifecycle**, validation included: a `failOnStartupError: false` entry that fails to parse is skipped with a loud warning and the rest of the tree mounts. This is what the name already describes.
2. **Keep validation fatal but say so** — document that the flag applies only after a valid entry begins starting, and that a config error is unconditionally fatal. Cheapest honest option; a host then guards its own input knowingly rather than by accident.
3. **Give the host a boundary** — let a config-tree layer be marked non-essential, so a host can declare which plugins are load-bearing. For the consumer here the MCP servers, a vision bridge and a skin are all optional; the client UI is not.

We took option 2 in a fork, documenting the boundary on both config interfaces rather than changing behaviour, because making validation non-fatal per entry means making the transactional mount partial and that is a design decision rather than a fix.

Option 3 is the one that actually fits the problem, and it is why this is filed here rather than carried as a patch: it is a design proposal, not something a fork should invent.

discussions.title: dsh web announces readiness on success and stays silent on failure, so a host cannot tell failed from still-loading
sandbox-windows-acl gates on resolvePwshPath but launches literal pwsh, so escape-regression tests silently never run
discussions.body:
`packages/sandbox/sandbox-windows-acl/tests/runner.spec.ts` gates on `resolvePwshPath()` but launches the literal `pwsh`. Those are not the same shell: `resolvePwshPath()` falls back to Windows PowerShell 5.1, so on a host with no pwsh 7 the gate passes and the launch then fails — and the **escape-regression** tests never execute.

That is the failure mode worth caring about. The suite reports success; the tests that would catch a sandbox escape simply did not run.

## Fix

Gate and launch through the same resolved path, so the tests either run against the shell that was found or skip visibly. Applied in a fork at `fd345a1a2c`.

Worth checking whether upstream CI is exercising these at all — if the Windows lane there also lacks pwsh 7, the escape-regression coverage has been silently absent rather than passing.

discussions.title: Hook bridge suites mount LocalBashExecutor unconditionally, testing a shell no Windows host runs hooks through
discussions.body:
The hook bridge suites (`hooks-claude-code`, `hooks-codex`) mount `LocalBashExecutor` unconditionally. On Windows that tests a shell no host runs hooks through, and it addresses hook scripts by a path that `bash -c` destroys.

So on Windows the suites are testing a configuration that does not exist in production, and failing for reasons that say nothing about the bridge.

## Fix

Select the executor for the host rather than assuming bash, and address hook scripts in a form the chosen shell preserves. Applied in a fork at `4f05ad8b12`.

The general shape: a test that hard-codes one shell is fine while one platform is supported, and becomes a false signal the moment a second is. These suites are worth a look on any Windows lane upstream runs.

discussions.title: dsh-claude-move：四源迁移向导 —— Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode / Hermes 会话一键迁入 DSH（可续聊）

大家好，我发布了 `dsh-claude-move`（npm 0.2.7）：一个四源迁移向导，把 Claude Code、Codex、OpenCode、Hermes 的历史会话、记忆、技能、指令与斜杠命令迁入 DeepSeek Harness，作为可续聊的 DSH 会话（复制式、审批门控、幂等）。

```

discussions.title: No testTimeout is configured, so Windows inherits a POSIX-calibrated 5s default that measures contention
discussions.body:
No `testTimeout` is configured anywhere, so every lane inherits vitest's 5s default. That number is POSIX-calibrated, and on Windows it measures **contention rather than correctness**.

Measured on a Windows runner: a full run failed **30 tests across 13 files**, and every one of those files passed when run alone. Windows pays hundreds of milliseconds to start each process — Windows PowerShell 5.1 alone is expensive — and this suite runs many spawn-heavy files in parallel.

Raising the deadline to 30s left 2 failures; 60s left 3. Past roughly 30s there is no threshold to find, only residual flake that shuffles between runs — so 30s is the knee, and a larger value would only make a genuine hang cost more.

## Fix

A per-platform deadline: 30s on Windows, vitest's 5s default retained on POSIX so CI keeps a fast failure signal, with an env override for host tuning. Applied in a fork at `411dfd772a`.

## One thing that bit us afterwards, worth knowing before adopting this

A raised default only reaches tests that do not override it. One `describe`-level `{ timeout: 15_000 }` sat **below** the new Windows figure, so it did not raise that lane — it halved it, in a file whose tests drive real `git` and `node` processes and take ~4s each with the machine idle. It surfaced as a single timeout in a full run that CI had passed on the same commit.

If you take the per-platform deadline, grep for `{ timeout:` at the same time. Every such literal is part of the change.

discussions.title: Windows DSH_SNAPSHOT=refresh writes literal cwd paths: the JSON-escaped spelling is not tokenized
discussions.body:
A Windows `DSH_SNAPSHOT=refresh` regenerates web fixtures carrying the literal workspace path where the goldens carry `{{cwd}}`, so the refresh cannot be run from a Windows host without producing a diff full of machine-specific paths.

## Cause

The serialized log is JSON, so on Windows the cwd appears **twice in different spellings**: the plain form, and its escaped double-backslash form inside JSON string values. The tokenizer matched only the plain one.

```
C:\Users\dev\project          <- tokenized
C:\Users\dev\project       <- not matched, written literally
```

On POSIX the two spellings coincide, which is why this is invisible there.

## Fix

Tokenize both spellings in the web scaffold. Applied in a fork at `92615b9e84`.

Worth noting the original diagnosis here was too broad — "refresh cannot be run from Windows" sounded like a platform limitation and it was one missing escape spelling.

discussions.title: A vitest worker dies mid-run: every test passes, the job fails, and the totals do not add up
discussions.body:
A vitest worker process dies mid-run and the job fails while **every test passes**. Reported here without a fix, because the mechanism has resisted 20 reproduction attempts and more eyes may recognise it.

## Recognising it

There is no `FAIL` line, because no test failed:

```
 Test Files  830 passed | 5 skipped (836)
      Tests  13988 passed | 64 skipped (14081)
     Errors  1 error
```

Read the **totals**: 830 + 5 is 835 against 836, and 13988 + 64 is 14052 against 14081. A file and its remaining tests are missing. Collection runs before execution, so the totals still count tests that never ran, and a file whose worker dies produces no result line at all — it leaves the reported list rather than appearing as a failure.

## What is established

**It is a termination, not a thrown error.** A worker hard-killed with `SIGKILL` reproduces the log exactly — `Worker exited unexpectedly`, vitest-internal frames, no message. A worker dying from an uncaught exception produces the same passing-looking summary but **its message appears**; worker stderr is not swallowed. The failing logs carry no message of any kind.

`process.exit()` does not reproduce it — vitest intercepts that and turns it into an ordinary test failure.

**The same file is lost every time**, three occurrences on a Windows runner: `packages/workflow/workflow-worker-thread/tests/workflow-worker-thread.spec.ts`. The third was caught with per-spec tracing, so it was established by comparing files that started against files that finished within one run rather than by diffing against a control.

That file is also the slowest in the suite (~40s), which is a genuine confound: it is where a worker most often *is*, so "the same file three times" is weaker evidence than it looks.

## What is ruled out

- The spec's own `worker death` tests, which raise an uncaught exception on purpose — that would have printed.
- V8 heap exhaustion — a heap OOM prints `FATAL ERROR: ... JavaScript heap out of memory`, which by the probe above would have survived.

## Reproduction: 0 for 20

Twelve runs of the file alone, four of those with the box saturated; three forcing it into one worker with the FFI-loading specs; five full local suites, one capped to the runner's core count. Nothing. It has only ever appeared on the Windows runner.

One thing that looked promising and is not: constraining `--maxWorkers` does **not** increase worker reuse. At `maxWorkers=8` the suite took 40% longer and the worker count went *up* (666 to 686) — concurrency and reuse are independent.

## If anyone wants to dig

A worker-identity trace costs one line in a setup file and turns this from inference into a reading. Two notes if you try it: write with `writeSync(2, ...)` because vitest intercepts console output from a setup file and drops it, and do not use the pid as the identity — Windows recycles pids fast enough that one run used 508 distinct pids for 837 files. `VITEST_POOL_ID`/`VITEST_WORKER_ID` do not recycle.

discussions.title: dsh-pi-agent: run the Pi coding agent loop inside DSH (web frontend unchanged)
discussions.body:
# Third-party integration showcase: run the Pi coding agent loop inside DSH (dsh-pi-agent)

## Summary

[dsh-pi-agent](https://github.com/Micheleww/dsh-pi-agent) is a community plugin that drives DSH sessions with the [Pi coding agent](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) loop (`pi --mode rpc` child process) instead of `dsh-agent-loop`, while keeping the web frontend, session persistence, and hooks unchanged. The subagent engine can also be swapped to Pi independently via a custom `SubagentProvider` (mirroring the shipped claude-code/codex bridges).

## Motivation

Two reasons this is interesting beyond the plugin itself:

1. **Engine choice as config.** The plugin validates that the `AgentFactory` slot and the `SubagentProvider` registry are clean, independent seams: main loop and delegation engine are separately switchable rows in `cordis.patch.yml` (pi main + native subs, native main + pi subs, or both).
2. **Clean A/B surface.** Same frontend, same session format, one config row to flip — it gives a reproducible comparison between DSH's native loop (prompt assembly, tools, guard plugins) and a minimal external loop on identical tasks.

## How the seams are used

- `ctx.agents.setFactory()` with an `AgentFactory` that spawns `pi --mode rpc --no-session`, translates Pi's RPC event stream into DSH durable session events (`turn/*`, `step/*`, `assistant/chunk`, `tool/call`, `tool/result`), and maps `send(next-turn|next-step)` to Pi's `steer`.
- A `SubagentProvider` (registered on `ctx.subagents`) where each accepted run spawns `pi -p <task>` in the delegating session's cwd — one-shot, out-of-process, `inheritsParentContext: false`.
- No prompt or tool injection in either seam: the Pi child owns its own context entirely.

Verified end-to-end against 0.1.1-rc: session create/resume, streaming turns, steering, subagent delegation (three consecutive delegations returning correct results), and native↔pi fallback.

## Question for the team

Is there (or will there be) a place in the docs/website to list community plugins like this? Happy to contribute a short ecosystem page entry if useful — the seam design (`agent-presets`, provider registry) deserves more examples, and this one is small (~900 lines) and reads as a reference implementation of the factory/provider contracts.

discussions.title: [Bug] spawn 子代理路由两源拼接：provider 继承父会话、model 落全局默认，多 provider 下产生非法组合（UNKNOWN_MODEL）
discussions.body:
spawn 子代理路由两源拼接：provider 继承父会话、model 落全局默认，多 provider 下产生非法组合（UNKNOWN_MODEL）

环境：dsh web，多 LLM provider 配置（llm-pi-ai 多 provider + 抽屉切换）

复现步骤：

抽屉切换默认模型到非 DeepSeek 原生 provider（如 opencode-go-free / ox-alpha-free）
触发任何走 spawn 且未显式指定模型的子代理（如 auto-memory 的压缩员）
子代理 turn 立即失败：pi-ai provider "opencode-go-free" has no configured model "deepseek-v4-flash" (code=UNKNOWN_MODEL)
根因：子代理路由为两源拼接——provider 继承父会话上下文，model 落到宿主全局默认（deepseek-v4-flash）。两者来自不同来源，多 provider 下必然拼出父 provider 目录中不存在的组合。

证据：子代理会话日志 turn/end reason.kind=error, code=UNKNOWN_MODEL；同父会话本体使用 ox-alpha-free 正常。

期望行为：子代理未显式指定模型时，应整对继承父会话路由（provider+model 成对）；仅当用户显式提供完整 route 时才覆盖。

建议修复：spawn 解析处改为 pair inheritance；或至少在 UNKNOWN_MODEL 时回退父会话实际模型。

discussions.title: dsh-session-export: /transcript — human-readable session transcripts written to a host path
discussions.body:
# Third-party integration showcase: human-readable session transcripts via /transcript (dsh-session-export)

## Summary

[dsh-session-export](https://github.com/kittimzhe/dsh-session-export) is a community plugin that adds a `/transcript` command exporting a finished or running session as a human-readable transcript written directly to a host path — Markdown and/or JSON, under `<session cwd>/dsh-transcripts/`. On npm as `dsh-session-export@0.1.0` (MIT).

## Motivation

Two reasons this is interesting beyond the plugin itself:

1. **The human-command plane is a genuinely zero-token surface.** The plugin is a small worked example of the `ctx.commands` contract — registration, flag grammar, `CommandInvocation` handling, success/error results — running alongside the model plane without ever entering model history.
2. **`sessionQuery` as a backend-agnostic read seam, exercised.** Rendering goes through `ctx.sessionQuery.readSession()`/`traceSession()` only, so the same transcript code runs unchanged over any persistence backend — and has to honor the surface semantics (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-session/surface`): the transcript renders **append-origin surface events** (what the user actually saw), not the model-visible surface whose compaction replacements would erase conversation the user already read.

## What the output looks like

- Header block: session id, project, agent preset, message/tool-call/token totals, generator
- Subagent lineage tree (via `traceSession`)
- Message flow with per-assistant-message token usage and provider/model provenance
- Editor tool calls (`str_replace_editor` / `edit` / `write`) rendered as diff blocks
- `--full`: log-only events appendix (command lifecycles, compaction markers)

## Try it

```
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-session-export
# restart dsh web, then in a session:
/transcript
```

Variants: `--json`, `--full`, `--out <path>`, `--id <sessionId>`.

## How the seams are used

- `inject: ['commands', 'sessionQuery']` — nothing else touched
- Ships a `dsh.bundle` patch, so a plain `dsh plugin add` joins the profile layer stack automatically (no manual composition edits)
- Pure rendering on top of `readSession` events; no writes to session state

Verified end-to-end: npm install → auto-activation → `/transcript` in the web UI on a ~1.1M-token live session (379 messages, 199 tool calls); 32 unit tests; decode validated against real JSONL storage records (multi-frame zstd). The shipped `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-log-export` covers the raw-log browser-download case — this plugin covers the complementary deferrals its own README lists: host-path writes, any query backend, human-readable output.

## Question for the team

Is there appetite for a convention on where host-side exports should land — e.g., a shared output-directory convention under the session cwd, or a profile-level default? The plugin currently defaults to `<session cwd>/dsh-transcripts/` with `--out`/config overrides, but a standard would help ecosystem tools compose.

discussions.title: [frp 公网访问修复] 11 项兼容性补丁脚本 (Cloudflare CDN + 非安全上下文)
discussions.body:
## 问题描述

通过 frp 公网 HTTP 地址访问 DeepSeek Harness web UI 时，存在多个兼容性问题导致无法正常工作。

## 修复内容

`dsh-fix-patches.sh` 脚本包含以下 11 项修复：

1. **crypto.randomUUID polyfill** — 非安全上下文下浏览器不暴露此 API
2. **trustedHosts 通配符支持** — `trustedHosts: [\"*\"]` Host 信任检查
3. **特权方法 403 修复** — settings/agentPreset/host 等方法允许非 loopback
4. **第三方插件设置命名空间白名单扩展**
5. **dsh-ssh 插件 loopback-only 限制移除** — 非 loopback 访问 `/api/dsh-ssh/*`
6. **SSE 替换 WebSocket + 移除 426 阻塞** — Cloudflare CDN 兼容
7. **LLM stream error finish_reason 修复** — 已产出内容时改为 stop
8. **Cloudflare Rocket Loader 禁用** — `data-cfasync=false` 禁用脚本重排序
9. **SSE x-accel-buffering=no + 5s 心跳** — 防止 nginx/CF 缓冲断连
10. **host.describe 添加 home 字段** — 返回 `os.homedir()`
11. **插件 bundle cache-control 长缓存** — `max-age=31536000, immutable`

## 修复脚本

修复脚本已上传至 fork 仓库：

- [dsh-fix-patches.sh](https://github.com/ojbkxc/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-fix-patches/dsh-fix-patches.sh)（完整版，11 项修复）
- [dsh-fix-patches-run.sh](https://github.com/ojbkxc/deepseek-harness/blob/dsh-fix-patches/dsh-fix-patches-run.sh)（运行版，前 5 项修复）

## 用法

```bash
cd /opt/deepseek-harness && bash dsh-fix-patches.sh
```

脚本幂等，可安全多次执行，已应用的补丁会跳过。

## 环境

- 服务器: frp 公网 HTTP 转发
- CDN: Cloudflare
- 浏览器: 非安全上下文 (HTTP)

---

希望官方能考虑修复这些兼容性问题，使 DeepSeek Harness 能更好地支持 frp 公网访问场景。

discussions.title: web_search 工具硬编码走 DeepSeek，绕过用户当前选择的对话模型
discussions.body:
### Bug: web_search 工具硬编码走 DeepSeek，绕过用户当前选择的对话模型

**环境**：
- DSH version: 0.1.1-rc.2
- Profile: web
- 默认配置 + 用户自定义 llm-pi-ai providers（minimax-cn）

**复现步骤**：
1. 配置 `~/.dsh/settings.yaml`：`agent-default-model.provider: minimax-cn` + `model: MiniMax-M3`
2. 把 DEEPSEEK_API_KEY 填进 `.credentials.yaml`
3. 在 Web UI 里选 MiniMax-M3，对话中触发 web_search（例如："搜索 2026 年 DeepSeek 最新动态"）

**期望**：
- web_search 应该跟随当前对话模型，或至少用户能配置让它跟随 minimax provider
- 文档/UI 上明确告知 web_search 会消耗 DEEPSEEK_API_KEY

**实际**：
- 每次 web_search 调用都打到 `api.deepseek.com`，用 DEEPSEEK_API_KEY 计费
- 即使用户当前对话用的是 minimax 模型也照扣
- 用户难以发现，因为对话模型选择器和 web 搜索走的是不同的 key

**根因**（参考 dsh-base cordis.patch.yml line 404-412）：
- `web` 服务的 `searchProvider` 默认是 `deepseek-official`（硬编码）
- `web-search-deepseek` 的 `apiKeyEnv` 是 `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`（硬编码）
- `tool-web` 的 `search: true`（默认开）

**建议修复**：
- 短期：文档 + Web UI 上标注 web_search 会用 DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
- 长期：让 searchProvider 跟随 agent-default-model 或当前 selection

discussions.title: 功能建议：会话中途热更新 persona / prompt，无需重建会话
discussions.body:
问题描述
打个比方：我开着一辆车以 80 巡航，现在想提到 120，难道必须换一辆车吗？——我只是在 preset 里加了一条 prompt 规则，为什么必须重建整个会话？

当前 agent preset 是「每个会话挂载一次」，其 persona / prompt 段落在会话创建时即被冻结。当我编辑 preset 的 persona（例如追加一条事实核查规则）时，改动只对新会话生效，当前正在进行的会话仍保留旧的 persona。这导致迭代 prompt 级规则时摩擦很大：每加一条小规则，就得放弃当前会话（丢失上下文与历史）另开新会话，而实际只改了 prompt 文本。

期望的解决方案
提供一种方式，让已运行会话能应用 persona / prompt 段落的改动，且不丢失该会话的上下文。具体可以是：

一个命令，如 /reload-persona（或 /reload-preset），把更新后的 prompt 段落重新注入当前会话；和/或
一个可选开关：当 preset 的 composition 文件在磁盘上发生变化时自动热加载。
已知权衡（prompt caching）
本项目将 per-conversation prompt caching 视为神圣原则（会话中途重新注入系统提示词会使缓存前缀失效）。本提案在知情的前提下接受这一成本：方案 1 由用户主动触发（用户明确请求的一次性缓存失效）；方案 2（若采纳）应为 opt-in，且在轮次边界/空闲时刻生效，绝不在轮次中途生效。

已考虑过的替代方案
重建会话 —— 可用，但会丢失上下文/历史，且在迭代规则时很打断。
把新规则贴进对话 —— 可作一次性补救，但不是持久的、强制的改动；对话滚出上下文后规则就失效了。
范围与补充说明
我理解 tool-schema（工具模式）的改动大概率仍需新建会话（工具模式是按会话固定的）。本建议只针对 prompt / persona 文本层，这一层重新注入的成本相对低。

如果「会话快照不可变」是刻意设计，也希望能：

明确写明这一点；以及
提供一种更轻量的方式迭代 prompt 规则，而不必整会话重建。
使用场景
我维护一个个人 agent preset，其 persona 会随着时间不断累积规则（事实核查规范、记忆/交接约定、引用要求等）。每加一条规则，当前就得放弃活跃会话另开新会话，尽管工具面没有任何变化。

期望得到的答复
希望得到以下任一的明确答复：

「已支持 / 将支持」（并给出机制指向），或
「这是刻意设计、不会改」（并给出设计理由），或
「这是迭代 prompt 规则的推荐替代做法」。

discussions.title: Windows restricted-token sandbox: Schannel TLS fails with SEC_E_NO_CREDENTIALS
discussions.body:
# DSH 缺陷 / 文档反馈 — Windows 沙箱受限 token 阻断 Schannel TLS 凭据

> 面向 DeepSeek Harness (DSH) 项目组的 bug / 文档缺陷反馈。
> 起草日期：2026-08-23 ｜ 提交人：sxdtlili@qq.com
> 性质：**行为与文档不符（documentation/behavior mismatch）** + 一个未文档化的可用性缺口。

## 中文概要（供快速审阅）

DSH 在 Windows 上的沙箱（`dsh-sandbox-windows-acl`）用一个受限令牌（`WRITE_RESTRICTED` + `DISABLE_MAX_PRIVILEGE` + `LUA_TOKEN`）约束被沙箱包裹的 shell 子进程。这个令牌**只拦截写访问**（文档如此声明），但**顺带让 Windows 的 Schannel（系统 TLS 提供方）拿不到客户端凭据**，导致走 Schannel 的工具——`curl.exe`、`git.exe`、`Invoke-WebRequest`、PowerShell 的 `SslStream`（以及本环境里的 `pip`）——**在 TLS 握手阶段全部失败**（`SEC_E_NO_CREDENTIALS`）。而 **OpenSSL 栈的 Python 网络（`requests`/`urllib`）完全不受影响**，harness 进程自身的 `web_search`/`web_fetch`（不被沙箱包裹）也正常。

DSH 文档多处声明"网络不受限（network stays unrestricted）"、"本 seam 不表达任何网络限制"、"读写/网络/进程可见性不受限"。这些说法在**裸 socket / 原始 TCP** 层面成立（TCP 连接确实能建立），但对 **Schannel 型 TLS** 不成立，会误导用户以为沙箱 shell 能正常走 HTTPS。**建议修正文档措辞，或将"让受限令牌具备 Schannel 凭据"作为一个明确的安全决策**，而不是让这一能力缺口继续作为未文档化的副作用存在。

---

## 提交信息（可直接复制）

**提交目标（GitHub Issues）**

- 仓库：`deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness`（DeepSeek AI 官方）
- 提交页：<https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/issues> → "New issue"
- CLI：`gh issue create --repo deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness ...`（需在**非沙箱**终端 + 已认证）

**标题**

- 英文：`Windows restricted-token sandbox: Schannel TLS fails with SEC_E_NO_CREDENTIALS`
- 中文：`Windows 受限 token 沙箱导致 Schannel TLS 失败（SEC_E_NO_CREDENTIALS）`

**一句话摘要**

- 英文：On Windows, the DSH sandbox's restricted token (`DISABLE_MAX_PRIVILEGE | LUA_TOKEN | WRITE_RESTRICTED`) prevents Schannel from acquiring client credentials, so Schannel-based TLS clients (`curl`/`git`/`Invoke-WebRequest`/`pip`) fail at the handshake with `SEC_E_NO_CREDENTIALS`, while raw TCP sockets and OpenSSL-based clients (Python `requests`/`urllib`) still work — contradicting the docs' claim that "network stays unrestricted."
- 中文：在 Windows 上，DSH 沙箱的受限 token（`DISABLE_MAX_PRIVILEGE | LUA_TOKEN | WRITE_RESTRICTED`）让 Schannel 拿不到客户端凭据，导致走 Schannel 的工具（`curl`/`git`/`Invoke-WebRequest`/`pip`）在 TLS 握手阶段即失败（`SEC_E_NO_CREDENTIALS`），而裸 TCP 与 OpenSSL 栈的 Python（`requests`/`urllib`）仍正常工作——这与文档"网络不受限"的声明不符。

**一次性复现（issue 评论区/邮件开场白）**

> Repro (one-liner): from a sandboxed Windows shell run `curl -I https://api.deepseek.com` — it fails with `SEC_E_NO_CREDENTIALS`; run the same URL over Python `urllib` and it succeeds. Root cause is the restricted token stripping Windows Schannel client credentials.

---

## Summary

On Windows, the DSH sandbox (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-windows-acl`) wraps the sandboxed shell child in a restricted token built with
`CreateRestrictedToken(..., flags = 13, ...)` where `13 = DISABLE_MAX_PRIVILEGE(0x1) | LUA_TOKEN(0x4) | WRITE_RESTRICTED(0x8)`.
This token intersects **writes** only (as documented), but it also **prevents Windows Schannel (the OS TLS provider) from acquiring client credentials**,
so every Schannel-based HTTPS/TLS client fails at the handshake with `SEC_E_NO_CREDENTIALS (0x8009030e)`.

**Not affected:** raw TCP sockets (connect succeeds), **OpenSSL-based** clients (Python `requests`/`urllib`), and the harness node process (e.g. `web_search`/`web_fetch`), which is not wrapped by the restricted token.

**Contradiction with docs:** DSH docs state the sandbox expresses "no network ... restrictions" and that "network stays unrestricted / reads, network, and process visibility are not [restricted]". This is true for raw sockets but *not* for Schannel-based TLS.

## Environment

- Product: DeepSeek Harness — `@deepseek-ai/dsh` `0.1.1-rc.2`
- Packages: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-local`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-windows-acl`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-bash-sandbox` / `@deepseek-ai/dsh-pwsh-sandbox`
- OS: Windows, sandbox mode `workspace-write` (ACL restricted-token runner)
- Network client tested: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (`pwsh`), `git`, `curl.exe`, Python 3.14 (`urllib`)

## Expected vs. Actual

|     | Expected (per docs) | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Raw TCP socket (443) | unrestricted | ✅ works (connect succeeds) |
| Schannel-based TLS (curl/git/Invoke-WebRequest/SslStream) | should work ("network unrestricted") | ❌ fails at handshake — `SEC_E_NO_CREDENTIALS` |
| OpenSSL-based TLS (Python requests/urllib) | should work | ✅ works (reaches server) |
| Harness `web_search`/`web_fetch` | not sandboxed | ✅ works |

## Root cause & evidence

The restricted token is built in machine-independent DSH code with a fixed flag set that strips privileges and produces a limited/write-restricted token. Under this token:

1. **Schannel cannot acquire client credentials** → `SEC_E_NO_CREDENTIALS`.
  - `curl.exe -I https://api.deepseek.com` → `curl: (35) schannel: AcquireCredentialsHandle failed: SEC_E_NO_CREDENTIALS (0x8009030e)`
  - `Invoke-WebRequest` / `.NET SslStream.AuthenticateAsClient` → `Exception calling "AuthenticateAsClient": No credentials are available in the security package`
  - `git ls-remote https://github.com/...` → `Failed to connect to github.com:443 ... Could not connect to server`
2. **Token is privilege-stripped** (consistent with `DISABLE_MAX_PRIVILEGE`):
  - `whoami /all` lists only `SeChangeNotifyPrivilege` (bypass traverse checking); a normal interactive token carries many more.
3. **Serialization matches a genuine network, not a firewall**:
  - Raw TCP connect to `github.com:443`, `www.baidu.com:443`, `registry.npmjs.org:443`, `pypi.org:443`, `api.deepseek.com:443`, `*.deepseek.com:443` all succeed; only `www.google.com:443` fails to answer (SYN-level, unrelated — Google's resilience to probes).
4. **OpenSSL path is unaffected** (decisive contrast):
  - `python -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('https://api.deepseek.com')"` → `HTTPError 401: 'Authorization Required'` — i.e. **TLS handshake succeeded** and the request reached the server (401 = no API key, as expected).

## Reproduction

```powershell
# 1) TCP works — no network firewall
$c = New-Object System.Net.Sockets.TcpClient
$c.Connect("api.deepseek.com",443); "TCP OK"

# 2) Schannel-based TLS fails
curl.exe -I https://api.deepseek.com     # SEC_E_NO_CREDENTIALS

# 3) OpenSSL-based TLS works
python -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('https://api.deepseek.com')"  # 401 (reached server)

# 4) Restricted token — stripped privileges
whoami /all
```

## Impact

- **Broken in the sandboxed Windows shell:** `git clone`, `curl`, `Invoke-WebRequest`, PowerShell TLS, and `pip` (in this environment) — all the native-Windows TLS tools fail at the handshake.
- **Not broken:** Python `requests`/`urllib` (OpenSSL) and harness-level `web_search`/`web_fetch`.
- Practical consequence: the model's sandboxed shell cannot perform ordinary HTTPS work that relies on Schannel (git operations, downloads, PowerShell web calls), even though the host has full internet (the harness node process itself reaches `api.deepseek.com` for LLM + web search).

## Suggested resolution (options)

1. **Documentation-only (lowest risk):** Amend the "network is unrestricted / seam expresses no network restrictions" statements in `dsh-sandbox/README.md`, `dsh-bash-sandbox/README.md`, and `dsh-sandbox-windows-acl/README.md` to note that, on the Windows restricted-token runner, **Schannel client-credential acquisition fails**, so Schannel-based TLS clients are unavailable; OpenSSL-based and harness-level clients are unaffected.
2. **Behavioral change (needs a deliberate security decision):** If sandboxed-shell network access is desired, provide a mechanism for Schannel credentials under the restricted token (or route HTTPS through a non-Schannel path), explicitly weighing the fact that the current behavior is arguably security-positive (it prevents HTTPS-based exfiltration / arbitrary downloads from the sandboxed shell).
3. **State the intent:** Either way, the current limitation should be a documented, deliberate choice rather than an unplanned side effect, so callers don't rely on "network unrestricted" to mean Schannel-based TLS works.

## Scope & confidence

- **Observed on a single Windows host**, DSH `0.1.1-rc.2`, `workspace-write` sandbox (2026-08-23).
- **Root-cause inference is high-confidence:** the token-construction flag set is machine-independent DSH code, and the observed symptoms (stripped privileges + Schannel `SEC_E_NO_CREDENTIALS` + working OpenSSL) follow directly from it.
- **Cross-machine confirmation is pending** (has not been reproduced on a second Windows host). Treat "affects all Windows DSH sandboxes" as a strong inference, not a verified universal fact.
- Note: the OpenSSL-works finding was already captured locally in this workspace (`research-assistant/docs/network-verification.md`, 2026-08-16); this report is the upstream-facing version.

## References

- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox/README.md` — *"File effects are the whole policy vocabulary — the seam expresses no network, process, syscall, device, or credential restrictions."*
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-bash-sandbox/README.md` — *"File effects only ... Network stays unrestricted"*; Known Limitations: *"Confinement covers file effects only — network restriction ... absent."*
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-windows-acl/README.md` — *"Writes are restricted; reads, network, and process visibility are not. `WRITE_RESTRICTED` intersects write accesses only, so a confined child can ... open sockets."*
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-windows-acl/lib/types/token.d.ts` + `lib/types/win32-abi.d.ts` — `DISABLE_MAX_PRIVILEGE = 1`, `WRITE_RESTRICTED = 8`, `LUA_TOKEN = 4`; `createRestrictedToken(..., 13, ...)`.
- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-search-deepseek/README.md` — harness-level `web_search` reaches the network via `ctx.web` → `POST {baseURL}/messages` (DeepSeek Anthropic-compatible API), outside the sandbox.

discussions.title: Feature Request: Voice/speech-to-text input for the Web GUI composer
discussions.body:
### Summary

Add a speech-to-text (voice input) option to the Web GUI chat composer so users can dictate long instructions instead of typing, with privacy-first local handling.

### Motivation

- Typing long, complex instructions is slow and error-prone; voice dictation makes describing multi-step tasks much more natural.
- Tablet / touchscreen and remote-access scenarios often lack a physical keyboard.
- Accessibility: voice input helps users who have difficulty typing.
- Peer products (Codex client dictation, Claude mobile apps, etc.) already ship voice input; adding it helps Harness reach more users.

### Proposed behavior

1. A mic button next to the chat composer input box.
2. Click to start continuous dictation; click again (or auto-stop after a pause) to stop.
3. Recognized text is inserted at the cursor in the composer; the user edits it before sending (never auto-send).
4. Support Chinese, English, and mixed-language dictation, with auto-punctuation.
5. Show interim recognition results when the underlying API supports them.

### Privacy (important)

- Privacy-first: prefer local/system speech recognition by default; do not upload audio to third-party services without explicit user consent.
- If cloud STT is offered, it must be an opt-in setting with a clear notice, consistent with the "local-first, data stays on the machine" philosophy of Harness.

### Suggested implementation

- v1: browser Web Speech API (SpeechRecognition) - zero dependencies, works in Chrome/Edge, audio stays in the browser.
- v2 (optional): local Whisper (e.g. faster-whisper) for higher-quality offline dictation.
- Cloud STT only as an opt-in.
- Graceful fallback: when unsupported, disable the button and hint at OS-level dictation (Windows Win+H, macOS dictation).

### Acceptance criteria

- Mic button starts/stops dictation in current Chrome/Edge.
- Long Chinese dictation (200+ chars) is usable with reasonable accuracy and punctuation.
- Inserted text is editable before manual send.
- No audio leaves the machine without explicit user consent.

### Environment

- Windows 11, Chrome/Edge, local DeepSeek Harness Web GUI.

discussions.title: An API to remove terminal job records (distinct from cancel)
discussions.body:
Two long-standing reports document the same gap from different sides:

- #1204 — job_list records cannot be deleted; the title states it directly: "no remove API".
- #3994 — terminal job records are never reclaimed; the store grows unbounded and every scan is O(n) over accumulated history.

**The ask:** a `jobs.remove`-style API (host + client surface) that deletes a terminal job's record from the store and the UI list. Whether removing a still-running job should be rejected or implicitly cancel-then-remove is open for discussion — the core need is record lifecycle after termination.

**Explicitly not in scope:** cancelling a running job. The producer-level `cancel()` mechanism already exists (#4109 is a bug in that path — a hang without timeout — not a request for the mechanism), and #1517 covers managed jobs with cancellation. This request is about what happens to the record once the job is done.

**Why it matters:** in long-lived workspaces the job list becomes permanent clutter — failed subagents that can't be cleared from the UI (#1202), sandbox noise, one-off tasks from days ago. And per #3994 the cost isn't only visual: every scan pays O(n) over the accumulated history.

Happy to sketch the store-level reclaim semantics if that would help move this forward.

discussions.title: [Bug] Cold history resolves the wrong presenter for agent-scoped shadow tools
discussions.body:
## Summary

A tool registered on a live agent scope may legitimately shadow a same-name tool from its preset. Live presentation resolves through the agent and uses the definition that actually executed. After that agent is gone, `session.history` resolves presenters through the recorded preset's standing key instead. The former agent layer is absent, so a same-name preset definition wins—even though it did not execute the logged call.

When the two definitions have different argument schemas, the standing definition's `defineTool` wrapper soft-rejects the logged arguments before its presenter runs. The result falls back to a generic card. Persisted `presentationMeta` cannot help because the registry chooses the wrong definition first.

This means a scoped shadow tool can render correctly live but lose its result card after restart/cold history.

## Concrete downstream case

[`dsh-better-edit` issue #25](https://github.com/Rianico/dsh-better-edit/issues/25) asks why its hash-anchored `edit` results never render as diff cards.

The plugin is mounted on the host plane and, at `agent/session-start`, registers its `edit` on `agent.ctx`, intentionally shadowing the preset's built-in `edit` ([install](https://github.com/Rianico/dsh-better-edit/blob/c2b993cefda1e4e6987603210b35527c13687a7d/src/index.ts#L109-L120), [registration](https://github.com/Rianico/dsh-better-edit/blob/c2b993cefda1e4e6987603210b35527c13687a7d/src/tool-edit.ts#L119-L120)). Its arguments are `{ path, edits }`; the built-in edit expects `{ file_path, old_string, new_string }`.

I implemented the apparent fix locally: structured canonical output carrying diff data, `output.presentationMeta`, defensive metadata narrowing, and `presentResult`. Live presentation and JSON-round-tripped metadata worked, and 679 tests passed. A separate registry/history review found the cold-path failure, so I did not publish that patch as a PR.

Cold replay does this:

1. Resolve `edit` at the preset standing key.
2. Select the built-in edit, because the agent-local shadow no longer exists in that view.
3. Soft-validate the persisted `{ path, edits }` against the built-in schema.
4. Return no view and render the generic result card.

The correct diff metadata is present but never reaches the presenter that understands it.

## Source path

Current master inspected at `b150a551b8d465e31e418e1b2eaf5e79bbb7d28e`:

- [`ToolRuntime.register()` stores the whole definition in the caller's layer; same-layer duplicates fail](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/b150a551b8d465e31e418e1b2eaf5e79bbb7d28e/packages/core/tools/src/index.ts#L1032-L1058).
- [`ToolRuntime.get(name, scope)` returns the nearest visible same-name definition](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/b150a551b8d465e31e418e1b2eaf5e79bbb7d28e/packages/core/tools/src/index.ts#L1196-L1205).
- [`viewFor()` selects that definition by logged name before invoking `presentCall` / `presentResult`](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/b150a551b8d465e31e418e1b2eaf5e79bbb7d28e/packages/host/apiproxy/src/api-proxy.ts#L685-L713).
- [A cold session deliberately uses `agentPresets.standingKeyFor(...)`, without resuming an agent](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/b150a551b8d465e31e418e1b2eaf5e79bbb7d28e/packages/host/apiproxy/src/api-proxy.ts#L1537-L1555).

The individual pieces are internally consistent, but the log stores only the tool name/arguments/result metadata—not the identity of the scoped definition/presenter that produced them.

## Why the plugin cannot repair this cleanly

- A global `edit` presenter/definition loses to the preset's nearer built-in `edit`.
- Registering another `edit` in the standing layer collides with the built-in definition.
- A child/agent registration is unavailable once cold history has no agent.
- A distinct tool name avoids the collision but changes the plugin's public tool contract.
- Resuming an agent only to render history would add side effects and defeat the cold-history design.

There is currently no presenter-only registry or supported arbitrary-scope presentation overlay.

## Minimal regression

1. Register built-in `edit` on a preset standing scope.
2. Register a different `edit` definition on a child live-agent scope, with incompatible arguments and a diff presenter.
3. Execute/log the child definition and persist its presentation metadata.
4. Assert live presentation returns `card: "diff"`.
5. Remove the live agent and request `sessions.history` for the same log.
6. Current result: the standing built-in definition returns no view.
7. Desired result: cold history still resolves the presenter that produced the logged metadata and returns the diff card.

A sibling preset that never installed the shadow should continue resolving the official edit presenter.

## Possible provider-neutral seams

Either of these would make the invariant representable without restoring execution authority:

1. A durable `presentationKey`/definition identity recorded with tool events plus a separate registry of pure presenters. Cold history resolves by that key; unknown or obsolete keys fall back generically.
2. Persist a validated, JSON-only `ToolEventView` at execution time and let history replay it after validating the view schema.

The first keeps current presenters reusable and versionable; the second makes historical rendering independent of current composition. In either design, the presentation identity must not grant tool execution, metadata remains untrusted/validated, and failure should retain today's generic fallback.

## Environment

- Reproduced against published `0.1.0-rc.6` contracts.
- Re-audited on master `b150a551b8d465e31e418e1b2eaf5e79bbb7d28e`.
- Windows 11 / Node 24; the failure is scope/log topology, not platform-specific.

discussions.title: [Bug] Deleted/modified agent preset ("Mode") strands recorded sessions after host restart: preset "X" not found
discussions.body:
## 中文

**删除或修改模式（Agent Preset，agent 预设）后，使用该模式的会话在宿主重启后无法恢复**

### 摘要

会话创建时记录所用模式，每次恢复都按记录重新挂载。当该模式后来从名册消失——`$DSH_HOME/.agent-presets` 下对应目录被删除、改名，或模式被修改后不再以原 id 出现在名册——宿主一旦重启，**所有记录了该 id 的会话都以笼统的 `internal` 错误恢复失败**，且没有任何受支持的手段让这些对话继续。

同一进程内其实已经容忍删除：`AgentPresets.remove()` 会为已挂载会话保留 standing mount（见 `packages/preset/agent-presets/src/index.ts` 中 `remove()` 上方注释）。缺口只在**冷恢复路径**：宿主重启后，磁盘上已不存在的模式无法再被挂载。

### 环境

- dsh `0.1.1-rc.2`（npm 全局安装），profile `web`
- Node `v24.19.0`，Windows 11（10.0.26100）

### 复现步骤

1. 新建一个用户模式：`~/.dsh/.agent-presets/router-standard/agent.cordis.yml`（拷贝任意内置预设即可）；
2. 在该模式下建会话并跑至少一轮，然后停止会话；
3. 删除、改名该目录，或修改该模式使其 id 从名册消失；
4. 重启宿主，打开该会话（或点模式选择器触发懒恢复）。

实际结果（本次复现，完整错误信息）：

```text
模型操作失败：internal: resume failed for session "session-2c50143f-cf3e-4236-a0ee-d462bb2e605e": Error: agent-presets: preset "router-standard" not found (available: standard, code, minimal, cordis, liangshen)
```

（`liangshen` 是该宿主上既有的用户模式，其余四个为内置预设。）同一消息也出现在 RPC 的 `error.message` 里：

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "internal",
    "message": "resume failed for session \"session-2c50143f-cf3e-4236-a0ee-d462bb2e605e\": Error: agent-presets: preset \"router-standard\" not found (available: standard, code, minimal, cordis, liangshen)",
    "details": {}
  }
}
```

UI 仅弹出这个“模型操作失败”开头的笼统提示，该 id 下所有会话永久卡死。实测一个真实环境里 78 个持久会话中有 20 个因单个被删 id 而搁浅。

期望结果：要么会话仍可恢复（有文档化的降级），要么给出结构化、可行动的错误与恢复路径，而不是笼统 `internal`。

### 根因

恢复链路：`api-proxy.ts` 的 `composeAgent(presetId)` -> `presets.resolve(id)` 抛 `UnknownPresetError`（`preset.ts`）-> 被 `packages/api/remotes/src/agent-lookup.ts` 的兜底捕获包装成 `{ code: 'internal' }`，丢弃了线协议已定义的 `agent-preset-not-found` 结构化细节（`{ agentPreset, available }`）。

对比之下冷读历史已经优雅降级（`standingKeyFor` 失败被吞掉、历史仍可查看），唯独恢复硬失败，行为不一致且难排查。另外持久层已具备显式改绑的全部机制（`agent-preset/selected` 事件、最新者胜），只是没有暴露给搁浅场景。

### 修复方向建议

1. 最小改动：让恢复路径透传 `agent-preset-not-found`（而非 `internal`），客户端即可提供恢复入口；
2. 恢复流：报错时允许客户端为会话追加一条 `agent-preset/selected` 事件以改绑到现有模式——与空白期 `agentPreset.select` 同一持久化机制，扩展到搁浅场景；
3. 文档化回退：缺失 id 解析为部署默认组合（ghost id 下），并输出告警。下方插件证明该方案端到端可行。

### 已验证的进程内 workaround

通过 home patch 层挂载的小插件包裹服务实例的 `resolve`：未知 id 返回默认模式行（保留 ghost id 作隔离键），全部消费路径随之降级，20 个搁浅会话无需重建任何目录即恢复。核心代码见英文节。

### 已检索的既有报告

Discussions/Issues 中检索 `preset not found`、`resume failed`、“删除预设 会话”均无重复；最接近的是 #3018（改默认预设对复用空白会话不生效），同属预设生命周期领域但症状不同。

---

## English

### Summary

A session records the agent preset it was composed under — the same thing the UI calls a "Mode" — and re-mounts that preset on every resume. When the preset later disappears from the roster (its user-authored directory deleted or renamed under `$DSH_HOME/.agent-presets`, or the preset itself modified), **every session recorded under that id fails to resume with a generic `internal` error after a host restart**, and there is no supported way to keep those conversations alive.

In-process behavior already tolerates deletion - `AgentPresets.remove()` keeps standing mounts for joined sessions (`packages/preset/agent-presets/src/index.ts`, comment above `remove()`). The gap is only the **cold-resume path**: once the host restarts, nothing can re-mount a preset that no longer exists on disk.

### Environment

- dsh `0.1.1-rc.2` (npm global install), profile `web`
- Node `v24.19.0`, Windows 11 (10.0.26100)

### Minimal reproduction

1. Author a user preset: `~/.dsh/.agent-presets/router-standard/agent.cordis.yml` (a copy of any shipped preset works).
2. Create a session under it, run at least one turn, close/stop the session.
3. Delete or rename `~/.dsh/.agent-presets/router-standard/`, or modify it so that id leaves the roster.
4. Restart the host; open the session (or click the Mode selector, which lazily resumes).

Actual (verbatim from the affected host):

```text
模型操作失败：internal: resume failed for session "session-2c50143f-cf3e-4236-a0ee-d462bb2e605e": Error: agent-presets: preset "router-standard" not found (available: standard, code, minimal, cordis, liangshen)
```

(`liangshen` is an unrelated user preset already on that host; the other four are the shipped built-ins.) The same message arrives in the RPC `error.message`:

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "internal",
    "message": "resume failed for session \"session-2c50143f-cf3e-4236-a0ee-d462bb2e605e\": Error: agent-presets: preset \"router-standard\" not found (available: standard, code, minimal, cordis, liangshen)",
    "details": {}
  }
}
```

The UI surfaces only that generic `模型操作失败` toast, and every session recorded under the missing id strands permanently. In one real deployment here, 20 of 78 persisted sessions stranded behind a single deleted id.

Expected: either the session still resumes (documented fallback), or the failure is a structured, actionable error with a recovery path - not an opaque `internal`.

### Root cause

Resume funnels through the recorded effective preset (newest `agent-preset/selected` event, else the header - `packages/preset/agent-presets/src/session.ts`, `resolveSessionPreset`) into:

- `packages/host/apiproxy/src/api-proxy.ts` -> `composeAgent(presetId)` -> `presets.resolve(id)` -> throws `UnknownPresetError` (`packages/preset/agent-presets/src/preset.ts`),
- which the generic resolver catch wraps into `{ code: 'internal' }` (`packages/api/remotes/src/agent-lookup.ts`, `resume failed for session ...`), discarding the structured `agent-preset-not-found` details (`{ agentPreset, available }`) that the wire protocol already defines.

Notably, the **cold transcript read already degrades gracefully**: `standingKeyFor` failures are swallowed so history stays viewable without the preset. Resume is the only path left failing hard, which makes the inconsistency easy to hit and confusing to diagnose.

A session's preset is deliberately fixed at creation (`assertPresetUnchanged`), and blank-session switches are recorded as `agent-preset/selected` log events where the newest wins - i.e. the persistence layer already has everything needed to re-point a session at another composition explicitly.

### Suggested directions (pick per taste)

1. **Minimal:** let the resume path surface `agent-preset-not-found` instead of `internal` (the RPC details map already carries `{ agentPreset, available }`). Clients could then offer recovery.
2. **Recovery flow:** on that error, let the client adopt the session under an existing preset by appending an `agent-preset/selected` event - same durability mechanism `agentPreset.select` uses while blank, extended to the stranded case.
3. **Documented fallback:** resolve missing ids to the deployment default composition under the ghost id, with a warning. A tiny process-level shim proves this is viable end-to-end (below).

### Verified workaround (process-level plugin)

A home-patch plugin wrapping the live service instance keeps all 20 stranded sessions resumable with no directories recreated:

```js
export const inject = ['agentPresets']
export function apply(ctx) {
  const presets = ctx.agentPresets
  const original = presets.resolve.bind(presets)
  presets.resolve = async (id) => {
    try { return await original(id) }
    catch (error) {
      if (!(error instanceof Error) || typeof error.presetId !== 'string') throw error
      const standIn = await original(undefined) // deployment default
      return { ...standIn, id }                 // ghost id keeps scope isolation
    }
  }
}
```

All consumers (create/resume/fork/cold read via `resolveMountable`/`standingKeyFor`) degrade together because they funnel through `resolve()` / `this.resolve()`.

### Prior art checked

Searched Discussions & Issues for `preset not found`, `resume failed`; no duplicate found. Closest: #3018 (default-preset change not applying to a reused blank session), same lifecycle area, different symptom.

discussions.title: DSH Plugin Bench 0.2.0 — evidence-backed, type-aware plugin quality scorecards
discussions.body:
I built DSH Plugin Bench to answer a narrower question than a plugin directory or Stars leaderboard: for one exact plugin artifact and commit, what quality is actually proven, and what remains unknown?

It distinguishes Bundles, native Cordis plugins, Skills, Presets, and repositories that only carry the `dsh-plugin` topic. The scorecard covers eight areas across the lifecycle: functional results; install/activation/upgrade/removal; DSH integration; reliability; permissions/privacy; performance; UX/operability; and release maintenance.

A few deliberate boundaries:

- `UNPROVEN` is missing evidence, not failure.
- GitHub Stars and identity labels are adoption metadata and never change the quality score.
- Runtime credit must be bound to the full commit and artifact, with the DSH/Node/OS/profile recorded.
- “Official” or beta identity stays `UNPROVEN` without first-party, version-specific evidence. This project is independent and is not an official DeepSeek project.

The 0.2.0 pilot includes 11 pinned samples, shareable Markdown scorecards/SVG badges, and independent GPT and DeepSeek Harness reviews. Only one pilot sample crossed the 80% evidence-coverage gate; that is not a “best plugin” claim—it means the remaining samples need more commit-bound runtime evidence before comparison is responsible.

Source and release: https://github.com/B1lli/dsh-plugin-bench

Try it from a checkout (the npm package is not published yet):

```bash
npm ci
npm run score -- owner/repo
```

Plugin maintainers: I would especially value feedback on which runtime-evidence checks are practical to reproduce in an isolated DSH profile, and whether the generated scorecard makes the evidence gaps clear enough to act on.

discussions.title: Bug: Web bundle exposes an empty agent preset roster outside the CLI
[BUG/PR]dsh fails to boot inside Sandboxie: "exists and is not a symlink" although the path is a junction
discussions.body:
**Describe the bug**

Running `dsh` (or DSH Desktop, which embeds the same `@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot`) inside a Sandboxie sandbox on Windows fails at every profile boot with:

```
dsh: C:\Users\<user>\.dsh\profiles\node_modules\dsh-plugin-desktop exists and is not a symlink; remove it so dsh can manage the installation fallback
```

The path **is** a reparse point (junction) — `fsutil reparsepoint query`, `GetFileAttributes` and `dir /a:l` all confirm it — yet the guard in `ensureSymlink` (`packages/boot/app-boot/src/profile.ts`) rejects it and the CLI exits 1. Deleting the link lets the current run succeed (the CLI recreates it), but the error returns on every later start.

**Environment**

- Windows 10/11 (NTFS), 64-bit
- dsh `0.1.1-rc.2` / DSH Desktop `2.0.2` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot` `0.1.1-rc.2`)
- Sandboxie-Plus, standard isolation sandbox

**Root cause**

`ensureSymlink` detects links with `lstatSync(link).isSymbolicLink()`. On Windows, Node (libuv) implements `lstat` through `GetFileInformationByHandle`, which is supposed to report `FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT`. Inside Sandboxie that attribute is masked, so a junction is reported as a plain directory (mode `0o40666`) and the guard throws. This is the same family of symlink/reparse-point quirks tracked in [sandboxie-plus/Sandboxie#3491](https://github.com/sandboxie-plus/Sandboxie/issues/3491).

Measured inside the sandbox, same process context:

| Detection | Underlying API | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `fs.lstatSync().isSymbolicLink()` | `GetFileInformationByHandle` | ❌ false (plain directory) |
| `fs.readlinkSync()` | `NtQueryInformationFile(ReparsePoint)` | ❌ EINVAL |
| `fs.readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true })` → `dirent.isSymbolicLink()` | `FindFirstFile` | ✅ true |
| `GetFileAttributes` / `fsutil reparsepoint query` / `dir /a:l` | FindFirstFile / DeviceIoControl | ✅ reparse point visible |

So directory enumeration (FindFirstFile) still sees the reparse flag; handle-based queries do not.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Run dsh (or DSH Desktop) inside a Sandboxie sandbox on Windows.
2. Trigger any profile boot (`dsh --dump-config`, `dsh web`, or the desktop app launch).
3. The first run creates the fallback junctions under `$DSH_HOME/profiles/node_modules`; every subsequent run fails with the error above.

**Expected behavior**

The junction is recognized as a link and boot continues (native-Windows behavior).

**Actual behavior**

`dsh: <path> exists and is not a symlink; remove it so dsh can manage the installation fallback`, exit code 1, on every start until the link is manually deleted.

**Proposed fix**

In `ensureSymlink`, when `lstat` reports a non-symlink, re-check the path through the parent directory listing (FindFirstFile attributes stay intact under Sandboxie). If it is a reparse point, keep the link and return; otherwise throw the original error — a real directory is still rejected, so the guard is not weakened.

```diff
--- a/packages/boot/app-boot/src/profile.ts
+++ b/packages/boot/app-boot/src/profile.ts
@@ -24,7 +24,7 @@
 
 import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
 import {
-  existsSync, lstatSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, readlinkSync, symlinkSync, unlinkSync, writeFileSync,
+  existsSync, lstatSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, readdirSync, readlinkSync, symlinkSync, unlinkSync, writeFileSync,
 } from 'node:fs'
 import { basename, dirname, join } from 'node:path'
 import type { EntryOptions } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis-plugin-loader'
@@ -179,7 +179,16 @@ function ensureSymlink(link: string, target: string): void {
   }
   if (stat !== undefined) {
     if (!stat.isSymbolicLink()) {
-      throw new Error(`dsh: ${link} exists and is not a symlink; remove it so dsh can manage the installation fallback`)
+      // Windows reparse points (junctions) can be masked from lstat inside
+      // Sandboxie, which reports them as plain directories via
+      // GetFileInformationByHandle. Re-check through the parent directory
+      // listing, whose FindFirstFile attributes keep the reparse flag.
+      if (!isReparsePointLink(link)) {
+        throw new Error(`dsh: ${link} exists and is not a symlink; remove it so dsh can manage the installation fallback`)
+      }
+      // A real junction: keep it. Sandboxie also cannot read the link target
+      // (readlinkSync throws EINVAL), so target verification is skipped.
+      return
     }
     if (readlinkSync(link) === target) return
     // unlink deletes the reparse point itself on Windows too; rmSync treats a
@@ -201,6 +210,20 @@ function ensureSymlink(link: string, target: string): void {
   }
 }
 
+/**
+ * Windows: detect a reparse point (symlink or junction) through the parent
+ * directory listing instead of lstat, because Sandboxie masks the reparse
+ * attribute from GetFileInformationByHandle while FindFirstFile keeps it.
+ */
+function isReparsePointLink(link: string): boolean {
+  try {
+    const entries = readdirSync(dirname(link), { withFileTypes: true })
+    return entries.some(entry => entry.name === basename(link) && entry.isSymbolicLink())
+  } catch {
+    return false
+  }
+}
+
 /**
  * Maintain the flat module fallback `$DSH_HOME/profiles/node_modules`: one
```

**Verification**

Tested end-to-end inside the sandbox (patched `lib/index.js` of `@deepseek-ai/dsh-app-boot@0.1.1-rc.2`):

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `dsh --dump-config` with existing junctions (the restart case) | ❌ error | ✅ exit 0 |
| second consecutive boot, junctions still present | ❌ | ✅ exit 0 |
| fresh `$DSH_HOME` (create all links) | ✅ | ✅ |
| a **real directory** placed at a link path (guard) | ❌ original error | ❌ original error (intact) |

The fix is behavior-neutral on native Windows (there `lstat` already reports junctions as symlinks, so the new branch is never reached).

**Notes**

- The same change is currently carried as an interim patch in the DSH Desktop repo ([anywhere-labs/deepseek-harness-desktop](https://github.com/anywhere-labs/deepseek-harness-desktop), `patches/dsh-app-boot@0.1.1-rc.2.patch`). Landing it here would let the desktop drop that patch and bump the package version.
- Secondary (not touched here): the `EEXIST` race branch of `ensureSymlink` also calls `lstatSync`/`readlinkSync`, which behave the same way under Sandboxie; it can be hardened with the same fallback if desired.

discussions.title: Proposal: add Russian (ru) locale to the Web UI (zh/en/ru)
discussions.body:
Proposal: add Russian (ru) locale to the Web UI (zh/en/ru)

Hi everyone,

I've been using dsh with the Web UI and wanted to contribute a Russian translation. Since the repo currently doesn't accept external PRs, I'm posting this here as a proposal and would love feedback from the maintainers and the community.

## What it does

Ships Russian as a full third GUI locale alongside zh and en. The Language switcher in Settings → General now offers 中文 / English / Русский, and the whole Web UI is translated.

## What's included

- Core LOCALE_IDS / LOCALES change to add ru.
- Russian dictionaries for every client namespace — roughly 1,000 strings across ~28 client packages (ui-conversation, ui-trajectory, ui-settings-models, ui-agent-preset, ui-permission-presets, etc.).
- Correct Russian plural categories (one / few / other) in all the selection sites that count items.
- Localized trajectory / session-export / permission-preset strings.
- Layout (CSS) fixes where Russian text renders wider than zh/en, e.g. the trajectory table and subagent lineage headers.
- html lang is set to the active locale (ru) so assistive tech and browser features behave correctly.

## How it's kept correct

zh stays the key-set source of truth (per the repo's zh-first convention). The typed registration contract is now register(ns, { zh, en, ru }), so a missing or extra ru key is a compile error — complete Russian coverage is enforced by the type system, not by review.

## Verification

- typecheck: green
- locale tests: 35/35 passed
- affected GUI packages: 752/752 (trajectory 107/107, permission presets 14/14)

## Where it lives

- Branch: feat/ru-locale
- Commit: a449619 — "feat(web): add Russian (ru) locale to the Web UI"
- Fork: github.com/Ragnoryok1/deepseek-harness_ru

Happy to rebase onto master whenever the upstream moves, and to open a PR as soon as you're able to accept them. Feedback, corrections, and style nits are very welcome — especially from native Russian speakers.
